result.walkthrough: STEP 0 — Read the book figure. Fig 8.1 is a LEFT-hand ~90° corner (rider enters bottom-right heading up, exits top-left heading west) on a two-lane road with a double-yellow centreline and white edge lines. It contains: a solid RED line from a red hourglass marker labelled "premature turn point", through a red ring "early apex" ON the centreline, running wide to the outer edge at the exit; a solid GREEN line from a green hourglass "delayed turn point" through a green ring "delayed apex" on the centreline, exiting in-lane; DASHED red and green sight lines cast from each turn point across the inside of the corner (labelled "sight lines"); a bush occluder in the grass inside the bend; and an oncoming SUV ON the road, in the oncoming lane, facing the corner — the prop the delayed sight line reveals. STEP 1 — Cold start per 08 §2: I run `linelab schema scene`, `schema road-dsl`, `schema occluders`, `schema mistakes`, `schema view`. The mistakes teaching table (08 §5.1) correctly steers me to `early_apex` for the book's red line despite its "premature turn point" label — the naming trap is defused at the surface. But `linelab explain early_apex` fails: 08 §3's explain signature accepts only envelope|checkId|errorCode, though 01 §4.3 and 03 §7.1 both promise `explain(kind)`. Nothing at the schema surface promises preset expansions, so I cannot yet know `book90` is a right-hander. STEP 2 — Author the scene. Recipe (e) (08 §6) says use `book90` + ideal + early_apex + hedge; following it produces a MIRROR of fig 8.1 (right-hander: apex against the road edge instead of the centreline; run-wide crosses into the oncoming lane instead of off the outer edge). Having viewed the book image, I instead hand-flip the preset expansion: `road: lane 3.5 | S 12 | L 12 ^90 | S 16`, then `lines:` `delayed: ride entry=34 label="delayed turn point"` and `premature: mistake early_apex early_by_m=6 label="premature turn point"` (whether a mistake entry accepts label= is unspecified in 04 §7), `occluders: hedge inside c1 +3x8 margin=1.5 depth=4` for the bush (the closed vocabulary has no `bush`; hedge's organic-blob glyph substitutes; note the occluder token grammar itself is inconsistent — bare `c1` in bookBlind vs `entry|exit|mid:<id>` in §4's grammar vs 08 recipe (c)'s double-offset `entry:c1-25 -1.0x30`). The oncoming SUV stops me cold: `vehicle` is advertised as "(parked or oncoming-lane vehicle)" but the placement grammar only measures margins OUTWARD from the road edge for band kinds and specifies no lateral rule at all for the vehicle rectangle — there is no way to put it ON the road in the oncoming lane. I add `marks: all` (default `auto` marks only the good line; the book marks both), guessed labels (`mid:c1 -4 "early apex"` — the `apex:c1` sugar resolves only against the GOOD line's apex, so labelling the red line's early apex is station guesswork), `view: mode=diagram window=auto`. STEP 3 — `scene fig-08-01.scene --check` lints, then bake. Here the causal chain breaks: the solved plan is exactly four actions (brake, tangent_inside turn_in, crack, roll-on — 04 §4.2), the controller tracks target_lean set only by plan actions (02 §3), turn_in has no lifetime and lean_deg ∈ (0,90) excludes zero, and position actions overlapping a turn_in are rejected (03 §6.1). Nothing ever commands lean back to zero, so under the EOM (psi_dot = G·tanφ/v) every line keeps yawing after the corner (~33°/s at 28°/9 m/s) and curls across the lane on the 16 m exit straight — the green line cannot self-verify clean, and the book's straight exit arrows are asserted, not derivable. STEP 4 — Assuming an implementer invents the unwind: colour law v2 gives book colours honestly (clean solve → green; early_apex pinned runoff → red — though 01 §4.3 says "wide/runoff" while 03 §7.1 pins "runoff", and the oracle pins ONE class). Sight rays default to each line's turn_in event (06 §3.1 item 7) — exactly the book's device, red ray shorter/bush-blocked, green ray deeper. But the red TRAJECTORY renders short-dashed (mistake role, 06 §5.2) in the same red as its dashed sight ray — the book's solid-path/dashed-sight grammar is conflated. The red line's endpoint is arbitrary: lateral departure is not in 02 §7's termination precedence (crash → stopped → road/corner end → guards), off-road mu is unspecified (default 1.0 = dry asphalt on grass), so the runoff line keeps integrating to the road-end station. Which line defines the auto window is unspecified (the mistake line has no exit event), as is the "designated eye sample" for occluded shading and window clamping at road bounds. STEP 5 — G7/proportion check: 7 m width / R12 = 0.583, inside the 0.45–0.95 band at true scale (the preset math is genuinely good; amusingly the literal auto-width_exag formula yields 0.943 < 1 with no ≥1 clamp, and book90's TRUE-mode straight share is 0.60 vs the ≤0.45 band that 09 §5.3 says presets should already "land near"). Net: a compact, mostly book-like two-line figure with correct colours, markers, and sight rays is reachable ONLY by overriding the recipe's preset by hand, and it ships without the oncoming vehicle, without per-line apex labels, with a dashed red path, and with a red tail whose end means nothing — on top of an engine spec that cannot actually produce the exits drawn.

findings.title: No lean-unwind: the specified action vocabulary cannot produce any exit
findings.claim: Nothing in the specified plan vocabulary or controller ever returns lean to zero, so the out-in-out exit that fig 8.1's green line (and every other figure) requires is asserted rather than derivable. The solved plan is exactly four actions; turn_in commits a lean target with no specified lifetime; lean_deg is constrained to (0,90) so a second turn_in cannot target upright; position actions overlapping a turn_in are rejected; and roll-on only widens the arc (kappa falls as v² grows) — it never stops the yaw. At ~28° lean and 9 m/s, psi_dot = G·tanφ/v ≈ 33°/s, so on book90's 16 m exit straight the 'clean' line's heading diverges ~60° and crosses the lane edge — self-verification can never return clean, and the scene bake for fig 8.1 fails or renders the ideal line non-green. The same hole makes bookEsses unrideable: turn_in has no direction/sign field, so alternating-hand corners cannot even be commanded.
findings.evidence: 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §6.1: turn_in `target: "tangent_inside" | {lean_deg ∈ (0, 90)}` (closed action set brake/turn_in/throttle/position; no straighten, no sign, no lifetime); same §: position overlapping turn_in rejected `INEFFECTUAL, position_overlaps_turn_in`. 04-solver-and-authoring.md §4.2: "The solved plan is the canonical four actions — brake…, deferred tangent_inside turn-in, maintenance crack, drive roll-on". 02-physics-model.md §2: `psi_dot = G·tan(phi)/v`, `phi_dot = clamp(roll_cmd …)` with roll_cmd tracking target_lean set only by the plan; §2 claims only "rolling on widens" — widening ≠ straightening. 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §4.1 defines exit as "heading has returned to the road's exit heading", and §4.2 quotes the book's mechanism ("countersteer out of it") that D3 explicitly cut with no replacement.
findings.improvement: Specify the missing semantic explicitly: give turn_in a defined lifetime (e.g. 'a turn_in's lean commitment ends at the corner's geometric end or at the next steering action, after which target_lean = 0 under the profile roll rate'), or add a signed/zero-capable steering target plus a per-corner sign-inference rule for chained corners. State it in 02 §3 (controller), 03 §6.1 (action semantics), and 04 §4.2 (solved-plan shape), and add a golden asserting the C30 exit straightens.

findings.title: The oncoming vehicle of fig 8.1 cannot be placed on the road
findings.claim: Fig 8.1's payoff prop — an SUV in the oncoming lane that the delayed sight line reveals — is inexpressible. The occluder vocabulary advertises `vehicle` as "(parked or oncoming-lane vehicle)", but the shared placement grammar defines lateral position only for band kinds as margins measured OUTWARD from the road edge, and gives the vehicle rectangle no lateral placement rule at all: no lane selector, no f/d coordinate, no negative-margin semantics. As designed, a vehicle can only be conjured beside the road on the grass (or not at all — the implementer must invent semantics, exactly the guessing D8 exists to abolish). Tellingly, 01 §6 lists the vehicle among what the book figure encodes and then silently drops it from linelab's own "equivalent" composition.
findings.evidence: 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §4: vehicle = "discrete rectangle (parked or oncoming-lane vehicle)", defaults "1.8 × 4.5 m" only; hedge/wall/bank defined "from margin_m outside the edge, extending depth_m further out"; placement grammar = side + station anchor + span, nothing lateral for on-road placement. 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §6: "dashed sight lines from each turn point, an obstruction (the bush), and an oncoming vehicle. The equivalent linelab figure is a one-scene composition: occluder + two lines + per-line sight rays" — the vehicle vanishes from the equivalence claim while G7 (01 §2) promises figure parity.
findings.improvement: Give `vehicle` an explicit lateral placement field — e.g. `lane=own|oncoming` or `f=<value>` (with f>1 meaning the oncoming lane, consistent with the corridor algebra) — resolving through the same sideSign/anchor machinery; state that an on-road vehicle both blocks sight (its footprint intersects eye→centreline rays, so the green line's limit point lands at the vehicle, matching the book's teaching) and is drawn with the rounded-rectangle glyph on the carriageway.

findings.title: book90/bookBlind and recipe (e) produce a mirror image of fig 8.1
findings.claim: Fig 8.1 is a LEFT-hander: apexes touch the yellow centreline, the premature line runs wide off the OUTER road edge, and the oncoming lane is the inside of the curve. `book90` expands to `R 12 ^90` — a right-hander — and recipe (e) presents it as producing "a figure equivalent to the book's Fig 8.1". On the right-hander every doctrinally salient placement mirrors: the apex sits against the road edge (not the centreline), and running wide crosses the centreline INTO the oncoming lane (a different, un-book lesson) rather than off-road. There is no hand parameter on presets, and preset expansions are only disclosed in results ("the resolved DSL appears verbatim in every result"), not promised at the schema surface — so a cold-start agent (08 §2 bar) discovers the mirroring only after rendering. The vision judge, applying the parity bar, could legitimately fail the shipped fig 8.1 example scene.
findings.evidence: 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §3.1: `book90` = `lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16`, "(figs 8.1–8.3 archetype)"; `bookBlind` = "book90 geometry + hedge". 08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §6(e): "the scene text names the book90 road preset… Expect: a figure equivalent to the book's Fig 8.1". 06-rendering-and-projection.md §7 parity requirement: "must read as an equivalent of the book's figure". Book image fig-08.01: left-hand bend, apex rings on the double-yellow, red line exiting toward the outer white edge.
findings.improvement: Flip the fig-8.1-facing presets to left-hand (`L 12 ^90`), or add a `hand=left|right` preset parameter, and state each preset's handedness and full expansion in the `schema road-dsl` output so cold-start agents see it; amend recipe (e) to name the handed variant.

findings.title: Runoff lines never terminate: the red line's drawn endpoint is meaningless
findings.claim: Lateral departure from the road is not a termination condition — 02 §7's precedence is crash → stopped → road/corner end → runaway guards, and no off-road event exists — so the early_apex line, after crossing the edge, keeps integrating on grass at the default mu = 1.0 (dry asphalt; muAt(s,d) off-road is unspecified) until the road-end station or a guard fires. The rendered red trajectory therefore ploughs through the grass (and potentially through the hedge glyph) for the rest of the road, its arrowhead landing wherever the road spec happened to end — a plausible-looking but physically meaningless tail, precisely the "wrong-but-plausible picture" the placard policy forbids, and visibly unlike the book's red arrow that ends at the road edge. Where the diagram window crops it is also undefined, since the auto window is built from turn_in/exit events without saying which line's, and a runoff line has no exit event.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §7: "Termination precedence per step: crash → stopped (v < v_floor) → road/corner end → runaway guards" — no lateral condition; §4: "mu_default = 1.0" with muAt patches only from hazards. 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §8 placard policy: "A wrong-but-plausible picture a student could believe is strictly worse than an honest 'not modelled'". 06-rendering-and-projection.md §2.4: `window.from = first(turn_in, brake_start) − …`, `window.to = exit + …` with no owning-line rule; 05 §5 lists `run_wide_detect` as an event but nothing terminal.
findings.improvement: Add a typed terminal event `off_road` (bike's lateral offset beyond road edge + margin for more than a bracketed crossing) to the termination precedence, with the event carrying the exact edge-crossing coordinates so the drawn line ends at the departure point plus a short specified overshoot; specify off-road mu (or make continuing off-road an explicit refusal); define the multi-line auto window as the union over lines using each line's terminal event when exit is absent.

findings.title: Mistake-role short dash collides with the dashed sight-ray device
findings.claim: Under colour law v2 the red early_apex TRAJECTORY renders short-dashed (role channel) while its SIGHT RAY renders dashed in the same red at reduced opacity — two dashed red curves radiating from the same turn point. The book's visual grammar is the opposite: trajectories are solid, only sight lines are dashed. In the one figure this design most explicitly targets (recipe (e), G7), a reader can mistake the red path for a sight ray or vice versa, and the exported figure fails the parity bar's "same annotation devices" reading even though every individual rule was followed.
findings.evidence: 06-rendering-and-projection.md §5.2: "mistake → short dash"; §3.1 item 7: "Sight rays — dashed rays from the eye position to the limit point … drawn in the owning line's verdict colour at reduced opacity"; §7 parity requirement: "same annotation devices (sight rays, turn points, apexes)". Book image fig-08.01: both trajectories solid; only sight lines dashed.
findings.improvement: Reserve dash for non-trajectory ink: render all trajectories solid and carry role through stroke weight + legend + marker shape (the accessibility redundancy 06 §5.2 wants), or give sight rays a visually distinct treatment (e.g. dot-dash plus a divergent arrow glyph) and property-test that no line style is shared between a trajectory and any annotation stroke.

findings.title: Labels cannot anchor to a specific line; the mistake line's apex is unlabelable first-try
findings.claim: Fig 8.1 labels both lines' features ("premature turn point", "early apex", "delayed turn point", "delayed apex"). Scene labels are corner-relative road-station anchors, and the `apex:<id>` sugar is defined to resolve "against the good line's solved apex" only — there is no `apex-of-line` or `turn_in-of-line` anchor, so labelling the red line's early apex requires running the bake, reading the emergent apex station off the result, and hand-writing `mid:c1 -4` offsets — a two-pass workflow that defeats the first-try cold-start bar for this figure, and the leader line targets a road station, not the intended line, so on two nearby lines the callout is ambiguous.
findings.evidence: 04-solver-and-authoring.md §7: "apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's *solved* apex"; 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §8: labels are "corner-relative callouts… a callout always resolves onto the road, never into empty space". Book image fig-08.01: four per-line feature labels with leader arrows.
findings.improvement: Extend the label anchor grammar with line-qualified emergent anchors resolved post-run, e.g. `apex@<lineName>:c1` and `turn_in@<lineName>:c1`, and have the renderer attach the leader to that line's projected point (P-PROJ-MARKER already guarantees on-line landing for markers; reuse it for leaders).

findings.title: Occluder token grammar is internally inconsistent across its three appearances
findings.claim: The placement grammar says the station anchor is `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset`, but the worked token and the bookBlind preset use a bare corner id (`hedge inside c1 -6x26`) that the grammar does not define (entry? mid?), and 08's recipe (c) writes `--occluder "hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30"` — an anchor-embedded offset (−25) AND a leading `<offset>` (−1.0) whose meaning is then unassigned. A cold-start agent reading `schema occluders` cannot determine what the number before the `x` means, and the bush placement for fig 8.1 becomes a guess.
findings.evidence: 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §4: "a station anchor (corner-relative `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`…)" vs token example "`hedge inside c1 -6x26`"; §3.1 bookBlind: "`hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2 depth=2.5`"; 08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §6(c): "`--occluder "hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30"`".
findings.improvement: Pick one canonical token shape — `<kind> <side> <anchor><±off>x<span> [key=val…]` with a mandatory `entry|exit|mid:` prefix — define bare `<cornerId>` as sugar for `mid:` (or reject it), regenerate all examples/presets to conform, and add a round-trip lint example to `schema occluders`.

findings.title: explain(kind) is required by 01/03 but not accepted by 08's explain verb
findings.claim: 01 §4.3 requires "every input surface that lists mistake kinds (`schema`, `explain`)" to state each kind's outcome and book mapping, and 03 §7.1 says "`explain(kind)` must state each kind's pinned outcome and book figure" — but 08 defines `explain` to accept only `<envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>`. In my session `linelab explain early_apex` is a schema-invalid invocation; the naming-trap teaching survives only because `schema mistakes` also carries it, but the docs disagree about the surface.
findings.evidence: 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §4.3: "Every input surface that lists mistake kinds (`schema`, `explain`) must state each kind's canonical outcome class"; 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §7.1: "`explain(kind)` must state…"; 08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §3 verb table: "`explain <envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>`".
findings.improvement: Add mistake kinds (and plan-action types) to explain's accepted argument set in 08 §3/§5.2, or amend 01/03 to route kind-teaching exclusively through `schema mistakes`.

findings.title: early_apex outcome pin disagrees between 01 and 03, and the oracle needs one class
findings.claim: 01 §4.3's table gives early_apex the emergent outcome "`wide`/`runoff`" while 03 §7.1 pins it to "`runoff` (runs wide)", and 09 §4's oracle asserts "the outcome class matches the pinned table" — singular. An implementer must guess which table is the pinned one, and whether a `wide` result (feasible corrective exists) is a red suite or a pass; the distinction also decides the line's colour only loosely (both map to red), but the oracle's iron rule ("never fixed by editing the expectation") makes the ambiguity a future fight.
findings.evidence: 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §4.3 table: early_apex → "`wide`/`runoff`"; 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §7.1 table: early_apex → "`runoff` (runs wide)"; 09-verification-and-testing.md §4: "the outcome class matches the pinned table… a mismatch is… never fixed by editing the expectation".
findings.improvement: Declare 03 §7.1 the single normative pin table, and make each pin either one class or an explicit accepted set (`{wide, runoff}`), with 01's table cross-referencing rather than restating.

findings.title: 'Designated eye sample' for occluded-region shading is designated nowhere
findings.claim: The occluded-region wash — the grey area beyond the limit point that shows "what the rider cannot see" — is drawn "for the figure's designated eye sample", but no grammar designates it: ViewSpec carries only mode/window/compression fields, and the scene `view:` line speaks that vocabulary. On the two-line fig 8.1 the red and green turn-ins have different limit points; which one greys the road is an implementer guess, and the choice changes the figure's teaching (the wash from the premature eye dramatizes the mistake; from the delayed eye it doesn't).
findings.evidence: 06-rendering-and-projection.md §3.1 item 6: "for the figure's designated eye sample, the road area beyond the limit point is washed…"; §2.1 ViewSpec = {mode, window, width_exag, straight_compress, taper_compress} — no eye field; 04 §7 `view:` "vocabulary owned by 06".
findings.improvement: Add `eye=<lineName>[@<event|station>]` to ViewSpec/`view:` with a stated default (e.g. the first ride line at its turn_in event) and record the designation in the export manifest.

findings.title: Scene doc contradicts itself on the one-ride-line rule
findings.claim: 04 §7's mistake bullet says mistakes compile "against the figure's first `ride` line (exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against)", yet the format example ten lines above shows two `ride` entries (`good:` and `wide: ride … role=alternative`), and recipe R3 requires two ride lines in one blind-corner figure. An implementer cannot tell whether a second ride line is a validation error.
findings.evidence: 04-solver-and-authoring.md §7: example block with `good: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto` and `wide: ride entry=34 vis=cautious role=alternative` vs the bullet "(exactly one `ride` line is required…)"; §8 R3 composes two solved ride lines on one road.
findings.improvement: Reword to "at least one ride line; the FIRST is the mistake-compile reference", matching the example and R3.

findings.title: Preset true-mode proportions and auto width_exag edge cases contradict their own gates
findings.claim: book90's true-scale straight share is (12+16)/(28+18.85) ≈ 0.60, above the ≤ 0.45 gate band, while 09 §5.3 requires each preset in TRUE mode to "already land near the proportion bands"; and the auto width_exag rule ("pick the smallest factor such that … ≥ 0.55") literally evaluates to 0.943 (< 1) for book90's 7 m/R12 = 0.583, silently narrowing the drawn road, since no ≥ 1 floor is stated. Window clamping when `turn_in − 15 m` precedes road start or `exit + 25 m` overruns road end is likewise unspecified (06 §2.6 types only empty/inverted windows). None of these blocks the figure, but each is a guess an implementer must make and a gate that may misfire on the shipped fig 8.1 scene.
findings.evidence: 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §3.1: book90 = S 12 + R12^90 (arc ≈ 18.85 m) + S 16; 06-rendering-and-projection.md §6.1: `straight_share ≤ 0.45`; §2.3: "pick the smallest factor such that (road_width × width_exag)/R ≥ 0.55", clamp stated only at the max (12); §2.4 window formulas without boundary clamps; 09-verification-and-testing.md §5.3: presets in true mode "must already land near the proportion bands".
findings.improvement: Add `width_exag ≥ 1` and window clamp-to-road rules to 06 §2.3/§2.4; either relax 09 §5.3 to name which metrics presets must meet in true mode or shorten book90's straights (e.g. S 8 / S 10) so the claim holds arithmetically.

wins: The premature/early_apex naming trap is defused at every surface an agent actually touches: 01 §4.3's explicit resolution, 03 §7.1's per-kind pin-and-book-mapping table, 08 §5.1's schema teaching table, and recipe (e)'s inline warning — in the simulated session I picked `early_apex` for the book's red 'premature turn point' line on the first try.

Sight rays default to exactly the book's anchor: 06 §3.1 item 7 draws one dashed ray per line from its turn_in event to its limit point — fig 8.1's central device (two sight lines from the two turn points, the delayed one seeing deeper past the bush) falls out of the default with zero authoring.
The carried marker vocabulary (hourglass = turn point, ring = apex) matches the book's own fig 8.1 glyphs almost exactly — the red/green bowtie turn-point markers and apex circles need no adaptation.

Colour law v2 yields the book's colours honestly: the solved delayed line goes green because its verdict is clean and the early_apex line goes red because the engine emits runoff — no painted roles, and a mis-picked `premature` (contained → amber) would visibly tell the author they chose the wrong kind instead of silently lying.

The book-proportion arithmetic of the presets genuinely works: 7 m road / R12 = 0.583 sits inside the measured 0.55–0.9 band at true scale, so the diagram projection is a mild correction for this figure, exactly as 09 §5.3 intends.

The hand-independent lane fraction `f` plus the hand-resolved `inside/outside` occluder sides mean my handedness fix was a single token (R→L) in the DSL with every other scene line unchanged — the abstraction did its job once I bypassed the preset.

Failed-line first-class citizenship (D6/D7) delivers real value for this figure: the red line carries the full sample contract including per-sample `sight_m`/`ssd_m`, so the book's qualitative claim ('turning early restricts your ability to see') becomes a quantified per-station comparison readable via stateAt without re-running anything.

The `scene --check` lint and the typed, schema_ref-carrying error discipline (08 §2) made the simulated authoring loop tight: every dead end I hit was at least designed to fail loudly with a named path rather than bake a wrong figure silently.

verdicts.title: No lean-unwind: the specified action vocabulary cannot produce any exit
verdicts.note: Checked all ten docs: no mechanism returns target_lean to zero. 03 §6.1 pins the closed action set with turn_in target "tangent_inside" | {lean_deg ∈ (0, 90)} (no straighten, no sign, no lifetime) and rejects position overlapping turn_in (INEFFECTUAL); 04 §4.2: "The solved plan is the canonical four actions"; 02 §2's psi_dot = G·tan(phi)/v stays positive at any lean and roll-on only slows rotation (heading grows log-divergently), so the exit-straight stabilization every figure shows is underivable — 01 §4.1's exit event (heading match) fires mid-lean and the line then diverges off the lane, so self-verify cannot return clean. 02's stand-up term acts only under hard decel; 05's events and 07's viewer add nothing. Two blemishes that do not defeat the claim: "countersteer out of it" appears in the book text (part0014 line 69), not in 01 §4.2 as the evidence says; and the esses sign could plausibly be inferred from corner hand, though no doc specifies that resolution.

verdicts.title: The oncoming vehicle of fig 8.1 cannot be placed on the road
verdicts.note: 03 §4 defines lateral placement only for band kinds ("from margin_m outside the edge, extending depth_m further out"); the vehicle row carries only "discrete rectangle (parked or oncoming-lane vehicle)" and "1.8 × 4.5 m" — no lane selector, no d/f coordinate, no negative-margin semantics, so the advertised oncoming-lane configuration is inexpressible. 07 §5.3 adds only presentation height; 08's --occluder defers to 03. And 01 §6 does drop the vehicle: "an obstruction (the bush), and an oncoming vehicle. The equivalent linelab figure is a one-scene composition: occluder + two lines + per-line sight rays" — one occluder, no vehicle, while G7 promises figure parity.

verdicts.title: book90/bookBlind and recipe (e) produce a mirror image of fig 8.1
verdicts.note: The book image confirms fig 8.1 is a left-hander (apex rings on the double-yellow centreline, oncoming SUV on the inside lane, red line exiting toward the outer white edge); 03 §3.1's book90 = "lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16" is a right-hander, so under the lane-constrained default the apex sits at the road edge and running wide crosses INTO the oncoming lane — mirrored doctrine-salient placements. No hand parameter exists on presets, and expansion disclosure is results-only ("the resolved DSL appears verbatim in every result"). 08 §6(e) claims "a figure equivalent to the book's Fig 8.1" against 06 §7's parity bar. Only the closing clause (vision judge "could legitimately fail" it) is speculative — the parity bar does not name hand explicitly — but the mirroring itself is doc- and image-verified.

verdicts.title: Runoff lines never terminate: the red line's drawn endpoint is meaningless
verdicts.note: The nucleus survives: 02 §7's termination precedence ("crash → stopped (v < v_floor) → road/corner end → runaway guards") has no lateral-departure condition, off-road muAt is unspecified (mu_default 1.0), and 06 §2.4's auto window names no owning line. But the categorical "never terminate" half is defeated by 05 §4 — "A query beyond a line's early termination (crash, run-off) is BAD_RANGE" — and 07 §3.4 — "A line that ends early (crash, road-end/run-off, stop) freezes at its terminal sample" — which show the design intends run-off as an early termination. The real defect is an internal inconsistency (02, the termination owner, omits what 05/07 assume), not a specified plough-through-grass tail with a meaningless arrowhead.

verdicts.title: Mistake-role short dash collides with the dashed sight-ray device
verdicts.note: Both premises verified verbatim: 06 §5.2 "mistake → short dash" and §3.1 item 7 sight rays "dashed rays … drawn in the owning line's verdict colour at reduced opacity" — two dashed red curves from the same turn point in recipe (e)'s figure. The book image shows the opposite grammar: both trajectories solid, only sight lines dashed. No doc resolves the collision (reduced opacity is the only distinguishing channel, and ray dash pattern vs 'short dash' is unspecified), and 06 §7's parity bar requires "same annotation devices".

verdicts.title: Labels cannot anchor to a specific line; the mistake line's apex is unlabelable first-try
verdicts.note: 04 §7: label anchors are "corner-relative only" with "apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's *solved* apex" — no per-line anchor exists anywhere (03 §8's callouts "always resolve onto the road"; marks: all draws markers but no named callouts; mistake-line label= is legend text only). Labelling the red line's emergent early apex therefore requires reading the baked result and hand-writing station offsets — a two-pass workflow against the fig 8.1 figure whose image shows four per-line feature labels, and a road-station leader is ambiguous between nearby lines.

verdicts.title: Occluder token grammar is internally inconsistent across its three appearances
verdicts.note: All three appearances verified: 03 §4's grammar defines the anchor as "entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m" yet its own worked token and 03 §3.1's bookBlind use bare "c1" ("hedge inside c1 -6x26"), which the grammar never defines (entry? mid? s0?); 08 §6(c)'s "hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30" carries both an anchor-embedded −25 and a leading −1.0 whose slot meaning is then unassigned. A cold-start agent cannot determine the pre-x number's semantics from schema occluders.

verdicts.title: explain(kind) is required by 01/03 but not accepted by 08's explain verb
verdicts.note: 01 §4.3: "Every input surface that lists mistake kinds (`schema`, `explain`) must state each kind's canonical outcome class"; 03 §7.1: "explain(kind) must state each kind's pinned outcome and book figure"; but 08 §3/§5.2 define explain to accept only <envelope.json | checkId | errorCode> — mistake kinds are neither check ids nor error codes, so `linelab explain early_apex` is schema-invalid. The docs genuinely disagree about the surface; only `schema mistakes` carries the naming-trap teaching, exactly as the finding says.

verdicts.title: early_apex outcome pin disagrees between 01 and 03, and the oracle needs one class
verdicts.note: 01 §4.3's table gives early_apex "wide/runoff" while 03 §7.1 pins "runoff (runs wide)" (04 R2 and 08 §6(b) side with runoff), and 09 §4 asserts "the outcome class matches the pinned table" — singular, with the iron rule "never fixed by editing the expectation". Ownership arguably designates 03 as the pinned table (03 §7.1 says "pinned to by test"), which softens the guessing claim slightly, but the two tables state materially different pins: an engine yielding `wide` passes 01's expectation and fails 03's.

verdicts.title: 'Designated eye sample' for occluded-region shading is designated nowhere
verdicts.note: 06 §3.1 item 6 washes the road "for the figure's designated eye sample", but no grammar designates one: 06 §2.1's ViewSpec = {mode, window, width_exag, straight_compress, taper_compress}, 04 §7's view: line speaks that vocabulary, and 03 §8's Figure carries only labels/marks/view/note. Sight rays (item 7) get a per-line default (each line's turn_in), but the single wash eye has none — on the two-line fig 8.1 the choice between the red and green turn-in changes the teaching, and it is left to the implementer.

verdicts.title: Scene doc contradicts itself on the one-ride-line rule
verdicts.note: The textual conflict is real — 04 §7's mistake bullet says "(exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against)" while the format example ten lines up shows two ride entries and §8 R3 needs two — but the claim that "an implementer cannot tell whether a second ride line is a validation error" is defeated by the same section: the role-default rule explicitly handles "subsequent `ride` → `alternative`" and 04 §7 states "No count caps and no exclusivity rules — D9 removed the prior one-amber-slot…", so multiple ride lines are unambiguously legal and the parenthetical is sloppy wording for 'at least one'. The wording defect survives; the implementer-blocking scope does not.

verdicts.title: Preset true-mode proportions and auto width_exag edge cases contradict their own gates
verdicts.note: All three sub-claims check out arithmetically and textually: book90 true-scale straight share = (12+16)/(12+16+18.85) ≈ 0.60, above 06 §6.1's ≤ 0.45 band, while 09 §5.3 requires presets in true mode to "already land near the proportion bands"; 06 §2.3's "pick the smallest factor such that (road_width × width_exag)/R ≥ 0.55" yields 0.55/(7/12) ≈ 0.943 for book90 with only a max clamp (≤ 12) stated, so the literal rule narrows the drawn road; and 06 §2.6 types only empty/inverted windows, leaving the turn_in − 15 m before-road-start and exit + 25 m past-road-end cases unclamped. Correctly rated polish: implementer guesses and gate misfires, nothing figure-blocking.

result.walkthrough:
FIGURE INVENTORY (viewed fig-08.02__slow-steering.jpeg): a 90-degree LEFT-hander; two-lane road with double-yellow centerline and white edge lines on grass; rider in the outer (right-traffic) lane, entering from the bottom along the outer white edge. Exactly ONE red/white hourglass on the outer edge where the straight meets the arc, callout "turn point". Both lines depart that single point: the red "slow-steer line" stays wide, drifts to the outer edge through the exit and its arrowhead terminates on-pavement pointing at a dark dirt/gravel patch straddling the outer road edge; the green "quick-steer line" arcs tighter and exits mid-lane near the double yellow. Three leader-line callouts, arrowheads on both lines, no sight rays, no apex ring, no exit dot. Ch.8 text: slow steering = same turn point, roll-in too slow; "You risk going off the edge of the road at the exit."

COLD START (08 §2 bar: schema+explain only). Step 1: `linelab schema mistakes` — the teaching table gives slow_steer: roll_rate_factor=0.3, pinned outcome runoff/roll-rate-limited, book mapping fig 8.2 (03 §7.1). It ALSO prints early_apex mapped to "Fig 8.1/8.2's red line" (08 §5.1, 01 §4.3) — two kinds claim my target figure; only the "Slow Steering" name disambiguates, and early_apex would move the turn point, contradicting the figure's single shared marker. I pick slow_steer. Step 2: `linelab schema scene`, `schema road-dsl`. The book90 preset is a RIGHT-hander (`R 12 ^90`) but the figure is a left-hander, so I author the mirror by hand.

SCENE AUTHORED (fig-08-02.scene):
  road:    lane 3.5 | S 12 | L 12 ^90 | S 16
  lines:
    quick: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto label="quick-steer line"
    slow:  mistake slow_steer label="slow-steer line"
  hazards: gravel outside exit:c1 -2x4 mu=0.4
  marks:   auto
  labels:
    entry:c1-2  "turn point"
  view:    mode=diagram window=auto
  note:    "Figure 8.2 — Slow Steering"
GUESS LOG while writing it: (a) hazard station ref — 03 §4's grammar says anchors are `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId>` but every worked token (`hedge inside c1 -6x26`, 03 §3.1/04 §7) uses bare `c1`; I guessed `exit:c1` works. (b) There is no turn-point label anchor — the turn-in station is solve-emergent and only `apex:` gets post-solve sugar (04 §7), so I anchored "turn point" at entry:c1-2 and hoped the leader lands near the hourglass. (c) Whether `label=` is legal on a `mistake` entry is unstated (04 §7 shows it only on `ride`). (d) Which lane is "the rider's own lane" (03 §2) is never stated; fig 8.2 needs right-hand traffic. (e) Where the gravel d-band actually sits laterally (and whether it may straddle the road edge like the book's patch) is undefined — gravel has only `width 1.4`, unlike occluders' margin/depth semantics.

RUN: `linelab scene fig-08-02.scene --check` → exit 0 (the lint verb is a genuine win). `linelab scene fig-08-02.scene --out out/` → per 04: solve({road, entry 34}) feasibility-probes, bisects decel to apex lean ≈28° (0.70×reserve) and roll-on to exit f=0.85, self-verifies clean → GREEN. compileMistake(slow_steer): same plan, roll rate 50→15 deg/s — turn-in STATION is untouched (the perturbation is not placement), so the shared turn point is preserved by construction. But tracing the causal chain through 02: the compiled artifact has no legal wire form (rider.profile is a closed enum with fixed roll_rate_dps; no plan action and no schema field carries a roll rate), and the plan diff R2 promises ("exactly one changed control") is EMPTY for this kind. Physics: on R12 at ~9.4 m/s the road demands ~45 deg/s of heading rate over a 2 s arc; rolling at 15 deg/s from a start at f=1.0 (default outside edge, 0.4 m outboard margin) accumulates ~1.5 m of outboard drift within the first second — the red line leaves the pavement roughly a third of the way around the corner, not at the exit as the book draws. Then nothing in 02 §7 terminates a runoff (precedence is crash/stopped/road-end/runaway only), so the red line keeps integrating through the grass (mu off-road undefined) until station reaches road end — its arrowhead lands in the grass, nowhere near the book's on-pavement termination at the hazard. The gravel patch I placed for book-parity is physics-active: at exit-f 0.85 the SOLVED GREEN line is driven toward the outside where the patch sits, and mu 0.4 (phiMax 21.8°) could flip the ideal line's verdict — the book's decorative prop is not expressible as decoration.

RENDER/GATES: crop window turn_in−15 to exit+25 covers nearly the whole 47 m road; straights compress ×5 → straight_share ≈0.23 (≤0.45 ✓); width_ratio 7/12 ≈0.58 in band 0.45–0.95 with width_exag≈1 (the book-proportioned geometry needs almost no projection, exactly as 09 §5.3 promises); colours emerge correctly (clean→green, runoff→red per 06 §5.1) matching the book with no painting. `marks: auto` yields exactly one hourglass (good line only — no duplicate at the shared point) but also a ring and dot the book figure lacks, with no vocabulary to suppress them; `all` would stack a second hourglass at the identical station with no dedup rule. Remaining visible deltas vs the book: green exits at f 0.85 (near the outer edge, close to where the book puts the FAILING line) instead of the book's tight mid-lane exit — fixable only via a D10 constraint (`f<=0.5@exit:c1`) no fig-8.2 mapping mentions; the coincident approach renders green (ideal drawn on top, 06 §3.1) where the book draws it red; the red line's shape and endpoint are qualitatively wrong per the physics trace above. G7 "equivalent figure" survives on vocabulary (markers, arrows, lane markings, stippled patch, red/green law) but the red line's geometry — the entire lesson of the figure — is not credibly reproduced by the specified defaults on the recommended road scale.

findings.title: Slow-steer roll rate has no schema home; one-perturbation claims false for this kind
findings.claim: compileMistake(slow_steer) perturbs roll rate ×0.3, but roll rate lives nowhere an input can express: the wire schema's rider block is `{profile, start, plan}` with profile a closed enum mapping to fixed roll_rate_dps, and no plan action carries a roll-rate field. The compiled mistake (street ×0.3 = 15 deg/s) is therefore not representable as an explicit-plan scenario, contradicting 'same validation, same engine, no privileged path' and 'anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON'; and the design's own claims that a mistake is 'the solved good line's own plan with exactly one control perturbed' and that 'diff of the two plans shows exactly one changed control' are both false for slow_steer — its plan diff is empty and the delta lives in an unspecified location an implementer must invent.
findings.evidence: 03 §6 rider schema: `rider: { profile, start: {speed_kmh, f? | d?}, plan: [PlanAction…] }`, `rider.profile ∈ casual | street | trained | racer`; 02 §3 profile table fixes roll_rate_dps per profile; 03 §6.1 plan-action table has no roll-rate field; 03 §7 'the solved good line's own plan with exactly one control perturbed'; 03 §7.1 `slow_steer | roll rate × roll_rate_factor = 0.3`; 04 §2(c) 'Same validation, same engine, no privileged path'; 04 §8 R2 'diff of the two plans shows exactly one changed control'; 08 §4.1 'flags are sugar, not a second schema'.
findings.improvement: Add an effectual, schema-valid `rider.roll_rate_dps` override field (profile supplies the default) that compileMistake(slow_steer) writes into the compiled scenario; restate the one-perturbation invariant as 'exactly one field of the compiled scenario differs' and fix R2's plan-diff claim to a spec-diff claim.

findings.title: Runoff never terminates the run — the red line's endpoint is undefined and lands in the grass
findings.claim: The book figure's red line terminates on-pavement at the outer edge, arrowhead pointing at the exit hazard. In linelab, leaving the road is a classification (`runoff`) but not a terminator: the per-step precedence is crash → stopped → road/corner end → runaway, so a slow-steer trajectory that departs the pavement keeps integrating across the grass (with off-road mu, lane-fraction semantics, and station projection all unspecified) until station reaches road end or a guard fires. Where the drawn red teaching line ends — the exact device the book uses to point at the consequence — is therefore an implementer guess, and the natural reading produces an arrowhead wandering in the grass, visibly unlike fig 8.2.
findings.evidence: 02 §7 'Termination precedence per step: crash → stopped (v < v_floor_ms) → road/corner end → runaway guards' — no lane/road-departure terminator; 02 §7 outcome list defines `runoff` as 'left the road/lane and no feasible corrective returns it' (a verdict, not a stop rule); 02 §4 `muAt(s, d)` defined only via road-model patches, silent off-road; 05 §2.1 `s` = 'Arc-length station along the road centreline' with no off-road projection rule; book ch.8 text: 'You risk going off the edge of the road at the exit'.
findings.improvement: Specify a runoff termination rule in 02 §7 (e.g., terminate with exact-crossing bracketing when the bike passes a stated distance beyond the road edge, recording the crossing as the trajectory's final sample) plus an explicit off-road mu policy, so the drawn failing line ends where the teaching needs it.

findings.title: On the recommended figure-scale road, slow_steer defaults leave the road mid-corner, not at the exit
findings.claim: The design asserts slow_steer maps to fig 8.2 but never checks that the emergent geometry resembles the figure. On book90-scale geometry (R12, ~34 km/h, ~2 s of arc, ~45 deg/s heading demand) a roll rate of 50×0.3 = 15 deg/s starting from the default f = 1.0 (the outside usable edge, ~0.4 m from pavement) accumulates well over a metre of outboard drift in the first second — the red line exits the pavement roughly a third of the way around the corner. The book draws the slow-steer line on the road the entire way, running out only at the exit; the pinned outcome class (`runoff`) still holds, so no test catches that the picture teaches 'instant runoff at turn-in' instead of the book's exit-runoff lesson. Compounding this, the mistake-oracle's base road is never named, so the pin may be blessed on C30 (R30, where the same defaults plausibly DO produce exit-area runoff) while figure recreation is steered to book90 — two different geometry regimes under one pin.
findings.evidence: 03 §7.1 `slow_steer | roll rate × roll_rate_factor = 0.3 | runoff / roll-rate-limited | fig 8.2`; 03 §3.1 book90 = `lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16`, 'canonical single 90° corner (figs 8.1–8.3 archetype)', suggested entry 34 km/h; 03 §6 `rider.start.f (default 1.0 — the outside usable edge)`; 02 §3 street roll_rate_dps = 50; 09 §4 pins only 'the outcome class matches the pinned table' with no base-road named and no geometry assertion; 06 §7 parity requires the export 'read as an equivalent of the book's figure'.
findings.improvement: Name the oracle's base road per kind, and pin a geometry expectation alongside the class (e.g., 'lane-departure station ≥ 60 % of corner sweep for slow_steer on its figure road'); define roll_rate_factor relative to the corner's required roll duration (or retune per figure road) so the compiled line reproduces the book's exit-runoff shape.

findings.title: Marker vocabulary cannot express the figure's marker set
findings.claim: Fig 8.2 carries exactly one hourglass and nothing else. `marks` accepts only `auto | all`: auto draws the good line's full marker set (hourglass + apex ring + exit dot — two markers the book figure lacks, on the wrong line for a figure whose featured object is the red line), and `all` draws per-line markers, stacking a second hourglass at the identical shared station with no coincident-marker rule. There is no way to request the turn-point marker alone, and no statement of what overlapping markers of different verdict colours render as.
findings.evidence: 03 §8 '`marks` (`auto | all`) controls turn-point/apex/exit markers'; 04 §7 'marks: auto | all # optional (default auto: good-line marks)'; 06 §3.1 item 9 'Markers — carried vocabulary: hourglass = turn point, ring = apex, dot = exit; each inherits its line's colour' — per line, no dedup rule.
findings.improvement: Extend `marks` to accept a marker-kind list (e.g., `marks: turn_in` or `marks: quick:turn_in`), and specify that coincident markers of identical kind and station collapse to one glyph (colour rule stated).

findings.title: Fig 8.2 is attributed to two mistake kinds — a cold-start selection trap
findings.claim: An agent recreating 'figure 8.2' from schema output alone reads early_apex mapped to 'Fig 8.1/8.2's red line' and slow_steer mapped to 'fig 8.2 — slow steering'. Two kinds claim the target figure. Picking early_apex moves the turn-in station — directly contradicting the actual figure, whose entire lesson is one shared turn point with a roll-rate error. The design prides itself on resolving the premature/early_apex naming trap at the API surface, then creates an adjacent trap for the very figure whose book caption says only 'Slow Steering'.
findings.evidence: 08 §5.1 '`early_apex` → "turned in too soon, runs wide" → Fig 8.1/8.2's red line'; 01 §4.3 early_apex row 'figs 8.1–8.2 teaching'; 03 §7.1 slow_steer row 'fig 8.2 — slow steering'; 03 §7.1 'explain(kind) must state each kind's … book figure so an agent picks the right kind … on the first try'; the viewed figure shows both lines sharing one hourglass.
findings.improvement: Reserve fig 8.2 to slow_steer in every teaching table (01 §4.3, 03 §7.1, 08 §5.1); describe early_apex as fig 8.1 only, with prose noting the shared-consequence relationship.

findings.title: No turn-point label anchor and no line-addressed callouts
findings.claim: The figure's three callouts point at the turn-point marker and at each of the two lines. Scene labels anchor only to road stations (`entry|exit|mid:<id>±m`) plus post-solve `apex:` sugar — the turn-in station, the doctrine's 'master decision' and the one thing every book figure labels, is solve-emergent with no anchor, forcing the author to guess a station offset; and a label cannot name WHICH line its leader points to where two lines occupy the anchored station, so 'slow-steer line' vs 'quick-steer line' callouts are unauthorable as drawn.
findings.evidence: 04 §7 'Label anchors are corner-relative only (`entry|exit|mid:<id>[±m]`, plus `apex:<id>` sugar resolved against the good line's solved apex' — no `turn_in:` sugar; 03 §8 'a callout always resolves onto the road, never into empty space' (road-anchored, not line-anchored); 01 §4.1 'the choice of a turning point — the master decision'; 06 §3.1 item 10 labels anchor to corner-relative stations only.
findings.improvement: Add `turn_in:<lineName>` post-solve label sugar (same mechanism as `apex:`) and an optional `line=<name>` qualifier that attaches a callout's leader to a named line's sample at the anchored station.

findings.title: The book's hazard prop is only expressible as physics, and gravel's lateral placement is unspecified
findings.claim: The dark patch at fig 8.2's exit is a consequence prop. linelab's only hazard is `gravel`, a mu override — placing it where the book draws it puts mu 0.4 (phiMax ≈ 21.8°) directly where the solved GREEN line is driven (exit target f = 0.85 approaches the outside), risking flipping the ideal line's verdict; the author cannot know without a run. Worse, gravel's lateral geometry is undefined: occluders get explicit `margin_m`/`depth_m` band semantics, but gravel gets only `width 1.4` with no statement of where the band sits relative to the named side or whether it may straddle the road edge as the book's patch does. Separately, the placement token examples use a bare corner ref (`gravel outside c1 +8x3`) while the placement grammar defines anchors as `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId>` — the meaning of bare `c1 ± offset` is a guess.
findings.evidence: 03 §4 hazards table: '`gravel` | mu override inside a d-band over a station span | width 1.4 m, mu 0.4' (no margin/offset semantics), vs the occluder rows' 'from margin_m outside the edge, extending depth_m further out'; 03 §4 placement grammar 'a station anchor (corner-relative `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`…)' vs the token examples `hedge inside c1 -6x26` (03 §3.1) and `gravel outside c1 +8x3` (04 §7); 04 §4.1 `exit_target 0.85`.
findings.improvement: Give gravel the same edge-anchored margin/offset placement semantics as occluders (explicitly allowing bands beyond the lane edge), define bare-`c1` refs (or remove them from every example), and state in G7's parity note that consequence props are physics-active by design — or add a declared annotation-layer prop.

findings.title: Default exit target puts the good line where the book puts the failing one
findings.claim: The solver always drives the ideal exit to f = 0.85 (out-in-OUT doctrine), but fig 8.2's green quick-steer line exits tight/mid-lane — the drawn contrast between 'more line options at the exit' (green, conservative) and 'forced to the outer edge' (red) is the figure's payload. A faithful recreation needs `f<=~0.5@exit:c1`, which D10 can express, but nothing in any fig 8.2 mapping (03 §7.1, 08 §5.1, 01 §4.3) mentions the override, so a cold-start recreation renders a green line hugging the outside at exit, muting the lesson.
findings.evidence: 04 §4.1 'exit lane fraction `exit.f = exit_target`' with 'exit_target 0.85 (driven out to the outside but contained)'; book fig 8.2 caption 'A quick steering input … allows for more line options at the exit'; viewed figure: green arrowhead mid-lane near the double yellow, red at the outer white line; 01 §2 G7 test 'the per-figure mapping … is covered by shipped example scenes' — no fig 8.2 scene content specified anywhere.
findings.improvement: Specify the shipped fig-08-02.scene (G7's own test artifact) including the exit f_max constraint on the ride line, and note in the mistakes teaching table that fig 8.2 parity requires it.

findings.title: Which lane is the rider's is never stated
findings.claim: The lane-constrained corridor is 'the rider's own lane', but no document states whether that is the right or left lane of the two-lane road — i.e., traffic handedness. The doctrine layer hides this behind hand-independent f, but the rendered figure does not: fig 8.2 parity requires the rider in the right (outer) lane of a left-hander, and every oncoming-lane relation (P3's 'oncoming-lane relations are preserved', vehicle occluders in the oncoming lane) depends on the same unstated convention.
findings.evidence: 03 §2 'the usable corridor is the rider's own lane inset by bike_margin_m' — no side stated; 03 §6 schema has no traffic-side field; 06 §2.5 P3 'inside/outside and oncoming-lane relations are preserved' presumes a defined oncoming lane; 01 §8 'flat, constant-width, two-lane roads'.
findings.improvement: State right-hand traffic as the v1 default in 03 §2 (rider's lane = right of centreline in the direction of travel), with the token position reserved for a future `traffic=left` flag.

findings.title: Coincident-approach overdraw inverts the book's entry colour
findings.claim: Up to the shared turn point the good and slow-steer trajectories are byte-identical (same plan prefix, same start), and role draw order puts ideal on top, so the shared approach renders green; the book draws the approach as the red line's tail (the featured error owns the entry). Combined with the frame-edge speed chip the book lacks, the recreated entry region reads slightly un-book-like.
findings.evidence: 06 §3.1 item 8 'Lines, in role order reference → alternative → mistake → ideal (ideal on top)'; 06 §2.4 'an inbound arrow with a speed chip ("braking from 82 km/h")'; viewed figure: the entry tail along the outer edge is red.
findings.improvement: Offer a per-figure draw-order override (or dash the coincident segment) so a featured mistake line can own visually shared segments; make the entry speed chip suppressible in `view:`.

wins: The one-perturbation rule genuinely preserves the shared turn point: slow_steer touches only roll rate, so the hourglass lands at the identical station for both lines with zero author effort — exactly fig 8.2's central device (03 §7, 03 §7.1).
Colour law v2 reproduces the book's palette from physics alone: clean → green for quick-steer, runoff → red for slow-steer, no hand-painting and no role coupling (06 §5.1, D9).

The `schema mistakes` teaching table (params, defaults, pinned Tier 1R outcome, book-figure mapping printed at the API surface) got the kind selection right on the first cold-start try — the design bar of 08 §2 mostly held (08 §5.1, 03 §7.1).
The diagnosis vocabulary contains exactly the right cause: `roll_rate_limited` is a closed-set member, so `explain` can narrate the figure's precise lesson off the envelope (05 §6.1).

A book-proportioned left-hander is one DSL line (`lane 3.5 | S 12 | L 12 ^90 | S 16`) and already sits inside every proportion-gate band at ~unity exaggeration — the projection is the promised gentle correction, not a rescue (03 §3, 06 §6.1, 09 §5.3).
Sight rays are correctly conditional on occluders, so the rayless fig 8.2 comes out rayless with no suppression flag needed (08 §6(e), 06 §3.1).
The scene ergonomics work: the whole figure fits in ~9 lines with a no-solve `--check` lint before the bake, close to the ≤6-line bar (04 §2(d), §7).

D10 constraints can express the book's tight green exit (`f<=0.5@exit:c1`) without ever authoring a path — the emergent-line invariant survives contact with a figure whose ideal line deviates from the solver default (04 §4.5).
Renderer vocabulary covers every prop the figure needs: centreline/edge markings, arrowheads inheriting line colour, stippled gravel patches, callout boxes with leaders (06 §3.1).

verdicts.title: Slow-steer roll rate has no schema home; one-perturbation claims false for this kind
verdicts.note: The schema-gap half survives and is the finding's core: 03 §6's rider block is `{profile, start, plan}` with profile a closed enum (20/50/65/85 deg/s — 15 deg/s matches none), 03 §6.1's plan actions carry no roll-rate field, and compileMistake's return shape `{kind, plan, roadSpec, outcome, diagnosis, label}` (03 §7) has no slot for the delta — yet 03 §8 requires 'Each line resolves to a full Scenario (§6)', which slow_steer cannot. The contradiction half is overstated: D6 shareability routes slow_steer through the mistake spec `{kind, params, scope}` (03 §7.3; 05 §7 `source: {kind: "mistake", mistakeSpec}`), which IS JSON — so 08 §4.1's 'anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON' holds via `--mistake` ↔ mistake-spec; 04 §2(c)'s 'no privileged path' describes the explicit-plan rung, not a promise every mistake reduces to one; and 04 §8's 'diff of the two plans shows exactly one changed control' is stated in R2, an early_apex recipe, not a per-kind universal.

verdicts.title: Runoff never terminates the run — the red line's endpoint is undefined and lands in the grass
verdicts.note: 02 §7's 'Termination precedence per step: crash → stopped (v < v_floor_ms) → road/corner end → runaway guards' contains no lateral-departure terminator, and 07 §3.1 states outright that ''run-off' is an *outcome* class, not an event'. 05 §4 and 07 §3.4 do list 'run-off' among early terminations, but no document defines the stop rule — deepening, not defeating, the finding (02, the reimplementable-alone physics contract, says integrate to road-end station). Off-road mu (02 §4 muAt defined only via hazard patches, so grass reads mu 1.0) and off-road station projection (05 §2.1) are unspecified as claimed. One parenthetical quibble: lane-fraction semantics off-road ARE specified ('>1 = beyond the corridor (oncoming lane or off-road)', 03 §2), but that does not rescue the endpoint.

verdicts.title: On the recommended figure-scale road, slow_steer defaults leave the road mid-corner, not at the exit
verdicts.note: The geometry nucleus is confirmed: at book90 (R12, solved corner speed ~28–34 km/h, ~2–2.4 s of arc, required lean ~28–37°) a 15 deg/s roll rate needs ~1.9–2.5 s just to reach target lean, accumulating >1 m outboard drift in the first second from f=1.0 with 0.4 m of margin — corridor departure in the corner's first half, where the book's red line stays on-road until the exit ('You risk going off the edge of the road at the exit'). And 09 §4's mistake oracle indeed names no base road. But 'no test catches that the picture teaches instant runoff' overstates scope: 06 §7's parity bar ('must read as an equivalent of the book's figure') and 09 §7's vision judge ('mistakes reading as the mistakes they teach') are the designed editorial catch for exactly this defect, with roll_rate_factor marked TUNING subject to that loop. What survives is that no MECHANICAL pin covers the geometry — only the outcome class.

verdicts.title: Marker vocabulary cannot express the figure's marker set
verdicts.note: The viewed figure carries exactly one hourglass, no ring, no dot. The entire marks vocabulary is `auto | all` (03 §8, 04 §7 'default auto: good-line marks'); `auto` draws the good line's turn/apex/exit set — two markers the book figure lacks, on the green line — and there is no `none`, no subset selection, and no per-kind toggle. Under `all`, slow_steer's unchanged plan puts both lines' turn_in at the identical station, stacking two hourglasses of different verdict colours; 06 §3.1 item 9 assigns each marker its line's colour with no coincident-marker rule anywhere in the doc set.

verdicts.title: Fig 8.2 is attributed to two mistake kinds — a cold-start selection trap
verdicts.note: Every mapping surface double-claims fig 8.2: 08 §5.1 'early_apex → …Fig 8.1/8.2's red line', 01 §4.3 early_apex 'figs 8.1–8.2 teaching', 00 §4 'the book's canonical Fig 8.1/8.2 error', versus 03 §7.1/01 §4.3 slow_steer 'fig 8.2 — slow steering'. The viewed figure shows both lines sharing one hourglass with the error being roll rate, so early_apex (which moves the turn-in station 5 m early) contradicts the figure's lesson. The design's own bar — explain(kind) states each kind's book figure 'so an agent picks the right kind…on the first try' (03 §7.1) — makes the overlap a genuine trap; no document assigns 8.2 exclusively to slow_steer.

verdicts.title: No turn-point label anchor and no line-addressed callouts
verdicts.note: 04 §7: 'Label anchors are corner-relative only (`entry|exit|mid:<id>[±m]`, plus `apex:<id>` sugar resolved against the good line's solved apex' — the post-solve-sugar pattern exists but turn_in got none, despite 01 §4.1 calling the turn point 'the master decision' and the solved turn-in being emergent (turnIn=auto default). Labels resolve onto the road (03 §8), and the label grammar (`anchor "text"`) carries no line reference, so 'slow-steer line' vs 'quick-steer line' callouts cannot name their target where two lines occupy the anchored station; per-line naming exists only as legend text (05 §7 `label`). 09 §5.1's P-PROJ-MARKER phrase 'lands on its line's projected image' even presumes line-attachment the authoring grammar cannot express.

verdicts.title: The book's hazard prop is only expressible as physics, and gravel's lateral placement is unspecified
verdicts.note: All three sub-claims verify. (1) Hazards are only `gravel` = mu 0.4 override (03 §4); the book's exit patch sits where the solved green line is driven (exit_target 0.85, 04 §4.1), so recreating the prop physically perturbs the ideal line's checks — and D8 forbids inert decorative inputs, so no non-physical prop can exist. (2) Occluders get explicit band semantics ('from margin_m outside the edge, extending depth_m further out') but gravel gets only 'width 1.4' with no statement of where the band sits relative to the named side or whether it may straddle the edge as the viewed patch does. (3) The placement grammar defines anchors as `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m` (03 §4) yet the token examples use bare `c1` (`hedge inside c1 -6x26`, `gravel outside c1 +8x3`) while 08 §6(c) uses the qualified `entry:c1-25` — bare-ref semantics are nowhere defined.

verdicts.title: Default exit target puts the good line where the book puts the failing one
verdicts.note: 04 §4.1 fixes the ideal exit at `exit_target 0.85` ('driven out to the outside but contained'); the viewed figure's green arrowhead is mid-lane by the double yellow while the red is at the outer white line, and the caption's payload is 'allows for more line options at the exit'. D10 can express the fix (04 §4.5's own example: 'f_max = 0.7 over the exit span clips exit_target down from 0.85'), but none of the fig 8.2 mappings (03 §7.1, 08 §5.1, 01 §4.3) mentions it and no fig 8.2 scene content is specified anywhere (G7 names the requirement, not the scene), so a cold-start recreation drives the green line to the outside at exit.

verdicts.title: Which lane is the rider's is never stated
verdicts.note: A grep across all ten docs finds no traffic-handedness statement: 03 §2 says only 'the rider's own lane', the 03 §6 schema has no side field, 00 §4's vocabulary is silent, and every oncoming-lane construct (06 §2.5 P3 'oncoming-lane relations are preserved', 03 §4's 'oncoming-lane vehicle', 05 §2.1 'f… >1 = oncoming') presumes a convention never written down. Hand-independent `f` hides it from doctrine but not from rendering: the viewed fig 8.2 places the rider in the outer (right) lane of a left-hander, and which pavement lies beyond f=1 (oncoming asphalt vs grass) changes every recreated figure.

verdicts.title: Coincident-approach overdraw inverts the book's entry colour
verdicts.note: slow_steer changes only the roll-rate cap (03 §7.1), so both trajectories are identical from start until turn-in; 06 §3.1 item 8 fixes draw order 'reference → alternative → mistake → ideal (ideal on top)' with the ideal solid and thickest (06 §5.2), so the thick green fully overdraws the thin short-dashed red on the shared approach — while the viewed figure's entry tail below the hourglass is red. One caveat on the garnish: the 06 §2.4 speed chip appears only when approach geometry is cropped out of the window, and book90's 12 m entry likely fits inside the 15 m window lead, so the chip may not even render there; the core overdraw claim stands regardless, at the stated polish severity.

result.walkthrough:
VIEWING THE BOOK FIGURE. Fig 8.3 is a ~90-degree LEFT-hander (rider enters bottom heading up, exits top-left), a two-lane road with double-yellow centreline and white edge lines on a grass field. Both lines stay in the rider's own (outer) lane. The RED fifty-pence line carries hourglass turn-point markers — I count SIX red circles in the raster (the brief said five; six actually matches the chapter's "increase your chances of making a mistake, by about 500 percent" = 6 inputs vs 1) — its FIRST marker sits at the very bottom, EARLIER than the green line's single marker (callout: "fifty pencing is almost always associated with premature initiation"), so red runs INSIDE green early, crosses it mid-corner, and exits wide near the outer edge line ("fifty-pencing line runs wide"). The GREEN line has exactly ONE hourglass, apexes near the double yellow, exits tight ("single-steer line exits tight"). Four callout boxes with leader arrows; "multiple turn points" has TWO leaders to two different red markers. No apex rings, no exit dots, no sight rays, no occluders; both lines solid with arrowheads. Measured off the raster, road-width:radius is ~0.57 — inside 06 §6.1's claimed band.

SIMULATED SESSION (cold start, 08 §2: schema+explain only). (1) `linelab schema mistakes` — the teaching table (08 §5.1) maps fifty_pence → wide/runoff → fig 8.3; correct kind on first try. (2) `linelab schema scene`, `schema road-dsl`. book90 is `R 12 ^90` — a right-hander — so I hand-mirror: `lane 3.5 | S 12 | L 12 ^90 | S 16` (losing the preset's suggested-entry metadata and 09 §5.3's preset blessing). (3) Author fig-08-03.scene:
  road: lane 3.5 | S 12 | L 12 ^90 | S 16
  lines:
    single: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto label="single-steer line exits tight"
    fifty:  mistake fifty_pence label="fifty-pencing line runs wide"
  marks: all
  labels:
    entry:c1-8 "premature initiation"
    exit:c1 "multiple turn points"
  view: mode=diagram window=auto
(4) `linelab scene fig-08-03.scene --check` → exit 0 lint per 04 §7 / 08 §3. (5) `linelab scene fig-08-03.scene --out out/` → per 03 §8 / 05 §7 / 06 §7: two-line envelope (green clean `single`, red `fifty` pinned wide/runoff), SVG + manifest with proportion metrics. Gate arithmetic: width_ratio 7/12 = 0.58 (band 0.45–0.95 pass), straight_share with x5 compression ≈ (28/5)/(5.6+18.85) ≈ 0.23 (≤ 0.45 pass). So the frame IS book-compact — that part of the design works.

WHERE IT BREAKS. (a) The mistake compiler places the 6 facets AT the solved turn-in (03 §7.1: "single turn-in → facets = 6"); fifty_pence has no early_by_m param and the one-perturbation rule forbids stacking `premature` on top — so the compiled red line's first turn point COINCIDES with green's, red starts outside green and never crosses it: the book's premature-first-marker, red-inside-green-early, one-crossing topology is unreachable, and my "premature initiation" label points at nothing true. (b) Physics headroom: at 34 km/h on R12 the good line sits near 28 deg lean (kappa = g·tan(phi)/v²); alternating facets are capped by phiMax 45 deg, bounding path humps to ~0.15–0.25 m over ~3 m facets — resolved fine at ds 0.5 m (6 samples/facet, visible in the phi channel of the controls strip) but ~2–3 % of drawn road width: a subtle wobble, not the book's polygon, and width_exag ≈ 1 here so the projection amplifies nothing. (c) marks: `auto` gives the red line NO markers; `all` adds apex rings and exit dots the book lacks; hourglass-per-facet is stated nowhere. (d) Labels are road-anchored ("a callout always resolves onto the road"), so two callouts at the same station cannot name which LINE they mean, and the two-leader callout is inexpressible. (e) Whether the red line even renders red is asserted, not derivable: no facet amplitude/deficit parameter guarantees the corridor is exceeded; a contained result renders AMBER under 06 §5.1. Escape hatch found: a scene `plan <file.json>` line with six hand-placed early turn_in actions can draw the book's topology — but it abandons the mistake compiler, its diagnosis/label, the one-perturbation diff, and the D6 mistake-spec sharing story.

findings.title: Fifty-pence premature initiation is inexpressible through the mistake compiler
findings.claim: The book's red line begins with an EARLY first turn point (bottom callout: premature initiation; red runs inside green early, crosses it once, exits wide). compileMistake fifty_pence anchors its facets at the solved turn-in and exposes only a facet count, and the one-perturbation rule forbids combining it with premature's early_by_m — so the compiled line's first turn point coincides with the green line's, red sits outside green from turn-in onward, and the crossing topology, early first hourglass, and the figure's own caption cannot be reproduced. The only route to the book's geometry is a hand-authored `plan` line, which forfeits the mistake compiler's provenance, diagnosis, one-perturbation diff, and D6 mistake-spec sharing — the very machinery G5/D6 make first-class. Not a blocker only because that plan-line escape hatch exists.
findings.evidence: 03 §7: "exactly one control perturbed"; 03 §7.1 table: fifty_pence = "single turn-in → facets = 6 alternating partial inputs" with no early_by_m (contrast premature: "turn in early_by_m = 10 early"); book_text part0014 lines 51-57 ("he keeps making corrections as he realizes his initial input was insufficient") and fig-08.03 callout "fifty pencing is almost always associated with premature initiation"; 04 §7: "plan <file.json>: an explicit wire scenario included as a line"; 01 §2 G7: "linelab produces an equivalent figure from a scene file".
findings.improvement: Add an early_by_m parameter (default ≈ premature's 10 m) to fifty_pence and define the perturbation as one steering-channel replacement (early first facet + 5 corrections), explicitly noting in 03 §7.1 that this remains a single perturbed control; pin the red-inside-green-then-cross topology as part of the fig 8.3 fixture expectation.

findings.title: fifty_pence's failing outcome and faceted shape are asserted, not derivable
findings.claim: The design pins fifty_pence to wide/runoff, but specifies no facet amplitude, spacing, timing, or lean-deficit parameter — only a count. "Alternating partial inputs" does not determine whether the schedule net-under-steers enough to exceed the usable corridor before corrections catch up; a promptly-correcting schedule stays contained, which yields outcome violation and an AMBER line under colour law v2 — the book's red line would render amber, and the mistake oracle would go red with no designed knob to fix it (the oracle forbids editing the expectation). Even the word "alternating" is ambiguous between add-lean/relax-lean scallops and a sign-flipping weave, which are different pictures.
findings.evidence: 03 §7.1: "fifty_pence | single turn-in → facets = 6 alternating partial inputs | wide/runoff (always fails single_input)" — defaults column names only facets; 03 §7.1: "Outcome classes are empirically pinned, never asserted" (but no mechanism is given from which wide follows); 06 §5.1: "contained if outcome = violation ... contained → amber"; 09 §4: "a mismatch is an engine, compiler, or doctrine bug — never fixed by editing the expectation".
findings.improvement: Specify the facet schedule in 03 §7.1: e.g. each input reaches fraction q (TUNING ~0.6) of the currently-required lean, held for gap_m (TUNING) before the next correction, with defaults chosen so cumulative under-rotation provably exits the corridor on book90; state the alternation semantics (toward-target then partial relax, same sign throughout).

findings.title: True physics on book90 cannot produce the book's dramatic polygon
findings.claim: At book90's suggested 34 km/h on R12 the good line already needs ~28 deg lean; the 45 deg ceiling and 40.36 deg reserve leave curvature headroom that bounds facet path-deviation to roughly 0.15–0.25 m per ~3 m facet. At 0.5 m sampling the humps are numerically resolved (~6 samples per facet) and clearly visible in the controls strip's phi vs cmd_lean channel, but on the drawn 7 m road they are ~2–3 % of road width — an order of magnitude subtler than the book's polygonal red line — and auto width_exag ≈ 1 on this already-in-band corner amplifies nothing. Because every drawn line must be a ridden line (G1), the recreated figure's central visual device (the faceted path) will read as a faint wobble; no mechanical test pins facet visibility, leaving only the editorial vision judge.
findings.evidence: 02 §2: "kappa(v, phi) = G · tan(phi)/v²"; 02 §4: "phiMax(mu) = atan(mu) (45.0° at mu = 1.0)", "40.36° at skill 0.85"; 02 §3: street roll_rate 50 deg/s; 03 §3.1: book90 "R 12 ^90", "Suggested entry 34 km/h"; 06 §2.3: exaggeration solved only up to WIDTH_RATIO_TARGET, so an in-band corner gets ~1; 09 §3.4 property list contains no facet-amplitude or shape-visibility property; 09 §7: judge leg is the only check that the mistake "reads as the mistake it teaches".
findings.improvement: Choose the fifty_pence canonical fixture at a lower entry speed (more curvature headroom) and/or add a pinned property (e.g. max lateral deviation between consecutive turn_in events ≥ X m in true geometry, X TUNING) plus an explicit vision-judge rubric item "faceting legible at export scale".

findings.title: Marker system cannot express fig 8.3's marker set
findings.claim: The figure needs turn-point hourglasses ONLY, on BOTH lines: ~6 on the red line (one per steering input) and exactly 1 on the green, with no apex rings and no exit dots. The design gives a figure-level binary marks: auto|all where auto marks the good line only (red line gets nothing — and "multiple turn points" IS the figure) and all presumably adds every marker type to every line (rings and dots the book lacks). Whether an hourglass is drawn per turn_in EVENT (6 on a faceted line) or once per line is stated nowhere; even facets = 6 is ambiguous between 6 inputs and 6 flat segments (5 corrections).
findings.evidence: 03 §8: "`marks` (`auto | all`) controls turn-point/apex/exit markers"; 04 §7: "marks: auto | all # optional (default auto: good-line marks)"; 06 §3.1 item 9: "hourglass = turn point, ring = apex, dot = exit; each inherits its line's colour" — vocabulary only, no cardinality, no per-line/per-type selection; fig-08.03 raster: six red hourglasses, one green, zero rings/dots.
findings.improvement: Define markers as emitted at every turn_in (and apex/exit) EVENT, and extend marks to a per-type/per-line selector (e.g. marks: turn_points@all, or marks entries per line) so a scene can say "turn points on all lines, nothing else".

findings.title: Labels cannot target lines, so the four callouts are unreproducible
findings.claim: All four fig 8.3 callouts point at line features: "runs wide" at the red line near exit, "exits tight" at the green line near the same stations, "premature initiation" at the red line's first marker (adjacent to the green marker), and "multiple turn points" with TWO leader arrows to two different red markers. The label grammar is road-station-anchored only ("a callout always resolves onto the road, never into empty space") with no line reference and one anchor per label — two labels at near-identical stations cannot be disambiguated between the red and green lines, and a two-leader label is inexpressible. The recreated figure's annotations would be ambiguous exactly where the book's teaching is sharpest.
findings.evidence: 03 §8: "labels are corner-relative callouts (entry|exit|mid:<id> ± m ...); a callout always resolves onto the road"; 06 §3.1 item 10: "Callout labels — corner-relative anchors ... with leader lines" — no line-qualified anchor anywhere; fig-08.03: "multiple turn points" box with two leaders to two red markers; "single-steer line exits tight" and "fifty-pencing line runs wide" at nearly the same station on different lines.
findings.improvement: Extend label anchors with a line qualifier and event sugar (e.g. `turn_in:fifty#1`, `exit@single`), and allow a label to carry multiple anchors (multiple leaders).

findings.title: Sight-ray trigger contradicts between 06 and 08
findings.claim: 06 §3.1 draws sight rays "one per selected sample (default: each line's turn_in event)" with no occluder condition, while 08's recipe (e) says rays are "drawn automatically whenever occluders are present". Fig 8.3 has no occluders and no sight rays; under the literal 06 reading my recreation sprouts spurious dashed rays (to road end) — up to six on the faceted line if per-turn_in-event. Two docs disagree and the implementer must pick.
findings.evidence: 06 §3.1 item 7: "Sight rays — dashed rays from the eye position to the limit point ..., one per selected sample (default: each line's turn_in event)"; 08 §6(e): "sight rays are drawn automatically whenever occluders are present — 06 §3.1" (a condition 06 never states).
findings.improvement: State in 06 §3.1 that sight rays render only when the figure has at least one occluder (and define the multi-turn_in default as the FIRST turn_in event per line).

findings.title: Failing-line termination and drawn endpoint are unspecified
findings.claim: The book's red line completes the corner on-road and exits the frame with an arrowhead. In linelab, outcome runoff means "left the road/lane", but 02's termination precedence (crash → stopped → road/corner end → runaway) contains no lateral-departure termination, and off-road integration (what mu, whether the run continues on grass) is undefined — so where the red trajectory ends, and therefore where its drawn arrow sits (mid-corner at the edge line vs continuing to road end), is an implementer guess that visibly changes every failing-line figure.
findings.evidence: 02 §7: "Termination precedence per step: crash → stopped (v < v_floor_ms) → road/corner end → runaway guards" — nothing for lateral departure; 02 §7 outcome: "runoff — left the road/lane and no feasible corrective returns it"; 03 §4 hazards define mu only for on-road patches; fig-08.03: red line runs to the frame edge with an arrowhead.
findings.improvement: Specify in 02 §7 whether lateral road departure terminates the run (with event-bracketed crossing coordinates) or integration continues to road-end s on a defined off-road mu; specify that the renderer draws to the terminated sample.

findings.title: tangent_inside runtime semantics are never defined
