findings.claim: The wire plan may carry turn_in target "tangent_inside", and 04 says even the SOLVED canonical plan retains the "deferred tangent_inside turn-in" — meaning the engine's controller must map tangent_inside to a target_lean at run time. No document gives that algorithm (aim point, update rate, relation to the corridor), yet the good green line of every figure — including this one — depends on it; it also blurs the physics-is-not-the-generator stance since the controller is now choosing a steering magnitude by an unspecified rule.
findings.evidence: 03 §6.1: "turn_in | target: tangent_inside ... tangent_inside defers the magnitude to the solver"; 04 §4.2: "The solved plan is the canonical four actions — brake ..., deferred tangent_inside turn-in, maintenance crack, drive roll-on"; 02 §3: the controller returns {target_lean, roll_rate, a_cmd} with no tangent_inside resolution rule anywhere in 02.
findings.improvement: Either have the solver rewrite tangent_inside to a concrete lean_deg before the wire plan is frozen (so the engine never sees it), or specify the controller's tangent-tracking law in 02 §3 with named constants.

findings.title: single_input check arithmetic (and the carried check-id list) absent from this doc set
findings.claim: fifty_pence "always fails single_input", and 01 requires verdicts to be computed from the trajectory regardless of author — so single_input must detect multiple steering inputs from lean history. No document defines the detection (hump amplitude threshold, deadband, how roll-on widening or the exit countersteer avoid counting as inputs), and the carried 12 check ids themselves are never enumerated in 01–09, only in extract/. A wrong guess either fails the green line (exit stand-up counted as a second input) or passes a gentle fifty-pence line.
findings.evidence: 03 §7.1: "(always fails `single_input`)"; 01 §3 Axis B: "The verdict is a property of the trajectory, computed identically no matter who authored the inputs"; 05 §6.2: "The carried 12-check concept is extended" — ids not listed; 00 §5: "where a sibling document is silent, the prior design's choice is a reasonable default" (forcing implementers into extract/).
findings.improvement: Enumerate the v2 check-id list in 05 §6.2 and specify single_input's arithmetic (e.g. count of same-sign lean-rise episodes above a deg threshold after turn_in, TUNING) with a deadband, plus a test that the solved good line passes it.

findings.title: Diagnosis vocabulary has no cause for faceting
findings.claim: compileMistake returns a diagnosis, and the envelope's diagnosis.cause is a closed set — overspeed_entry, grip_exceeded, roll_rate_limited, sight_deficit, late_brake, plan_gap, stand_up — none of which names multiple steering corrections. The fifty_pence line's diagnosis must therefore mislabel its mechanism (plan_gap? roll_rate_limited?), so `explain` on the fig 8.3 envelope cannot say "fifty-pencing" as the cause, weakening the errors-teach loop for exactly this figure.
findings.evidence: 05 §6.1: "diagnosis.cause : 'overspeed_entry' | 'grip_exceeded' | 'roll_rate_limited' | 'sight_deficit' | 'late_brake' | 'plan_gap' | 'stand_up'"; 03 §7: "compileMistake(kind, params, ctx) → Result<{kind, plan, roadSpec, outcome, diagnosis, label}>"; 08 §5.2: explain narrates "the diagnosis chain (cause → station → corner)".
findings.improvement: Add a `multi_input` (or `faceting`) cause to the closed diagnosis vocabulary, emitted when repeated steering corrections are the proximate cause of wide/runoff.

findings.title: book90 preset handedness is mirrored versus figs 8.1–8.3
findings.claim: book90 expands to a RIGHT-hander (`R 12 ^90`) and is advertised as the "figs 8.1–8.3 archetype", but fig 8.3 (and the premature/slow-steer archetype it shares) is drawn as a LEFT-hander. A cold-start agent following the schema's preset guidance produces a mirrored figure; recreating the book exactly requires abandoning the preset for hand-written DSL, losing the preset's suggested-entry metadata and the 09 §5.3 preset-proportion blessing. No view-level mirror exists.
findings.evidence: 03 §3.1: "book90 | lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16 | 34 km/h | canonical single 90° corner (figs 8.1–8.3 archetype)"; fig-08.03 raster: entry heading up, exit heading left = left-hander; 06 §2.1 ViewSpec has mode/window/compression only, no mirror.
findings.improvement: Add left-handed preset variants (book90L) or a hand= parameter on presets, or note in 03 §3.1 that handedness parity with the book requires the L-form DSL.

findings.title: window=auto is underspecified for multi-line figures and terminated lines
findings.claim: The default camera is defined off "first(turn_in, brake_start)" and "exit + WINDOW_TAIL_M" without saying which LINE supplies these events in a multi-line figure; a runoff mistake line may terminate before any exit event exists (exit is a measured post-hoc event), so the window derivation for exactly the fig 8.3 envelope — one clean line, one failing line with possibly no exit — is a guess. Cropping to the wrong line's events can cut the red line's wide exit out of frame.
findings.evidence: 06 §2.4: "window.from = first(turn_in, brake_start) − WINDOW_LEAD_M ... window.to = exit + WINDOW_TAIL_M" — singular events, no per-line rule (only multi-CORNER union is specified); 05 §5: "apex and exit are measured post-hoc"; 02 §7: early termination on runoff-adjacent outcomes.
findings.improvement: Define window=auto over the UNION of all lines' events, with fallbacks (terminated sample stands in for a missing exit).

findings.title: Role dash patterns visibly diverge from the book's solid lines
findings.claim: Colour law v2 renders the mistake role as short-dash while every line in fig 8.3 (and the other chapter-8 figures) is solid; the parity requirement promises "same marker/colour vocabulary" as the book, so every recreated mistake line will read texturally unlike its book counterpart. The accessibility rationale is sound, but the tension with the stated parity bar is unacknowledged.
findings.evidence: 06 §5.2: "mistake → short dash"; 06 §7 parity requirement: "read as an equivalent of the book's figure — same compact proportions, same marker/colour vocabulary"; fig-08.03: both lines solid.
findings.improvement: Acknowledge the divergence in 06 §7's parity language (parity modulo the role-dash accessibility channel) or make dash a style toggle for book-parity exports with the legend carrying role.

wins: The schema mistakes teaching table (08 §5.1) with per-kind outcome and book-figure mapping got me from cold start to the correct kind (fifty_pence → fig 8.3) on the first try — the naming-trap documentation at the API surface works as intended.

The facets = 6 default (03 §7.1) exactly matches the chapter's own arithmetic ("increase your chances of making a mistake, by about 500 percent" = 6 inputs vs 1) and my count of six hourglasses in the raster — the parameter default is book-grounded even though its surroundings are underspecified.

Lane-fraction f semantics (03 §2, 01 §4.1) map cleanly onto the figure's geometry: entry f≈1 at the outer edge, green apex f→0 at the double yellow, red exit f>1 running wide — hand-independent, so the mirrored left-hander costs no sign bookkeeping.

The proportion-gate bands are genuinely right for this figure: measured from the raster, fig 8.3's road-width:radius ≈ 0.57 sits inside 06 §6.1's 0.55–0.9 book band, and the book90-class geometry passes at true scale (7/12 = 0.58, straight_share ≈ 0.23 after x5 compression) — the stretched-figure defect the gate exists for would be caught and is avoided here.

Colour is honestly derivable: green from the solved line's clean verdict, red from the mistake line's emergent wide/runoff (if the pin holds) — no painted colour anywhere in the session, and the D9 decoupling means the picture cannot lie to protect the lesson.
Authoring ergonomics held: the whole figure is one ~9-line .scene file plus one bake, with scene --check lint before solving (04 §7, 08 §3), and a one-command zero-file alternative exists (08 §4).

Inspection depth exceeds the book: even where the drawn faceting is subtle, the per-sample cmd_lean vs phi channels (05 §2.1) and the controls strip (06 §4) expose all six commanded corrections and the rate-limited tracker's response numerically — stateAt makes the mistake line exactly as inspectable as the good one (D6/G5).

verdicts.title: Fifty-pence premature initiation is inexpressible through the mistake compiler
verdicts.note: 03 §7 pins "exactly one control perturbed" and §7.1 gives fifty_pence only "facets = 6" (no early_by_m; that param belongs to premature/early_apex); scene grammar (04 §7) takes one kind per mistake line, so premature+fifty_pence cannot combine. The raster confirms the book's red line initiates before the green marker (bottom callout: "fifty pencing is almost always associated with premature initiation"), runs inside green early, and crosses once — geometry the facet-count-only surface cannot author. One softening: the docs never actually state facets anchor at the solved turn-in (placement is unspecified, so an implementer could bake early initiation into the default schedule), but no parameter or text mandates it, and the plan escape hatch (04 §7) genuinely forfeits mistake-spec provenance/diagnosis/one-perturbation diff — a plan line shares only as {kind: "scenario"} per 05 §7. Major severity fair given G7 targets this exact figure.

verdicts.title: fifty_pence's failing outcome and faceted shape are asserted, not derivable
verdicts.note: The underspecification nucleus survives: 03 §7.1's defaults column names only a count ("facets = 6 alternating partial inputs") — no amplitude, spacing, timing, or lean-deficit parameter anywhere in 00–09, so whether the schedule nets wide/runoff is not derivable from the docs, and "alternating" is genuinely loose (though 01 §4.3's "several lean humps" leans toward same-sign scallops, not a weave). But "no designed knob to fix it" is refuted: 03 §7.1 says "a pin that stops holding is an engine bug or a mis-tuned default — never patched by editing the pin", and 09 §4 names "compiler" bugs as a fix target — the compiler's TUNING defaults are the designed knob; a contained-amber first run is a tuning event the design anticipates, not an unfixable oracle deadlock. Severity overstated; a spec-gap (minor/major boundary) survives, the amber-lock trap does not.

verdicts.title: True physics on book90 cannot produce the book's dramatic polygon
verdicts.note: The book90-specific arithmetic checks out: 04 §4.1 pins apex lean ≈ 28° (lean_frac 0.70), 7 m/12 m = 0.58 ≥ WIDTH_RATIO_TARGET 0.55 so auto width_exag ≈ 1, and even a full-straighten deficit bounds per-facet deviation to ~0.3 m over a ~3 m facet (~3–4 % of road width); 09 §3.4 indeed has no facet-visibility property, leaving only the §7 judge leg. But the "only route is the vision judge / faint wobble is inevitable" conclusion ignores a designed alternative the critic did not address: 03 §3.1 explicitly says "Figures teaching the book's 45–80 km/h prose speeds use realistic roads plus the diagram projection", and 06 §2.2 applies width_exag to "every trajectory's d" — a realistic-road fig-8.3 scene amplifies facet deviations ~3.5×, well into visibility. Also, the fig-8.3 raster's own per-facet kinks are modest — the polygon device is carried largely by the six hourglass markers — so "order of magnitude subtler than the book" overstates the gap. Severity major is wrong; the book90-scoped nucleus and missing mechanical test survive.

verdicts.title: Marker system cannot express fig 8.3's marker set
verdicts.note: The raster shows hourglasses only: six red, one green, zero rings/dots. The entire marker surface is the binary `marks: auto | all` (03 §8, 04 §7 — "default auto: good-line marks"), with no per-type or per-line selection anywhere: 06 §3.1 item 9 gives vocabulary and colour inheritance only, 08's render verb has no marker flag, and 07 §6.3's viewer state list has none. Under `auto` the red line gets nothing (and "multiple turn points" IS the figure); under `all` nothing suppresses the apex rings and exit dots the book lacks. Per-event vs per-line hourglass cardinality is indeed stated nowhere. One sub-point is weak: the table's gloss "facets = 6 alternating partial inputs" reads fairly clearly as 6 inputs (matching the six book markers), so that ambiguity is mild — but the core inexpressibility stands.

verdicts.title: Labels cannot target lines, so the four callouts are unreproducible
verdicts.note: The label grammar in 03 §8 and 04 §7 is station-anchored only (`entry|exit|mid:<id> ± m`, `apex:<id>` sugar) with one anchor and one text per label; 06 §3.1 item 10 adds leader lines but no line-qualified anchor and no multi-leader form. The raster confirms all four callouts point at line features, including a two-leader "multiple turn points" box targeting two red markers, and "runs wide"/"exits tight" at near-identical stations on different lines. The closest counter-evidence is 09 §5.1 P-PROJ-MARKER ("every marker and callout anchor... lands on its line's projected image"), which presumes a line association — but no authoring surface exists to name that line, and it even contradicts 03 §8's "a callout always resolves onto the road". The gap is real.

verdicts.title: Sight-ray trigger contradicts between 06 and 08
verdicts.note: 06 §3.1 item 7 draws rays "one per selected sample (default: each line's turn_in event)" with no occluder condition anywhere in 06; 08 §6(e) states "sight rays are drawn automatically whenever occluders are present — 06 §3.1", attributing to 06 a conditional it never contains. Fig 8.3 has no occluders and no rays; under literal 06 semantics a default render sprouts rays to road end (03 §5.1: "With no occluders... sight runs to the road end"), potentially one per turn_in event on the faceted line. No third doc resolves the trigger (01 §6 and 04 R3 only describe occluded scenes). A genuine, implementer-must-pick inconsistency; minor is the right severity.

verdicts.title: Failing-line termination and drawn endpoint are unspecified
verdicts.note: 02 §7's termination precedence ("crash → stopped → road/corner end → runaway guards") contains no lateral-departure entry, and the outcome definition ("runoff — left the road/lane...") is a classification, not a termination rule. No doc defines off-road μ (03 §4 hazards are on-road d-band patches) or whether integration continues on grass to road end; 07 §3.4's "road-end/run-off" terminal-badge mention presumes an ending it never defines. Since 06 §3.1 item 8 puts the arrowhead at the path end, where a runoff line's drawn arrow sits (mid-corner at the edge vs continuing off-road to road end) is genuinely an implementer guess. The fig-8.3 raster's red line completing the corner on-road with a frame-edge arrowhead makes the gap visible for exactly this figure. Minor severity as stated.

verdicts.title: tangent_inside runtime semantics are never defined
verdicts.note: 03 §6.1 says only "tangent_inside defers the magnitude to the solver", yet 04 §4.2 confirms the SOLVED canonical plan still carries the "deferred tangent_inside turn-in" — so the magnitude is not resolved into the plan and the runtime controller must interpret it. 02 §3 defines the controller's return shape ({target_lean, roll_rate, a_cmd}) with no tangent_inside resolution rule; 04 §3/§4 search decel and roll-on, never the steering law. Nothing in 00–09 gives the aim-point/update algorithm, and every good line (04 §4.1's apex-lean bisection target only works through this unspecified law) depends on it. The extract/ fallback (00 §5) exists but the claim as stated — absent from this doc set — is true. Minor severity fits.

verdicts.title: single_input check arithmetic (and the carried check-id list) absent from this doc set
verdicts.note: 03 §7.1 pins fifty_pence to "(always fails `single_input`)" and 01 §3 requires verdicts computed from the trajectory, but the detection arithmetic appears nowhere: 05 §6.2 claims to pin "the id list" yet enumerates only the two new visibility checks ("The carried 12-check concept is extended"), 01 §3 points back to 05 for "check ids and arithmetic", and 05 §6.2 even flags "the single-steering-input smoothness bar" as re-derived without stating it. The circular ownership plus 00 §5's extract-as-default rule confirms implementers are pushed outside the design of record. The green-line hazard (exit countersteer/roll-on widening counting as a second input) is plausible and unguarded. Minor severity as stated.

verdicts.title: Diagnosis vocabulary has no cause for faceting
verdicts.note: The enum gap is real: 05 §6.1's closed diagnosis.cause set (overspeed_entry | grip_exceeded | roll_rate_limited | sight_deficit | late_brake | plan_gap | stand_up) has no multiple-corrections entry, so a compiled fifty_pence line's cause must borrow an adjacent label. But the claimed consequence — "explain... cannot say 'fifty-pencing'... weakening the errors-teach loop" — is overstated: the envelope carries the mistake kind and label in provenance (05 §7 LineResult.source = {kind: "mistake", base_line_id, mistakeSpec}; compileMistake returns a label per 03 §7), and 08 §5.2 has explain narrate "every doctrine check with verdict and evidence stations" — the failing `single_input` check names the mechanism. The diagnosis.cause chain alone mislabels; the explain output as a whole does not. The enum-gap half survives at minor; the teaching-loop half does not.

verdicts.title: book90 preset handedness is mirrored versus figs 8.1–8.3
verdicts.note: Verified against all three rasters: figs 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3 each enter heading up and exit heading left — left-handers — while 03 §3.1's book90 expands to `R 12 ^90` (right-hander) and is labelled the "figs 8.1–8.3 archetype". 06 §2.1's ViewSpec (mode/window/width_exag/compressions) has no mirror, and no other doc adds one. A cold-start agent following the schema's preset guidance does produce a mirrored figure. The stated costs are inflated — the fix is a one-token DSL edit (R→L) with the suggested 34 km/h documented beside the preset, and the 09 §5.3 proportion blessing is hand-independent — but at the claimed minor severity the finding is accurate.

verdicts.title: window=auto is underspecified for multi-line figures and terminated lines
verdicts.note: 06 §2.4 defines the window from singular events ("first(turn_in, brake_start)", "exit + WINDOW_TAIL_M") and specifies a union only across multiple CORNERS, never across multiple LINES — nothing says which line supplies the events when a figure carries a premature-initiating mistake line (earlier turn_in) beside the good line. 05 §5 confirms exit is a measured post-hoc event ("heading has returned to the road's exit heading"), which a wide/runoff line may never emit, and 02 §7 allows early termination — so window.to for exactly the fig-8.3 envelope is underivable. No other doc (07's viewer, 08's render flags) supplies the missing rule. Minor severity fits.

verdicts.title: Role dash patterns visibly diverge from the book's solid lines
verdicts.note: 06 §5.2 pins mistake → short dash as a normative role channel; the fig-8.3 raster (and 8.1/8.2) shows every line solid. 06 §7's parity bar promises figures that "read as an equivalent of the book's figure — same compact proportions, same marker/colour vocabulary, same annotation devices" — dash texture is technically outside that enumerated list, but the tension is nowhere acknowledged or reconciled in the doc set, and every recreated mistake line will differ texturally from its book counterpart. At polish severity, the observation is accurate as stated.

result.walkthrough: I viewed fig 8.4: a TEARDROP left-hander (enter bottom-right heading up, loop counterclockwise well past 180°, exit bottom-left heading down), radius visibly tightening toward exit; road drawn with white edge lines only, NO centreline; both lines swing edge to edge (full carriageway); GREEN = single-late-apex line with one green hourglass ("single-apex turn point") and one green ring apex; RED = the double-apex STRATEGY line with two red hourglasses ("double-apex turn point 1/2") and two red rings; five callout boxes with leaders; arrowhead terminations; no sight rays, props, speed chips, or exit dots. The caption says the red path is takeable ("you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed"). Simulated session, cold-start per 08 §2: (1) `linelab schema scene`, `schema road-dsl`, `explain` — the mistakes/solve teaching tables carry me. (2) Road: preset `bookDecreasing` expands to `lane 3.5 | S 10 | R 16>9 ^130 | S 14` (03 §3.1) — wrong hand (book is a left-hander) and 130° sweep vs the book's ~230°+; I authored `road: lane 3.5 | L 16>9 ^130 | S 14` instead. A faithful `L 16>9 ^230` hinges on the super-tight refusal "sweep ≥ 170° AND r ≤ 15 m" (02 §7, 03 §3.1): for a taper the docs give the corner record a single `r` (03 §2) and never say whether refusal tests r1, r2, or min — if r_min, the faithful shape is OUT_OF_SCOPE; the projection cannot help because P5 preserves sweep exactly (06 §2.5). (3) Full width: the wire schema has `use_full_width` (03 §6) but it is deliberately not DSL-expressible (03 §3) and the scene grammar (04 §7) has no road-options key, and 08 §4.1's flag list has no `--full-width` — so from a .scene file both lines are lane-constrained to a ~2.7 m corridor, nothing like the figure. (4) Green line: `single: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto` → solve pipeline (04 §4) should verify clean; but suggestTurnIn ranks candidates by |apex_pct − 58| (04 §3) while the decreasing-radius late bar is "apex past 60 %" (01 §5) — the ranking prefers candidates that fail the special-case check, and step 3 only full-solves the top 4. (5) Red line: `double: ride entry=34 style=double_apex role=alternative` → solveDoubleApex is specified in one parenthetical sentence (04 §4.4): no turn-point parameter surface, no acceptance detail beyond 01 §5's "two distinct lane-fraction minima… to be validated in implementation", no failure semantics. Tracing the causal chain: its "ascending gentlest-decel scan" can always slow further, so it plausibly converges to a CONTAINED two-touch line → outcome `violation` → colour-law-v2 quality "contained" → AMBER (06 §5.1), not the promised red; to earn red the engine must emit wide/runoff/crash (06 §5.1, 02 §7) — i.e. a line that leaves the road, which the book's on-road red line never does; and if no contained line exists the result is a typed NO_SOLUTION with nothing to draw. 01 §3/§5's claim that the fig 8.4 companion "renders red because its verdict is red" is asserted, not derivable — and contradicts both the book caption and 01 §3's own book-wins rule. (6) Labels: anchors are corner-relative stations plus `apex:<id>` sugar resolved against the GOOD line's solved apex only (04 §7) — the red line's turn points/apexes are emergent and unaddressable, so "double-apex turn point 1/2" became guessed `entry:c1-4`-style offsets, breaking the first-try bar (G4). (7) Bake: `linelab scene fig-08-04.scene --check` then `--out out/`; projection compresses the taper — the corner itself — by C_TAPER=1.25 (06 §2.2 calls tapers "transitions") which, with sweep preserved, shrinks drawn radius ~×0.8, pushing tight-end width_ratio to ≈ 7/(9/1.25) ≈ 0.97, above the 0.95 hard band (06 §6.1) — a possible gate FAIL, and which radius width_ratio uses for a taper is unspecified. The gate has no sweep/topology metric, so the 130° stand-in passes bands while visibly failing G7's teardrop parity; only the editorial vision judge could catch it.

findings.title: Red double-apex line cannot render red as promised
findings.claim: The design promises that fig 8.4's double-apex companion line "renders red because its verdict is red", but no causal chain in 02/04/06 can produce a renderable red line that matches the book. Colour law v2 maps red only to outcome ∈ {wide, runoff, crash}; solveDoubleApex's ascending gentlest-decel scan can always slow further, so it either converges to a contained two-touch line (outcome `violation` → AMBER) or finds nothing (typed NO_SOLUTION → no line to draw). A genuinely wide/runoff line would leave the road, unlike the book's on-road red path with an exit arrow. Worse, the book caption explicitly sanctions the double-apex path ("you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed"), so the design's assertion that it is "legitimately failing" contradicts the book — and 01 §3's own rule says the book wins disputes. The red in the book encodes 'inferior strategy', a semantic colour law v2 deliberately cannot express.
findings.evidence: 01 §3: "a *legitimately failing* second strategy (fig 8.4's double-apex companion) renders red because its verdict is red, not because someone painted it"; 01 §5: "The book's fig 8.4 draws the correct single-late-apex line green and a double-apex *strategy* line red — under colour law v2 that red is simply the second strategy's own failing verdict"; 06 §5.1: "failing if outcome ∈ {wide, runoff, crash}", "contained if outcome = violation"; 04 §4.4: "solveDoubleApex (the planned two-touch line with its ascending gentlest-decel scan…)"; 02 §7: wide = "ran wide but a feasible add-lean corrective exists", runoff = "left the road/lane"; book_text part0014 line 79: "you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed"; 01 §3: "when linelab and the book disagree, the book wins."
findings.improvement: Decide the fig 8.4 story explicitly: either (a) add a strategy-aware verdict mechanism analogous to the chain-aware check set of 04 §5 — a `wrong_strategy_for_corner` doctrine failure that maps to red for a contained line whose strategy mismatches the corner archetype — or (b) follow the book's actual caption and specify the double-apex companion as AMBER (contained-but-inferior), amending 01 §3/§5 accordingly. Also specify solveDoubleApex's failure mode: whether a non-verifying scan returns a renderable non-clean line (like 04 §4.2's self-verify rule) or a NO_SOLUTION.

findings.title: use_full_width is unreachable from scene text and CLI flags
findings.claim: Fig 8.4's road has no centreline and both lines use the full carriageway edge to edge, but a .scene file cannot express `use_full_width`: the road DSL deliberately excludes it, the scene grammar's only road key is a DSL line or preset name with no road-options key, and 08's zero-file flag list omits it too — despite 08 claiming every authoring field has a flag. G7's test is parity "from a scene file", so the shipped fig-08-04 scene is forced lane-constrained (a ~2.7 m corridor in a 7 m road), producing lines confined to half the road that visibly cannot match the book figure.
findings.evidence: 03 §3: "`bike_margin_m`, `use_full_width`, and `ds_m` are deliberately not DSL-expressible"; 03 §6 wire schema road object: "{ lane_width_m, bike_margin_m?, use_full_width?, segments: […] } | { preset }"; 04 §7 scene grammar: "road: <road-DSL line> | preset <name> # required, exactly one" with no other road key; 08 §4: "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag" vs §4.1's enumerated list containing no full-width or bike-margin flag; 01 §2 G7: "linelab produces an equivalent figure from a scene file".
findings.improvement: Add a `road_options:` scene key (e.g. `road_options: full_width margin=0.4`) or key=val suffixes on the `road:` line outside the DSL round-trip (mirroring how `preset` already sits there), plus `--full-width`/`--bike-margin` CLI flags; define whether the options compose with the `{preset}` form of the wire road object (currently the union type suggests they cannot).

findings.title: Faithful teardrop geometry is refused or unreachable; taper refusal radius undefined
findings.claim: The book corner sweeps well past 180° with radius tightening to a hairpin-like exit; the closest faithful DSL is a taper like `L 16>9 ^230`, but the super-tight refusal (sweep ≥ 170° AND r ≤ 15 m) likely rejects it — and for a taper the docs never say which radius the refusal tests, since the derived corner record carries a single `r` while a taper has r1 and r2. The design's own answer, the bookDecreasing preset, caps sweep at 130° precisely to dodge the refusal, and the projection preserves sweep exactly (P5), so no rendering step can restore the teardrop. I argue the scope cut itself is miscalibrated here: the refusal targets the sub-25 km/h U-turn regime, but a road-speed decreasing-radius sweep whose entry radius is 16 m is not a parking-lot U-turn — the conjunction as written makes the chapter's own fig 8.4 archetype shape un-authorable.
findings.evidence: 03 §3.1: `bookDecreasing` = "lane 3.5 | S 10 | R 16>9 ^130 | S 14" and "(U-turn rejection requires angle_deg ≥ 170 and r ≤ 15 m)"; 02 §7: "super-tight geometry (sweep ≥ 170° and r ≤ 15 m) is rejected at validation"; 03 §2 corners list: "{id, hand, s0, s1, s_mid, r, angle_deg}" — one `r` for a taper `r1 → r2`; 06 §2.5 P5: "Corner hand, sweep angle … are preserved"; book image: teardrop sweeping well past 180°; 01 §2 G7 promises fig 8.1–8.6 parity.
findings.improvement: Define the taper refusal explicitly (recommend: refuse only if r_min ≤ 15 AND the sweep accumulated while r ≤ 15 is itself ≥ 170° — a taper that spends most of its sweep at ridable radii should pass), pin what `r` means in a taper's corner record (state r1/r2/min as separate fields), and revise bookDecreasing toward the book's shape (e.g. `L 24>12 ^210`, left-handed) or add an explicit scope note to G7 conceding fig 8.4 parity is at reduced sweep.

findings.title: solveDoubleApex is specified in one sentence
findings.claim: The only authoring path to the figure's red line is `ride … style=double_apex`, but solveDoubleApex has no implementable specification: no parameter surface (where do the two turn points come from — the scene grammar's `turnIn=` takes one value), no search description beyond "ascending gentlest-decel scan", no acceptance criteria beyond 01 §5's cross-reference ("two distinct lane-fraction minima … to be validated in implementation, not assumed"), no statement of whether it self-verifies and reports non-clean like the main pipeline, and no typed failure semantics. On the corner where double-apex is the wrong strategy — exactly the fig 8.4 case — the behaviour is unknowable from the docs; the deliverable depends on a solver whose contract does not exist.
findings.evidence: 04 §4.4 in full: "solveDoubleApex (the planned two-touch line with its ascending gentlest-decel scan; under Tier 1R the mid-corner stand-up drift between touches … becomes representable, and the solver's expect_fail declarations shrink accordingly)"; 04 §7 ride grammar: only "turnIn=auto|<m>" (singular); 01 §5: "a solved double-apex plan must produce two distinct lane-fraction minima; this is a solver acceptance criterion … to be validated in implementation, not assumed"; contrast 04 §4.1–4.2's fully specified main pipeline.
findings.improvement: Give solveDoubleApex a section of its own: the two-turn-point search space (e.g. sweep turn-point pairs over station grids), per-touch targets, the plan shape it emits (two turn_in actions with the drift phase per 01 §5), self-verification and non-clean reporting per §4.2, its typed NO_SOLUTION sub-reasons, and what its `expect_fail declarations` are and who consumes them.

findings.title: target_apex_pct=58 fights the decreasing-radius late bar (>60%)
findings.claim: suggestTurnIn ranks surviving turn-in candidates by |apex_pct − 58| and full-solves only the top 4, returning the first that verifies clean. On a decreasing-radius corner the doctrine moves the late-apex bar to "apex past 60 % of swept angle", so the ranking is anti-correlated with the check: candidates nearest 58% rank first and fail late_apex, while doctrinally correct >60% candidates rank lower and may fall outside the top-4 full-solve cut — yielding a spurious "non-clean band" failure or a needlessly fragile solve on the exact corner archetype fig 8.4 teaches. Nothing in 04 says the target adapts by corner type.
findings.evidence: 04 §3: "Rank the surviving band by |apex_pct − 58| (target_apex_pct = 58, TUNING — the doctrinal late apex)" and "Full-solve the top 4 …; return the first that verifies clean"; 01 §5: "the late-apex bar moves later (apex past 60 % of swept angle rather than 50 %)" for decreasing radius.
findings.improvement: Make target_apex_pct corner-type-aware (e.g. 58 for constant arcs, 65+ for decreasing-radius tapers, `na` for increasing radius per 01 §5), or rank primarily by clean-verdict feasibility with apex-pct distance as a tiebreak; state the rule in 04 §3 so the constant cannot silently defeat the special-case doctrine.

findings.title: C_TAPER treats the fig 8.4 corner as a 'transition' and can fail the gate it must pass
findings.claim: The diagram projection compresses taper segments ×1.25, described as "transitions compress gently" — but in this design the taper IS the corner for the decreasing-radius archetype, so the teaching corner itself gets compressed while P5 preserves its sweep, which forces the drawn radius down ~×0.8. At bookDecreasing's tight end that pushes width_ratio to ≈ 7/(9/1.25) ≈ 0.97, above the 0.95 hard band — a proportion-gate FAIL on the design's own preset — and the gate never defines which radius width_ratio uses for a corner whose radius varies. 03's and 06's conceptions of 'taper' (corner archetype vs transition spline) are in unacknowledged conflict.
findings.evidence: 06 §2.2: "c(taper) = C_TAPER = 1.25 // TUNING: transitions compress gently" vs "c(arc) = 1 // corners draw at (near) true arc length"; 06 §2.5 P5: sweep preserved; 06 §6.1: width_ratio band "0.45 – 0.95", defined as "drawn road width / drawn centreline radius" per corner — singular radius; 03 §2: taper is the segment type for "decreasing … and increasing radius corners"; 09 §5.3: "each book preset rendered in true mode must already land near the proportion bands".
findings.improvement: Set c(taper)=1 when the taper is itself a derived corner (compress only tapers adjoining a same-hand arc as true transitions), and define per-corner gate metrics for variable-radius corners (e.g. evaluate width_ratio at r_min and r_max and require both in band, or use arc-length-weighted mean radius); add a taper case to the projection property tests.

findings.title: Callout labels cannot anchor to the alternative line's emergent features
findings.claim: Five of the book figure's six annotations point at line-specific emergent features — the red line's two turn points and two apexes, and the green line's turn point — but the label grammar only offers road-station anchors plus `apex:<id>` sugar resolved against the good line's solved apex. There is no way to address the alternative line's apexes or any line's turn-in event, and no lateral targeting (a callout "resolves onto the road", laterally unspecified). Authoring fig 8.4's labels therefore degenerates to guessing station offsets, iterating bake-inspect-edit — directly violating the G4/08 §2 first-try cold-start bar for exactly the annotation device the figure exists to teach.
findings.evidence: 04 §7: "Label anchors are corner-relative only (entry|exit|mid:<id>[±m], plus apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's *solved* apex"; 03 §8: "a callout always resolves onto the road, never into empty space" — no lateral or per-line addressing; book image: labels "double-apex turn point 1", "double-apex turn point 2", "double-apex line" all target red-line features; 01 §2 G4 / 08 §2: "correctly on the first try".
findings.improvement: Extend label anchors with line-qualified event references — e.g. `turn_in@double`, `apex1@double`, `apex@single` — resolved post-solve against the named line's events (events already exist per 05 §5, so this is anchor sugar, not new computation), and define leader targeting as the anchored line's position at that station.

findings.title: Scene grammar contradicts itself on how many ride lines are allowed
findings.claim: 04 §7's mistake bullet says "exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against", yet the same section's example scene contains two ride lines (`good:` and `wide:`) and the role-default rule speaks of "subsequent `ride` → alternative". The fig 8.4 scene needs two ride lines (single + double_apex); whether that validates depends on which sentence an implementer believes.
findings.evidence: 04 §7: "(exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against)" vs the grammar example's "good: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto" and "wide: ride entry=34 vis=cautious role=alternative", and "Role defaults: first `ride` → ideal, subsequent `ride` → alternative".
findings.improvement: Reword to "at least one ride line is required; mistakes compile against the first" so multi-strategy figures (8.4/8.5) are unambiguously legal.

findings.title: Default sight-ray drawing is inconsistent between 06 and 08
findings.claim: Fig 8.4 contains no sight rays, so the recreation must not draw any. 06's draw order says sight rays are drawn "one per selected sample (default: each line's turn_in event)" with no occluder condition — read literally, an occluder-free figure gets dashed rays from each turn-in to the road end. 08's recipe (e) instead asserts "sight rays are drawn automatically whenever occluders are present — 06 §3.1", citing a conditional 06 never states. Neither the scene grammar nor ViewSpec offers a toggle, so an implementer must guess, and one guess visibly corrupts the fig 8.4 recreation.
findings.evidence: 06 §3.1 item 7: "Sight rays — dashed rays from the eye position to the limit point …, one per selected sample (default: each line's turn_in event)"; 08 §6(e): "(sight rays are drawn automatically whenever occluders are present — 06 §3.1)"; 04 §7 scene grammar and 06 §2.1 ViewSpec: no sight-ray key or flag.
findings.improvement: Move the occluder-presence condition into 06 §3.1 as the normative rule (rays drawn only when the figure has occluders), and add an explicit `rays=` override to the scene `view:`/ViewSpec for authors who want them on or off.

findings.title: Centreline rendering under full-width usage is unspecified
findings.claim: The book road is drawn as a single full-width surface with edge lines and no centreline. The renderer draws "lane markings — centreline and edge lines per the road spec", but no rule connects `use_full_width` to marking suppression, and the road model is fixed two-lane; a compliant implementation would paint a centreline through the middle of the fig 8.4 recreation that the book figure lacks, right where both lines cross it.
findings.evidence: 06 §3.1 item 3: "Lane markings — centreline and edge lines per the road spec"; 03 §2: "use_full_width: true opts into the full carriageway (track-day framing)"; 01 §8: "flat, constant-width, two-lane roads"; book image: edge lines only, no centreline.
findings.improvement: Specify in 06 §3.1 that `use_full_width: true` suppresses the centreline marking (track framing), keeping edge lines — one sentence closes the guess.

findings.title: Preset handedness and mandatory chrome diverge from the book figure
findings.claim: bookDecreasing is a right-hander (`R 16>9`) while fig 8.4 is a left-hander, so the preset recreation is mirrored; the marker vocabulary adds exit dots the book figure lacks; and the mandatory entry-annotation speed chip and disclosure footnote (no documented off-switch) add chrome absent from the book art. Individually cosmetic, but together they mean even a best-case recreation reads noticeably different, and the agent must abandon the preset (hand-writing the mirrored DSL) for hand-parity.
findings.evidence: 03 §3.1: bookDecreasing = "R 16>9 ^130" vs book image's counterclockwise left-hander; 06 §3.1 item 9: "dot = exit" markers; 06 §2.4: frame edge "carries an entry annotation — an inbound arrow with a speed chip"; 06 §2.7: "Every diagram-mode figure carries a standard footnote"; book image: arrowhead terminations only, no chips or footnote.
findings.improvement: Mirror the preset to `L 16>9 …` to match the book's hand (or note the mirroring in the preset table), and let `marks:` distinguish exit dots from turn/apex markers; the footnote and speed chip are defensible honesty devices and can stay mandatory.

wins: The taper segment type (`L r1>r2 ^deg`) makes decreasing radius a first-class one-line geometry (03 §2–3) — the fig 8.4 archetype has a dedicated, greppable DSL form and a named preset with disclosed expansion, satisfying G6 for this corner class at reduced sweep.

The two-strategy figure pattern is genuinely first-class: D9's role/verdict decoupling plus the no-cap scene grammar (04 §7) lets one 6-line scene carry a `ride` single line and a `ride style=double_apex role=alternative` line — the prior design's amber-slot and exclusivity rules would have blocked this figure outright.

The cold-start surface held up for the green line: `schema road-dsl` + `schema scene` + the solve section's intent surface (08 §5.1) were sufficient to author the single-late-apex line correctly on the first try, and `scene --check` (04 §7, 08 §3) lints placements before paying for a bake.

The decreasing-radius doctrine itself is faithfully encoded: the moved late-apex bar (apex past 60 %, 01 §5) and the emergent-line invariant (D7) mean the green line's delayed single turn point is measured, not drawn — matching the caption's 'with a delayed entry, it can be safely completed with only one turning point'.

Honest refusal beats fake physics: the super-tight/vertical placards (01 §8, 02 §7) and the never-ship-unproduced-trajectories stance mean the tool fails loudly on the teardrop rather than silently emitting an invalid low-speed path — the right instinct even where I argue the threshold is miscalibrated.

The verification spine anticipated this exact failure mode in principle: 09 §5.3's rule that presets must land near the proportion bands in TRUE mode, and the gate's audit mode re-deriving metrics from SVG geometry, are exactly the kind of mechanical self-distrust that would catch the C_TAPER distortion once a sweep-aware metric exists.

Per-sample identical citizenship for the alternative line (05 §7, D6) means the red strategy — however it ends up coloured — is fully steppable and stateAt-inspectable, so the 'why is double-apex worse here' lesson is quantifiable (lean demand at the second touch, grip margin) rather than pictorial.

verdicts.title: Red double-apex line cannot render red as promised
verdicts.note: The rendering-impossibility nucleus is confirmed: 01 §3 promises the fig 8.4 companion "renders red because its verdict is red", 06 §5.1 grants red only to outcome ∈ {wide, runoff, crash}, and the book's red line is contained on-road (two inside touches, on-road exit arrow) — any line with that geometry grades violation at worst → amber, so a book-matching red is unproducible by construction; the one-sentence solveDoubleApex spec (04 §4.4) supplies no mechanism to rescue this (a contained solve → amber, an unmet scan → NO_SOLUTION, and a returned failing line must exceed f=1, diverging from the book's contained path). What does NOT survive is the book-contradiction leg: the caption sanctions the double-apex only conditionally — "you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed" (part0014 line 79) — so the design's "legitimately failing" reading (fails at the figure's shared demo speed) is a defensible book interpretation, not a 01 §3 book-wins violation. Core defect stands at blocker weight for G7/colour-law v2; the doctrine-contradiction sub-claim is overstated.

verdicts.title: use_full_width is unreachable from scene text and CLI flags
verdicts.note: Every cited fact checks out and no other doc closes the gap: 03 §3 — "`bike_margin_m`, `use_full_width`, and `ds_m` are deliberately not DSL-expressible"; 04 §7's scene grammar offers only "road: <road-DSL line> | preset <name>" with no road-options key and no preset sets full width; 08 §4 claims "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag" yet §4.1's enumerated flag set has no full-width or bike-margin flag (internal inconsistency verified). The wire schema does accept `use_full_width` (03 §6), so raw scenario JSON can express it — but G7's test is explicitly "an equivalent figure from a scene file" covered by "shipped example scenes" (01 §2), forcing the fig-08-04 scene into the lane-constrained default (3.5 − 2×0.4 = 2.7 m corridor in a 7 m carriageway) against a book figure whose two lines sweep the full uncentrelined road edge to edge.

verdicts.title: Faithful teardrop geometry is refused or unreachable; taper refusal radius undefined
verdicts.note: Confirmed nucleus: the derived corner record carries a single `r` (03 §2: "{id, hand, s0, s1, s_mid, r, angle_deg}") while the refusal (02 §7: "sweep ≥ 170° and r ≤ 15 m") never says which radius a taper tests — a genuine spec gap; and bookDecreasing caps sweep at 130° while P5 preserves sweep exactly, so the shipped recreation cannot show the book's past-180° teardrop. Refuted scope: "the conjunction as written makes the chapter's own fig 8.4 archetype shape un-authorable" is false — the conjunction refuses only r ≤ 15 m, so a past-180° decreasing taper with both radii above 15 m (e.g. `L 20>16 ^230`) validates under any radius reading. The miscalibration argument is also weak: a 9 m-radius tail rides at ≈ 25 km/h (v = √(9.81·9·tan 28°) ≈ 6.9 m/s), squarely inside the sub-25 km/h regime 01 §8/D3 deliberately refuse — the cut is doing what it says.

verdicts.title: solveDoubleApex is specified in one sentence
verdicts.note: The nucleus is confirmed: 04 §4.4's parenthetical is the entire specification, the scene grammar's `turnIn=auto|<m>` is singular with no surface for two turn points, the only acceptance criterion is 01 §5's deferred "two distinct lane-fraction minima … to be validated in implementation", and behaviour on a corner where double-apex is the wrong strategy (fig 8.4) is unknowable from the docs — 09 names no double-apex solver test. Three sub-claims are defeated elsewhere: (1) self-verification IS stated — 04 §1's blanket rule "every solver re-runs the engine on its own output before reporting success" covers it; (2) typed failure semantics exist generically — 08 §7.2's `NO_SOLUTION` "found no feasible target (04's typed sub-reasons ride in at/message)"; (3) `ride style=double_apex` is not the only authoring path — 04 §7's `plan <file.json>` line kind admits an explicit two-`turn_in` wire plan (01 §5 gives the plan shape). Major severity for the surviving core is fair.

verdicts.title: target_apex_pct=58 fights the decreasing-radius late bar (>60%)
verdicts.note: Both citations verified verbatim: 04 §3 ranks survivors by "|apex_pct − 58|" and "Full-solve the top 4 …; return the first that verifies clean"; 01 §5 moves the decreasing-radius bar to "apex past 60 % of swept angle rather than 50 %". Nothing in 04, 05, or 09 adapts `target_apex_pct` by corner type (checked the whole set — 09 §3.5's solver-intent tests cover only constraints and vis knobs). Since "verifies clean" requires all doctrine checks to pass (06 §5.1), a 58%-apex candidate fails `late_apex` on this archetype, so the ranking genuinely prefers failing candidates and doctrinally correct >60% candidates can fall outside the top-4 cut — the spurious "non-clean band" mode is a fair inference on the design's own exact-figure archetype.

verdicts.title: C_TAPER treats the fig 8.4 corner as a 'transition' and can fail the gate it must pass
verdicts.note: The 03-vs-06 conflict is real and unacknowledged: 03 §2 makes `taper` the segment type FOR decreasing-radius corners (bookDecreasing's only corner is its taper), while 06 §2.2 comments "c(taper) = C_TAPER = 1.25 // TUNING: transitions compress gently" vs "c(arc) = 1 // corners draw at (near) true arc length" — so the teaching corner itself is compressed. The math checks: with sweep preserved (P5) and arc length ÷1.25, drawn curvature scales ×1.25, drawn radius ×0.8; at the 9 m tail, 7/(9/1.25) ≈ 0.97 versus the 0.45–0.95 band with auto width_exag already satisfied at 1 (06 §2.3: tight corners "need little or none"). And 06 §6.1's width_ratio uses a singular "drawn centreline radius" per corner, undefined for a varying-radius corner — the same single-`r` gap as the refusal test. Only softener: 06 §6.2's fail-vs-warn margin zones are themselves not numerically pinned, so "FAIL" vs "warn" is indeterminate — but that indeterminacy is part of the finding's point, not a rescue.

verdicts.title: Callout labels cannot anchor to the alternative line's emergent features
verdicts.note: Verified against the image: the callouts "double-apex turn point 1", "double-apex turn point 2", and "double-apex line" (leaders to both red apex rings) all target red-line emergent features, and "single-apex turn point" targets the green line's solved turn-in. The label grammar has no per-line addressing anywhere in the set: 04 §7 — "Label anchors are corner-relative only (entry|exit|mid:<id>[±m], plus apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's *solved* apex"; 03 §8 — "a callout always resolves onto the road, never into empty space" with no lateral targeting; 06 §3.1 item 10 adds nothing. `marks: all` draws markers on every line but provides no text anchoring, and the line-entry `label="…"` is legend text only. 09 §5.1's P-PROJ-MARKER even speaks of an anchor landing "on its line's projected image" — an intent the grammar cannot express. Station-offset guessing plus bake-inspect-edit is the only route, against 08 §2's "first try" bar.

verdicts.title: Scene grammar contradicts itself on how many ride lines are allowed
verdicts.note: All three passages coexist in 04 §7: the mistake bullet's "(exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against)", the grammar example containing both "good: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto" and "wide: ride entry=34 vis=cautious role=alternative", and "Role defaults: first `ride` → ideal, subsequent `ride` → alternative" — the last two presuppose multiple ride lines the first forbids. 04 §9 compounds it by carrying "the one-`ride`-line scene rule" as a design invariant. The fig 8.4 scene needs two ride lines (style=single + style=double_apex per 01 §5's "Both lines are full solved strategies"), so the contradiction lands on a required deliverable. Minor severity is right — the intent ("at least one, first is the mistake reference") is guessable but the text genuinely conflicts.

verdicts.title: Default sight-ray drawing is inconsistent between 06 and 08
verdicts.note: Verified: 06 §3.1 item 7 states rays are drawn "one per selected sample (default: each line's turn_in event)" with no occluder condition — and since 03 §5.1 says without occluders "sight runs to the road end", the literal reading draws dashed rays to road-end in an occluder-free figure. 08 §6(e) asserts "(sight rays are drawn automatically whenever occluders are present — 06 §3.1)", citing a conditional that 06 never states. No toggle exists: 04 §7's `view:` key and 06 §2.1's ViewSpec (mode, window, width_exag, straight_compress, taper_compress) carry no sight-ray field, and 07 owns only the interactive viewer. Fig 8.4 has no occluders and no sight rays, so one of the two readings visibly corrupts the recreation.

verdicts.title: Centreline rendering under full-width usage is unspecified
verdicts.note: 06 §3.1 item 3 mandates "Lane markings — centreline and edge lines per the road spec", and no document connects `use_full_width` (03 §2: "opts into the full carriageway (track-day framing)") to marking suppression — checked 03, 06, 07, and 08. The world is fixed two-lane (01 §8: "flat, constant-width, two-lane roads"), and the book figure shows edge lines only. "Per the road spec" is a hook an implementer could stretch, but no rule is stated, so a compliant implementation painting a centreline through the fig 8.4 recreation is a fair reading — exactly where both book lines cross mid-road. Minor severity is right.

verdicts.title: Preset handedness and mandatory chrome diverge from the book figure
verdicts.note: All four facts verified: bookDecreasing expands to `R 16>9 ^130` (03 §3.1) while the fig 8.4 image is a counterclockwise left-hander, so the preset recreation is mirrored (hand-fixable only by abandoning the preset for `L 16>9 …`, losing the disclosed-preset ergonomics); the marker vocabulary mandates "dot = exit" (06 §3.1 item 9) where the book terminates lines in bare arrowheads; the cropped frame "carries an entry annotation — an inbound arrow with a speed chip" (06 §2.4) and "Every diagram-mode figure carries a standard footnote" (06 §2.7), neither with a documented off-switch, and the book art has neither. Individually cosmetic as the finding itself concedes — polish severity is correctly calibrated.

result.walkthrough:
FIGURE INVENTORY (viewed fig-08.05__double-apex-turn.jpeg): a ~200-degree left-hand horseshoe (enter bottom-right heading up, exit bottom-left heading down), full-width dark road with white edge lines and NO centreline, grass background, no occluders, no sight rays. GREEN line: outside entry, hourglass "turn point 1", ring "apex 1" (~30% sweep), drifts out to hourglass "turn point 2" (outer edge, ~50%), ring "apex 2" (~70%), wide exit with arrowhead. RED line: mid-road entry, ring labelled "typical late apex" (~40-45% sweep), drifts outward, a FORCED red hourglass at ~70% ("Houston, we have a problem"), then "yikes! braking AND increasing lean" — the save is DRAWN: the red line bends and stays on the road near the outer edge to an arrowhead. Both lines end on-road.

SESSION (cold-start bar, 08 §2: schema+explain only). Step 1: `linelab schema road-dsl` / `schema scene` / `schema mistakes` / `schema solve`. Step 2 — road: 03 §3.1 presets are book90 (8.1-8.3), bookDecreasing (8.4), bookEsses (8.6), bookHairpin (R10 ^150, teaches plain late-apex), bookBlind. Fig 8.5 is absent, so I must write DSL. One-arc option `lane 3.5 | S 10 | L 18 ^200 | S 12` passes the U-turn refusal (needs sweep>=170 AND r<=15; r=18 clears it) and mints ONE corner c1. Two-arc option `L 18 ^100 | S 8 | L 18 ^100` (matches the figure's straightish top) mints TWO corners c1,c2 per 03 §2 — which flips the figure into linked-turns semantics (chainedSolve, chain-aware verdict, per-corner apex labels) and leaves `style=double_apex corner=c1` aimed at half the horseshoe. Nothing in the docs adjudicates. I chose one arc.

Step 3 — scene file fig-08-05.scene:
road: lane 3.5 | S 10 | L 18 ^200 | S 12
lines:
  good: ride entry=30 style=double_apex
  bad:  ride entry=44 style=single role=alternative
marks: all
labels:
  mid:c1-10 "apex 1"
  mid:c1+14 "apex 2"
view: mode=diagram window=auto
note: "Double Apex Turn"
Immediately: no way to express the book's full-width road — `use_full_width` exists only in the wire schema (03 §6), is deliberately non-DSL (03 §3), the scene `road:` key takes only DSL/preset (04 §7), and 08 §4.1's flag list has no `--use-full-width`. So the baked road carries a centreline (06 §3.1 stage 3) and both lines are squeezed into one 3.5 m lane on an R18 corner. Also no preset means no suggested entry speed; `entry=` is required, so I guessed twice.

Step 4 — bake `linelab scene fig-08-05.scene --out out/`. The `good` line goes to solveDoubleApex, specified in ONE sentence (04 §4.4) with the two-minima criterion explicitly "to be validated in implementation, not assumed" (01 §5). If it returns, its verdict fails single-input/out-in-out class checks by definition ("requires at least one mid-corner correction") and colour law v2 (06 §5.1) maps clean-with-failed-checks to AMBER — no doc exempts expected failures from quality(), so the book's green line plausibly bakes amber. The `bad` line: at entry=44 (tan phi = 12.2²/(9.81·18) ≈ 0.85 → ~40°+, over the 40.36° street reserve) the feasibility probe (04 §4.2) issues a typed infeasible refusal → NO red line in the figure; at entry<=~38 the single-apex solve verifies CLEAN → a second green line, no lesson. The book's red line exists only in an undesigned sliver where bisection rails and self-verify reports non-clean-but-rendered. Step 5 — hunt the window: `linelab sweep fig85.json --param plan.<id>.<field> ...` cannot touch entry speed (only plan.<id>.<field> is sweepable; entry lives at rider.start.speed_kmh), so I fished by hand. Step 6 — mistake kinds: `chop` (03 §7.1's own mapping for "fig 8.5's failure mechanic") perturbs the FIRST ride line — the double-apex line — 5 m after its roll-on, so red would hug green through both apexes and flare only at exit: wrong geometry versus the book, where red diverges from entry with its own apex. `early_apex` commits an early kiss relative to the double-apex line's turn-in — wrong apex position, pinned `runoff` (off-road), while the book's red stays on-road. Step 7 — fallback: hand-author the red line as an explicit wire plan (turn_in lean for an imagined ~100° corner, then a second turn_in + brake at ~65% sweep = "braking AND increasing lean"); Tier 1R supports the save (a_noreturn ≈ 5.4 m/s² street, so decel ~3.5 with added lean holds the road, 02 §5.3-5.4) — but this is trial-and-error tuning in JSON, blowing the ≤6-line bar, and labels still cannot point at "typical late apex"/"Houston" (anchors are corner-relative plus apex:<id> sugar resolved against the GOOD line's apex only, 03 §8 / 04 §7). Step 8 — render/gates: proportions pass plausibly (drawn width_ratio auto-raised to 0.55; straights compress ×5; ~200° sweep preserved; aspect ~1.5), but the parity/vision leg (06 §7, G7) would fail on: centreline present, half-width line amplitude, missing/mislabelled red line, single apex slot in the verdict, and a possibly amber "good" line.

findings.title: No designed author path for fig 8.5's red line (believed-road / best-failing-attempt gap)
findings.claim: The book's red line is a plausible-but-failing single-apex attempt: a plan formed for a normal corner, executed on a 200-degree corner, salvaged by braking-at-lean, ending on-road. linelab as designed cannot produce it by any one-liner: `ride style=single` at a slow entry self-verifies CLEAN (green, no lesson); at a fast entry the feasibility probe short-circuits with a typed infeasible refusal and returns NO line; the only failing-but-rendered outcome is an undesigned sliver where bisection rails and self-verify reports non-clean. The mistake kinds cannot substitute: `chop` perturbs the double-apex reference line and diverges only after its roll-on; `early_apex` is pinned to `runoff` (leaves the road) at the wrong apex position. The docs internally disagree about which mechanism owns this line, and neither works. There is no 'solve on a believed road, execute on the real road' concept and no 'accept best failing attempt' solver mode anywhere in the set, so G7's promised fig-8.5-equivalent scene cannot be shipped as designed.
findings.evidence: 04 §4.2: probe 'short-circuits with a typed infeasible reason'; §4.2.3 non-clean self-verify 'is reported as such (and still renders)' — but no verb requests it. 03 §7.1 maps `chop` to 'fig 8.5's failure mechanic' (a perturbation of the figure's first `ride` line per 04 §7); 01 §5 instead describes 'a single late apex attempted on this corner, salvaged by braking while leaned' — a full strategy, and 01 §5 (fig 8.4 bullet) says companion strategies are 'full solved strategies, not perturbations'. 01 §2 G7: 'linelab produces an equivalent figure from a scene file' for figs 8.1–8.6.
findings.improvement: Add a first-class 'planned-vs-actual' mechanism: e.g. a `mistake underread sweep_deg=<S>` kind (compile the plan the solver would produce for a corner of sweep S, run it on the true road), or `ride ... assume_road="<dsl>"` (solve against the believed road, execute on the figure's road), plus an explicit `accept=best_failing` solve mode that returns the self-verified non-clean line instead of refusing. Reconcile 01 §5 and 03 §7.1 to name one mechanism.

findings.title: sweep cannot sweep entry speed
findings.claim: The teaching window for the failing single-apex line (and 'Arc = Speed' generally) is governed by entry speed, but the sweep verb's parameter grammar addresses only plan actions. `rider.start.speed_kmh` is not a plan action, so the one exploration tool the CLI offers cannot search the one variable the doctrine says matters most; the agent falls back to manual bisection by re-running solve.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 verb table: `sweep <scenario> --param plan.<id>.<field> --range a:b:step` — the path grammar is exclusively `plan.<id>.<field>`. Entry speed lives at `rider.start.speed_kmh` (03 §6) and as solve input `entry_kmh` (04 §2a). The book's core equation is 'Arc = Speed' (ch.8 text).
findings.improvement: Widen the sweep path grammar to any id-addressed scenario or solve-spec field (`--param rider.start.speed_kmh`, `--param solve.entry_kmh`), keeping the id-addressed (never index) rule.

findings.title: use_full_width is unreachable from scene text and CLI flags
findings.claim: Fig 8.5's road is full-width with no centreline; the double-apex sweep uses the whole carriageway. `use_full_width` exists only in the wire scenario's road object; the DSL deliberately excludes it, the scene `road:` key accepts only DSL-or-preset, and the zero-file flag list omits it. A scene-baked fig 8.5 therefore draws a centreline (renderer stage 3) and confines both lines to a 3.5 m lane on an R18 corner — halving the drawn line amplitude and turning 'runs wide' into oncoming-lane crossing, a different lesson. Since G7's test says 'from a scene file', this alone breaks 8.5 (and 8.4) parity; the only full-width route is hand-written scenario JSON via `compare`, which loses labels/marks/note.
findings.evidence: 03 §3: '`bike_margin_m`, `use_full_width`, and `ds_m` are deliberately not DSL-expressible'; 04 §7 scene grammar: 'road: <road-DSL line> | preset <name>'; 08 §4.1 flag list contains no `--use-full-width`; 06 §3.1 stage 3 'Lane markings — centreline and edge lines per the road spec'; 01 §2 G7 test text. Book fig 8.5 image: no centreline.
findings.improvement: Add scene-level road options (`road_opts: full_width bike_margin=0.4`) and a `--use-full-width` flag mapping to the existing schema field; specify that use_full_width suppresses the drawn centreline.

findings.title: The legitimate double-apex line renders amber, not the book's green
findings.claim: Colour law v2 maps 'clean with failed checks' to contained/amber. A double-apex line by the design's own definition fails the single-steering-input / out-in-out check class, and `expect_fail` is specified only as a test oracle — no document says expected failures are excluded from quality(). The linked-turns case received an explicit chain-aware path to green; the double-apex case has no analogue, so the figure's headline green line plausibly bakes amber, violating the book's colouring and the 'correctly-shaped line in the wrong colour is a failure' rule.
findings.evidence: 06 §5.1: 'contained if outcome = clean with failed checks' → amber; 01 §5: double apex 'requires by definition at least one mid-corner correction'; 03 §6 `expect_fail` is 'the oracle mechanism' (09 §4); contrast 04 §5: linked lines are 'graded by a chain-aware check set … maps to green' — no equivalent sentence exists for solveDoubleApex (04 §4.4 mentions only shrinking `expect_fail` declarations); 01 §3: 'a correctly-shaped line in the wrong colour is a failure'.
findings.improvement: Specify a double-apex-aware check set: when a line is solved `style=double_apex` and meets the two-minima acceptance criterion, `single_input`/`out_in_out` read `na` (like `late_apex` on increasing radius), so verdict and colour reach green on merit.

findings.title: Verdict, labels, and markers cannot represent two apexes in one corner
findings.claim: On the one-arc horseshoe (one minted corner), the result contract records exactly one turn_in_s/apex_s/apex_pct/apex_f per corner, so the second touch — the property 01 makes a solver acceptance criterion — is unrecordable in the verdict. Label sugar `apex:c1` resolves against 'the good line's solved apex' (singular; ambiguous between two f-minima), and no anchor grammar addresses apex-1 vs apex-2, the mistake line's apex ('typical late apex'), or its forced second turn point ('Houston, we have a problem'). The marker data source (events vs verdict) is unspecified; if verdict-sourced, the figure loses the turn-point-2 and apex-2 markers entirely.
findings.evidence: 05 §6.3 corners: 'turn_in_s, apex_s, apex_pct, apex_f' — singular fields; 01 §5: 'a solved double-apex plan must produce two distinct lane-fraction minima; this is a solver acceptance criterion'; 03 §8 / 04 §7 labels: corner-relative anchors 'plus apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's solved apex'; 01 §4.1 defines apex as 'a measured minimum' (one); 06 §3.1 stage 9 names marker glyphs but not their data source. Book figure labels: 'turn point 1/2', 'apex 1/2', 'typical late apex', 'Houston, we have a problem'.
findings.improvement: Add a per-corner `touches: [{turn_in_s, apex_s, apex_pct, apex_f}, …]` array to the verdict, emit one apex/turn_in event per touch (markers defined as event-sourced), and extend anchors: `apex:c1#1`, `apex:c1#2`, plus line-scoped anchors (`<line_name>.apex`, `<line_name>.turn_in#2`) for annotating mistake-line features.

findings.title: solveDoubleApex is one sentence, with contradictory corner targeting
findings.claim: The solver that produces fig 8.5's entire green line is specified as 'the planned two-touch line with its ascending gentlest-decel scan' — no search space, no placement strategy for the two turn-ins, no parameters, no scene knobs, no worked recipe (it appears in none of 04 §8's R1–R6 nor 08 §6's a–f), so the cold-start bar is unreachable for the one style this figure needs and an implementer must invent the solver. Separately, scene `ride` says `corner=<id>` (default first) while 08's recipe (d) says a bare run on a multi-corner road chain-solves automatically — so on the two-arc composition (which matches the figure's straight-top geometry and mints c1,c2) it is undefined whether `style=double_apex` attempts two touches inside c1 alone, spans the sequence, or should be abandoned for chainedSolve with different verdict semantics.
findings.evidence: 04 §4.4 (the full solveDoubleApex spec is one clause); 01 §5 'to be validated in implementation, not assumed'; 04 §7: 'corner=<id> (default first)'; 08 §6(d): 'a chained ideal line (solved corner-by-corner)' from a bare `run`; 03 §2: corner ids 'minted in segment order' — two arcs mint two corners; 08 §2 cold-start bar.
findings.improvement: Specify solveDoubleApex to the same depth as §4.1–4.3: candidate space for both turn-ins, the inter-touch drift mechanism, acceptance (two minima with a minimum separation), multi-corner behaviour, and add a worked recipe plus a fig-8.5 road preset (e.g. `bookHorseshoe: lane 3.5 | S 10 | L 18 ^200 | S 12`, suggested entry) to 03 §3.1.

findings.title: Wide-outcome lines: is the ridden save in the shipped trajectory?
findings.claim: The book draws the red line's save — 'yikes! braking AND increasing lean' — as part of the path, ending on-road. linelab defines `wide` as 'ran wide but a feasible add-lean corrective exists' and describes the corrective as a solver feasibility shot, yet also gives the rider a reaction delay 'used by run-wide correction' and a `correction` event kind — leaving unspecified whether the shipped trajectory is the uncorrected drift (line visibly departs the lane; corrective exists only in the verdict) or the plan-plus-ridden-corrective (line bends back, as the book draws). The two readings produce visibly different red lines at exactly the figure's annotated spot.
findings.evidence: 02 §7: 'wide — ran wide but a feasible add-lean corrective exists'; 04 §4.3: 'the corrective-action solver (the "can this run-wide be saved?" shot)'; 02 §3: 't_react_s is the recognition delay used by run-wide correction'; 05 §5 event kinds include `run_wide_detect`, `correction`; 05 §6.3 corners carry 'corrective | null'. No doc states which trajectory ships.
findings.improvement: Pin it in 02/05: the shipped trajectory is the integrated plan only; the corrective is a separate, optionally-rendered overlay (or: after `run_wide_detect` + t_react the engine rides the corrective and marks it with `correction` events). Either answer works; the contract must choose.

findings.title: One-arc vs two-arc road composition is undecidable and changes semantics
findings.claim: The figure's road (two bends joined by a short straight top) is naturally two arc segments, but composing it that way mints two corners and silently reclassifies the lesson as linked turns (chain-aware verdict, per-corner mistakes scope, different label vocabulary), while one 200-degree arc keeps one corner but collides with the single-apex-slot contracts. The docs offer no guidance on which composition a double-apex lesson should use, and the resulting figures differ in verdict, colour, labels, and markers.
findings.evidence: 03 §2: derived corners list, 'ids minted in segment order'; 04 §5 chain-aware grading vs 01 §5 double-apex doctrine as a single-corner concept ('Corners that require two or more apexes'); book fig 8.5 road shape (straightish top between bends).
findings.improvement: Specify a corner-merging rule (adjacent same-hand arcs separated by a straight shorter than a threshold coalesce into one corner for doctrine purposes, or an explicit `corner_group` annotation), and state which composition the fig-8.5 example scene uses and why.

findings.title: Scene bake behaviour on a per-line solver failure is unspecified
findings.claim: When one scene line's solve returns a typed refusal (the fast-entry single-apex line hitting the feasibility probe, or solveDoubleApex failing its two-minima criterion), the docs do not say whether `scene` fails the whole bake, emits a partial figure missing that line, or which exit code applies — the exit table covers `solve` (exit 3 non-clean) but not scene lines. Relatedly, a `plan <file.json>` scene line embeds a scenario carrying its own road, colliding with the one-road-per-figure rule with no specified resolution — the only scene rung that could smuggle in `use_full_width` is undefined.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 verb table (`scene`) and §3.1 exit codes (no scene-line case); 04 §7 typed errors are specified for scene syntax only; 03 §8 / 04 §7 `plan <file.json>` 'an explicit wire scenario included as a line' vs 05 §7 'One road per figure. Lines that need different roads are different figures.'
findings.improvement: Specify: a scene line whose solve refuses produces a bake error naming the line (exit 3) unless the line carries `optional=true`; a `plan` line's embedded road must hash-equal the figure's road or the bake rejects with a typed SCHEMA error.

findings.title: No figure orientation control; entry chip not suppressible
findings.claim: Roads start at the origin heading +x, and ViewSpec offers mode/window/compression only — no rotation or mirroring — so the recreated horseshoe cannot match the book's enter-bottom-right/exit-bottom-left layout; the frame also always carries the entry annotation speed chip, which fig 8.5 lacks. Neither affects correctness, but both are visible deltas the vision-judge parity leg will notice.
findings.evidence: 03 §2: 'The road starts at the origin heading +x'; 06 §2.1 ViewSpec fields (no rotation); 06 §2.4: 'the frame edge carries an entry annotation — an inbound arrow with a speed chip'. Book figure orientation and absence of any speed chip.
findings.improvement: Add `rotate_deg` (and optionally `flip`) to ViewSpec — pure rigid transforms that cannot violate P1–P6 — and make the entry annotation suppressible (`entry_chip=off`) in the view spec.

wins: The marker vocabulary is literally the book's: fig 8.5's green hourglasses at turn points and rings at apexes match linelab's carried hourglass/ring/dot glyphs (06 §3.1 stage 9), and `marks: all` extends them to the red line as the book requires.

Colour law v2 was designed for exactly this figure pattern: a failing second strategy 'renders red on its own merits' with no special slot (01 §3, 06 §5.1), and fig 8.4/8.5's two-strategy figure is named first-class authoring (01 §9).

The Tier 1R run-wide slice makes the 'yikes! braking AND increasing lean' physics honestly emergent rather than asserted: braking past A_SU_ONSET at lean widens, and the point-of-no-return (~5.4 m/s² street, 02 §5.3) leaves headroom below it for a successful add-lean save — the book's salvage is representable physics, and the commanded-vs-delivered sample pair (05 §2.1) makes the fight visible in the controls strip.

The U-turn refusal is a conjunction (sweep ≥ 170° AND r ≤ 15 m, 02 §7 / 03 §3.1), so a 200-degree R18 horseshoe is legitimately in scope — the scope cut was drafted precisely enough not to exclude fig 8.5's geometry.
Sight rays appear only when occluders are present (08 §6e), so the recreation automatically omits them exactly as the book's fig 8.5 does — no configuration needed.

The diagram projection handles this figure gently and verifiably: sweep angle is preserved exactly (the ~200° reads as ~200°), the short straights compress, auto width_exag is mild on a compact R18 corner, and the proportion-gate bands (06 §6.1) plausibly pass — the compactness machinery designed against fig 8.1-class defects carries over cleanly.

The explicit-plan rung (04 §2c) is a genuine escape hatch: the red line, once hand-tuned, is fully expressible (two turn_ins + mid-corner brake), and identical-citizenship (05 §7) then makes it steppable and per-sample inspectable like any good line — the failure of the one-liner paths is an authoring gap, not an engine gap.

verdicts.title: No designed author path for fig 8.5's red line (believed-road / best-failing-attempt gap)
verdicts.note: The nucleus survives: no one-liner produces the red line — solve refuses infeasible placements ('short-circuits with a typed infeasible reason', 04 §4.2), suggestTurnIn returns typed failures for empty/non-clean bands (04 §3.4), chop compiles 'against the figure's first ride line' (04 §7) i.e. the double-apex reference, early_apex is pinned 'runoff' (03 §7.1), and no 'believed-road' or 'accept best failing attempt' mode exists anywhere in the set — yet 06 §5.1 promises 'a single-apex line on a double-apex corner' renders red with no solver mechanism behind it. But the BLOCKER verdict ('G7's scene cannot be shipped as designed') fails: (a) the scene `plan <file.json>` rung (04 §7, 03 §8) admits an explicit wire plan with mid-corner brake + re-lean actions, with `expect_fail` (03 §6) covering legitimate non-clean lines — G7 requires 'a scene file', not one-liners; (b) the non-clean render path is designed, not an 'undesigned sliver': 04 §4.2 explicitly specifies railing 'cleanly to a bound when a target is unreachable' and 'a non-clean self-verification is reported as such (and still renders)'; (c) the 'docs internally disagree' framing overreads mechanism language — 02 §5.6 lists 'the chop mistake and fig 8.5's failed single-apex strategy' as two distinct things, and 01 §4.3 says chop is 'the mechanism behind fig 8.5's failed line', consistent with 01 §5's strategy description. Real severity: major authoring/recipe gap, not blocker.

verdicts.title: sweep cannot sweep entry speed
verdicts.note: 08 §3 defines sweep's path grammar exclusively as `--param plan.<id>.<field>` ('id-addressed, never array-indexed'); entry speed is `rider.start.speed_kmh` (03 §6) / `entry_kmh` solve input (04 §2a) / `--entry` flag (08 §4.1) — not a plan action, so structurally unreachable by the grammar. No other doc adds a sweep surface (compare diffs pre-run envelopes; 04 §3's coarse sweep is internal to suggestTurnIn). The book's 'Arc = Speed' (ch.8 text line 63) and the slow-in doctrine make entry speed the doctrinally central exploration variable; the only recourse is manually re-running run/solve per speed, exactly as claimed. Major is fair given 08 §2's agent-first design bar.

verdicts.title: use_full_width is unreachable from scene text and CLI flags
verdicts.note: Verified across all ten docs: `use_full_width` exists only in the wire road object (03 §6); 03 §3 excludes it from the DSL ('deliberately not DSL-expressible'); the scene `road:` key takes only '<road-DSL line> | preset <name>' (04 §7) and presets expand to 'a road DSL string' (03 §3.1); 08 §4.1's flag list omits it. Book figs 8.4 and 8.5 (images verified) are full-width with no centreline, while 06 §3.1 stage 3 draws 'centreline and edge lines per the road spec' — so a scene-baked recreation is lane-confined with a centreline, and G7's test is explicitly 'from a scene file' (01 §2). One caveat that does not defeat the finding: 08 §4.1 also states 'Anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON and vice versa', so the flag-list omission may be incompleteness rather than designed unreachability — but the G7 vehicle is `scene`, which cannot express it regardless.

verdicts.title: The legitimate double-apex line renders amber, not the book's green
verdicts.note: 06 §5.1: contained (amber) 'if outcome = violation, or outcome = clean with failed checks'; 02 §7 defines clean as 'all checks pass', so a contained double-apex line failing any check lands `violation` → amber either way. 01 §5: double apex 'requires by definition at least one mid-corner correction' and the book text (line 103) agrees — so single-input/out-in-out-class checks fail. `expect_fail` is wired only into the test oracle (03 §6 'the oracle mechanism', 09 §4); no doc feeds it into quality() or the colour mapping. The asymmetry is real: linked lines got an explicit chain-aware path to green (04 §5 'that chain-aware verdict maps to green'); no analogous sentence exists for double apex anywhere (checked 01 §5, 04 §4.4, 05 §6.2, 06 §5.1 — 04 §4.4 mentions only shrinking expect_fail declarations). Book draws the line green; 01 §3: 'a correctly-shaped line in the wrong colour is a failure'.

verdicts.title: Verdict, labels, and markers cannot represent two apexes in one corner
verdicts.note: 05 §6.3 corners carry singular 'turn_in_s, apex_s, apex_pct, apex_f' per corner while 01 §5 makes 'two distinct lane-fraction minima' a solver acceptance criterion — the second touch has no verdict field. 01 §4.1 defines apex as 'a measured minimum' (singular), and label sugar is 'apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's solved apex' (04 §7, 03 §8) — singular and good-line-only, so the mistake line's 'typical late apex' and apex-1 vs apex-2 are unaddressable by the anchor grammar (only raw entry/mid/exit±offset hand-placement remains, which requires knowing emergent positions in advance). 06 §3.1 stage 9 names marker glyphs but no data source; 07 §3.1 confirms events drive viewer ticks but nothing binds figure markers to events vs verdict. No refutation found in 05 §5 (events) or 07.

verdicts.title: solveDoubleApex is one sentence, with contradictory corner targeting
verdicts.note: 04 §4.4's entire spec is the parenthetical clause 'the planned two-touch line with its ascending gentlest-decel scan…' — no search space, placement strategy, parameters, or acceptance procedure beyond 01 §5's two-minima criterion ('to be validated in implementation'). It appears in none of 04 §8's R1–R6 nor 08 §6's (a)–(f) recipes, and 03 §3.1 has no double-apex preset despite G6 requiring 'a worked DSL example' per archetype — so the 08 §2 cold-start bar has nothing to stand on for this style.
