The targeting contradiction is real: 04 §7 gives `ride` 'corner=<id> (default first)' while 08 §6(d) says a bare run on a multi-corner road yields 'a chained ideal line (solved corner-by-corner)'; with 03 §2 minting one corner per arc, a two-arc horseshoe leaves style=double_apex semantics (two touches in c1? span? chainedSolve?) undefined.

verdicts.title: Wide-outcome lines: is the ridden save in the shipped trajectory?
verdicts.note: The tension is verbatim in the docs: 02 §7 defines `wide` by counterfactual feasibility ('ran wide but a feasible add-lean corrective exists', the 'can this run-wide be saved?' shot of 04 §4.3), yet 02 §3 gives the rider a reaction delay 'used by run-wide correction' and 05 §5 includes a `correction` event kind, and 05 §6.3 carries 'corrective | null' — implying a ridden correction can appear in a trajectory. Grep across all ten docs for corrective/correction/save confirms no sentence states whether the shipped samples are the uncorrected drift or plan-plus-ridden-save. The book draws the save as part of the red path ('yikes! braking AND increasing lean', on-road exit), so the two readings produce visibly different lines at the figure's annotated spot.

verdicts.title: One-arc vs two-arc road composition is undecidable and changes semantics
verdicts.note: 03 §2 mints one corner per arc segment, so the two-arc composition creates c1,c2 and triggers linked-sequence machinery (chained solving per 08 §6(d), chain-aware grading per 04 §5, per-corner mistake scope per 03 §7.2), while a single 200° arc keeps one corner but hits the singular apex-slot contracts (05 §6.3). No doc gives composition guidance for a double-apex lesson, and — reinforcing the gap — 03 §3.1 contains presets for every other special-case archetype (bookDecreasing, bookEsses, bookHairpin, bookBlind) but none for double apex, despite 01 §2 G6's test that 'every archetype in §5 has a worked DSL example'. Minor severity is appropriate.

verdicts.title: Scene bake behaviour on a per-line solver failure is unspecified
verdicts.note: 08 §3.1's exit table covers `run`, `solve` (exit 3 non-clean), bad input (2), and write failures (1), but no case for a scene line whose solve returns NO_SOLUTION mid-bake, and 04 §7's typed scene errors cover syntax/placement only ('offending token and 1-based line number'); whether `scene` fails whole, emits a partial figure, or which exit applies is genuinely unstated. On the plan-line road collision: 03 §8 does say 'each line resolves to a full Scenario (§6) sharing the figure's road', which establishes the figure road governs — but the wire schema makes `road` required in the embedded scenario (03 §6) and no doc specifies whether a differing embedded road is rejected or silently overridden (the latter off-brand under D8's typed-rejection culture), so 'no specified resolution' stands in substance. Minor severity fits.

verdicts.title: No figure orientation control; entry chip not suppressible
verdicts.note: 03 §2: 'The road starts at the origin heading +x'; 06 §2.1's ViewSpec is exactly {mode, window, width_exag, straight_compress, taper_compress} — no rotation or mirroring, and grep across all docs finds no other orientation surface (07 §6.3's viewer controls are cursor/focus/lock/mode only; 05 §7 meta.view defers to 06's vocabulary). 06 §2.4 states the cropped frame 'carries an entry annotation — an inbound arrow with a speed chip' with no suppression option, and the book fig 8.5 image (verified) has no chip and enters bottom-right/exits bottom-left. Polish severity is right: 06 §7's parity bar asks for an 'equivalent', not an identical layout, but both deltas are visible to the 09 §7 vision-judge leg exactly as claimed.

result.walkthrough:
STEP 0 — What the book figure actually contains (viewed fig-08.06__linked-turns.jpeg, ~600x1000 portrait): a dark full-width road snaking top-to-bottom through four alternating bends with white EDGE lines only — no centreline. Two solid lines run the whole chain: red (early turn points) and green (delayed), both with arrowheads exiting the bottom. Both lines carry per-corner hourglass turn-point markers and ring apex markers in their own colour (red pairs and green pairs at each annotated corner), plus ~12 callout boxes with leader lines pointing at specific markers ("early turn point", "delayed apex", "incorrect line causes exit of turn to aim at outside of turn", "incorrect line causes an early turn point, which forces a large steering input", "correct line flows smoothly from turn to turn"). No sight rays, no occluders, no exit dots. Chapter text: "A mistake on the initial turn gets amplified with each successive turn."

STEP 1 — Cold start per 08 §2: `linelab schema scene`, `schema road-dsl`, `schema mistakes`, `schema view`. The scene grammar (04 §7), DSL (03 §3), and the mistakes teaching table (early_apex → "turned in too soon, runs wide" → fig 8.1/8.2) are all reachable; `scope=all_corners` is spellable in the scene mistake line per 04 §7. First guess: nothing in the schema surface maps any kind to fig 8.6 — the chained device is found only by knowing 03 §7.2 exists.

STEP 2 — Road. `preset bookEsses` = `lane 3.5 | S 8 | L 12 ^75 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75 | S 10` — three corners, starts left-hand; the book draws four alternating bends starting right-hand. Guessed a custom DSL instead: `lane 3.5 | S 8 | R 14 ^80 | L 14 ^80 | R 14 ^80 | L 14 ^80 | S 10` (sweeps and radii guessed from the art).

STEP 3 — Authored scene file (the ≤6-line bar blows out to ~16 lines with labels):
```
road:  lane 3.5 | S 8 | R 14 ^80 | L 14 ^80 | R 14 ^80 | L 14 ^80 | S 10
lines:
  good: ride entry=32 turnIn=auto
  bad:  mistake early_apex scope=all_corners
marks: all
labels:
  entry:c1 "delayed turn point"
  mid:c1-8 "early turn point"          # guessing metres to sit near the red marker
  mid:c1+4 "early apex"
  exit:c1  "incorrect line causes exit of turn to aim at outside of turn"
  ...
view:  mode=diagram window=auto
note:  "Linked Turns — a mistake on the initial turn gets amplified with each successive turn"
```
Then `linelab scene fig-08-06.scene --out out/`.

STEP 4 — Immediate wall: the book road is FULL-WIDTH with no centreline. `use_full_width` exists only on the wire-schema road object (03 §6); it is "deliberately not DSL-expressible" (03 §3), the scene `road:` key takes only DSL-or-preset (04 §7), and 08 §4.1's flag list has no flag for it despite claiming "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag... and vice versa". The JSON detour (explicit scenario with use_full_width + `mistake --on` + `render`) forfeits labels/marks entirely — `render` (08 §3) has no annotation flags; labels and marks live only on the scene-authored Figure (03 §8). So as designed I must ship a half-road, centreline-painted figure — visibly not the book's.

STEP 5 — Solving the green line. The scene `ride` grammar has `corner=<id> (default first)` and `style=single|double_apex|geometric` — no chained spelling; whether `ride entry=32` on a 4-corner road invokes `chainedSolve` (04 §5) or solves c1 only is a guess. If chained: 04 §5 gives one paragraph; the single-corner machinery it "reuses" has a roll-on bracket of +35..+90 m past turn-in (04 §4.1) on corners whose arcs are ~19.5 m with zero gaps, a brake_gap of 4 m before turn-in that cannot exist between abutting corners without braking at lean (which arms the 02 §5 stand-up slice: decel bracket 2.4–3.8 m/s² vs A_SU_ONSET 2.5), and a suggestTurnIn sweep reaching 24 m back into the previous corner. Whether the green line even solves is not derivable; no chained golden exists (02 §8 goldens are all single-corner C30).

STEP 6 — The red line. `compileMistake("early_apex", {}, {scope:"all_corners"})`: at corner 1, turn in 5 m early with an "auto-derived largest inside-kissing lean" (03 §7.1). For corners 2–4 the design says each perturbation is "seeded by the emergent state of the mistaken line through the corner before" (03 §7.2) with mechanics "living with chainedSolve in 04" — but 04 §5 only restates the sentence. Unanswered: what station is corner-n's perturbed turn-in when the good turn-in no longer matches the mistaken entry? Against which entry state is the inside-kissing lean derived (deriving from the mistaken state requires interleaved engine runs — a solve, inside the "compiler")? What happens when the mistaken line sits outside the corridor at that station? Does the one-perturbation diff property (03 §7) survive N rewritten turn_ins? Also 02 §7 lists "road/corner end" as a termination cause without saying when corner-end termination is armed — read literally, the red line could terminate at corner 1's end. Encouragingly, runoff is NOT a termination reason, and on alternating esses the "outside" you drift to is the next corner's inside — so compounding is physically plausible; but nothing in 09 pins it (the mistake oracle covers one preset per kind, single corner; A-CHAIN-VIS is the only chain acceptance test).

STEP 7 — Verdicts/colour. Red line: wide/runoff → red per 06 §5.1 — fine. Green line: 04 §5 asserts the chain-aware check set "(containment + link-continuity + flow)" maps to green, but no such check ids exist in 05 §6.2's pinned v2 list, 01 §5 names none, and the trigger rule (which lines get chain grading) is unstated — the green promise is asserted, not derivable from quality() = clean + zero failed checks.

STEP 8 — Bake and gate. Working the numbers from the design's own constants: the 4-corner chain (~66 m centreline, 7 m road) lays out diagonally from origin heading +x (no rotation control exists in ViewSpec, 06 §2.1); straights compress 18 m→3.6 m; auto width_exag solves only width_ratio ≥ 0.55 (06 §2.3) giving exag ≈ 1.1; bounding frame ≈ 67×54 m ⇒ frame_aspect ≈ 1.24 (in band — but landscape-diagonal, not the book's 0.6 portrait, which the band also admits) and road_ink ≈ 0.14–0.15 vs the 0.25 floor ⇒ gate FAIL ⇒ export exits non-zero (06 §6.2). Manual width_exag ≈ 1.8 scrapes ink to ~0.25 while pushing width_ratio to ~0.9 — a knife-edge the auto path never finds, and the warn-vs-fail "hard bounds"/"margin zones" split is never numerically defined. Even 09 §5.3's own preset-in-true-mode round-trip fails on bookEsses by this arithmetic. Final rendered differences from the book even if everything passes: centreline painted, lines confined to half the road, marks:auto would have hidden all red-line markers (marks:all needed, and it adds exit dots the book lacks), labels leader to road stations not to the red line's markers, red line drawn short-dashed (role law 06 §5.2) where the book's is solid, and orientation rotated ~90°.

findings.title: Full-width road unreachable from every figure-authoring surface
findings.claim: Fig 8.6 (and most Ch.8 art) draws a full-width road with no centreline and lines using the whole carriageway, but the only switch for this — use_full_width — cannot be expressed anywhere a figure can be authored: not in the road DSL, not in scene text, not in a preset, not as a CLI flag. The JSON escape hatch (explicit wire scenario) exists but the render verb accepts no labels or marks, which live only on the scene-authored Figure — so no documented path produces the book's full-width, annotated figure. The scene bake would emit a half-road, centreline-painted figure that is materially not the book diagram, defeating G7 for this figure.
findings.evidence: Book image fig-08.06 (no centreline, full-width usage). 03 §2: "use_full_width: true opts into the full carriageway"; 03 §3: "bike_margin_m, use_full_width, and ds_m are deliberately not DSL-expressible"; 04 §7: "road: <road-DSL line> | preset <name>"; 03 §3.1 presets expand to "a road DSL string plus, where noted, occluders" (no width flag); 08 §4.1 flag list omits it while claiming "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag" and "Anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON and vice versa" — an internal contradiction; 08 §3 render verb: "--views ... --mode ... --at ... --out" (no labels/marks); 03 §8: labels/marks are Figure fields. 06 §3.1 stage 3 draws "centreline and edge lines per the road spec" with no stated suppression under full-width.
findings.improvement: Add road-option keys to scene text (e.g. a `road_opts: full_width bike_margin=0.3` line or DSL-reserved tokens), a --use-full-width CLI flag, and define lane-marking rendering under use_full_width (edge lines only). Alternatively let `render` accept a sidecar annotation spec so the JSON path can carry labels/marks.

findings.title: Chained-mistake seeding (scope=all_corners) is one sentence, not a mechanism
findings.claim: The fig 8.6 device — the same perturbation applied at every corner, each "seeded by the emergent state of the mistaken line through the corner before" — is promised in three documents but specified in none. For early_apex the compile needs, per corner n>1: the perturbed turn-in station when the good line's solved turn-in no longer matches the mistaken entry state; the entry state against which the "auto-derived largest inside-kissing lean" is derived (deriving it from the mistaken state requires interleaved engine probes — a solver embedded in the "compiler", crossing the compiler/solver boundary); behaviour when the mistaken line sits outside the corridor at the perturbed station; and whether the one-perturbation diff property survives N rewritten turn_in actions. Separately, 02 §7 lists "road/corner end" as a termination cause without saying when corner-end termination applies — read literally, the mistaken line could terminate at corner 1's end instead of compounding. Whether "each corner wider" actually emerges is asserted, never pinned: the mistake oracle covers single-corner presets only and no chained-mistake fixture exists in 09.
findings.evidence: 03 §7.2: "each corner's perturbation seeded by the emergent state of the mistaken line through the corner before... Per-corner compile order and seeding mechanics live with chainedSolve in 04-solver-and-authoring.md"; 04 §5's entire treatment: "the perturbation is applied at each corner in sequence, each seeded by the mistaken line's own emergent state, so the error compounds corner-over-corner exactly as fig 8.6 teaches" — a restatement, not mechanics. 03 §7.1 early_apex: "auto-derived largest inside-kissing lean if lean_deg omitted". 03 §7: "a diff between good and mistake lines isolates precisely the intended delta". 02 §7: "Termination precedence per step: crash → stopped (v < v_floor_ms) → road/corner end → runaway guards". 09 §4: oracle is "one per kind", no chained entry; §3.5's only chain test is A-CHAIN-VIS.
findings.improvement: Specify the incremental compile loop: integrate the mistaken line to corner n's perturbed turn-in station (define it as good turn-in − early_by_m, clamped into corner n's approach), derive the committed lean from the actual state via a bounded probe, emit a typed error (NO_SOLUTION sub-reason) when derivation fails; restate the one-perturbation rule for chained scope; state that chained runs always integrate to road end; add a chained early_apex oracle fixture on bookEsses pinning per-corner apex_f monotonically worsening.

findings.title: chainedSolve is uninvocable from scene text and its constants contradict zero-gap esses
findings.claim: The scene ride grammar offers no way to request chain solving — `corner=<id>` defaults to the FIRST corner and the style set is single|double_apex|geometric — so whether `ride entry=32` on a multi-corner road chains or solves c1 alone is a guess. And the machinery chainedSolve "reuses" carries single-corner constants that cannot fit the very preset named for fig 8.6: the roll-on bisection bracket (+35..+90 m past turn-in) exceeds the entire ~15.7 m arc of a bookEsses corner and lands inside the next corner; brake_gap (braking complete 4 m before turn-in) is impossible between abutting corners without braking at lean, which arms the run-wide slice (decel bracket 2.4–3.8 m/s² straddles A_SU_ONSET 2.5); the suggestTurnIn sweep (s0 − 24 m) reaches into the previous corner's arc where a `tangent_inside` target is undefined mid-opposite-corner. No chained golden pins any of this — every golden in 02 §8 is single-corner.
findings.evidence: 04 §7: "corner=<id> (default first)", "style=single|double_apex|geometric"; 04 §4.1: "roll-on bracket +35 … +90 m past turn-in", "brake_gap 4 m", "decel bracket 2.4–3.8 m/s²"; 02 §5.2: "A_SU_ONSET 2.5 m/s² — decel below this never stands the bike up"; 03 §3.1 bookEsses: "L 12 ^75 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75" — "zero inter-corner straights" (arc ≈ 15.7 m); 04 §3: sweep "from corner.s0 − 24 m"; 02 §8: goldens C30/C30-chop/C30-trailbrake/C30-DR, none chained; 04 §5 says only "Carried shape: ... solved corner-by-corner".
findings.improvement: Define the chain trigger (multi-corner road ⇒ chainedSolve unless corner= narrows it; or add style=chain). Specify the chain-adapted action template: per-corner brackets scaled to available inter-corner span, explicit rule for when roll-on is omitted, and whether inter-corner braking is allowed below A_SU_ONSET. Add a bookEsses golden (solved plan stations, per-corner apex_pct, outcome) to 02 §8/09 §3.2.

findings.title: Chain-aware verdict is asserted green but its checks do not exist
findings.claim: The design promises the linked good line grades green via a "chain-aware check set (containment + link-continuity + flow)", but no such check ids appear in the pinned checks_version:2 list, no arithmetic is given, and no rule states which lines are graded chain-aware (by road corner count? by solve kind? what about an explicit-plan line on a multi-corner road?). Under 06 §5.1 green requires outcome=clean and zero failed checks; how the carried single-corner checks (late-apex, out-in-out) read on corners whose exits are deliberately sacrificed is unstated — an implementer inventing this decides the figure's central colour outcome.
findings.evidence: 04 §5: "graded by a chain-aware check set (containment + link-continuity + flow) rather than the single-corner clean bar. Under colour law v2 (D9) that chain-aware verdict maps to green"; 05 §6.2: "check ids (v2): the carried line-selection checks + stop_within_sight + hold_wide_for_sight, checks_version: 2" — no link-continuity or flow id; 01 §5 linked-turns bullet requires chained grading but names no ids; 06 §5.1: "good if outcome = clean and no doctrine check failed".
findings.improvement: Name the chain checks (e.g. link_continuity, chain_flow), their arithmetic and evidence fields in 05 §6.2 (bumping checks_version), define the applicability rule (a line whose trajectory spans >1 corner is graded per-corner with exit-sacrifice checks replacing out_in_out on non-final corners), and state how single-corner checks read (na) on chained lines.

findings.title: Proportion gate road_ink fails multi-corner chains and no authorable lever fixes it
findings.claim: Worked from the design's own constants, a 3–4 corner esses figure lands road_ink ≈ 0.14–0.22 against the 0.25 floor: the chain lays out diagonally from origin heading +x (ViewSpec has no rotation field), the axis-aligned frame wastes its corners, straights are already near-zero so straight compression gains nothing, and auto width_exag stops at the smallest factor satisfying width_ratio ≥ 0.55 — far short of ink compliance, while pushing exag high enough for ink (~1.8×) drives width_ratio to the 0.95 edge. Gate fail exits non-zero, so the flagship linked figure cannot be exported on the default path; even 09 §5.3's requirement that presets land "near the proportion bands" in true mode fails on bookEsses by this arithmetic. Additionally the gate's two-tier semantics ("fail outside hard bounds; warn in the margin zones") reference margin zones that are never numerically defined — §6.1 gives one band per metric.
findings.evidence: 06 §6.1: road_ink "0.25 – 0.60", frame_aspect "0.55 – 1.8"; 06 §2.1 ViewSpec fields (mode, window, width_exag, straight_compress, taper_compress — no rotation); 06 §2.3: "pick the smallest factor such that ... ≥ WIDTH_RATIO_TARGET = 0.55"; 06 §6.2: "fail outside hard bounds → the export command exits non-zero" vs "warn in the margin zones" with no second band anywhere; 03 §3.1 bookEsses geometry (≈65 m centreline, 7 m road ⇒ drawn road area ≈ 355–465 m² in a ≈1600–3600 m² frame); 09 §5.3: "each book preset rendered in true mode must already land near the proportion bands". Book fig 8.6 is 0.6-aspect portrait — inside the frame_aspect band, but linelab can only produce the ~1.2–1.5 landscape-diagonal layout.
findings.improvement: Add auto-orientation to the projection (rotate drawn frame to the road's principal axis, or an explicit ViewSpec rotate/orient field) so chains fill a portrait frame like the book's; define a chain-figure gate profile (or make road_ink scale with corner count); publish the warn-vs-fail band pairs; verify bookEsses against the gate numerically in 09 §5.3.

findings.title: marks: auto|all is too coarse for the book's marker set
findings.claim: Fig 8.6's teaching depends on turn-point and apex markers on BOTH lines at every corner; the default marks:auto draws good-line marks only, silently producing a figure missing every red marker the callouts point at. marks:all fixes that but adds exit dots the book never draws, and there is no per-line or per-marker-type selection to match the book exactly.
findings.evidence: 04 §7: "marks: auto | all # optional (default auto: good-line marks)"; 03 §8: "marks (auto | all) controls turn-point/apex/exit markers"; book image: red and green hourglass+ring pairs at each corner, no exit dots.
findings.improvement: Extend marks to a selective grammar, e.g. `marks: turn_in,apex @all-lines` or per-line `marks=` overrides on line entries, keeping auto/all as sugar.

findings.title: Labels cannot anchor to the mistake line's markers
findings.claim: Most of fig 8.6's callouts point at the RED line's markers ("early turn point", "early apex", "incorrect line causes..."), but label anchors are corner-relative road stations and the apex: sugar resolves against the good line's solved apex only — there is no line-qualified anchor, so every red-line callout must be faked with hand-guessed ±offset_m stations whose leader lines point at the road, not the marker.
findings.evidence: 03 §8: "labels are corner-relative callouts (entry|exit|mid:<id> ± m, plus author-layer apex:<id> sugar resolved post-solve); a callout always resolves onto the road"; 04 §7: "apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's solved apex after the engine runs"; book image's leader lines terminate on specific red/green markers.
findings.improvement: Add line-qualified anchors — `apex:c2@bad`, `turn_in:c1@bad` — resolved against the named line's own events post-run, falling back to a typed error if the line lacks the event.

findings.title: Lane fraction f is undefined on straights and at hand flips; rider's-lane side never chosen
findings.claim: f is defined by the corner's inner/outer usable edge, so it has no meaning on the entry straight (where start.f defaults to 1.0) and flips sides discontinuously at every hand change of a zero-gap esses chain — exactly the geometry of the fig 8.6 figure. Separately, no document states which physical side of the two-lane road is "the rider's own lane" (left- vs right-hand traffic), which determines every corner's usable corridor and therefore the entire drawn figure under the lane-constrained default.
findings.evidence: 03 §2: "f = 0 inner usable edge, f = 1 outer usable edge" (hand-dependent by construction) and "the usable corridor is the rider's own lane" with no side convention anywhere in 00–09; 03 §6: "rider.start.f (default 1.0 — the outside usable edge)" on a straight where no corner defines outside; 03 §3.1: bookEsses "zero inter-corner straights" — adjacent opposite-hand corners share a station.
findings.improvement: Define f outside corners (e.g. measured against the NEXT corner's hand, with the flip station pinned at the segment boundary and the discontinuity documented in 05 §2.1), and add a traffic-side config field (default right-hand traffic) to compose.

findings.title: bookEsses is three corners against the book's four-bend chain
findings.claim: The preset advertised as the fig 8.6 road (and used by recipe R4, and implicitly by G7's "shipped example scenes" coverage claim) has three corners starting left-hand, while the book figure draws four alternating bends starting right-hand — the shipped "equivalent" figure drops one full compounding step of the amplification lesson and mirrors the handedness. An author can write a custom DSL, but the design's own parity artifact is short.
findings.evidence: 03 §3.1: bookEsses = "lane 3.5 | S 8 | L 12 ^75 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75 | S 10 ... linked turns, zero inter-corner straights (fig 8.6)"; 04 §8 R4: "preset bookEsses → ... the corner-over-corner amplification figure (fig 8.6 equivalent)"; 01 §2 G7: "the per-figure mapping in §4–§6 is covered by shipped example scenes"; book image: four alternating bends, first annotated corner right-hand, marker pairs at three-plus corners.
findings.improvement: Extend the preset to four corners matching the book's handedness (`lane 3.5 | S 8 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75 | S 10`), or document the deliberate reduction in the preset table and G7 mapping.

findings.title: Role dash law renders the book's solid red line as short-dashed
findings.claim: Every recreated book figure's mistake line will draw short-dashed under the role-dash channel, while the book draws both lines solid and distinguishes by colour alone — a systematic visual departure from the art the parity bar says exports must be judged equivalent to.
findings.evidence: 06 §5.2: "mistake → short dash" (roles render as dash patterns); 06 §7 parity requirement: figures "must read as an equivalent of the book's figure — same ... marker/colour vocabulary"; book fig 8.6: both lines solid with arrowheads.
findings.improvement: Add a view-level `dash=off` (book-parity) toggle that moves the role channel entirely into the legend for exports, with the accessibility default unchanged in the viewer.

wins: Colour law v2 (D9) genuinely fixes the prior 'contained linked good line renders red' defect class structurally — the design names the defect, the mechanism, and the consequence (01 §3, 04 §5, 06 §5.1), and the red mistake line gets red from its own emergent verdict, no painting.

scope=all_corners exists as a first-class concept with scene (`scope=all_corners`), CLI (`early_apex@c1,c2`), and API spellings — the prior design's admitted linked-figure blocker is at least structurally addressed (03 §7.2, 04 §7, 08 §3).

The renderer's device vocabulary maps almost one-to-one onto fig 8.6's visual grammar: grass background, hourglass turn points and ring apexes inheriting line colour, arrowheads, callout boxes with leader lines and repulsion layout (06 §3.1 stages 1, 8–10) — the book's marker language is directly expressible.
Sight rays draw only when occluders are present (08 §6 recipe e, 06 §3.1) — correctly absent from a fig 8.6 recreation, matching the book, with no author action needed.

Runoff is not a termination cause (02 §7), so a failing line integrates the full chain and stays scrubbable/inspectable end to end — the precondition for the compounding red line existing at all, and for D6's per-instant inspection of it.

The alternating-esses physics story is honestly representable: on opposite-hand corners the wide exit becomes the next corner's inside, so the book's amplification mechanic can genuinely emerge from the engine rather than being drawn — the emergent-line invariant (D7) makes the figure a demonstration, not an illustration.

The frame_aspect band 0.55–1.8 (06 §6.1) was actually measured to admit the book's portrait figures — fig 8.6's 0.6 aspect sits inside it, so the gate's aspect metric is not the obstacle (ink and orientation are).

The cold-start surface is real for this task's first half: schema sections for scene, road-dsl, and mistakes exist as a closed list (08 §5.1), and the early_apex-vs-premature naming trap is documented at the API surface (03 §7.1) — an agent picks the right mistake kind for the red line on the first try.

verdicts.title: Full-width road unreachable from every figure-authoring surface
verdicts.note: The authoring gap is real: 03 §3 makes use_full_width "deliberately not DSL-expressible", scene roads are "<road-DSL line> | preset <name>" (04 §7), presets expand to "a road DSL string" (03 §3.1), and labels/marks exist only on the scene-authored Figure (03 §8) while render takes only --views/--mode/--at/--out (08 §3) — so the full-width AND annotated combination has no documented path, and the book image indeed shows a centreline-free road used full-width. But 'blocker / defeats G7' overstates: (a) 08 §4.1's normative rule "Flags mirror schema fields one-to-one... Anything expressible... in JSON [is expressible by flag]" mandates a use_full_width flag — the enumerated list omitting it is the internal contradiction the critic himself quotes, so "cannot be expressed... as a CLI flag" is not doc-proven; and (b) the design's own parity definition (06 §7: "same compact proportions, same marker/colour vocabulary, same annotation devices") and G7's per-figure mapping (01 §5, which maps fig 8.6 to chained solving + chained mistakes) never require full-width usage — lane-constrained is the deliberate doctrinal framing ("the outside of the road is the oncoming lane", 01 §4.2; use_full_width is "track-day framing", 03 §2). Also "half-road" is wrong: the whole two-lane road is drawn; only the lines are confined to one lane. Severity should be major (authoring-surface hole + flag-list contradiction), not blocker.

verdicts.title: Chained-mistake seeding (scope=all_corners) is one sentence, not a mechanism
verdicts.note: The nucleus is confirmed: 03 §7.2 defers "per-corner compile order and seeding mechanics" to 04, and 04 §5's entire chained-mistake treatment is the quoted single restating sentence — none of the listed questions (perturbed turn-in stations for corner n>1, the state against which the auto-derived lean resolves, out-of-corridor behaviour, N-perturbation diff semantics) is answered anywhere in 00–09. Two supporting sub-claims fail, though. The corner-1-termination reading is defeated by the wider contract: the verdict records per-corner exit measurements (05 §6.3 "exit {s, d, f, heading_err_deg}") and every golden has an exit straight (02 §8, C30's 25 m exit), which require integration past corner end — 02 §7's "road/corner end" cannot mean stop-at-first-corner-end. And "no chained-mistake fixture exists in 09" is overstated: 08 §6 states "09 pins each [recipe] as an executable acceptable test" including recipe (d)'s chained early_apex@c1,c2, and 09 §6 names "the largest committed preset figure (the linked-chain fixture)". What survives exactly: the seeding mechanics hole and the fact that no oracle-grade pin asserts per-corner widening (recipe (d)'s expectation is qualitative; 09 §4's oracle is one preset per kind).

verdicts.title: chainedSolve is uninvocable from scene text and its constants contradict zero-gap esses
verdicts.note: Confirmed nucleus: the scene ride grammar has no chain spelling — "corner=<id> (default first)", style ∈ single|double_apex|geometric (04 §7) — which sits in genuine tension with 08 recipe (d), where plain `run --turn-in auto` on a two-corner road yields "a chained ideal line (solved corner-by-corner)"; whether a scene `ride` line chains is unresolvable from the docs. Also confirmed: every 02 §8 golden is single-corner. But the constants argument is constructed, not doc-stated: 04 §5 specifies chainedSolve as its own mechanism — "an ascending decel scan — the gentlest fully-contained decel wins. Coarse per-corner search, full-resolution re-verify" — and never says it inherits solve §4.1's roll-on bracket (+35..+90 m), brake_gap, or suggestTurnIn's s0−24 m sweep; the claimed impossibilities all presuppose that inheritance. "Uninvocable from scene text" is also too strong on the mistake side: 04 §7 explicitly provides `mistake <kind> ... [scope=<cornerId>|all_corners]` in scene text. And chained coverage is not zero: A-CHAIN-VIS solves "the blind-esses fixture" chain-wide (09 §3.5) and the linked-chain preset figure is a committed fixture (09 §6). Ambiguity finding stands; the numeric-contradiction half does not.

verdicts.title: Chain-aware verdict is asserted green but its checks do not exist
verdicts.note: Verified across the whole set. 04 §5 promises "a chain-aware check set (containment + link-continuity + flow)" mapping to green, but 05 §6.2's pinned v2 id list is only "the carried line-selection checks + stop_within_sight + hold_wide_for_sight" — no link-continuity or flow id, no arithmetic anywhere. Worse, the docs give three inconsistent answers to the chained line's colour: 04 §5 says green; 06 §5.1's arithmetic ("good if outcome = clean and no doctrine check failed") makes a line that is "contained, not clean" (04 §5's own words) amber; 01 §3 hedges "renders amber or green per its verdict". No document states which lines are graded chain-aware (by corner count, solve kind, or for explicit plans on multi-corner roads), and no rule says how carried single-corner checks (late_apex, out_in_out) read on deliberately sacrificed exits. An implementer genuinely decides the flagship figure's central colour. Major is the right severity.

verdicts.title: Proportion gate road_ink fails multi-corner chains and no authorable lever fixes it
verdicts.note: The default-path arithmetic checks out: bookEsses (7 m road, R12 corners) has width_ratio 7/12 ≈ 0.58 ≥ 0.55, so auto width_exag ≈ 1 (06 §2.3 picks "the smallest factor"); the L-R-L chain zigzags diagonally from origin (+x start, 03 §2; ViewSpec has no rotation field, 06 §2.1); independent re-computation gives road_ink ≈ 0.19–0.22 vs the 0.25 floor even with straights compressed — so the default diagram export of the flagship chain plausibly exits non-zero (06 §6.2 fail tier). The undefined warn "margin zones" (one band per metric in §6.1, no second band anywhere) is also confirmed. But two claims overreach. "No authorable lever fixes it": width_exag is an authorable ViewSpec field reachable from scene `view:` (04 §7 — "vocabulary owned by 06"); manual width_exag ≈ 1.6 gives ink ≈ 0.30 with width_ratio ≈ 0.93 — tight but inside both bands on the same arithmetic (the critic's own figure of ~1.8× needed is an estimate, not doc text). And 09 §5.3 requires presets land "NEAR the proportion bands" in true mode (where the gate only warns, 06 §6.2) — 0.19 vs a 0.25 floor does not clearly fail a "near" test. Real defect at wrong scope: defaults likely fail, but an escape exists and the true-mode claim is stretched.

verdicts.title: marks: auto|all is too coarse for the book's marker set
verdicts.note: Quoted evidence holds exactly: 04 §7 "marks: auto | all (default auto: good-line marks)" and 03 §8 "marks (auto | all) controls turn-point/apex/exit markers" — the only two settings, with no per-line or per-marker-type selection anywhere in 00–09. The book image shows red AND green hourglass+ring pairs at each annotated corner and no exit dots; default auto therefore omits every red marker the callouts point at, and the only alternative (all) governs turn/apex/exit together, adding exit dots the book art lacks. No other document supplies a finer control (06 §3.1 stage 9 just draws "Markers — carried vocabulary"). Correctly scoped as minor.

verdicts.title: Labels cannot anchor to the mistake line's markers
verdicts.note: Verified: label anchors are corner-relative road stations only — 03 §8 "labels are corner-relative callouts (entry|exit|mid:<id> ± m, plus author-layer apex:<id> sugar resolved post-solve); a callout always resolves onto the road" — and 04 §7 pins the sugar to one line: "apex:<id> sugar resolved against the good line's *solved* apex". No line-qualified anchor exists anywhere in 00–09; the book's fig 8.6 callouts ("early turn point", "early apex", "incorrect line causes...") point at the red line's markers, whose emergent stations an author cannot reference — only hand-guessed ±offset_m road stations. (09 §5.1's P-PROJ-MARKER phrase "every marker and callout anchor... lands on its line's projected image" gestures at a line association but defines no authoring grammar for it — if anything it exposes the same gap.) Minor is the right severity.

verdicts.title: Lane fraction f is undefined on straights and at hand flips; rider's-lane side never chosen
verdicts.note: Verified against all ten docs. f is defined only via corner-relative edges (03 §2 "0 = inside usable edge, 1 = outside usable edge"; 01 §4.1 "f = 0 inner usable edge"), which has no meaning on a straight — yet rider.start.f defaults to 1.0 "the outside usable edge" on the entry straight (03 §6) with no stated convention for which corner defines it. At a zero-gap hand flip (bookEsses abuts L|R|L at a shared station) inner/outer swap, so f jumps x → 1−x; 04 §6's chain composition even sets cross-corner f targets ("the exit of corner n steers toward the hold of corner n+1") without addressing the flip. And a grep across design/ confirms no document states which physical side of the two-lane road is the rider's lane — only "the rider's own lane" (03 §2) and "the outside of the road is the oncoming lane" (01 §4.2) — though that choice fixes every corner's usable corridor, sight geometry, and drawn figure. All three sub-claims stand at the stated minor severity.

verdicts.title: bookEsses is three corners against the book's four-bend chain
verdicts.note: The preset is indeed three corners starting left (03 §3.1: "S 8 | L 12 ^75 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75") and R4 calls it the "fig 8.6 equivalent" (04 §8), and the book art does snake through roughly four bends with the first annotated corner right-hand for the descending rider — so the visual mirror and the extra drawn bend are real. But "drops one full compounding step of the amplification lesson" is defeated by the figure's own annotation set: the image carries exactly three turn-point pairs and three apex pairs (the critic's own evidence says "marker pairs at three-plus corners"), so the annotated compounding chain is three corners — which bookEsses matches; the fourth bend is unannotated entry/exit context. Handedness mirroring alters no teaching under the hand-independent f coordinate (03 §2). What survives is a cosmetic-parity quibble (mirrored, one context bend short), consistent with minor severity but with the "drops a lesson step" scope wrong.

verdicts.title: Role dash law renders the book's solid red line as short-dashed
verdicts.note: Accurate as stated at polish severity: 06 §5.2 pins "mistake → short dash" as the role channel, so every recreated book figure's mistake line draws short-dashed, while the book image shows both lines solid with arrowheads distinguishing by colour alone — a systematic visual difference in every fig-8.x recreation. No doc exempts exports from the dash law, and the only escape (any entry may override role=, 04 §7) would falsify the legend since roles are semantic labels (D9). Mitigating context, which fits the polish grade rather than refuting the claim: the dash channel is a deliberate accessibility rule (06 §5.2 — colour never the sole carrier), and 06 §7's parity enumeration ("same compact proportions, same marker/colour vocabulary, same annotation devices") does not name line style, leaving the departure to the editorial vision judge rather than a mechanical gate.

result.walkthrough:
I simulated an agent whose entire context is what the docs promise `schema` and `explain` print: the ten schema sections listed in 08 §5.1 (`scenario, plan, road-dsl, occluders, mistakes, solve, scene, view, envelope, cli`), their stated content rules (mistakes teaching table; envelope output fields; solve intent surface with vis knobs + one worked constraint token), and `explain`'s envelope/checkId/errorCode narration (08 §5.2).

TASK 1 — right-hander with mid-corner gravel, then stateAt at the patch. Attempt A (zero-file): `linelab run --road "lane 3.5 | S 20 | R 25 ^90 | S 25" --entry 55 --turn-in auto --hazard "gravel inside mid:c1 0x4 mu=0.4"` → exit 2 (unknown flag): the 08 §4.1 flag list has `--occluder` but no `--hazard`, and `rg hazard 08-*.md` returns nothing — hazards are absent from the whole CLI doc, including the §2 "every input surface has a schema section" enumeration and the §5.1 section list. So the zero-file promise ("every field an authoring input can carry has a flag") is false for hazards. Attempt B (file): the wire schema (03 §6) has `hazards: [Hazard…]? // §4`, but §4 pins only the scene token form and a conceptual placement grammar — no JSON key names for Hazard/Occluder, and no JSON shape for road `segments` either (parameter names but no type discriminator or `hand` enum values). I had to invent `{"kind":"gravel","side":"inside","at":{"ref":"mid:c1"},"span_m":4,"mu":0.4}` — pure guesswork, failing the first-try bar. Then the query: `linelab stateAt env.json --line ideal --s 42.5` → exit 2 unknown verb. 05 §4 says stateAt is "exposed identically in the library and as a CLI verb (08)", but 08 §3's verb table has no stateAt row (confirmed by grep: it appears only in 08's preamble and the §7.1 library import list). The only in-table workaround is `export --as trace-csv` and reading the row nearest the patch — precisely the CSV-parsing 05 §4 promises agents never need. Locating the patch station from the output is itself awkward: 05 §7's FigureResult lists `{spec, figure_id, road, lines, meta}` with no occluders/hazards member, so the resolved patch span isn't in the envelope; I'd scan samples for the `mu` step.

TASK 2 — blind left-hander compare, vis=cautious plus a custom constraint. Commands: `linelab solve --road "lane 3.5 | S 30 | L 30 ^100 | S 30" --entry 60 --turn-in auto --occluder "hedge inside ??? " --out out/geom.json`, then the same with `--visibility-governed --vis-margin 1.5 --constraint "sight_margin_m>=8@entry:c1..mid:c1"`, then `linelab compare out/geom.json out/vis.json --lock station`. Spelling audit: the occluder token has two mutually incompatible committed examples — 03 §3.1/§4 write `hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2` (bare `c1` as ref, which the placement grammar `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m` does not admit; -6 read as offset, 26 as span) while 08 §6(c) writes `hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30` (anchor-with-offset as ref, leaving `-1.0` meaning unknown — a second offset? a margin that would put the hedge ON the road?). A cold-start agent cannot pick a spelling both docs endorse. The vis switch has three names (`--visibility-governed` CLI / `vis=cautious` scene / `vis:"cautious"` JSON) and each knob has three (`vis_hold_f` / `visHold=` / `--vis-hold`); the mapping is only recoverable if `schema cli` prints it. The constraint token itself checked out cleanly against 04 §4.5: field `sight_margin_m` with op `>=` maps to bound `sight_margin_min_m`; `sight_margin_m<=` correctly SCHEMA-rejected; span anchors match 03 §6.1. `--vis-margin` without `--visibility-governed` is a typed INEFFECTUAL — good. Loose ends: `--out` appears on solve/run in recipes (b)(c)(f) but not in those verbs' table syntax (and its interplay with "stdout is exactly one JSON document" is unstated); recipe prose at 08 line 114 invents a `--render diagram` flag that exists nowhere else; `compare` says only "Run all inputs" — whether inputs are scenarios, envelopes, or FigureSpecs is a guess; and whether `--constraint` triggers run's solver delegation is unanswerable because 08 §3's trigger list (`--turn-in auto`, any `--mistake`, `--visibility-governed`) omits it.

TASK 3 — sweep for the entry speed where `chop` tips wide→crash. The natural command `linelab sweep scen.json --param rider.start.speed_kmh --range 40:80:2 --metric outcome` is ungrammatical: 08 §3 pins `--param plan.<id>.<field>`, and entry speed lives at `rider.start.speed_kmh`, not in the plan. Mistake params (`chop offset_m`, `freeze_s`) and `config.mu` are equally unaddressable, and there is no path from a compiled mistake line back to a sweepable scenario (the mistake's concrete plan lives nowhere in the envelope — `source` carries only `{kind:"mistake", base_line_id, mistakeSpec}`). The `--metric` vocabulary is specified nowhere and there is no `sweep` schema section in §5.1's closed list. Fallback was a shell loop over `linelab run --road … --entry $v --turn-in auto --mistake chop` with jq on `.lines[].verdict.outcome` — workable because exit 0 covers crash, but fragile in exactly the interesting region: near the tipping speed the internal ideal-line solve may go non-clean or NO_SOLUTION, and 08 §3.1 is ambiguous about whether gate-less `run` that delegated to a non-clean solve exits 0 or 3 ("a non-clean `solve`" — the verb or any solve?). Also noted while checking mistake spellings: the sugar `--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"` (recipe d) vs the verb form `mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --corners c1,c2` vs scene `mistake early_apex early_by_m=6 scope=all_corners` are three grammars, and how params combine with `@` in the sugar (`chop:offset_m=8@c1`?) is never written down. Finally, the design bar's own enforcement is missing: 08 §2 says "09 specifies the cold-start test" and §6 says "09 pins each [recipe] as an executable acceptance test", but 09 contains neither the word "cold" nor "recipe" (grep-confirmed).

findings.title: stateAt promised as a CLI verb but absent from the verb table
findings.claim: The per-instant CLI query — the capability Task 1 needs ('query the state exactly at the patch') — cannot be produced as designed. 05 asserts stateAt is a CLI verb owned by 08; 08's normative verb table has no stateAt row, no argument syntax, no line-selection convention (the library signature takes a single LineResult, so a CLI verb over a multi-line envelope needs a --line selector nobody specifies), and no exit-code mapping for its BAD_RANGE/SCHEMA errors. An implementer building the CLI from 08 ships no such verb; an agent building on 05 issues a command that exits 2. The only in-table fallback is export --as trace-csv plus row-hunting — exactly what 05 §4 promises agents never need ('an agent inspects any instant of any line … without parsing CSVs').
findings.evidence: 05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §4: "`stateAt` is exposed identically in the library and as a CLI verb (`08-cli-and-agent-interface.md`)". 08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §3 verb table lists run/solve/mistake/scene/render/compare/sweep/check/schema/explain/serve/export only; grep shows `stateAt` in 08 appears only in the preamble (line 11) and the §7.1 library import list (line 261), never as a verb.
findings.improvement: Add a verb-table row to 08 §3: `stateAt <envelope.json|-> --line <line_id> (--s <m> | --t <s>)` → InstantState JSON on stdout, exit 0; out-of-domain query = typed BAD_RANGE, exit 2; default --line = the sole line when the envelope has one, required otherwise. Cross-reference it from 05 §4.

findings.title: Hazards have no CLI flag, no schema section, and are missing from the schema-complete enumeration
findings.claim: A mid-corner gravel patch — a carried, first-class input family — cannot be authored on the zero-file path at all, and a cold-start agent has no promised schema section from which to learn the hazard grammar. This directly falsifies 08 §4's claims that 'every field an authoring input can carry has a flag' and 'Anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON and vice versa': hazards are expressible in the wire schema and scene text but by no flag. The word 'hazard' does not occur anywhere in 08.
findings.evidence: 08 §4.1 flag list includes `--occluder <spec>` but no `--hazard`; 08 §2 enumerates input surfaces as "scenario JSON, plan actions, road DSL, occluders, mistake specs, scene text, view specs, CLI flags" (no hazards); 08 §5.1's closed section list `scenario, plan, road-dsl, occluders, mistakes, solve, scene, view, envelope, cli` has no hazards section. Meanwhile 03 §4 defines hazards as "Two distinct families" apart from occluders, 03 §6 carries `hazards: [Hazard…]?`, and 04 §7 scene grammar has a dedicated `hazards:` line.
findings.improvement: Add `--hazard <spec>` (repeatable) to 08 §4.1, add hazards to the §2 input-surface enumeration, and either add a `hazards` schema section or rename/scope the `occluders` section as `occluders-and-hazards` with both token tables.

findings.title: Occluder/Hazard/segment wire JSON shapes are unpinned and the occluder token examples contradict each other
findings.claim: The scenario wire schema points at 03 §4 for Occluder and Hazard shapes, but §4 defines only the scene token form and a conceptual placement grammar — no JSON key names exist anywhere in the design set (nor do road `segments` entries get a type discriminator or `hand` enum values, and the wire road accepts no DSL string, forcing hand-expanded segments). Worse, the two committed token examples are incompatible: 03 writes `hedge inside c1 -6x26` where the ref is bare `c1` — a form the placement grammar (`entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`, or `at_s`) does not admit — while 08's recipe (c) writes `hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30`, putting the offset inside the ref and leaving `-1.0` with no assignable meaning (a second offset? a negative margin that would place the hedge on the road?). The implemented `schema occluders` output will be whichever invention the implementer makes, so first-try authoring from schema output is not designed, only hoped for.
findings.evidence: 03 §6: `occluders: [Occluder…]?, // §4` and `hazards: [Hazard…]?, // §4`; 03 §4 placement grammar: "a station anchor (corner-relative `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`, or absolute `at_s`)" with token form `<kind> <side> <ref> <offset>x<span> [key=val …]`, example `hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2 depth=2.5`; 08 §6(c): `--occluder "hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30"`; 03 §2 segment table gives `len / r, angle_deg, hand` but no JSON encoding.
findings.improvement: Pin in 03: (a) the Occluder and Hazard JSON objects field-by-field (kind, side, anchor object reusing §6.1's `{ref, offset_m}|{at_s}`, span_m, per-kind keys), (b) the segment JSON encoding including the `hand` literal set, and (c) one occluder token grammar with `<ref>` defined; fix whichever example (03 or 08) is wrong.

findings.title: sweep --param cannot address entry speed, mistake params, or config — the tipping-point question is unanswerable
findings.claim: Task 3's question — at what entry speed does a chop mistake tip from wide to crash — is a canonical doctrine question (the same shape as fig 8.4's overspeed lesson), and the sweep verb cannot express it: the param grammar is pinned to `plan.<id>.<field>`, but entry speed lives at `rider.start.speed_kmh`, chop's knobs (`offset_m`, `freeze_s`) live in a mistake spec, and `config.mu` is likewise out of reach. There is also no route from a compiled mistake line to a sweepable scenario (LineResult.source for a mistake carries only `{kind, base_line_id, mistakeSpec}`, never the compiled plan). On top of that the `--metric` vocabulary is defined nowhere and §5.1's closed schema-section list has no `sweep` section, so a cold-start agent cannot even learn what metrics exist. The forced fallback is a shell loop over `run` — workable but it re-solves the ideal base at every speed, so nothing is held fixed, which is precisely what a sweep verb exists to guarantee.
findings.evidence: 08 §3: "`sweep <scenario> --param plan.<id>.<field> --range a:b:step [--param2 …] [--metric list]` | Grid-sweep 1–2 fields (id-addressed, never array-indexed — carried)"; 03 §6 places entry speed at `rider.start.speed_kmh`; 03 §7.1 chop params `offset_m = 5`, `freeze_s = 1.0`; 05 §7 LineResult.source mistake variant; 08 §5.1 section list lacks `sweep`.
findings.improvement: Widen the param grammar to any id-addressed scenario path (`rider.start.speed_kmh`, `config.mu`, `mistake.<line_id>.params.<key>`), define sweep's behavior when the swept scenario needs solving per cell, pin the metric name vocabulary (at minimum `outcome`, `apex_pct`, `grip_min`, `sight_margin_min_m`, exit `f`), and add a `sweep` schema section to §5.1.

findings.title: The cold-start test and recipe acceptance tests 08 delegates to 09 do not exist in 09
findings.claim: The design bar's own enforcement is dangling. 08 twice states that 09 owns the tests that make the bar and the recipes real — the cold-start test ('a testable requirement, not a slogan') and one executable acceptance test per recipe — but 09 contains neither: no cold-start section, no recipe tests (its only named acceptance test is A-CHAIN-VIS). The two statements of the bar also disagree about what the agent context contains: 08 §2's headline says 'from `schema` and `explain` output alone' while its description of 09's test says 'nothing but the printed `schema` output'. As designed, the deliverable this whole stress test targets is unverifiable, and an implementer cannot know whether explain output is in or out of the cold-start context.
findings.evidence: 08 §2: "**09** specifies the *cold-start test*: an agent context containing nothing but the printed `schema` output must produce a valid, effectual scenario"; 08 §6: "**09** pins each as an executable acceptance test so the recipes cannot rot"; 04 §8: "The bar these recipes are tested against (`09-verification-and-testing.md`)". `rg -i cold 09-*.md` and `rg -i recipe 09-*.md` both return nothing.
findings.improvement: Add a section to 09 specifying the cold-start harness (context = the literal `schema` full print plus, per one reconciled bar statement, named `explain` outputs; task battery = 08 §6's six recipes plus one novel-scenario task per input surface; pass = exit-0/expected-tier on first command sequence) and enumerate the six recipe acceptance tests as named A-* fixtures.

findings.title: run's solver-delegation triggers omit --constraint, leaving constraint-without-auto undefined
findings.claim: Constraints are solver-layer only (they never enter the wire plan), yet `run`'s delegation trigger list does not include `--constraint`. An agent issuing `run --road … --entry 55 --turn-in 12 --constraint "f>=0.6@entry:c1..mid:c1"` (explicit turn-in, no other trigger) hits behavior the design never defines: the constraint either silently does nothing (forbidden by D8), is rejected INEFFECTUAL (surprising, since constraints are a headline D10 feature), or forces delegation (contradicting the printed trigger list). First-try success on run+constraint is a coin flip.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 run row: "if the composed input needs solving (`--turn-in auto`, any `--mistake`, `--visibility-governed`), `run` delegates to the solver" — no `--constraint`; 00 D10 / 04 §4.5: "a constraint never appears in the wire plan and the engine never sees one"; 08 §4.1 lists `--constraint` among the zero-file flags run accepts.
findings.improvement: Add `--constraint` (and any future solver-only flag) to the delegation trigger list in 08 §3, and state that a constraint attached to a fully explicit plan with no solver involvement is rejected INEFFECTUAL with reason `constraint_without_solver`.

findings.title: Gate-less run that internally delegates to a non-clean solve: exit 0 or 3 is ambiguous
findings.claim: Exit 3 is defined for "a non-clean `solve`", but when `run` (no --gate) delegates internally — which every `--turn-in auto` invocation does — the docs never say whether the solve verb's authoring gate rides along. If yes, the headline scripting rule 'exit 0 = ran, any physics outcome' breaks for the most common agent command form; if no, the same composed input exits differently through two front doors. My Task-3 fallback loop (run over entry speeds with --mistake chop) depends on this exactly in the tipping region, where the internal ideal-line solve is most likely to go non-clean.
findings.evidence: 08 §3.1: exit 0 "Ran — any physics outcome (`clean`, `wide`, `runoff`, `violation`, `crash`)"; exit 3 "Doctrine tier: `run --gate` with a failed doctrine check, a non-clean `solve`"; 08 §3 run row: "`run` delegates to the solver internally and says so in the envelope".
findings.improvement: State in 08 §3.1 that the authoring gate is a property of the `solve` verb only: gate-less `run` always exits 0 when physics ran, recording solver non-cleanliness in the envelope; only `--gate` promotes it to exit 3.

findings.title: Three incompatible mistake-spec spellings and an undefined --mistake sugar grammar
findings.claim: The same mistake is spelled three ways — verb form `mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --on … [--corners c1,c2]`, flag sugar `--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"`, scene form `mistake early_apex early_by_m=6 scope=all_corners` — and the sugar's full grammar is never written: whether params combine with the corner shorthand (`chop:offset_m=8@c1`? `chop@c1:offset_m=8`?) is a guess, since only two parameterless examples exist in the entire set. A cold-start agent authoring any parameterized per-corner mistake via flags cannot succeed by design, only by luck of what the implementer chose.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 mistake row: `mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --on <solved.json> [--corners c1,c2]`; 08 §6(d): `--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"`; 04 §7: `mistake early_apex early_by_m=6` and `[scope=<cornerId>|all_corners]`; 03 §7.2: "the CLI's `<kind>@c1,c2` shorthand … maps to it" — nowhere a combined params+scope sugar example.
findings.improvement: Pin one canonical compact grammar in 08 §4.1 — e.g. `--mistake "<kind>[:k=v,…][@c1,c2|@all]"` — with a worked parameterized example, and state that the scene form is the same tokens space-separated.

findings.title: Phantom flags in recipes: --out and --render on run/solve are not in the verb table
findings.claim: Recipes (b), (c), (f) hang `--out out/….json` on run and solve, and §4's prose adds `--render diagram` to run — none of these appear in those verbs' table syntax or the §4.1 flag list. It is also unstated how `--out` interacts with the output discipline 'stdout is exactly one JSON document per invocation' (suppressed? duplicated?). An agent that trusts the verb table pipes stdout; one that trusts the recipes passes --out; the docs support both and define neither.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 run row syntax: `run [<scenario.json>|-] [zero-file flags] [--gate] [--trace out.csv]` (no --out); solve row: `solve [<input.json>|-] [zero-file flags] [--suggest]` (no --out); vs 08 §6(b) `--out out/fig81.json`, §6(c) `--out out/geom.json`, §4 line 114: "Add `--out fig/ --render diagram`"; 08 §3.2: "stdout is exactly one JSON document per invocation".
findings.improvement: Either add `[--out file]` (envelope also/only written to file, stdout unchanged) and `[--render <mode>]` to the run/solve rows and §4.1, or rewrite the recipes to use shell redirection and a separate render step.

findings.title: Triple naming drift on the visibility switch and knobs
findings.claim: One concept, three spellings per surface: the mode is `--visibility-governed` (CLI boolean), `vis=cautious` (scene enum), `vis: "cautious"` (JSON enum); each knob is `vis_hold_f`/`visHold=`/`--vis-hold`. The bijection is recoverable only if the implemented `schema cli` mapping table is complete and the agent thinks to read it; an agent that read `schema solve` (which 08 §5.1 says prints the knob field names) will plausibly try `--vis cautious` or `--vis-hold-f`. The boolean flag also cannot express a third mode if one is ever added, unlike the enum it mirrors.
findings.evidence: 08 §4.1: "`--visibility-governed` with its knob flags `--vis-hold <f>` and `--vis-margin <×>`" and "Flags mirror schema fields one-to-one"; 04 §6: "A ride spec may set `vis=cautious` (default `vis=none`)", knob fields `vis_hold_f`, `vis_margin`, "Scene and CLI spellings (`visHold=` / `--vis-hold`, `visMargin=` / `--vis-margin`)"; 04 §8 R3: `solve({road, entry_kmh: 32, vis: "cautious"})`.
findings.improvement: Rename the flag to `--vis cautious|none` (value-bearing, mirroring the field name literally) and align knob spellings to one kebab/snake rule (`--vis-hold-f` or rename the field `vis_hold`); state in 08 §5.1 that `schema cli` prints the full flag↔field table.

findings.title: explain does not accept a mistake kind, contradicting 03's API requirement
findings.claim: 03 requires `explain(kind)` to state each mistake kind's pinned outcome and book figure so the premature/early_apex naming trap is 'documented at the API surface' — but 08's explain verb accepts only an envelope, a check id, or an error code; a mistake kind is none of those. The cold-start agent survives via the `schema mistakes` teaching table, but the two docs disagree about where the trap's documentation lives, and an implementer following 08 ships an explain that rejects `explain early_apex`.
findings.evidence: 03 §7.1: "`explain(kind)` must state each kind's pinned outcome and book figure so an agent picks the right kind … on the first try"; 08 §3: "`explain <envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>`"; 08 §5.2: "given a **check id or error code**: its definition, arithmetic, and doctrine source".
findings.improvement: Extend 08's explain argument set to `envelope | checkId | errorCode | mistakeKind`, with the kind narration defined as the same content as the `schema mistakes` row plus the naming-trap note.

findings.title: compare and mistake --on are ambiguous over multi-line inputs
findings.claim: `compare` says only 'Run all inputs' — whether A.json/B.json are scenarios, envelopes, or FigureSpecs is unstated (recipe (c) feeds it solve outputs, implying envelopes, but the verb row never says so), and when an input envelope carries several lines it is undefined which lines enter the station-aligned diff. Likewise `mistake <kind> --on <solved.json>` never says which line of a multi-line envelope is the compile base; the scene format's 'first ride line' rule (04 §7) is scene-only. Also, the envelope may not even carry the resolved occluders/hazards an agent needs to align a diff or locate a patch: 05 §7's FigureResult lists `{spec, figure_id, road, lines, meta}` with no occluder/hazard member, though 03 §8's Figure binds them with the road.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 compare row: "`compare <A.json> <B.json> […]` | Run all inputs, emit per-line verdict deltas…"; 08 §3 mistake row: "Compile a mistake line off an existing solved line"; 04 §7: "exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against" (scene grammar only); 05 §7 FigureResult shape vs 03 §8 "Figure = { road (+ occluders/hazards), … }".
findings.improvement: State compare's accepted input types (scenario | envelope | FigureSpec, each recomputed per D6) and its line-pairing rule; give the mistake verb a `--base <line_id>` with a default of the sole/first `ideal` line; add `occluders`/`hazards` (resolved, absolute stations) to FigureResult.

findings.title: No grammar for --brake/--throttle/--position specs — flags cannot actually mirror plan actions
findings.claim: The zero-file flag list names `--brake <auto|decel>`, `--throttle <spec>`, `--position <spec>` but no document defines these `<spec>` grammars, and the flags↔JSON bijection claim is structurally strained: plan actions are an ordered, id-addressed list with anchors, `taper_to_s`, and `over_m`, while the flags as written carry one scalar-ish value each. How a flag expresses an action id (needed later for sweep's `plan.<id>.<field>` addressing) or a corner-relative anchor is unspecified — so a hold-wide `position` action, the D4/D8 headline capability, is not writable from flags on the first try.
findings.evidence: 08 §4.1: "`--brake <auto|decel>`, `--throttle <spec>`, `--position <spec>`" with no grammar anywhere; "Anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON and vice versa — flags are sugar, not a second schema"; 03 §6.1 plan actions carry `id`, anchors `at_s`/`{ref, offset_m}`, `taper_to_s?`, `over_m`; 08 §3 sweep addresses `plan.<id>.<field>`.
findings.improvement: Define one compact action token, e.g. `--position "p1: f=0.9 @entry:c1-20 over=15"` (id optional, auto-minted as `p1…pn`), reuse it for --brake/--throttle, and print it in the `cli` schema section.

findings.title: Recipe count self-contradiction in 08
findings.claim: 08 §1's coverage list promises "Five canonical agent recipes, end to end" while §5.2's heading text and §6 deliver "Six agent recipes" — trivial, but it is the kind of internal drift the cold-start bar is meant to make impossible, sitting in the very document that owns the bar.
findings.evidence: 08 §1 item 5: "Five canonical agent recipes, end to end."; 08 §6: "Six canonical end-to-end sequences".
findings.improvement: Change §1 to "Six".

wins: Exit-code tier 0 covering crash/runoff ('a crash is a valid, interesting run', 08 §3.1) is exactly right for agent scripting — my Task-3 fallback loop over entry speeds only works because a crash is not an error.

The single-JSON-stdout discipline plus the closed, greppable error vocabulary with schema_ref on every exit-2 error (08 §3.2, §2 'Errors teach') gives a one-round-trip repair loop; JSON.parse(stdout) always holding is a strong, simple contract.

The schema mistakes teaching table (08 §5.1) surfacing the premature/early_apex trap with pinned outcomes and book-figure mappings at the API surface is a genuine cold-start save — I picked kinds correctly in Tasks 2/3 from promised schema content alone.

The constraint compact token grammar (04 §4.5) survived adversarial spelling checks: field↔bound mapping is explicit, the closed-set rejections (v_kmh>=, sight_margin_m<=) are typed SCHEMA, the worked example is promised in schema solve, and NO_SOLUTION/constraint_unmet names the worst station and achieved-vs-required values — the agent's next move is legible from the error.
D8/INEFFECTUAL with named reasons (vis knobs without vis=cautious → vis_knob_without_vis_mode, 04 §6) abolishes the accepted-but-inert class that would otherwise be the top cold-start failure mode.

The zero-file precedence rules (08 §4.2: file → flags override → validate through the same entry point, indistinguishable downstream) are crisp and testable; run-as-universal-front-door with delegation disclosed in the envelope keeps the agent's mental model to one verb.
schema envelope documenting outputs before anything runs (08 §5.1) let the simulated agent plan jq extraction paths (verdict.outcome, constraints margins) without a trial run.

The 'schema-valid implies effectual' bar plus 09 §8's per-surface effectuality tests give the design bar real mechanical teeth on the input side, even though the cold-start harness itself is missing (see findings).

verdicts.title: stateAt promised as a CLI verb but absent from the verb table
verdicts.note: 05 §4 states verbatim: "`stateAt` is exposed identically in the library and as a CLI verb (`08-cli-and-agent-interface.md`)". 08's normative verb table (§3) lists exactly run/solve/mistake/scene/render/compare/sweep/check/schema/explain/serve/export — no stateAt row, syntax, multi-line selector, or exit mapping. stateAt appears in 08 only in the preamble contract list (line 11) and the §7.1 library import (line 261). Checked all ten docs: 01, 07, 09 reference stateAt only as a library function; nothing anywhere defines the CLI verb. The cross-doc contract genuinely dangles as claimed.

verdicts.title: Hazards have no CLI flag, no schema section, and are missing from the schema-complete enumeration
verdicts.note: rg confirms the word 'hazard' has zero occurrences in 08. §4.1's flag list has `--occluder <spec>` but no hazard flag; §2's input-surface enumeration ("scenario JSON, plan actions, road DSL, occluders, mistake specs, scene text, view specs, CLI flags") and §5.1's closed section list (`scenario, plan, road-dsl, occluders, mistakes, solve, scene, view, envelope, cli`) both omit hazards, while 03 §4/§6 and 04 §7 carry them as a first-class family. This directly falsifies 08 §4's "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag". Only nit: a hazard could ride stdin JSON (`run -`), so "cannot be authored on the zero-file path at all" is a hair strong, but the flag-completeness claim it targets is falsified as quoted.

verdicts.title: Occluder/Hazard/segment wire JSON shapes are unpinned and the occluder token examples contradict each other
verdicts.note: 03 §6 points `occluders`/`hazards` at §4, which gives only kind tables and the scene token form — no JSON key names anywhere in the set (grep across all ten docs); `segments: […]` likewise has no entry encoding, type discriminator, or `hand` enum values, and the wire `road` is `{…segments…} | {preset}` with no DSL-string variant. The token contradiction is real: 03's committed examples use bare `c1` (`hedge inside c1 -6x26`, also in preset bookBlind and 04 §7), a ref the stated anchor grammar (`entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`, or `at_s`) does not admit, while 08 §6(c) writes `hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30`, moving the offset inside the ref and leaving the `<offset>` token `-1.0` unassignable under `<kind> <side> <ref> <offset>x<span>`.

verdicts.title: sweep --param cannot address entry speed, mistake params, or config — the tipping-point question is unanswerable
verdicts.note: 08 §3 pins the grammar to `--param plan.<id>.<field>` ("id-addressed, never array-indexed"); entry speed lives at `rider.start.speed_kmh` (03 §6), chop's `offset_m`/`freeze_s` live in the mistake spec (03 §7.1), and `config.mu` is a config field — none reachable through a plan path. 05 §7's mistake source carries only `{kind, base_line_id, mistakeSpec}`, never the compiled plan. The `--metric` vocabulary is defined nowhere (grep across all docs) and §5.1's closed section list has no `sweep` entry. No other doc rescues this.

verdicts.title: The cold-start test and recipe acceptance tests 08 delegates to 09 do not exist in 09
verdicts.note: 08 §2: "**09** specifies the *cold-start test*"; 08 §6: "**09** pins each as an executable acceptance test". rg -i 'cold' hits only 08; rg -i 'recipe' in 09 returns nothing; 09's only named acceptance test is A-CHAIN-VIS (§3.5), and §8's contract-test list covers the verb table but no cold-start or recipe tests. The context discrepancy is also verified: 08 §2's headline says "from `schema` and `explain` output alone" (04 §8 agrees) while the same section's test description says "nothing but the printed `schema` output".

verdicts.title: run's solver-delegation triggers omit --constraint, leaving constraint-without-auto undefined
verdicts.note: The omission is real — 08 §3's run row lists only `--turn-in auto`, any `--mistake`, `--visibility-governed`, and no doc states run+constraint explicitly. But the 'coin flip' among silently-ignored / INEFFECTUAL / delegation is defeated by the governing clause plus D10: run delegates "if the composed input needs solving", and 04 §4.5 / 00 D10 pin constraints as solver-layer-only ("a constraint never enters the wire plan; the engine never sees one"), so a constraint-carrying input can only be a solve spec and delegation follows from the stated rule — the parenthetical reads as instances of 'needs solving', not a closed list. The surviving half: the printed trigger list is incomplete and the behavior is left to cross-doc inference, a legitimate but smaller gap than 'never defined'.

verdicts.title: Gate-less run that internally delegates to a non-clean solve: exit 0 or 3 is ambiguous
verdicts.note: The exit table answers this by verb scoping. 08 §3.1 defines exit 0 as "Ran — any physics outcome (`clean`, `wide`, `runoff`, `violation`, `crash`)" and assigns tier 3 to run only via `--gate`; the "non-clean `solve`" entry is the solve verb's own gate — 08 §3's solve row says "Non-clean solve exits 3 (the authoring gate)", naming it a property of "the explicit authoring door". A gate-less run that delegates internally is still `run`: it ran, the non-clean line has a physics outcome, it "says so in the envelope", and exits 0. The two doors exiting differently is the explicit design (universal front door with opt-in `--gate` vs the authoring gate), not an undefined case — so the Task-3 fallback loop's 'exit 0 = ran' rule holds.

verdicts.title: Three incompatible mistake-spec spellings and an undefined --mistake sugar grammar
verdicts.note: All three spellings verified: verb `mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --on <solved.json> [--corners c1,c2]` (08 §3), sugar `--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"` (08 §6d), scene `mistake early_apex early_by_m=6 [scope=…]` (04 §7). The combined params+scope sugar grammar is written nowhere — the only sugar examples in the whole set (`--mistake early_apex`, `early_apex@c1,c2`) are parameterless, and 03 §7.2 maps only the `<kind>@c1,c2` shorthand. 'Incompatible' is rhetorical (they are distinct surfaces with a claimed mapping), but the claim's core — a parameterized per-corner mistake via flags has no designed grammar — stands.

verdicts.title: Phantom flags in recipes: --out and --render on run/solve are not in the verb table
verdicts.note: Verified: run's syntax is `run [<scenario.json>|-] [zero-file flags] [--gate] [--trace out.csv]` and solve's is `solve [<input.json>|-] [zero-file flags] [--suggest]`; §4.1's flag list has neither `--out` nor `--render`. Yet §6(b) puts `--out out/fig81.json` on run, §6(c) puts `--out` on solve twice, and §4 line 114 adds `--out fig/ --render diagram` to run. `--out` exists in the table only for scene/render/compare/export. Interaction with §3.2's "stdout is exactly one JSON document per invocation" is unstated anywhere.

verdicts.title: Triple naming drift on the visibility switch and knobs
verdicts.note: All spellings verified: `--visibility-governed`/`--vis-hold`/`--vis-margin` (08 §4.1), `vis=cautious`/`visHold=`/`visMargin=` (04 §6–7), `vis: "cautious"`/`vis_hold_f`/`vis_margin` (04 §8 R3, §6). The design does deliberately document the mapping (04 §6 cross-references the spellings; `schema cli` prints the flag↔field table), but the finding already concedes that; its nucleus holds: the mode flag is a boolean mirroring an enum field with an unrelated name, which structurally strains 08 §4.1's "Flags mirror schema fields one-to-one" and cannot express a third `vis` mode. Minor severity is right.

verdicts.title: explain does not accept a mistake kind, contradicting 03's API requirement
verdicts.note: 03 §7.1 requires "`explain(kind)` must state each kind's pinned outcome and book figure … the naming trap is documented at the API surface". 08's explain accepts only `<envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>` (§3), and §5.2 confirms the non-envelope inputs are "a check id or error code" — a mistake kind is neither. No other doc extends explain's inputs (grep). The critic correctly notes the content survives in `schema mistakes`' teaching table, but the two docs do disagree about where the trap's API-surface documentation lives.

verdicts.title: compare and mistake --on are ambiguous over multi-line inputs
verdicts.note: compare's row says only "Run all inputs" — input type (scenario/envelope/FigureSpec) and line selection from a multi-line envelope are stated nowhere; recipe (c) feeds it solve outputs without the row saying envelopes are accepted. `mistake --on <solved.json>` never says which line of a multi-line envelope is the base; 04 §7's "exactly one `ride` line … the reference every mistake is measured against" is scene-grammar-only. And 05 §7's FigureResult is `{spec, figure_id, road, lines, meta}` where `road` is "ONE composed RoadModel" (03 §2's RoadModel carries no occluders), versus 03 §8's `Figure = { road (+ occluders/hazards), … }` — resolved occluders/hazards are recoverable only from per-line source specs, not from a shared envelope member.

verdicts.title: No grammar for --brake/--throttle/--position specs — flags cannot actually mirror plan actions
verdicts.note: `--brake <auto|decel>`, `--throttle <spec>`, `--position <spec>` occur exactly once in the whole set (08 §4.1 line 123) with no `<spec>` grammar anywhere (grep across all ten docs; the scene format's ride lines carry no throttle/position keys either). 03 §6.1 plan actions are an ordered list with `id`, `at_s`/`{ref, offset_m}` anchors, `taper_to_s?`, `over_m` — none expressible in the single-value flags as written, and no mechanism assigns the action ids that sweep's `plan.<id>.<field>` addressing later needs. The "vice versa" half of §4.1's bijection claim is unsupported as stated.

verdicts.title: Recipe count self-contradiction in 08
verdicts.note: The five-vs-six drift is real but mislocated. 08 §1's coverage list item 5 actually reads "Six agent recipes, end to end." — not the quoted "Five canonical agent recipes, end to end." The 'five' lives in the document preamble (line 6: "schema discoverability, and five canonical agent recipes"), contradicting §1 item 5 and §6's "Six canonical end-to-end sequences". So the internal drift the finding describes exists at polish severity, but its §1 quotation is fabricated from the wrong location; the surviving half is preamble-vs-§1/§6, not §1-vs-§6.

findings.title: Corrective-shot solver is a name, not a spec — runoff vs wide is undecidable
findings.claim: The headline outcome classes `runoff` and `wide` are defined entirely by whether "a feasible add-lean corrective exists," but the corrective shot is never specified anywhere in the doc set: no trigger predicate (the `run_wide_detect` event kind exists with no definition), no start time (only the hint that `t_react_s` is "the recognition delay used by run-wide correction"), no control policy (add lean to what target — phiReserve or phiMax? at what roll rate? with what longitudinal command?), no success predicate (return to f ≤ 1 by when?), and no shape for the verdict's `corrective` field. Ownership is circular: 02 points at 04 for correction solving, and 04 points back at 02. Since the mistake oracle pins `early_apex` to exactly `runoff` (corrective must FAIL) and `chop` to `wide`/`runoff`, the promised verdicts cannot be computed from these documents.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §7: "`runoff` — left the road/lane and no feasible corrective returns it (the corrective shot, integrated with the run-wide slice active, fails)"; "`wide` — ran wide but a feasible add-lean corrective exists." 02 §5.6: "Run-wide correction solving (`04-solver-and-authoring.md`) must integrate with the slice active." 04 §4.3: "The corrective-action solver (the 'can this run-wide be saved?' shot, `02-physics-model.md`)" — each doc cites the other; neither specifies it. 05 §5 lists `run_wide_detect` and `correction` in the Event kinds with no defining predicate; 05 §6.3 Verdict has `corrective | null` with no shape. 03 §7.1 pins `early_apex` → `runoff`.
findings.improvement: Add a dedicated section (04 is the natural home per 02's own 'feasibility by shooting' rule) specifying: the run-wide detection predicate (e.g. f crosses 1−margin with outward trend), corrective start = detect + t_react_s (+ freeze_s when a frozen mistake owns the window), the corrective policy (roll toward phiReserve at the profile roll_rate, a_cmd = 0), the success predicate (f returns ≤ 1 before road end with no ellipse/lean-ceiling violation), and the recorded `corrective` shape in the verdict.

findings.title: P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN flatly contradicts invariant 5.4.1 — the mandated suite cannot be green
findings.claim: 09's property test asserts any brake applied at lean produces a line "never tighter," while 02's invariant 1 and the C30-trailbrake golden require that light trail braking at lean (taper ≤ ~2.5 m/s²) "still tightens the line." A 2.0 m/s² brake carried past turn-in must tighten per 02 and must never tighten per 09.
