An implementation faithful to §5.2's equations (relu gate at A_SU_ONSET = 2.5 makes sub-threshold braking bit-identical to the point-mass, where decel at fixed lean tightens) will always fail P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN as written, so the design's own test regime is unsatisfiable.
findings.evidence: 09-verification-and-testing.md §3.4: "`P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN` — a `chop` or brake applied at lean produces a line at or wider than the unperturbed line from the perturbation station on; never tighter." 02-physics-model.md §5.4.1: "light trail braking (taper ≤ ~2.5 m/s²) still *tightens* the line — the advanced technique remains representable and gradeable"; 02 §8: "`C30-trailbrake` (2.0 m/s² taper carried past turn-in → still tightens…, invariant §5.4.1)."
findings.improvement: Qualify P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN's premise to the slice-active domain — sustained `−a_clip ≥ A_SU_ONSET` or `−a_cmd_rate ≥ RATE_THRESHOLD` at `|phi| ≥` some floor — and add a paired property (P-TRAILBRAKE-TIGHTENS) for the sub-threshold regime so both behaviours are pinned without contradiction.

findings.title: Invariant 5.4.2 is mathematically false at its own stated boundary: braking at a_noreturn tightens, and a whole decel band above it tightens too
findings.claim: The invariant claims sustained `−a_clip ≥ a_noreturn` at |phi| ≥ 15° makes the path radius grow and lane fraction move outward. Do the algebra on kappa = g·tan(phi)/v²: d(ln κ)/dt = φ̇/(sinφ·cosφ) + 2a/v under decel a. At exactly a = a_noreturn, the net roll rate is zero BY DEFINITION of a_noreturn (stand-up equals rider counter-authority), so φ holds while v falls — κ strictly rises and the line TIGHTENS, forever, until v_floor. Above the boundary there is still a tightening band: at φ = 30°, v = 15 m/s (street profile), widening requires a·(K_SU − 2·sinφcosφ/v) > roll_rate + K_SU·A_SU_ONSET, i.e. a > 6.70 m/s², while a_noreturn = 5.41 — everything in [5.41, 6.70] m/s² tightens despite being past the "point of no return." Worse, when φ does shed, the tanh envelope creates a small-lean equilibrium (at a = 6 m/s², φ settles ≈ 6°) and the still-falling v then re-tightens κ past the pre-brake arc. No choice of TUNING constants can rescue the invariant at the boundary because a_noreturn is defined as the net-zero-roll point — yet §5.4 declares the invariants ARE the specification ("the constants above are servants to them").
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §5.4.2: "For sustained `−a_clip ≥ a_noreturn` at `|phi| ≥ 15°`, the emergent path's radius grows relative to the pre-brake arc; the trajectory's lane fraction moves outward." §5.3: "`a_noreturn ≈ A_SU_ONSET + roll_rate / (K_SU · tanh(|phi|/PHI0))` … ≈ 5.4 m/s²" for street. §5.2 constants K_SU = 0.30, A_SU_ONSET = 2.5. §2: "kappa(v, phi) = G · tan(phi) / v²" and "decelerating tightens the arc." §5.4 preamble: "These are the specification; the constants above are servants to them."
findings.improvement: Decouple the two crossovers: keep a_noreturn as the roll-authority crossover (a teaching quantity), and restate invariant 2 over the geometric widening threshold a_widen(φ, v) = (roll_rate + K_SU·A_SU_ONSET) / (K_SU − 2·sinφcosφ/v), with the invariant pinned only for decels strictly above it (and v above the regime where no decel can widen, v ≤ 2·sinφcosφ/K_SU). Alternatively strengthen the model (e.g. stand-up gain that grows with decel faster than linearly) and re-derive; either way the invariant's domain must be one the equations actually satisfy.

findings.title: At deep lean the friction ellipse clips a_clip below a_noreturn — hard braking at 40° becomes a stable max-grip tightening spiral, the opposite of the book
findings.claim: S_sustained is driven by achieved decel `a_clip`, which is ellipse-clipped inside every stage to aLongAvail = G·√(1 − tan²φ) at mu = 1. At φ ≳ 39.8°, aLongAvail (5.34 m/s² at 40°) falls below a_noreturn (5.41), so the sustained stand-up can NEVER exceed rider authority at deep lean no matter how hard the rider commands the brake: S_su = 0.3·(5.34−2.5) = 0.852 < roll_rate 0.873, the rider holds lean, and the bike rides the ellipse at exactly ellipseMag = 1 (legal — crash requires > 1+1e-3) while v falls and κ tightens. Grabbing a fistful of brake at maximum lean — the book's cardinal sin — is rendered as a stable, grip-perfect trail-brake that tightens the line. This is precisely the behaviour D3 exists to eliminate, resurfacing in the regime where the lesson matters most; it also silently empties invariant 5.4.2's premise (−a_clip ≥ a_noreturn is unreachable) at deep lean.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §4: "`aLongAvail(aLat, mu) = aLongMax · sqrt(max(0, 1 − (aLat/aLatMax)²))`", "Clipping happens inside every integrator sub-stage", crash deadband "`ellipseMag > 1 + eps_mag (1e-3)`"; §5.2: "`S_sustained = K_SU · relu( −a_clip − A_SU_ONSET )`" (a_clip, not a_cmd); §5.3 a_noreturn ≈ 5.4 for street. 00-README.md D3: braking-at-lean must "widen the line as the book teaches, instead of pinching it inward."
findings.improvement: Drive part of the stand-up from commanded excess: e.g. S_sustained keyed to min(−a_cmd, aLongAvail-at-zero-lean) or add a grip-saturation term when the clip is active at lean (the physical reality: demanded braking beyond available grip at deep lean loses the front — even if Tier 1R won't crash it, it should not reward it). At minimum, add a doctrine check / placard when sustained commanded brake is ellipse-clipped at |φ| above the a_noreturn-reachable lean, so the misleading 'stable limit trail-brake' cannot grade clean.

findings.title: The transient term is an impulse ≈ K_CHOP·Δa: any stepped command change ≥ 0.04 m/s² at lean fully stands the bike up in ~5 ms, and plan-onset shaping is unspecified
findings.claim: a_cmd_rate is the finite difference of commanded accel across one dt = 0.005 s step, so a step drop Δa yields a one-step rate Δa/dt (a 2 m/s² chop → −400 m/s³, fifty times RATE_THRESHOLD) and an integrated lean impulse Δφ ≈ K_CHOP·|Δa| ≈ 12 rad — full stand-up within one step for ANY stepped drop ≥ RATE_THRESHOLD·dt = 0.04 m/s². Consequences: (a) chop severity is binary — P-RUNWIDE-MONOTONE ("a harder chop at the same lean widens the line monotonically") is vacuous because all stepped chops saturate identically, and its guard "within the model's stated validity range" references a range stated nowhere; (b) the wire schema's `brake` action ramps only its RELEASE (`taper_to_s`), never its onset, so gently squeezing the brake on mid-corner is inexpressible — every mid-corner brake engagement reads as 01's "grabs brake" and slams the bike upright, which quietly makes any brake-engaging corrective infeasible; (c) whether the chop freeze means 'target_lean held (tracker fights)' or 'zero roll command (rider yields)' changes the shed rate and is unspecified — currently moot only because the impulse dominates.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §6: "`a_cmd_rate` is the finite difference of commanded longitudinal accel between consecutive steps"; §5.2: "`S_transient = K_CHOP · relu( −a_cmd_rate − RATE_THRESHOLD )`", K_CHOP = 6.0 (rad/s)/(m/s³), RATE_THRESHOLD = 8.0 m/s³, dt_s = 0.005. 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §6.1: brake = "`decel > 0` (m/s²), `taper_to_s?` … optionally tapering to zero by a station" — no onset ramp. 09 §3.4: "`P-RUNWIDE-MONOTONE` — within the model's stated validity range, a harder chop at the same lean widens the line monotonically." 02 §5.4.3: "the panicked rider does not re-lean during the freeze." 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §mistakes table: "chop | Abruptly cuts throttle (or grabs brake) mid-corner."
findings.improvement: Specify command shaping: give every longitudinal action an onset slew (authored or a default first-order ramp), define chop severity as the authored ramp rate so RATE_THRESHOLD discriminates meaningfully, restate K_CHOP as an impulse gain with the Δφ ≈ K_CHOP·Δa semantics made explicit (it is dt-invariant — a virtue worth stating), pin whether a_cmd_rate is per-step ZOH across all four stages (and define it as 0 at the first step), and define freeze as target-hold or command-zero.

findings.title: Position actions have no specified physical channel — the model's only lateral control is lean, and nobody says how position becomes lean
findings.claim: 02's controller interface returns exactly `{target_lean, roll_rate, a_cmd}` — there is no lateral member — while 03 §6.1 requires an effectual lateral drift bounded by a_lat_pos_max = 0.8 m/s². The only physical channel that can move the bike laterally in this EOM is lean (the drift is an S-curve of lean setpoints, amplitude atan(0.8/9.81) ≈ 4.7°), but no guidance law, no heading-realignment condition, and no arbitration with the lean channel is specified — an implementer who injects lateral offset kinematically would create exactly the hidden second steering channel D3 forbids, and two implementations will produce different deterministic trajectories, breaking the goldens/hash story. Representability is also unexamined: at 34 km/h with the default over_m = 15 m, bang-bang ±0.8 m/s² delivers at most Δd = a·(T/2)² ≈ 0.51 m, but a hold-wide reposition f 0.5→0.9 in a 3.5 m lane (corridor 2.7 m) needs 1.08 m — the default window cannot reach typical targets and the docs never say what happens (partial reach? INEFFECTUAL? — D8 makes this limbo illegal). Finally, 04 §6's chained V2 generates position holds in inter-corner spans while the bike is still exiting corner n leaned; since 'when a turn_in commitment ends' is undefined, the solver's own generated plan can be rejected by 03's `position_overlaps_turn_in` validation rule.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §3: "returns `{ target_lean, roll_rate, a_cmd }`"; §2: only lateral mechanism is `psi_dot = G·tan(phi)/v`. 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §6.1: "the controller steers a lateral drift that reaches the target `f` by `at_s + over_m`, bounded by … `a_lat_pos_max = 0.8 m/s²`", `over_m` (default 15), and "`position` action whose transition window overlaps an active `turn_in` commitment is rejected … `position_overlaps_turn_in`". 04-solver-and-authoring.md §6: "the exit of corner n steers toward the hold of corner n+1 under the lateral `position` budget … when the gap is too short … the line holds as wide as the budget reaches" — shortfall defined for solver holds only, not wire plans. 00-README.md D3: "no handlebar/countersteer channel."
findings.improvement: In 02 §3, specify that `position` compiles to lean setpoints through the same rate-limited tracker via a stated guidance law (e.g. time-optimal S-curve in d(t) under a_lat_pos_max, target_lean = atan((a_corner + a_pos)/g)); add a validation-time reachability check for wire-plan position actions (reject BAD_RANGE or accept with declared partial-reach semantics matching 04 §6's rule); define the end of a turn_in commitment (the `steering_complete` event) so the overlap rule is decidable.

findings.title: P-ROLLRATE contradicts the model's own phi_dot composition — every chop fixture fails it
findings.claim: 09 pins "the realized roll rate never exceeds the rider profile's cap," but 02's equation of motion adds phi_dot_su OUTSIDE the clamp — `phi_dot = clamp(roll_cmd, ±roll_rate) + phi_dot_su` — and the entire point of the run-wide slice is that the stand-up "sheds lean faster than the rider can counter," i.e. realized |phi_dot| exceeds roll_rate during every stand-up event. The property test as written fails on the design's own C30-chop golden; an implementer must guess which document wins.
findings.evidence: 09-verification-and-testing.md §3.4: "`P-ROLLRATE` — the realized roll rate never exceeds the rider profile's cap." 02-physics-model.md §2: "`phi_dot = clamp(roll_cmd, −roll_rate, +roll_rate) + phi_dot_su`"; §5.1: "a stand-up tendency that sheds lean faster than the rider can counter."
findings.improvement: Rescope P-ROLLRATE to the tracker component only ("the commanded/clamped roll term never exceeds the cap") or to samples where phi_dot_su = 0, and add a complementary property that realized roll rate exceeds the cap ONLY when the stand-up term is active.

findings.title: The Sample contract violates its own §1 rule: the entire run-wide channel is engine-known but unrecorded, and the promised a_noreturn HUD display is contract-impossible
findings.claim: 05 §1's rule is "if the engine knew it during the run, the result records it" — yet the engine computes, every step, phi_dot_su and its S_sustained/S_transient split, a_cmd_rate, the realized roll rate, and (for chop) the frozen-rider state, and none appear in the Sample table or the CSV column order; a consumer cannot tell from a trace whether a line ran wide from the transient impulse or the sustained term, cannot audit the `stand_up` diagnosis, and the `slow_steer`/`roll_rate_limited` teaching has no per-sample evidence of rate-railing. Worse, 02 §5.3 promises a_noreturn is "a teachable, inspectable quantity (the HUD may display it)," but it appears neither in the Sample nor in stateAt's `derived` block, and 09's C-HUD-EQUALS-STATEAT forbids the viewer from re-deriving physics — the promised display cannot be built without breaking a mandated contract test. Reserve quantities (mu_use, phiReserve margin) that doctrine checks grade against are likewise per-sample-knowable but unrecorded.
findings.evidence: 05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §1: "If the engine knew it during the run, the result records it — commanded and delivered, kinematic and doctrinal"; §2.1 field table and §8.2 pinned CSV columns contain no stand-up, rate, or reserve fields; §4 `derived` block lists only `v_kmh, sight_margin_m, sight_trend, phi_max_deg, limit_point, action, corner_id, phase`. 02-physics-model.md §5.3: "This crossover is a teachable, inspectable quantity (the HUD may display it)." 09-verification-and-testing.md §6: "`C-HUD-EQUALS-STATEAT` — … The viewer never re-derives physics; this test is the enforcement."
findings.improvement: Append to the Sample (append-only is already allowed by design change): `phi_dot_su` (or the S_sustained/S_transained pair), `a_cmd_rate`, realized `phi_dot`, and a `frozen` flag; add `a_noreturn` and the reserve margins (`phi_reserve_deg`, `grip_reserve`) to stateAt's derived block so the HUD reads them contract-legally.

findings.title: Flagship presets ride at/below the design's own 25 km/h validity line while v_floor = 2 m/s masquerades as the model-validity guard
findings.claim: 00 D3/D5 declare the sub-25 km/h regime out of scope because the lean-driven quasi-static model is invalid there, yet 02 §7 and 01 §8 present v_floor = 2 m/s (7.2 km/h) as the point "below [which] the quasi-static lean model is invalid" — two contradictory validity claims an order of magnitude apart. The book presets live in the gap: bookHairpin (R10) solved at lean_frac 0.70 of the street reserve gives v_apex = √(9.81·10·tan 28.25°) = 7.26 m/s ≈ 26 km/h — one km/h above the declared out-of-scope regime — and every braking, overspeed-recovery, vis-governed, or corrective variant on the presets dwells well below 25 km/h with no placard, violating the project's own "wherever the model cannot honestly answer, the answer is a typed refusal" doctrine. The geometric U-turn refusal (sweep ≥ 170° AND r ≤ 15) does not police speed at all, so nothing does.
findings.evidence: 00-README.md D3: "the sub-25 km/h U-turn regime is out of scope." 02-physics-model.md §7: "`v_floor_ms` 2.0 m/s — model-validity floor: below this the quasi-static lean model is invalid." 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §8: "Below `v_floor` … the lean-driven point-mass model is invalid." 03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §3.1: presets "physically ridable at modest speeds (~25–36 km/h), which is the point"; `bookHairpin` = `R 10 ^150`, suggested entry 28 km/h. 01 §8 placard policy: "Wherever the model cannot honestly answer, the answer is a typed refusal."
findings.improvement: Introduce a distinct model-validity speed band (e.g. `v_valid_min_ms ≈ 7`, TUNING) separate from the numerical v_floor; record dwell-below-validity per sample or as a verdict-level `na`/warn placard; and either re-speed/re-radius the presets so solved apexes clear the band or explicitly (in 01 §8) re-argue why 26–29 km/h apexes are inside the trustworthy regime despite D3's 25 km/h line.

findings.title: tanh(|phi|/PHI0) with PHI0 = 5° is effectively binary over the doctrine range, and invariant 5.4.4's 'negligible below 2°' is quantitatively false
findings.claim: tanh(φ/5°) = 0.96 at 10°, 0.995 at 15°, ≈ 1.0 at all teaching leans — the envelope shapes nothing above ~10°, so a_noreturn's advertised lean-dependence is illusory (5.41 m/s² flat from 15° to the ellipse limit); the envelope's only real roles are continuity through zero and extinguishing at upright, which the doc partly says but §5.3's formula presentation implies a graded crossover that does not exist. Meanwhile invariant 4's claim that "at |phi| < 2° the term is negligible" is false as stated: at φ = 1.9° under max straight-ish braking, S_su·tanh = 0.3·(9.81−2.5)·0.38 ≈ 0.83 rad/s ≈ 48 deg/s — comparable to the street rider's entire roll authority. The PATH effect is negligible (κ at 2° is tiny), but the term is not, and 09's P-RUNWIDE-UPRIGHT tests only φ = 0 exactly, leaving the 0–2° claim untested and untestable as worded.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §5.2: PHI0 = 5.0 deg, "the `tanh(|phi|/PHI0)` envelope keeps the term continuous through zero-lean inflections … and extinguishes it upright"; §5.3 formula divides by tanh(|phi|/PHI0); §5.4.4: "At `|phi| < 2°` the term is negligible: straight-line braking is unchanged pure physics." 09 §3.4: "`P-RUNWIDE-UPRIGHT` — the run-wide term contributes nothing at zero lean."
findings.improvement: State explicitly that the envelope is a continuity device, not a lean-graded onset, and present a_noreturn as lean-independent above ~10°; restate invariant 4 as a falsifiable path bound (e.g. lateral deviation vs the slice-off run < eps over a braking run capped at |φ| ≤ 2°) rather than "the term is negligible."

findings.title: 'stopped' termination has no outcome class — the verdict for a stopped run is unspecified
findings.claim: 02 §7 makes `stopped` a termination reason ("a run that hits v_floor_ms reports `stopped`, never a fabricated low-speed path") and 05's Trajectory carries `terminated: {reason, s, t}`, but the Verdict's closed outcome set is `clean | wide | runoff | violation | crash | dnf-spec-error` with no mapping for a stopped run. A vis-governed line that legitimately brakes to walking pace, or a hard-brake mistake that stops before running wide, produces a verdict whose headline the implementer must invent — exactly the class of silent guesswork D8/the closed-vocabulary discipline exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §7: termination precedence "crash → stopped (`v < v_floor_ms`) → road/corner end"; "a run that hits `v_floor_ms` reports `stopped`." 05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §6.1: "outcome : \"clean\" | \"wide\" | \"runoff\" | \"violation\" | \"crash\" | \"dnf-spec-error\"" — no stopped.
findings.improvement: Define the mapping in 05 §6.1: either add a `stopped` outcome class (with its precedence slot) or specify that a stopped run grades on the checks it completed with `terminated.reason` surfaced in the headline, and pin it with a golden (e.g. a v_floor-terminating brake fixture).

findings.title: Invariant 5.4.5's no-verdict-flip promise cites deadbands that exist only for crash — unfalsifiable for wide/runoff/violation
findings.claim: Invariant 5 requires "no verdict may flip across an infinitesimal input change (deadbands in §7 still apply at classification time)," but §7 defines deadbands only for the crash boundary (eps_phi_deg, eps_mag). The wide/runoff boundary is the binary feasibility of the (unspecified) corrective shot, and violation/clean boundaries are doctrine-check thresholds — none carry a deadband, and discrete classes over continuous inputs must flip somewhere. As written the invariant is either unfalsifiable (no test can be built from it) or unsatisfiable (any test would fail at the class boundaries).
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §5.4.5: "no verdict may flip across an infinitesimal input change (deadbands in §7 still apply at classification time)"; §7: "Crash deadbands (carried…): crash only when `phi > phiMax + eps_phi_deg (0.05°)` or `ellipseMag > 1 + eps_mag (1e-3)`" — no deadband for wide/runoff/violation.
findings.improvement: Either narrow invariant 5 to what it can mean (phi_dot_su is C0 in its inputs; the crash boundary is deadbanded) or specify classification margins for the other boundaries: an f-excursion hysteresis for `wide`, a corrective-feasibility margin (the shot must succeed/fail by a stated buffer) for `runoff`, and per-check deadbands owned by 01.

findings.title: The (target−phi)/dt roll tracker is ambiguous under RK4 — per-stage evaluation gives geometric 0.625-approach, contradicting 'reaches the target within one step'
findings.claim: roll_cmd = clamp((target_lean − phi)/dt, ±roll_rate) embeds the step size in the ODE right-hand side. If evaluated per RK4 stage with the stage's own phi (the natural reading of §2's derivative list plus §6's "four stages share one derivative closure"), the small-error update is Δφ = 0.625·e — the tracker approaches the target geometrically and never reaches it, falsifying §3's claim that it "reaches the target within one step when close." If roll_cmd is instead frozen per step from pre-step phi (ZOH on the command), the claim holds exactly but the derivative closure no longer re-reads phi. The two readings produce different trajectories, different goldens, and different result hashes; the docs never say which is intended, and a dt-dependent RHS is not a well-posed ODE for an RK4 error analysis in any case.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §3: "`roll_cmd = clamp( (target_lean − phi) / dt, −roll_rate, +roll_rate )` … It reaches the target within one step when close, and never overshoots." §2: "`phi_dot = clamp(roll_cmd, −roll_rate, +roll_rate) + phi_dot_su`" (also a redundant double clamp). §6: "The four stages share one derivative closure"; "the controller is read once per step; its command holds across all four stages" — but roll_cmd is not part of the returned command triple.
findings.improvement: Pin the semantics: compute roll_cmd once per step from pre-step phi and hold it across all four stages (making phi's update exact and the 'reaches within one step' claim true), or replace the tracker with a proper dt-free rate law (phi_dot = clamp((target−phi)/tau_roll, ±roll_rate) with tau_roll a named constant). Remove the double clamp.

findings.title: Small contract inconsistencies: grip/n_lat ranges violated at crash samples, degree/radian mixing in formulas, single action_id under concurrent actions
findings.claim: A cluster of implementer traps: (a) `grip` is typed "0..1" and `n_long`/`n_lat` "−1..1", but a crash sample (phi past phiMax or ellipseMag past 1+eps) necessarily records grip < 0 and |n_lat| > 1 — the ranges are wrong at exactly the most-inspected sample of a failed line; (b) state phi is radians (02 §2) while PHI0 is "5.0 deg" and roll_rate is given in deg/s, so tanh(|phi|/PHI0) and the clamp are unit-inconsistent as literally written; (c) a_cmd_rate needs a previous step that doesn't exist at t = 0; (d) `action_id` is a single string ("the plan action currently driving control") but brake and position can be simultaneously active on an approach — which id wins is unspecified.
findings.evidence: 05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §2.1: "`grip` | number | 0..1", "`n_long` | number | −1..1", "`action_id` … `id` of the plan action currently driving control". 02-physics-model.md §2 state table: phi in rad; §5.2 table: PHI0 "5.0 deg"; §3 table: roll_rate_dps in deg/s; §6: a_cmd_rate "finite difference … between consecutive steps." 03 §6.1: brake and position are separate ordered actions with overlapping station windows possible.
findings.improvement: Fix the declared ranges (grip: ≤1, may go slightly negative at deadbanded crash samples; n_*: unbounded magnitude at crash), state the unit-normalization rule once (all §5 formulas in radians; constants converted at load), define a_cmd_rate = 0 at the first step, and specify action_id precedence (e.g. the longitudinal action wins; or make it an array by design change).

findings.title: Quasi-static/no-countersteer turn-in bias is disclosed as a scope cut but its known direction is never placarded where turn-in stations are taught
findings.claim: The scope cut itself is defensible (D3, and 01 §8 lists "gyroscopic and countersteer transients" as refused Tier-3), but the model's turn-in geometry carries a known systematic bias the docs never state: a real initiation includes a countersteer interval where the contact patch tracks outward and curvature onset lags roll, while the quasi-static identity generates inward curvature from the first instant of lean. Solved turn-in stations — a pinned golden quantity ("solved committed lean and turn-in station") and the direct answer of suggestTurnIn — are therefore systematically later, and entry transitions shorter, than a real bike can execute near the roll-rate limit. The bias direction happens to be doctrine-safe (later is the lesson), but presenting the station as a physics-derived teachable number without the one-line bias disclosure overstates precision, against the project's own honest-limitation ethos.
findings.evidence: 02-physics-model.md §2: "Quasi-static lean: curvature is the steady-state value at the current lean. There is no roll inertia state and no handlebar state (D3)"; §8 golden pins "solved committed lean and turn-in station." 04-solver-and-authoring.md §3: suggestTurnIn "answers 'where should I turn in?'". 01-scope-and-doctrine.md §8: Tier-3 cut lists "gyroscopic and countersteer transients." No doc states the bias direction of the simplification.
findings.improvement: Add one sentence to 02 §2 (and the placard vocabulary in 01 §8) stating the known bias: quasi-static initiation omits the countersteer transient, so solved turn-in stations are an upper bound (later) on real-world placement by roughly v·t_transient; optionally surface it as a `na`-style note wherever turn-in stations are displayed as teaching output.

result.walkthrough: I pretended core/ existed exactly as 02 specifies and ran five paper experiments against it, cross-checking 00/01/03/04/05/09 wherever an outcome had to be recorded, solved, or tested. (E1) C30-chop: cutting a_cmd from roll-on to 0 leaves v constant (no engine-braking/drag term exists), the transient term slams phi to ~0, kappa = g·tan(phi)/v² → 0, and the straightened path exits the lane — the D3 run-wide goal genuinely emerges. But the chop's mechanics exposed the transient's impulse nature: a_cmd_rate is a one-step finite difference, so ANY stepped command drop ≥ 0.04 m/s² produces Δphi ≈ K_CHOP·Δa (12 rad for a 2 m/s² chop) — full stand-up in 5 ms, chop severity binary, P-RUNWIDE-MONOTONE vacuous, and gentle mid-corner brake application inexpressible because the brake action's grammar ramps only its release. (E2) Sustained brake-at-lean: differentiating ln kappa = ln tan(phi) − 2 ln v through the slice shows that at exactly a_noreturn the net roll rate is zero by construction, so the line strictly TIGHTENS (v falls, phi holds); at street/30°/15 m/s the widen threshold is 6.70 m/s² vs a_noreturn = 5.41 — invariant 5.4.2 fails on a whole band of its own stated domain, and no constant tuning can fix the boundary case. (E3) Deep lean: the ellipse clip caps a_clip at 5.34 m/s² at 40° — below a_noreturn — so hard braking at maximum lean becomes a stable, grip = 0-margin tightening spiral, the exact behaviour the run-wide slice was built to kill. (E4) bookHairpin: solved apex speed at 0.70 of the street reserve is 7.26 m/s ≈ 26 km/h — one km/h above the regime D3 declares out of scope — while v_floor = 2 m/s masquerades as the validity floor; braking/mistake variants dwell below 25 km/h unplacarded. (E5) Authoring hold-wide: a position action at 34 km/h with default over_m = 15 can deliver at most ~0.5 m of the ~1.1 m a typical f 0.5→0.9 reposition needs, and 02's controller triple has no lateral member — the position→lean guidance law simply isn't specified anywhere. Finally I audited the closure of the doc set: the corrective shot that discriminates runoff from wide is a name both 02 and 04 attribute to each other; P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN contradicts invariant 5.4.1 (light trail braking must tighten AND never tighten); P-ROLLRATE contradicts phi_dot = clamp + phi_dot_su; and the Sample contract omits the entire stand-up channel its own §1 rule demands recorded, making 02's promised a_noreturn HUD display impossible under C-HUD-EQUALS-STATEAT.
wins: The pure-chop composition genuinely produces a run-wide path: with no engine-braking term, a_cmd→0 leaves v constant while the stand-up sheds lean, so kappa collapses and the line straightens outward — D3's core reclassification of chop from inward-pinch to run-wide is delivered by the model form (02 §2, §5.1–5.2).

a_noreturn is dimensionally sound ((rad/s)/((rad/s)/(m/s²)) = m/s²) and its roll-authority-crossover logic is correct for the roll channel — it is a real, teachable quantity even though its geometric meaning needs the fix in the findings (02 §5.3).

Invariant 5.4.1's bit-identity claim is exactly achievable: both relu gates give hard zeros below threshold, so 'Tier 1R ≡ point-mass below onset' is a crisp, falsifiable property — rare discipline in a physics spec (02 §5.2, §5.4.1).
Sub-stage ellipse clipping makes P-ELLIPSE true by construction — no transient grip violation can ever be emitted, exactly as 02 §4/§6 promise.

The transient term is accidentally dt-invariant for stepped commands (integrated Δphi ≈ K_CHOP·Δa regardless of step size) — a resolution-robust impulse formulation, even if currently over-gained and unstated.

The commanded/delivered split recorded per sample (cmd_a vs a_long, cmd_lean vs phi, clipped, n_long/n_lat) is a genuinely good inspection contract; 06's controls strip gets the stand-up deviation display for free from it (05 §2.1, 06 §4).
The one-μ naming policy — physical ceilings vs skill-derated reserves in separately named functions — is a real structural guard against the advisory-limit-as-physical-limit bug class (02 §4).

The emergent-curvature family carries the right causal signs (decel tightens at fixed lean, roll-on widens), so late-apex exit drift and the double-apex inter-touch drift emerge from physics rather than being drawn — D7 is honored by the equations themselves (02 §2).
bookHairpin is deliberately checked against the U-turn refusal (150° < 170°) — the design audits its own scope trap in-line (03 §3.1, 02 §7).
The determinism, event-bracketing, and two-tier time/arc-length scheme in 02 §6 is implementable as written and is what makes the D6 share-inputs-and-recompute honesty story mechanically credible.

verdicts.title: Corrective-shot solver is a name, not a spec — runoff vs wide is undecidable
verdicts.note: Every citation verifies. 02 §7 defines the wide/runoff split entirely by corrective feasibility; 02 §5.6 delegates: "Run-wide correction solving (`04-solver-and-authoring.md`) must integrate with the slice active"; 04 §4.3 delegates straight back: "The corrective-action solver (the 'can this run-wide be saved?' shot, `02-physics-model.md`)". Searched all ten docs: no trigger predicate for `run_wide_detect` (05 §5 lists it and `correction` bare), no start-time rule beyond 02 §3's t_react_s hint, no control policy, no success predicate, no shape for 05 §6.3's `corrective | null`. 03 §7.1 does pin early_apex to exactly `runoff` and chop to wide/runoff, so the mistake oracle is unimplementable without the missing spec. Blocker severity is fair: two headline outcome classes cannot be computed from the doc set.

verdicts.title: P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN flatly contradicts invariant 5.4.1 — the mandated suite cannot be green
verdicts.note: The literal contradiction is real: 09 §3.4's sentence has no threshold qualifier, and a 2.0 m/s² brake at lean must tighten per 02 §5.4.1 and C30-trailbrake. But the blocker claim ("the design's own test regime is unsatisfiable") is defeated by the doc set's own precedence machinery the critic did not weigh: 09 §3.4's preamble states "Each is one sentence here; thresholds and constants belong to `02-physics-model.md`", and 02 §5.4 declares "These are the specification" — invariants 1 and 2 supply the threshold-qualified reading (widening applies beyond A_SU_ONSET/a_noreturn) an implementer is directed to. What survives: P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN's wording is defective and, read alone, contradicts a mandated golden — a major wording bug, not an unsatisfiable suite.

verdicts.title: Invariant 5.4.2 is mathematically false at its own stated boundary: braking at a_noreturn tightens, and a whole decel band above it tightens too
verdicts.note: Algebra re-derived and correct: d(lnκ)/dt = φ̇/(sinφcosφ) + 2a/v. At a = a_noreturn (= 2.5 + 0.873/0.30 = 5.41 for street) the fighting tracker's net φ̇ = 0 by construction of a_noreturn, so φ holds while v falls and κ = G·tanφ/v² strictly rises — the line tightens, contradicting §5.4.2's "the emergent path's radius grows". The band checks out: at φ=30°, v=15, widening needs 0.30a − 0.75 − 0.873 > 2a·sin30·cos30/15, i.e. a > 6.70 m/s², so [5.41, 6.70] tightens despite exceeding the "point of no return"; the tanh equilibrium at a = 6 is φ ≈ 6.0° (tanh(φ/5°) = 0.873/1.05) with v still falling, re-tightening κ past the pre-brake arc before v_floor. No TUNING choice fixes the boundary since a_noreturn is defined as the net-zero-roll point, and §5.4 makes the invariants normative. Major is right.

verdicts.title: At deep lean the friction ellipse clips a_clip below a_noreturn — hard braking at 40° becomes a stable max-grip tightening spiral, the opposite of the book
verdicts.note: The sustained-term math is confirmed: aLongAvail(40°, μ=1) = 9.81·√(1 − tan²40°) = 5.34 < a_noreturn = 5.41 (crossover φ ≈ 39.85°), so S_su ≤ 0.30·(5.34 − 2.5) = 0.852 < roll_rate 0.873 — the sustained stand-up can never beat the fighting rider at deep lean, invariant 5.4.2's premise −a_clip ≥ a_noreturn is unreachable there, and riding ellipseMag = 1 exactly is legal under 02 §7's crash deadband (> 1 + 1e-3), producing a tightening max-grip spiral to v_floor. What fails is the headline scenario: "grabbing a fistful" is a stepped command, which fires S_transient at a_cmd_rate ≈ Δa/dt ≈ 1000 m/s³ (K_CHOP = 6) and violently stands the bike up — the book's cardinal sin does NOT read as a stable trail-brake. The defect is confined to progressively-applied braking (onset rate < RATE_THRESHOLD = 8 m/s³) to max decel at φ ≳ 39.8°. That surviving nucleus — invariant vacuity plus tightening under smooth hard braking in the danger zone — still warrants major.

verdicts.title: The transient term is an impulse ≈ K_CHOP·Δa: any stepped command change ≥ 0.04 m/s² at lean fully stands the bike up in ~5 ms, and plan-onset shaping is unspecified
verdicts.note: Verified: 02 §6 makes a_cmd_rate a one-step finite difference, so a stepped drop Δa yields a one-step lean impulse Δφ ≈ K_CHOP·Δa − K_CHOP·RATE_THRESHOLD·dt = 6Δa − 0.24 rad; a 2 m/s² chop gives ~11.8 rad — every realistic chop saturates to full stand-up in one step, making P-RUNWIDE-MONOTONE vacuous, and its guard's "model's stated validity range" appears nowhere in any doc. 03 §6.1's brake carries only `taper_to_s` (release) with no onset ramp, so any mid-corner brake engagement is a step that fires the transient; and 02 §5.4.3's freeze ("does not re-lean") never pins target-held vs zero-command semantics. One numeric caveat: at Δa = 0.04 the relu is exactly zero and full stand-up needs Δa ≳ 0.13 m/s² (0.04–0.13 gives partial impulses) — a small overreach in the headline that does not affect the consequences or the major severity.

verdicts.title: Position actions have no specified physical channel — the model's only lateral control is lean, and nobody says how position becomes lean
verdicts.note: 02 §3's controller returns exactly {target_lean, roll_rate, a_cmd} and 02 §2's only lateral mechanism is psi_dot = G·tanφ/v; checked 02/03/04/05/07/08 — no guidance law, no heading-realignment condition, no arbitration with the lean tracker anywhere. The representability math verifies: at 9.44 m/s over the default over_m = 15 (T = 1.59 s), bang-bang ±0.8 m/s² gives Δd ≈ 0.8·(0.79)² ≈ 0.51 m, versus 1.08 m for f 0.5→0.9 in the 2.7 m corridor; 03 §6.1's "reaches the target f by at_s + over_m, bounded by a_lat_pos_max" is self-contradictory when unreachable, and 04 §6's shortfall rule ("holds as wide as the budget reaches") covers solver-generated holds only. "When a turn_in commitment ends" is defined nowhere, so chained V2 holds vs 03's position_overlaps_turn_in rejection is undecidable. Major is right — divergent implementations break the reimplement-from-doc golden claim.

verdicts.title: P-ROLLRATE contradicts the model's own phi_dot composition — every chop fixture fails it
verdicts.note: 09 §3.4's P-ROLLRATE is categorical ("the realized roll rate never exceeds the rider profile's cap") while 02 §2 adds phi_dot_su outside the clamp, 02 §3 says physics delivers phi "rate-limited and stand-up-perturbed", and 02 §5.1's premise is shedding lean "faster than the rider can counter" — realized |φ̇| exceeds the cap in every stand-up event, including the C30-chop golden. Unlike P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN, 09's "thresholds and constants belong to 02" deferral cannot rescue it: the defect is the quantifier over which quantity is capped ("realized" = delivered in the doc set's own commanded/delivered vocabulary), not a missing threshold. Property tests run on fixtures per 09 §3.4, so the test as written fails the design's own golden. Major is right.

verdicts.title: The Sample contract violates its own §1 rule: the entire run-wide channel is engine-known but unrecorded, and the promised a_noreturn HUD display is contract-impossible
verdicts.note: The recording gap is real: 05 §2.1's field table, §8.2's pinned CSV columns, and §4's derived block contain no phi_dot_su, no S_sustained/S_transient split, no a_cmd_rate, no reserve fields, and no a_noreturn — verified. But two overstatements: (1) 02 §5.3 says the HUD "may display it" — permission, not a promise — and 07 §2.4 explicitly allows HUD values from "the return value of a pure core function", plus 05 §2.1 is "append-only by design change", so "contract-impossible" overreads a tension that a one-line field append resolves; (2) stand-up and rate-rail evidence is partially reconstructible from the recorded cmd_lean/phi/roll_rate/cmd_a fields — 06 §4 even advertises "phi vs cmd_lean overlaid — the run-wide slice's stand-up deviation is visible here". Surviving nucleus: the Tier-1R disturbance channel and its transient/sustained attribution are unrecorded against 05 §1's own stated rule, and P-ROLLRATE-style auditing of the stand_up diagnosis from a trace alone is not possible. Real, but below the stated major.

verdicts.title: Flagship presets ride at/below the design's own 25 km/h validity line while v_floor = 2 m/s masquerades as the model-validity guard
verdicts.note: The contradiction framing is defeated by doc text: 00 D3's cut is "the sub-25 km/h U-turn regime is out of scope" — a scope characterization of the U-turn regime, policed by the geometric rule that 03 §3.1 explicitly shows the hairpin clearing ("bookHairpin clears the carried out-of-scope cut — U-turn rejection requires angle_deg ≥ 170 and r ≤ 15 m"); 01 §8 ties invalidity to v_floor only ("Below v_floor … the lean-driven point-mass model is invalid"). No doc declares sub-25 km/h model-invalid, so the presets (whose ~25–36 km/h operating point 03 §3.1 states deliberately: "which is the point") do not sit in a "declared out-of-scope regime", and the v_apex ≈ 26 km/h computation, while arithmetically correct, measures against a line the docs never draw. Surviving nucleus (minor, not major): braking, overspeed-recovery, and vis-governed runs will dwell in the 7–25 km/h band with v_floor = 2 m/s as the only guard, and no doc justifies quasi-static-lean validity there or placards it — a fair disclosure gap for a project with an honest-limitation ethos.

verdicts.title: tanh(|phi|/PHI0) with PHI0 = 5° is effectively binary over the doctrine range, and invariant 5.4.4's 'negligible below 2°' is quantitatively false
verdicts.note: Numbers verify: tanh(2) = 0.964, tanh(3) = 0.995 — a_noreturn is flat at ≈5.41 m/s² from 15° to the ellipse limit, and 02 §5.3 itself only ever evaluates "at meaningful lean (tanh → 1)" while presenting a φ-dependent formula; the envelope's real roles (continuity through zero, extinguish upright) are the ones §5.2 names. The 5.4.4 falsity checks out: at φ = 1.9° under ~9.81 m/s² braking, S_su·tanh = 0.30·7.31·tanh(0.38) ≈ 0.83 rad/s ≈ 48°/s — comparable to the street profile's entire 50°/s roll authority, so "the term is negligible" is false as stated (only the path effect is negligible), and 09's P-RUNWIDE-UPRIGHT tests φ = 0 exactly, leaving 0–2° untested. Minor severity is right.

verdicts.title: 'stopped' termination has no outcome class — the verdict for a stopped run is unspecified
verdicts.note: 02 §7 makes `stopped` a termination reason ("a run that hits v_floor_ms reports `stopped`") and 05 §2's Trajectory carries terminated: {reason, s, t}, but 05 §6.1's closed outcome set (clean | wide | runoff | violation | crash | dnf-spec-error) has no mapping for it; 08 §3.1's exit-0 enumeration ("clean, wide, runoff, violation, crash") omits it too, and no doc says what headline a stopped run gets. Checked all ten docs — 07 §3.4 treats "stop" only as a terminal badge, and 05 §5 has a `stop` event kind, neither of which resolves the verdict headline. Minor severity is right.

verdicts.title: Invariant 5.4.5's no-verdict-flip promise cites deadbands that exist only for crash — unfalsifiable for wide/runoff/violation
verdicts.note: 02 §7 defines classification deadbands for crash only (eps_phi_deg 0.05°, eps_mag 1e-3); eps_m and eps_deg_report are labelled "Reporting tolerances". The wide/runoff boundary is the binary feasibility of the unspecified corrective shot (finding 1), and no doctrine-check deadband exists anywhere in the set — the only other deadband is 03 §5.1's sight_trend_deadband_m, which governs the trend field, not a verdict. 09 §3.1 even leans on the same nonexistent machinery ("discrete-verdict flips prevented by the deadbands specified in 02-physics-model.md"). As stated, 5.4.5 cannot be turned into a test for three of the boundaries. Minor severity is right.

verdicts.title: The (target−phi)/dt roll tracker is ambiguous under RK4 — per-stage evaluation gives geometric 0.625-approach, contradicting 'reaches the target within one step'
verdicts.note: Both readings are textually licensed and produce different trajectories. Per-stage: 02 §6's "four stages share one derivative closure" plus §4's precedent that stage quantities use "the stage's own phi" puts (target_lean − phi)/dt inside the RHS; RK4 on φ̇ = (T − φ)/dt with hλ = 1 gives amplification R(−1) = 1 − 1 + 1/2 − 1/6 + 1/24 = 0.375, i.e. Δφ = 0.625·e — geometric approach, never reaching, falsifying §3's "reaches the target within one step when close". Per-step ZOH: §6 holds "its command" across stages, but the returned command triple {target_lean, roll_rate, a_cmd} excludes roll_cmd, so the ZOH sentence does not settle it. The double clamp in §2 is indeed redundant. Different goldens/hashes under the two readings; minor severity is right.

verdicts.title: Small contract inconsistencies: grip/n_lat ranges violated at crash samples, degree/radian mixing in formulas, single action_id under concurrent actions
verdicts.note: All four verify: (a) crash requires ellipseMag > 1 + 1e-3 or phi > phiMax + 0.05° (02 §7), and 05 §3.1 retains "a final exact sample at termination", so the crash sample necessarily records grip = 1 − ellipseMag < 0 or |n_lat| > 1 (lean-driven a_lat is not clipped — only a_cmd is), violating 05 §2.1's typed "0..1"/"−1..1" ranges; (b) 02 §2 types phi in rad while PHI0 = "5.0 deg" and roll_rate_dps is deg/s — tanh(|phi|/PHI0) and the clamp are unit-mixed as literally written; (c) a_cmd_rate is "the finite difference … between consecutive steps" with no rule for the first step; (d) 05 §2.1's action_id is a single string but 03 §6.1 permits brake and position windows to overlap on an approach (only position×turn_in overlap is rejected) with no precedence rule. Polish severity is right.

verdicts.title: Quasi-static/no-countersteer turn-in bias is disclosed as a scope cut but its known direction is never placarded where turn-in stations are taught
verdicts.note: Verified across all ten docs: 02 §2/§5.5 and 01 §8 disclose the cut (no roll inertia, no handlebar/countersteer state) but no doc states the resulting direction of the turn-in-station bias, while 02 §8 pins "solved committed lean and turn-in station" as a golden quantity and 04 §3 presents suggestTurnIn as the direct answer to "where should I turn in?". The claimed direction is physically sound — the quasi-static identity generates inward curvature from the first instant of lean, where a real initiation has a countersteer interval with outward contact-patch track and curvature lagging roll, so solved turn-ins are systematically later and entry transitions shorter than a real bike near the roll-rate limit. The finding correctly concedes the bias is doctrine-safe; polish severity (a one-line disclosure ask, per the project's honest-limitation ethos) is right.

result.walkthrough: I simulated a cold-start agent doing exactly what 08 §2 promises is possible: work only from `linelab schema` + `explain` output, following the six recipes in 08 §6 and the workflows in 04 §8. Recipe (a) works as written: `run --road ... --entry 55 --turn-in auto`, exit 0, one JSON envelope on stdout, parseable. The trouble started the moment I stepped off the golden path. (1) I tried to inspect an instant of the run from the CLI — 05 §4 says `stateAt` is "exposed identically in the library and as a CLI verb", but 08 §3's verb table has no such verb, and no other verb takes an {s|t} query; per-instant CLI inspection is unreachable. (2) I ran `explain` on a failing envelope and got the doc's own example hint — "move `plan.b1.at_s` earlier" — but for a solver-authored line the envelope's LineResult carries only `{kind:"solve", solveSpec}` + trajectory + verdict (05 §7): the solved four-action wire plan is recorded nowhere, so there is no artifact in which `plan.b1.at_s` exists to edit or sweep; the explain→fix loop dead-ends. (3) I tried `sweep` on entry speed (the axis `overspeed` proves matters) — the grammar is `--param plan.<id>.<field>` only; entry speed, `config.mu`, `vis_margin`, constraint values and mistake params are all unaddressable, and sweep takes a scenario file that solver flows never emit. (4) I put `--gate` on the canonical fig-8.1 run (ideal + intended-fail mistake): 08 §3.1 says exit 3 on "a failed doctrine check", so the most canonical figure in the book apparently exits 3 when it succeeds — unless --gate is per-role/expect_fail-aware, which no doc says. (5) I ran `solve` on `bookEsses`: 04 §5 says a linked line is "contained, not clean", 08 §3 says "Non-clean solve exits 3", and 05 §6.1's closed outcome set has no "contained" value — three docs collide. (6) I tried composing mistakes: the verb spells `kind[:k=v,…] --corners c1,c2`, the sugar spells `early_apex@c1,c2`, the scene spells `mistake early_apex early_by_m=6 scope=...` — whether `kind:k=v@c1,c2` is one legal token, and which line in a multi-line `--on <solved.json>` is the base, is nowhere stated. (7) `compare A.json B.json` across two different roads: "station-aligned metric diff ... at shared stations" silently presumes one road; no refusal is specified and no error code fits. (8) `--line-id` appears in 08 §4.1's flag list and is never defined in any doc, while three operations (run --trace, export --as trace-csv, mistake --on) need exactly a per-line selector and have none. (9) Finally I asked which door an agent should use: the zero-file path is celebrated as the agent door, but everything beyond a scenario — labels, view, N lines — lives only in indentation-sensitive scene text (a third spelling of every field), and no verb accepts a Figure/FigureSpec as JSON, so D6's recompute-a-shared-spec promise has no CLI entrance at all. The single-scenario core (schema_ref errors, one-JSON stdout, exit tiers, D8/INEFFECTUAL) held up well throughout; nearly every failure was at the seams between verbs, layers, and the three grammars.

findings.title: stateAt promised as a CLI verb but absent from the verb table
findings.claim: Per-instant inspection from the CLI — a headline capability of the result contract — cannot be invoked as designed. 05 promises a CLI verb; 08's verb table (presented as the complete surface: 'One binary, `linelab <verb>`') contains no stateAt verb and no other verb accepts an {s|t} query, a line selector, or emits an InstantState. An implementer must invent the verb's entire syntax (query flags, line selection in a multi-line envelope, output wrapping) with zero guidance.
findings.evidence: 05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §4: '`stateAt` is exposed identically in the library and as a CLI verb (`08-cli-and-agent-interface.md`), so an agent inspects any instant of any line — including failed lines — without parsing CSVs or re-running the engine.' 08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §3 verb table lists only run, solve, mistake, scene, render, compare, sweep, check, schema, explain, serve, export — no stateAt. 08 §7.1 does import `stateAt` in the API list, confirming the library half only.
findings.improvement: Add a `state` verb row to 08 §3: `state <envelope.json> --line <line_id> (--s <m> | --t <s>)` → one InstantState JSON on stdout; specify that omitting --line on a multi-line envelope is a SCHEMA error naming the available line_ids, and that out-of-range queries surface 05 §4's BAD_RANGE with the valid interval.

findings.title: Solved and compiled plans are not recorded in the envelope — the explain→edit→sweep loop is unactionable
findings.claim: For solver-authored and mistake-compiled lines, the resolved wire plan (the canonical four actions with their ids and stations) appears nowhere in the result contract: LineResult carries only source ({kind:'solve', solveSpec} or {kind:'mistake', base_line_id, mistakeSpec}), trajectory, and verdict. Yet 08's own explain example tells the agent to 'move `plan.b1.at_s` earlier', sweep addresses `plan.<id>.<field>` of a scenario file the solver flows never produce, and stateAt's derived.action must return 'the full resolved PlanAction for action_id' — data the documented envelope does not contain. The design's flagship feedback loop (run → explain → adjust the named field → re-run/sweep) cannot be executed for any solver-authored line, and no export format ('Result JSON | Trace CSV | Static SVG') emits the solved scenario either.
findings.evidence: 05 §7 LineResult fields: 'source ... | trajectory | verdict' with solve lines recording only 'the solver inputs'; 04 §4.2 'The solved plan is the canonical four actions'; 08 §5.2 remediation hint 'move `plan.b1.at_s` earlier'; 08 §3 sweep: '--param plan.<id>.<field>'; 05 §4 derived.action: 'the full resolved PlanAction for action_id, or null'; 05 §8.2 export table has no solved-scenario format. 03 §7 compileMistake returns a plan at API level, but 05 §7 gives it no envelope slot.
findings.improvement: Add a pinned `resolved_scenario` (post-validation, absolute-station wire scenario) member to LineResult for every line regardless of source kind — it is what stateAt resolves action_id against, what explain's hints refer to, and what sweep consumes (optionally add `export --as scenario --line <id>`). State explicitly that resolved_scenario is output provenance, not shareable input (FigureSpec still carries sources only), so D6 is untouched.

findings.title: run→solve delegation: trigger list incomplete, failure exit tier undefined, and the 'says so in the envelope' field does not exist in 05
findings.claim: Three defects in the universal-front-door story. (a) The enumerated delegation triggers omit `--brake auto` (a bisection, solver-only) and `--constraint` (solver-layer by D10 — 'the engine never sees one'), so `run --constraint ...` with an explicit turn-in either delegates (unlisted) or carries a provably dead input (the exact class D8 forbids). (b) When the internal solve fails — non-clean self-verify or NO_SOLUTION — run's exit is undefined: exit 0 is 'any physics outcome', exit 3 is 'a non-clean `solve`' (the verb? the internal call?); an agent cannot predict whether `run --turn-in auto` on an infeasible corner exits 0, 2, or 3. (c) The claim that run 'says so in the envelope' has no pinned field: 05 §7's only candidate is per-line source.kind='solve', which 08 never names, FigureResult.meta is 'presentation hints only', and 08 §4.2 simultaneously claims flag/file composition is 'indistinguishable downstream, including in the envelope's recorded input'.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 run row: 'if the composed input needs solving (`--turn-in auto`, any `--mistake`, `--visibility-governed`), `run` delegates to the solver internally and says so in the envelope'; 08 §4.1 lists `--brake <auto|decel>` and `--constraint`; 00 D10 / 04 §4.5: 'a constraint never appears in the wire plan and the engine never sees one'; 08 §3.1 exit 0 'Ran — any physics outcome' vs exit 3 'a non-clean `solve`'; 05 §7: FigureResult has no delegation marker; meta is 'presentation hints only, never physics'.
findings.improvement: Make the trigger rule intensional, not enumerated: 'run delegates whenever the composed input contains any solver-layer field (turn-in auto, brake auto, mistakes, vis mode/knobs, constraints)'. Pin the exit rule: run always exits by outcome tier, with NO_SOLUTION from a delegated solve surfacing as exit 3 (or 2 — but choose), and name the envelope marker explicitly: 'delegation is recorded as LineResult.source.kind = "solve"' in both 08 and 05.

findings.title: --gate is undefined over multi-line envelopes containing intended-fail mistake lines
findings.claim: The design's most canonical workflow — ideal + mistake overlay (recipe b, fig 8.1) — collides with --gate: a mistake line fails doctrine checks by construction, so if the gate quantifies over all lines, every good-vs-mistake figure exits 3 even when it is exactly what the author wanted, making --gate useless in CI for the tool's primary artifact. No doc states whether the gate applies per line, only to non-mistake roles, or only to the first/ideal line; nor whether compileMistake populates the scenario-level `expect_fail` oracle so the gate can discount pinned failures.
findings.evidence: 08 §3.1: exit 3 = '`run --gate` with a failed doctrine check'; 08 §6(b) two-line envelope 'green ideal, red `early_apex` running wide'; 03 §6 `expect_fail` 'declares doctrine checks a *legitimate* non-clean line is expected to fail' — defined on a single scenario, with no stated connection to compiled mistake lines or to --gate; 05 §7 gives the envelope no per-line gate/expected-outcome field.
findings.improvement: Specify gate scope: --gate evaluates each line against its own expectation — mistake-sourced lines gate on matching their kind's pinned outcome class (03 §7.1), other lines gate on doctrine pass minus their expect_fail set; exit 3 only when a line misses its expectation. This turns --gate into a real regression gate for figures instead of a footgun.

findings.title: Chained solve is 'contained, not clean', non-clean solve exits 3, and the closed outcome set has no 'contained' value
findings.claim: Three normative statements cannot all hold. 04 declares a correctly-ridden linked line 'contained, not clean' and grades it green via a chain-aware check set; 08 declares 'Non-clean solve exits 3 (the authoring gate)'; 05's closed outcome vocabulary (clean|wide|runoff|violation|crash|dnf-spec-error) has no value for 'contained'. As specified, an agent running `solve` on `bookEsses` gets either a doctrinally-correct green line with exit 3 (teaching agents to avoid the explicit authoring door for chains) or an outcome value the contract does not define. Recipe (d) quietly sidesteps this by using `run` for the chain — evidence the seam is real.
findings.evidence: 04 §5: 'A linked line is **contained, not clean** ... graded by a chain-aware check set ... maps to **green**'; 08 §3 solve row: 'Non-clean solve exits 3 (the authoring gate)'; 05 §6.1: 'outcome : "clean" | "wide" | "runoff" | "violation" | "crash" | "dnf-spec-error"'; 08 §6(d) uses `run`, not `solve`, for the chain.
findings.improvement: Redefine the solve exit rule against the verdict, not the outcome word: exit 3 iff the line fails its applicable bar (single-corner clean bar, or the chain-aware bar for linked sequences). Either add a `contained` outcome to 05 §6.1's set with its precedence position, or state explicitly that contained linked lines carry outcome 'clean' under the chain-aware grading and strike the 'not clean' phrasing from 04 §5.

findings.title: The mistake spec has three spellings with no composed grammar, precedence, or base-line selection
findings.claim: An agent must guess whether params and scope compose inside one token: the verb spells `mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --on <file> [--corners c1,c2]`, the flag sugar spells `--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"`, and the scene spells `mistake early_apex early_by_m=6 scope=all_corners`. Is `--mistake "early_apex:early_by_m=6@c1,c2"` legal? Is `@all_corners` spellable in the shorthand, or is all_corners scene/JSON-only? What wins if both `--corners` and `@…` appear? And the verb's `--on <solved.json>` takes an envelope that may hold N lines with no stated rule for which is the base (the scene layer pins 'the figure's first ride line'; the CLI is silent). Every one of these is a first-try trap against the design bar.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 mistake row: '`mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --on <solved.json> [--corners c1,c2]` ... Also available as repeatable `--mistake` sugar'; 08 §6(d): '--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"'; 03 §7.2: 'the CLI's `<kind>@c1,c2` shorthand ... maps to it' plus `scope: "all_corners"`; 04 §7: scene form 'mistake <kind> [key=val …] [scope=…]' and 'compiled against the figure's first `ride` line'. No doc states the combined token grammar or CLI base-line rule.
findings.improvement: Define one canonical mistake-spec token grammar — `<kind>[:k=v[,k=v…]][@<cornerId>[,…]|@all]` — used identically by the verb, the sugar, and (space-normalized) the scene; forbid `--corners` when `@` is present (SCHEMA, not silent precedence); adopt the scene's first-ideal-line rule for `--on` and allow `--line-id` to override; print all of it in `schema cli` and `schema mistakes`.

findings.title: sweep can only address plan.<id>.<field> — none of the axes an author actually wants to sweep are reachable
findings.claim: The interesting one-dimensional questions in this design are: at what entry speed does the corner stop being clean (rider.start.speed_kmh — the axis the `overspeed` kind exists to teach), how does the line degrade with mu (config.mu), how does caution trade exit speed (vis_margin, D10's own knob), how tight can a constraint bound get before NO_SOLUTION (constraint value), and how sensitive is a mistake to early_by_m. Every one of these lives outside `plan.<id>.<field>`, so none is sweepable. Compounding it: sweep takes `<scenario>` (a file — the zero-file path does not extend to it), the solver flows emit envelopes rather than scenario files (see the solved-plan finding), the `--metric list` vocabulary is never defined, and the grid cap behind the `truncated` flag has no stated value.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 sweep row: '`sweep <scenario> --param plan.<id>.<field> --range a:b:step [--param2 …] [--metric list]` | Grid-sweep 1–2 fields (id-addressed, never array-indexed — carried) ... capped grid with an explicit `truncated` flag'; 03 §6 places speed at `rider.start.speed_kmh` and mu at `config.mu` — not under plan; 04 §6 defines `vis_margin` as a solve-spec field; 04 §4.5 constraints are solver-layer only.
findings.improvement: Widen the address grammar to the whole composed input: `start.speed_kmh`, `config.mu`, `solve.vis_margin`, `constraints.<id>.value`, `mistake.<line_id>.early_by_m`, alongside `plan.<id>.<field>` (still id-addressed); let sweep accept the same zero-file flags as run so the swept base can be composed inline; enumerate the metric vocabulary (verdict scalars: apex_pct, v_apex_kmh, grip_min, sight.margin_min_m, outcome, exit.f, …) in `schema cli`; state the grid cap value.

findings.title: compare semantics unspecified: input kinds, line pairing, and cross-road diffs
findings.claim: compare 'runs all inputs' and emits 'a station-aligned metric diff ... at shared stations' plus 'an overlay figure' — all three phrases silently presume the inputs share one road. Nothing specifies what happens when they do not (different DSL, or same corner at different scale): no refusal is mandated, no error code fits (each input is individually valid, so SCHEMA/BAD_RANGE misfire), and a naive implementation will happily diff station 40 of road A against station 40 of road B and emit doctrinally meaningless numbers — worse than an error for an agent. Also unspecified: the accepted input kinds (scenario? envelope? FigureSpec? recipe (c) passes solve outputs), how lines pair when both inputs are multi-line envelopes (by line_id? label? order?), and the diff domain when trajectories have different lengths (intersection? padded?).
findings.evidence: 08 §3 compare row: 'compare <A.json> <B.json> […] [--lock station|time] ... Run all inputs, emit per-line verdict deltas plus a station-aligned metric diff (sight, speed, lean, grip at shared stations) and an overlay figure'; 05 §7: 'One road per figure. Lines that need different roads are different figures' — a constraint compare would need to enforce but is never told to; 08 §6(c) passes two solve outputs without stating their type.
findings.improvement: Specify: inputs are anything run accepts plus envelopes/FigureSpecs (recomputed per D6); all inputs must resolve to spec-hash-identical roads, else a typed refusal (add sub-reason `road_mismatch` under SCHEMA or introduce it under BAD_RANGE — pick one); pairing is by line_id with unpaired lines listed, not dropped; the station diff runs over the intersection of sample ranges with the clipped span recorded in the output.

findings.title: --line-id is listed but never defined, and every operation needing a per-line selector lacks one
findings.claim: `--line-id <id>` appears once, in the zero-file flag enumeration, with no semantics anywhere in 03/04/05/08: does it name the authored line in the emitted envelope, select the base for --mistake, or select a line for output? Meanwhile the operations that genuinely need a line selector have none: `run --trace out.csv` on a two-line envelope (which line's CSV?), `export <envelope> --as trace-csv` (05 says the CSV is 'per line'; export's syntax has no selector), `mistake --on <envelope>` (which base line?), and the missing stateAt verb. With multiple repeatable `--mistake` flags, the ids of the generated mistake lines are also unspecified, so even a selector would have nothing predictable to name.
findings.evidence: 08 §4.1: '... `--constraint "<token>"` (repeatable ...), `--line-id <id>`.' — the flag's only appearance; 08 §3 run row shows `--trace out.csv` with no selector; 08 §3 export row: 'export <envelope.json> --as share-url|trace-csv|svg|envelope [--out …]'; 05 §8.2: 'Trace CSV (per line)'; 05 §7 requires 'line_id // stable string' but no doc states how CLI-composed lines are named.
findings.improvement: Define --line-id in 08 §4.1 as naming the primary authored line (default `ideal`), and pin the generated-id rule for sugar lines (e.g. `<kind>` or `<kind>@<scope>`, deduplicated → DUP_ID on collision). Add a uniform `--line <id>` selector to trace/export/state/mistake, defaulting to the sole line and erroring (SCHEMA, listing available ids) when the envelope is multi-line.

findings.title: Authored plan flags composed with the solver reopen the accepted-but-ignored hole D8 exists to abolish
findings.claim: The zero-file flag set lets an agent pass `--position`, `--brake <decel>`, and `--throttle <spec>` alongside `--turn-in auto`, and precedence says flags compose into one input that is validated and run. But the solve pipeline's output is 'the canonical four actions' — brake, turn-in, crack, roll-on — with no stated merge rule for author-supplied actions. Either the solver discards the authored `--position` (a schema-valid input that silently does nothing — precisely the class D8 forbids, and the exact field, `position`, whose prior silent death motivated D8), or it must incorporate it into the search, which no section specifies. Hold-wide authoring — the capability position actions exist for per 03 — is thus undefined exactly when combined with the agent-default `--turn-in auto`.
findings.evidence: 08 §4.1 flag set includes '--turn-in <auto|s>`, `--brake <auto|decel>`, `--throttle <spec>`, `--position <spec>`' with no composition caveat; 08 §4.2: 'Apply flags ... Validate the composed input'; 04 §4.2: 'The solved plan is the canonical four actions'; 00 D8: 'Every accepted input does something'; 03 §6.1: '`position` is the approach/exit tool that makes hold-wide authoring ... possible.'
findings.improvement: Specify the merge contract: authored brake/throttle values pin the corresponding solver control (skipping that bisection), and authored `position` actions are carried verbatim into every candidate plan the solver runs (present in the coarse sweep, the bisections, and self-verify). Any authored action the solver cannot honor is a typed INEFFECTUAL/NO_SOLUTION at compose time — never dropped.

findings.title: Error-code assignment is undecidable for several specified rejections, and INEFFECTUAL's definition has drifted
findings.claim: Several rejections the docs mandate carry no code, so implementers will assign inconsistently and agents lose the 'greppable across a whole agent session' property: the reserved DSL width suffix ('typed error that names the reservation' — SCHEMA? OUT_OF_SCOPE?), `apex:` refs in plans ('rejected ... with a typed error'), a mistake targeting a road with no corners, and out-of-domain fractions like `vis_hold_f = 1.7` (SCHEMA type-valid, BAD_RANGE 'non-physical number'? — the boundary between the two codes is never stated for unit-interval-ish fields). Separately, INEFFECTUAL is defined as 'input that would validate but provably do nothing', yet `position_overlaps_turn_in` uses it for an action that would very much do something (fight an active steering commitment) and is rejected by policy — a conflict, not a dead field — blurring the code's meaning for anyone grepping by it.
findings.evidence: 03 §3: 'The v1 parser rejects it with a typed error that names the reservation'; 03 §6.1: 'validate rejects `apex:` refs with a typed error' and '(INEFFECTUAL, `position_overlaps_turn_in`)'; 08 §7.2: 'INEFFECTUAL ... would validate but provably do nothing — rejected, naming the dead field'; 08 §7.2 BAD_RANGE: 'Non-physical number (negative radius, `mu ≤ 0`, …)' — no rule for range-vs-schema on bounded fractions.
findings.improvement: Add a decision rule to 08 §7.2 (type/shape wrong → SCHEMA; well-typed but outside physical domain → BAD_RANGE; well-typed, in-domain, but provably without effect → INEFFECTUAL; deliberate scope cut → OUT_OF_SCOPE), then assign every rejection named in 03/04 explicitly. Reclassify position_overlaps_turn_in under SCHEMA (structural conflict) or mint the reason under a documented 'conflicting-inputs' reading of INEFFECTUAL — but say which.

findings.title: The schema output's own structure is unspecified — 'schema text (wrapped)'
findings.claim: The entire design bar rests on an agent bootstrapping from `linelab schema` output, yet the shape of that output is the one contract never pinned: '(wrapped)' implies prose-in-a-JSON-string, but the mistakes section is described as a table, the envelope section documents the full Sample/verdict contract, and the cli section carries the flag↔field mapping — an agent needs to know whether it gets navigable JSON (sections as keys, kinds as objects with parameter/default/outcome fields) or a text blob to read. The full no-argument dump (ten sections including the complete output contract) is also large enough that section-granular retrieval is the realistic agent pattern, which only works well if the wrapper is structured.
findings.evidence: 08 §3.2: 'stdout is exactly one JSON document per invocation — the envelope, the validation report, the schema text (wrapped), the table'; 08 §5.1: 'Sections (closed list, versioned with the schema): scenario, plan, road-dsl, occluders, mistakes, solve, scene, view, envelope, cli' and 'The mistakes section is a teaching table'; 09 (per 08 §2) tests cold-start 'from the printed `schema` output alone' — format unstated.
findings.improvement: Pin the wrapper in 05-or-08: `{ok:true, value:{version, sections:{<name>: {fields|kinds|grammar, prose}}}}` with per-kind/per-field objects (name, type, default, units, effect, book_ref) and prose confined to `message`-style keys — the same structure-plus-sentences discipline `explain` already commits to.

findings.title: The figure layer has no JSON door: scene text is a mandatory second grammar and FigureSpec is not loadable by any verb — the zero-file default is pushed at the wrong layer
findings.claim: For an agent, writing a file is free; what is expensive is learning grammars. The design celebrates the zero-file path as the agent door, but zero-file only reaches the single-scenario layer: everything figure-shaped (N lines, roles, labels, callouts, view, note) is authorable only as indentation-sensitive scene text — a third spelling of every field (entry=34/vis=cautious/visHold= vs --entry/--visibility-governed/--vis-hold vs the JSON schema names) and a whitespace-significant format that is a classic agent failure mode. 03 §8 defines the Figure object and 05 §8.1 defines FigureSpec as canonical JSON, yet `scene` accepts only `.scene` files and no verb accepts a Figure/FigureSpec JSON at all — so D6's 'any consumer recomputes' promise has no CLI entrance for the very payload the share URL carries, and the stated principle 'Anything expressible by flag is expressible in JSON and vice versa — flags are sugar, not a second schema' is true at the scenario layer and false one layer up, where scene text is exactly a second schema. This is a scope/default argument, not an omission complaint: the zero-file investment solves a human friction agents don't have, while the agent-shaped door (one canonical JSON accepted everywhere) is missing at the figure layer.
findings.evidence: 08 §1: 'The CLI is the primary door for AI agents'; 08 §4: 'linelab requires none [no file]'; 08 §4.1: 'flags are sugar, not a second schema'; 08 §3 scene row accepts only '<file.scene>'; 04 §7 scene grammar: 'Top-level keys at column 0; `lines:` and `labels:` entries indented'; 03 §8 Figure object; 05 §8.1 FigureSpec with '#f=' URL form; no verb in 08 §3 lists FigureSpec/Figure JSON among its inputs (serve takes 'scenario|scene|envelope').
findings.improvement: Make FigureSpec JSON a first-class input: `scene` (or run) accepts `figure.json` interchangeably with `.scene` text, with the scene format redefined as sugar that compiles to FigureSpec (mirroring the flags→scenario relationship); add `export --as figure-spec` so the loop closes; then state in 08 that the recommended agent door is JSON-in/JSON-out at both layers, with flags and scene text as human sugar.

findings.title: The dnf-spec-error outcome is unmapped to exit tiers and unreachable given validate-as-sole-rejection-point
findings.claim: 05's closed outcome set includes `dnf-spec-error`, but 08's exit-0 row enumerates only five outcomes ('clean, wide, runoff, violation, crash'), and no doc explains how a spec error becomes a per-line outcome when 03 declares validation 'the sole rejection point' (which exits 2 before any line runs). The plausible scenario — a multi-line bake where one line's spec fails while siblings are fine — has no specified behavior: whole-figure exit 2, or a partial envelope with one dnf-spec-error line at exit 0? An agent cannot know which to handle.
findings.evidence: 05 §6.1: 'outcome : "clean" | "wide" | "runoff" | "violation" | "crash" | "dnf-spec-error"'; 08 §3.1 exit 0: 'Ran — any physics outcome (`clean`, `wide`, `runoff`, `violation`, `crash`)'; 03 §6: 'Validation ... is the sole rejection point'; 04 §7 scene lines may include 'plan <file.json>' — the obvious partial-failure source.
findings.improvement: Pick and pin one policy: either all-or-nothing (any line's spec failure → exit 2, no envelope; delete dnf-spec-error from the outcome set) or partial results (bad line becomes a trajectory-less LineResult with outcome dnf-spec-error, figure exits 0, error detail in the line's verdict) — and mirror the chosen list in both 05 §6.1 and 08 §3.1.

findings.title: Output-discipline edge cases: --out's two meanings, --render on run absent from the verb table, sweep's TSV, and no channel for proportion-gate failure
findings.claim: Four seams in the one-JSON-on-stdout discipline. (a) `--out` means 'write the envelope JSON to this file' in recipe (b) (`--out out/fig81.json`) but 'write figures into this directory' in §4's prose (`--out fig/ --render diagram`) — same flag, two semantics, and neither `--out` nor `--render` appears in run's verb-table syntax; what stdout carries when --out is given is unstated. (b) `sweep` promises a 'TSV/JSON table' with no flag selecting the format and no statement of how TSV squares with 'stdout is exactly one JSON document'. (c) Recipe (b) 'expects' an SVG that passes the proportion gate, but render defines no reporting or exit behavior for a gate failure — exit 3's '(per 09) a failed test/gate run' reads as the test harness, not the render verb — so a failing figure renders silently at exit 0 with the agent left to re-derive pass/fail from manifest metrics. (d) `check <file.scene>` duplicates `scene --check` with no statement that they are the same code path.
findings.evidence: 08 §3 run row syntax: 'run [<scenario.json>|-] [zero-file flags] [--gate] [--trace out.csv]' (no --out/--render); 08 §4: 'Add `--out fig/ --render diagram`'; 08 §6(b): '--out out/fig81.json'; 08 §3 sweep row: 'TSV/JSON table of metrics per cell'; 08 §3.2: 'stdout is exactly one JSON document per invocation'; 08 §6(b): 'a compact book-proportioned SVG that passes the proportion gate (**06**)'; 08 §3 check row vs scene row '--check'.
findings.improvement: Complete run's syntax line with --out/--render and define: stdout always carries the envelope; --out additionally writes files, --render selects figure output (its own directory flag distinct from the envelope path). Give sweep a `--format tsv|json` where tsv implies --out (stdout stays JSON). Make render/`run --render` include the gate verdict in the manifest JSON on stdout and honor --gate (exit 3 on proportion-gate failure). State that `check file.scene` ≡ `scene --check`.

findings.title: explain's accepted inputs omit mistake kinds, which 03 requires explain to handle
findings.claim: 03 makes `explain(kind)` the load-bearing mitigation for the premature/early_apex naming trap — 'the naming trap is documented at the API surface' — but 08's explain verb accepts only '<envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>'; a mistake kind is none of these, so the mandated call has no CLI spelling. The positional argument is also ambiguous by construction (a file path is disambiguated from a checkId only by existence-on-disk, which no doc states).
findings.evidence: 03 §7.1: '`explain(kind)` must state each kind's pinned outcome and book figure so an agent picks the right kind for the intended lesson on the first try'; 08 §3 explain row: 'explain <envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>'; 08 §5.2 elaborates only 'given an envelope' and 'given a check id or error code'.
findings.improvement: Extend explain's input set to '<envelope.json | checkId | errorCode | mistakeKind>' in 08 §3/§5.2, and pin the disambiguation order (existing file → envelope; else exact match against the closed check/error/kind vocabularies; else SCHEMA listing the vocabularies).

wins: The closed, greppable error vocabulary with mandatory {ok:false, error:{code, at, message, schema_ref?}} and 'errors teach' (08 §2, §3.2, §7.2) is genuinely excellent agent UX — one round trip from mistake to fix, and the D8/INEFFECTUAL abolition of the accepted-but-inert tier removes the worst silent failure class an agent faces.

Exit codes as outcome tiers rather than sim success (08 §3.1) — 'a crash is a valid, interesting run' at exit 0, input errors at 2, doctrine at 3, write failures at 1 that 'never mask the doctrine tier' — is exactly the right shape for a laboratory tool driven by scripts.
stdout-is-one-JSON-document / stderr-is-for-humans (08 §3.2), with --pretty still emitting valid JSON, means an agent may always JSON.parse(stdout) — a discipline most CLIs never achieve.
The CLI-as-thin-shell over a pure, synchronous, Result-based API with 'no CLI-only enrichment' (08 §7.1) lets an agent graduate from shelling out to importing without relearning any contract.

The zero-file precedence rules for the single-scenario case (08 §4.2: file → flags override → validate as if a file, indistinguishable downstream) are crisp and testable; --road-as-non-persisted-override is a well-carried idea.

schema as a closed, sectioned, versioned self-documentation surface with the mistakes teaching table and an output (envelope) section (08 §5.1) attacks the real cold-start problem, and pinning the six recipes as executable acceptance tests in 09 ('the recipes cannot rot') is the right enforcement mechanism for the design bar.

explain's structure — JSON with fixed keys, prose confined to message fields, remediation hints phrased against the closed vocabularies (08 §5.2) — is the correct dual-audience contract for agent+human consumption.
Id-addressed sweep paths ('never array-indexed — carried', 08 §3) with the explicit truncated flag protect saved sweeps from plan edits — a subtle, real durability win.
scene --check (08 §3) closing the prior lint-only-via-full-bake asymmetry, and check's exit-0/2 purity, give agents a cheap validation probe before spending a solve.

The typed NO_SOLUTION with constraint_unmet naming the constraint id, worst station, and achieved-vs-required values (04 §4.5, 08 §6(f)) makes solver refusal actionable — 'the agent's next move is legible from the error' is actually delivered here.

verdicts.title: stateAt promised as a CLI verb but absent from the verb table
verdicts.note: 05 §4 states verbatim: 'stateAt is exposed identically in the library and as a CLI verb (08-cli-and-agent-interface.md)'. 08 §3's table ('One binary, linelab <verb>') lists exactly run/solve/mistake/scene/render/compare/sweep/check/schema/explain/serve/export — no stateAt, and no other verb accepts an {s|t} query or emits an InstantState; stateAt's only 08 appearance is the §7.1 library import list. Checked all ten docs: 01 §2 (G2) and 07 reference only the library form; no doc supplies the CLI spelling, query flags, line selection, or output wrapping.
