A genuine cross-doc breach on a headline capability; blocker stands.

verdicts.title: Solved and compiled plans are not recorded in the envelope — the explain→edit→sweep loop is unactionable
verdicts.note: The nucleus is confirmed: 05 §7's LineResult carries only source/trajectory/verdict, a solve line's source 'records the solver inputs', no export format (05 §8.2) emits the resolved four-action plan (04 §4.2), so stateAt's derived.action ('the full resolved PlanAction for action_id') has no documented data source for solve/mistake lines and sweep's plan.<id>.<field> paths are unreachable for solver output — contradicting 05 §1's own rule 'If the engine knew it during the run, the result records it.' But 'cannot be executed for any solver-authored line' overstates scope: 08 §5.2's hint is explicitly dual ('move plan.b1.at_s earlier or reduce --entry') and D10's intent surface (--entry, --vis-margin, --constraint, turn-in) is the documented adjust-and-rerun lever for solver lines. Major-grade contract hole, not a blocker of the whole loop.

verdicts.title: run→solve delegation: trigger list incomplete, failure exit tier undefined, and the 'says so in the envelope' field does not exist in 05
verdicts.note: (b) survives: run's exit on a failed internal solve is genuinely undefined — exit 3 names 'a non-clean solve' phrased against the solve verb ('the authoring gate', 08 §3) while exit 0 is 'any physics outcome', and only recipe (f) pins NO_SOLUTION→3, for solve, never run. (a) is weakened: the operative rule is 'if the composed input needs solving' — the parenthesized triggers read as examples, and --brake auto/--constraint need solving by direct inference from 04 §4.1/§4.5, so no dead-input class is mandated. (c) is refuted: 05 §7 pins per-line source ('how this line came to be') as {kind:"solve", solveSpec} — that IS the envelope saying so; 08 §4.2's 'indistinguishable downstream' sentence concerns flag-vs-file composition, not solver delegation.

verdicts.title: --gate is undefined over multi-line envelopes containing intended-fail mistake lines
verdicts.note: Exit 3 is defined only as 'run --gate with a failed doctrine check' (08 §3.1) with no per-line or per-role quantification anywhere in the set; recipe (b)'s canonical figure contains a line that fails by construction ('red early_apex running wide'); 03 §6's expect_fail is a single-scenario test oracle (09 §4 uses it for mistake presets in the suite) with no stated wiring to compileMistake output or to --gate at the CLI; 05 §7 gives the envelope no expected-outcome field. Checked 09 too — nothing connects the gate to mistake roles. The gap is real and lands on the tool's primary artifact.

verdicts.title: Chained solve is 'contained, not clean', non-clean solve exits 3, and the closed outcome set has no 'contained' value
verdicts.note: All three quotes are exact and cannot jointly hold: 04 §5 bolds 'A linked line is **contained, not clean** ... maps to **green**'; 08 §3 pins 'Non-clean solve exits 3'; 05 §6.1's closed outcome set has no 'contained' value, and 06 §5.1 maps green ('good') to outcome=clean with no failed checks, so a green-but-not-clean line is unrepresentable. The only rescue (chain-aware checks all pass ⇒ outcome 'clean' per 02 §7's 'clean — all checks pass') works by falsifying 04's bolded 'not clean'. Recipe (d) does route the chain through run rather than solve. The seam is genuine as stated.

verdicts.title: The mistake spec has three spellings with no composed grammar, precedence, or base-line selection
verdicts.note: Three spellings verified (08 §3 'mistake <kind[:k=v,…]> --on <solved.json> [--corners c1,c2]'; 08 §6(d) '--mistake "early_apex@c1,c2"'; 04 §7 'mistake <kind> [key=val …] [scope=…]'). No doc states whether :k=v and @scope compose in one token, whether @all_corners is CLI-spellable (03 §7.2 maps only '<kind>@c1,c2' to the corner-id-list form; all_corners appears only in JSON/scene), or precedence when --corners and @… both appear. The base-line rule exists only at the scene layer (04 §7: 'compiled against the figure's first ride line'); the mistake verb's --on takes an envelope of 1..N lines (05 §7) with no selection rule. Confirmed against the stated first-try design bar.

verdicts.title: sweep can only address plan.<id>.<field> — none of the axes an author actually wants to sweep are reachable
verdicts.note: Nucleus confirmed: sweep's syntax admits only 'plan.<id>.<field>' (08 §3), so rider.start.speed_kmh and config.mu (03 §6), vis_margin (04 §6 solve-spec field), constraint values (04 §4.5, solver-layer only), and mistake params are unsweepable as written; '--metric list' has no defined vocabulary anywhere; the grid cap behind 'truncated' has no value; and sweep's syntax shows '<scenario>' without the [zero-file flags] the run/solve rows carry. Overstated half: 'none of the axes an author actually wants' — turn-in station (plan.t1.at_s) and brake decel are sweepable on explicit-plan scenarios and are canonical wants (turn-in placement is 01 §4.1's 'master decision'), so wanted axes do exist inside plan.*.

verdicts.title: compare semantics unspecified: input kinds, line pairing, and cross-road diffs
verdicts.note: All three headline gaps verified: compare's row (08 §3) specifies neither accepted input kinds (recipe (c) pipes solve --out files of unstated type), nor a pairing rule for multi-line envelopes, nor any refusal for inputs on different roads; 05 §7's 'One road per figure' constrains the overlay figure compare must emit, but no doc instructs compare to enforce it, and no code in the closed vocabulary (08 §7.2) fits a cross-input mismatch of individually-valid inputs. One quibble: 'at shared stations' does plausibly answer the different-length domain sub-question (intersection), but that is an 'also' item; the titled claims all stand.

verdicts.title: --line-id is listed but never defined, and every operation needing a per-line selector lacks one
verdicts.note: Verified by grep: '--line-id <id>' occurs exactly once in the doc set (08 §4.1 flag enumeration) with no semantics in 03/04/05/08. run's '--trace out.csv' and export's '--as trace-csv' syntaxes carry no line selector although 05 §8.2 pins Trace CSV as 'per line'; the mistake verb's --on has no base-line rule; the stateAt verb is absent entirely. And no doc states how CLI-composed lines acquire their line_id ('stable string', 05 §7) — 04 §7's unique-name rule is scene-text-only — so even a selector would lack predictable targets for repeatable --mistake lines.

verdicts.title: Authored plan flags composed with the solver reopen the accepted-but-ignored hole D8 exists to abolish
verdicts.note: 08 §4.1 lists --position/--throttle/--brake <decel> beside --turn-in <auto|s> with no composition caveat; §4.2 says flags compose into one validated input; 04 §4.2 pins solve output as 'the canonical four actions' with no merge rule for author-supplied actions. Checked 03 §6.1, 04 §2's ladder, and 09 §8: no section specifies either incorporation into the search or a typed rejection (e.g. an INEFFECTUAL analogous to vis_knob_without_vis_mode). 04 §4.5's constraint tokens ('hold-wide intent stated as a bound') show the intended solver-era substitute, but nothing closes the flag path — so hold-wide via --position plus the agent-default --turn-in auto is undefined, exactly the D8 class, on the field whose prior silent death motivated D8.

verdicts.title: Error-code assignment is undecidable for several specified rejections, and INEFFECTUAL's definition has drifted
verdicts.note: The code-assignment half is confirmed: the reserved width-suffix rejection (03 §3) and apex: ref rejection (03 §6.1) name no code, and no rule fixes the SCHEMA/BAD_RANGE boundary for bounded-fraction fields (08 §7.2's BAD_RANGE examples are only 'negative radius, mu ≤ 0'). The drift half is refutable: 05 §2.1 pins a single per-sample action_id — 'id of the plan action currently driving control' — so a position window overlapping an active turn_in commitment would be shadowed, i.e. provably do nothing, making (INEFFECTUAL, position_overlaps_turn_in) consistent with 08 §7.2's definition; the 'would fight an active steering commitment' reading presumes concurrent-action blending the Sample contract excludes.

verdicts.title: The schema output's own structure is unspecified — 'schema text (wrapped)'
verdicts.note: 'the schema text (wrapped)' (08 §3.2) is the output's entire format specification; §5.1 pins sections and content rules (teaching table, envelope section, solve section) but never whether the wrapper is navigable JSON or a prose blob — while every other contract in the set (Sample fields, verdict shape, CSV column order, error objects) is pinned exactly. 09's cold-start test runs 'from the printed schema output alone' with the format unstated. Checked all docs; nothing pins it. The one unpinned contract is the one the design bar rests on; minor is the right tier.

verdicts.title: The figure layer has no JSON door: scene text is a mandatory second grammar and FigureSpec is not loadable by any verb — the zero-file default is pushed at the wrong layer
verdicts.note: Verified across the verb table: no verb accepts Figure/FigureSpec JSON — scene takes only <file.scene>, serve takes 'scenario|scene|envelope', run takes a scenario — although 03 §8 defines the Figure object, 05 §8.1 defines FigureSpec as the canonical share payload, and the viewer loads it only from a URL fragment (07 §6.2). So D6's any-consumer-recomputes promise has no CLI entrance for that payload, and 08 §4.1's 'flags are sugar, not a second schema' holds only at the scenario layer: the figure layer is authorable solely as indentation-sensitive scene text (04 §7: 'Top-level keys at column 0; lines: and labels: entries indented') with a third spelling of fields (entry=/vis=/visHold= vs --entry/--visibility-governed/--vis-hold vs speed_kmh/vis:"cautious"/vis_hold_f).

verdicts.title: The dnf-spec-error outcome is unmapped to exit tiers and unreachable given validate-as-sole-rejection-point
verdicts.note: The exit-tier gap survives: 08 §3.1's exit-0 row enumerates only five outcomes, dnf-spec-error appears in no tier, and the multi-line partial-failure case (one bad 'plan <file.json>' scene line among good siblings, 04 §7) has no specified behavior — exit 2 vs partial envelope is undecidable. But 'unreachable' is refuted by 02 §7: '(dnf-spec-error covers invalid input surfaced at run time; validation should catch nearly all of these earlier per D8.)' — the design explicitly reserves the outcome for the run-time residue validation misses, so it is reachable by design; the critic did not read 02.

verdicts.title: Output-discipline edge cases: --out's two meanings, --render on run absent from the verb table, sweep's TSV, and no channel for proportion-gate failure
verdicts.note: (a), (b), (d) survive: --out is an envelope-JSON file path in 08 §6(b) but a figure directory in §4's prose; neither --out nor --render appears in run's verb-table syntax and stdout-when---out is unstated; sweep says 'TSV/JSON table' with no format selector against §3.2's one-JSON-document rule; no doc states check <file.scene> and scene --check share a code path. But (c) is refuted by 06 §6.2: '**fail** outside hard bounds → the export command exits non-zero (gate tier, 08-cli-and-agent-interface.md); a stretched figure cannot be called done' — proportion-gate failure has defined exit behavior (tier 3) and defined reporting (gate_verdict in the export manifest, 06 §7). The critic read only 08.

verdicts.title: explain's accepted inputs omit mistake kinds, which 03 requires explain to handle
verdicts.note: 03 §7.1 mandates 'explain(kind) must state each kind's pinned outcome and book figure', reinforced by 01 §4.3: 'Every input surface that lists mistake kinds (schema, explain) must state each kind's canonical outcome class and book-figure mapping.' Yet 08's verb accepts only '<envelope.json | checkId | errorCode>' and §5.2 elaborates only the envelope and check-id/error-code branches — a mistake kind is none of these, so the mandated call has no CLI spelling (schema mistakes covers kinds, but that is the schema surface, not explain). The positional path-vs-checkId disambiguation rule is likewise stated nowhere. Minor severity fits.

result.walkthrough: I read 00 and 01 in full, then all of 02–09 thoroughly, plus the book's Chapter 8 and 9 texts, and ran mechanical counts over the doc set. I then simulated four things as if the program existed exactly as specified. (1) Implementing the verdict: 01 §3 says "check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in 05"; 05 §6.2 says "The check content is doctrine and lives in 01... this document pins the record shape and the id list" — then lists only the two new visibility ids plus the phrase "the carried line-selection checks." Each doc points at the other; neither enumerates the ~12 checks that decide every colour. (2) Solving the canonical book figure: `book90` expands to `lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16` (arc 18.85 m, total road 46.85 m); `suggestTurnIn` sweeps "corner.s0 − 24 m to s0 + 8 m" — station −12 to +20, half off the road — and the solve pipeline's roll-on bracket "+35 … +90 m past turn-in" (04 §4.1) starts at station ≈43–47, i.e. at or beyond the road's end; the bisection on exit lane fraction cannot function on the design's own presets, and even on C30 (total 107 m) the +90 upper bracket is 13 m past the road end. (3) Sharing a URL across a re-bless: the FigureSpec (05 §8.1) is "the envelope minus every computed member" — no engine build version (only the format string "linelab/1"), no expected result_hash, and 09 §3.3's re-bless procedure covers committed fixtures only; nothing specifies what a consumer sees when the same URL recomputes to a different outcome. (4) Scrubbing a POV frame past a `wall`: eye height is 1.4 m (07 §5.2) while the wall's presentation height is 1.2 m in a list claimed to be "tall enough that every kind fully occludes the 1.4 m eye" (07 §5.3) — arithmetically false. Against the book, I checked the doctrine baseline: Ch. 9 itself teaches a "transition period where you are doing both actions simultaneously," shows an illustration of "a lot of trail braking... throttle applied before the brakes are completely released," and states the 50%-throttle-application-point rule — none of which the hard-coded brake-complete-then-steer solver or the (unenumerated) check suite demonstrably honors. Risk counts: 46 TUNING marks across the set (12 in 02-physics, 9 in 06-rendering), plus explicit hedges "to be validated in implementation, not assumed" (01 §5), "must be re-validated empirically as an implementation gate" (04 §4.3), and "believed impossible" (06 §2.6) — the run-wide slice and the solver brackets are what the doc set itself admits it is least sure of, and every mistake-outcome pin (03 §7.1) and book-figure recreation (G7) sits on top of them.

findings.title: The doctrine check suite is specified nowhere — circular ownership between 01 and 05
findings.claim: The product's judging core — the enumerated doctrine checks whose pass/fail decides every verdict, every colour, the mistake oracle's expect_fail targets, and `explain <checkId>` — does not exist in the design of record. 01 delegates it to 05, 05 delegates it back to 01, and neither enumerates the checks or their arithmetic. Colour law v2, the mistake oracle, G7's figure parity, and the cold-start `schema`/`explain` bar all consume a check list with `checks_version: 2` that an implementer can only reconstruct by excavating the superseded `extract/` set (sanctioned only as a silence fallback by 00 §5, which is unversioned and explicitly 'deliberately reversed' in several places, so an implementer cannot know which carried checks survived).
findings.evidence: 01 §3: "check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in `05-result-contract-and-inspection.md`"; 05 §6.2: "The check *content* is doctrine and lives in `01-scope-and-doctrine.md`; this document pins the record shape and the id list" — then pins only "the carried line-selection checks + stop_within_sight + hold_wide_for_sight". Check ids appear only incidentally: `late_apex`, `out_in_out`, `single_input` (01 §4.3 table), `late_brake` (08 §5.2 example), "taper check" (02 §8). 02 §1 claims the physics "can be reimplemented from the equations and constants here alone"; no equivalent claim is possible for the verdict.
findings.improvement: Add the enumerated check table to 01 (or a new 01a): id, doctrine source (book chapter/figure), arithmetic, thresholds with TUNING marks, per-special-case exemptions (e.g. `late_apex` reads `na` on increasing radius per 01 §5), and the chain-aware set 04 §5 references. 05 then genuinely pins the id list. Without this, Axis B is not implementable as designed.

findings.title: Book-as-doctrine hard-codes a contestable baseline the book itself complicates — and there is no rubric seam
findings.claim: The design elevates 'brake-complete-then-quick-steer' to structural truth: the solve pipeline can only generate lines whose braking completes `brake_gap` before turn-in, and trail braking is demoted to a 'separately-labelled advanced variant' that the solver can grade but never author. But Total Control itself teaches overlap: Ch. 9 prescribes a simultaneous brake/throttle transition period, its illustration celebrates heavy trail braking, and Ch. 11 teaches the technique — so the baseline is an interpretation of the book, not the book. Modern street pedagogy (YCRS/Ienatsch-style trail-braking-as-safety-skill) argues the opposite baseline precisely for the sight-limited entries linelab centers on, since a brake-complete rider has zero brake established when the blind hazard appears. The tool will paint a competent trail-braked line amber (contained: `late_brake` fails) forever, with no way to say 'graded under Parks-street rubric' vs anything else — `checks_version` is an integer version of one rubric, not a rubric identity.
findings.evidence: 01 §4.2: "Trail braking is a separately-labelled advanced variant, not the clean baseline — the baseline is brake-complete-then-quick-steer"; 04 §4.1: `brake_gap 4 m` "(braking completes before turn-in)" is baked into the only solved plan shape; 08 §5.2 example penalizes "brake action b1 ends 9 m past turn-in". Book ch9 (part0015) line 21: "The fix for this is to have a transition period where you are doing both actions simultaneously"; line 34: "a lot of trail braking... throttle is being applied before the brakes are completely released"; line 58: "the next step is to transition back and forth with the brakes... trail braking." 02 §5.4.1 keeps light trail braking merely "representable and gradeable". 03 §6: `checks_version` is the only doctrine-versioning field.
findings.improvement: Name the rubric in every verdict (e.g. `rubric: "parks-street/2"`), make the check suite a declared data pack so a second rubric is additive rather than a fork, and add a `style=trailbrake` solver variant graded under its own labelled variant checks. The book-wins-disputes rule then governs the Parks pack, not the tool.

findings.title: stop-within-sight uses a closed-form stopping model the design's own physics says is unrideable at lean
findings.claim: The safety-central check certifies stops via `ssd = v·t_react + v²/(2·a_ssd)` with `alert a_ssd = 7.0 m/s²`, evaluated per sample including mid-corner. But Tier 1R's own run-wide slice puts the street rider's point of no return at ≈5.4 m/s² at lean — braking at 7 m/s² while leaned forces a stand-up and runs the bike wide, likely out of lane, per the design's flagship physics addition. So a `vis=cautious` line can pass `stop_within_sight` at stations where the certified stop could not actually be executed in the design's own simulator without departing the corridor. This also flatly contradicts the design's stated conviction that feasibility is decided by shooting, 'never by a closed-form formula' — the one place a formula survives is the one place it is safety-load-bearing.
findings.evidence: 02 §1: "Feasibility is decided by *shooting* — re-integrating through the same pure stepper — never by a closed-form formula"; 03 §5.2: `ssd(v, model)` with `alert {a_ssd: 7.0}`; 02 §5.3: "a_noreturn ≈ 2.5 + 0.873/0.30 ≈ 5.4 m/s²... Braking harder than that while leaned *forces* the stand-up"; 02 §5.4.2: hard braking at lean "widens, never tightens". 05 §6.2: `stop_within_sight` — "at every station, v permits stopping within sight_m".
findings.improvement: Make `ssd` lean-aware at minimum (derate `a_ssd` by `aLongAvail` at the sample's lean and cap at `a_noreturn` while `|phi|` is meaningful), or define the check's mid-corner arm as a corrective-shot integration like the runoff/wide distinction already is. If the closed form is kept for cost, the check must carry a placard: mid-corner margins assume an upright bike.

findings.title: Share-by-recompute has unaddressed version skew: same URL, different physics, no mismatch contract
findings.claim: D6's recompute-everywhere honesty means a shared URL's meaning is a function of the consumer's engine version. After any re-bless — and the docs guarantee at least one (the Tier 1R landing), and every one of the 46 TUNING constants is a candidate — a URL shared as 'look, the chop line runs off at s=141' can silently recompute to a contained amber line while its authored labels, note, and captions still assert the old story. The FigureSpec carries no engine build version (only the format string 'linelab/1'), no expected outcome, and no expected result_hash (excluded by construction as a 'computed member'); no doc specifies what a consumer does on divergence. The re-bless discipline meticulously protects committed fixtures and says nothing about the artifact class the design is proudest of making shareable.
findings.evidence: 05 §8.1: "FigureSpec — the envelope minus every computed member" = `{spec, figure_id, road_spec, lines[{line_id, role, label, source}], meta}`; 05 §6.3: `engine: "linelab/1"` is a format id, no semver anywhere; 09 §3.3: re-bless enumerates goldens/presets/oracle table — URLs and exported scenes are absent; 07 §6.2: share strings are "recomputed on entry"; 09 §3.3 item 2 even boasts the decoupling: "No exported figure is baked into a committed teaching artifact."
findings.improvement: Add to FigureSpec: `engine_semver` plus optional per-line `expected: {outcome, result_hash}` stamped at export. Consumers compare after recompute and, on mismatch, render a first-class placard (the design already has the vocabulary): "recomputed under engine 1.3.0 — line 'chop' was runoff, now violation; authored labels may not match." This is squarely inside the placard policy of 01 §8 and costs ~40 bytes of URL.

findings.title: Two products in one, no phasing: the six figures need a spine; the doc set's own hedges mark the rest as risk
findings.claim: V1 scope is engine + solvers + mistake compiler + projection + top-down renderer + controls strip + CLI (12 verbs) + viewer + stepper + compare mode + POV, with all of G1–G9 as v1 requirements and no build order or milestone anywhere in the set. The concrete deliverable that anchors the project — the six Chapter-8 figures (G7) in book proportions (G8) — needs only core/road/solve/mistake/render-topdown/CLI-run-render. The docs implicitly concede where the risk lives: 46 TUNING marks (12 in the physics doc, 9 in rendering), 'to be validated in implementation, not assumed' on the double-apex acceptance criterion, 'must be re-validated empirically as an implementation gate' on the solver brackets, and 07's own admission that the POV is 'the largest subsystem with no prior equivalent.' D1 declares the interactive viewer *the product* and static SVG a mere export — inverting deliverable-vs-risk order: the highest-confidence, book-anchored deliverable is demoted, and the three least-precedented subsystems (POV, stepper, projection) are promoted to the critical path.
findings.evidence: 00 D1: "static SVG figures are an *export target*, not the product"; 01 §2: G1–G9 all stated as v1 testable requirements; 07 §1: "the largest subsystem with no prior equivalent"; 00 §3 doc map contains no phasing; TUNING counts by rg: 00:2, 02:12, 03:8, 04:6, 05:2, 06:9, 07:4, 09:3 = 46; 01 §5: "to be validated in implementation, not assumed"; 04 §4.3: "re-validated empirically as an implementation gate."
findings.improvement: Add a normative phasing section to 00: v0.1 = engine + solve + mistake + true-scale presets + topdown render + run/render/check/schema (delivers G1, G6, G7, G8-via-presets); v0.2 = stepper + stateAt viewer + serve; v0.3 = POV + compare; projection when realistic-road figures are actually needed. Cut first: POV (biggest unprecedented subsystem, zero role in the six figures), then compare mode, then the diagram projection (see next finding).

findings.title: The diagram projection is philosophically strained and, per the design's own presets, largely redundant for v1
findings.claim: A tool whose creed is 'a wrong-but-plausible picture a student could believe is strictly worse than an honest not modelled' ships, as its default figure mode, geometry with straights compressed ×5 and width exaggerated ×~3.5, disclosed by a footnote 'rendered small in the frame margin.' The distortion is topology-safe (P1–P6) but destroys quantitative visual lessons: braking distance — the thing Ch. 8 riders systematically underestimate — draws at one-fifth length; a drawn line's lateral motion is 3.5× its longitudinal truth, so 'smooth single arc' vs 'faceted' becomes a partially fabricated visual distinction that only the vision judge can police ('only eyes can confirm the compressed figure doesn't visually lie' — 09 §7 admits the residual risk). Meanwhile the design already built the honest alternative: the book-proportioned presets are 'simultaneously true-scale and book-compact,' must pass the proportion gate in true mode (09 §5.3), and cover the Chapter-8 archetypes — so the entire projection subsystem, its six invariants, gate, and disclosure machinery serve only the secondary 'realistic roads at prose speeds' path in v1.
findings.evidence: 01 §8: "A wrong-but-plausible picture a student could believe is strictly worse than an honest 'not modelled'"; 06 §2.1: default mode "diagram"; 06 §2.2: `C_STRAIGHT = 5`; 06 §2.7: footnote "rendered small"; 03 §3.1: presets are "simultaneously true-scale and book-compact"; 09 §5.3: "If a preset needs violent compression to pass the gate, the preset is wrong"; 09 §7: "only eyes can confirm the compressed figure doesn't visually lie."
findings.improvement: For v1, make true-scale presets the figure path and defer the projection (or ship it behind `mode=diagram` as non-default). If kept: upgrade disclosure from footnote to structure — dual scale bars (longitudinal per-segment, lateral), a visible 'not to scale' badge, and an inset true-scale thumbnail. That resolves the coherence tension: distortion is fine when it cannot be mistaken for measurement.

findings.title: D7 absolutism blocks the highest-value coaching input, and D10 shows the invariant already quietly renegotiated
findings.claim: Refusing all path input is defended as the honesty spine, but the actual honesty property is narrower and already independently guaranteed: 'never ship a trajectory the engine didn't produce.' D10's constraint grammar concedes that authors need spatial intent — `f_min`/`f_max` over arbitrary spans is corridor authoring; stack enough spans and 'where it may not go' converges on 'where it goes' — so the invariant has silently weakened from 'no path input' to 'no waypoints, corridors fine' without the design saying so. Meanwhile the genuinely valuable path-shaped input is banned wholesale: a rider with a GPS/lean-logger trace of their actual ride cannot ask linelab 'grade MY line' — the single most natural coaching request for a riding-line laboratory — because no surface accepts an observed trajectory even as evidence, and nothing in the docs mentions the use case.
findings.evidence: 00 D7: "no `apex` field anywhere... apex/exit/run-wide are measured outputs"; 00 D10: "Constraints are acceptance bounds, not waypoints: D7 is untouched"; 04 §4.5: closed bound set, `v_kmh>=` rejected `SCHEMA`; 01 G1: "no input surface accepts path points, radii-of-line, or an apex"; 01 §7: even alternatives are authored only as plans or perturbations. No document mentions observed/ridden traces.
findings.improvement: Restate the invariant honestly as its output form ('every rendered line is engine-integrated') and add a plan-fit front door: `fit(trace) → Result<{plan, residual}>` that searches plan actions reproducing an observed trace within tolerance, then grades the fitted plan normally. Rendered lines remain engine-produced; the fit residual is itself teaching material ('your ride is best explained by a turn-in 6 m early').

findings.title: Read-mostly viewer is defended by a rationale D1 already invalidated
findings.claim: The viewer offers zero authoring — not even parameter nudging — sending the human user (the interview-derived rider, not just agents) back to CLI flags and scene text to move a turn-in point 2 m. The stated rationale is that 'a second authoring surface inevitably drifts from the solver's validation and defaults' — but that argument belonged to the prior no-build architecture; under D1 the viewer imports the identical `plan/` and `solve/` ESM modules ('there is no bundled viewer build of the physics that could drift'), so drift is structurally impossible for parameter-level controls. The design even paid for the capability it refuses to use: the ≤100 ms full-recompute budget exists precisely so recomputation is interactive. The result is a cause-and-effect teaching tool whose one interactive surface cannot vary a cause.
findings.evidence: 07 §6.3: "read-mostly... no scenario editing... a second authoring surface inevitably drifts from the solver's validation and defaults" vs 07 §2.1: "The viewer imports the same modules the CLI imports; there is no bundled 'viewer build' of the physics that could drift" and "a full multi-line recompute is targeted at ≤ 100 ms"; 09 `C-RECOMPUTE-BUDGET` institutionalizes the budget. 00 §2: decisions made after "a user interview" — the user is human.
findings.improvement: Keep the hard line (no hand-drawn geometry, lean never editable) but add solver-input what-if controls in v1: entry-speed slider, turn-in offset nudge, mistake toggle, vis-knob sliders — each calling the same `solve`/`validate` the CLI calls, displaying the same typed errors. This is view-level state over the one authoring path, not a second one.

findings.title: Solver constants are absolute metres tuned for the dead R60 world and provably cannot work on the design's own presets
findings.claim: The solve pipeline's carried defaults are stated in fixed metres: turn-in sweep `s0 − 24 m … s0 + 8 m`, roll-on bracket `+35 … +90 m past turn-in`, `brake_gap 4 m`, `crack_gap 8 m`. The new canonical roads are an order of magnitude shorter: book90's arc is 18.85 m on a 46.85 m road. There, the sweep begins at station −12 (before the road exists) and the roll-on bracket's *lower* bound lands at station ≈43–47 — at or past the road end — so the exit-fraction bisection has no valid domain and the solver rails or fails on the exact preset that recreates figs 8.1–8.3; even C30 (107 m) has the +90 upper bound 13 m off the end of the road. Separately, any legal roll-on ≥35 m past turn-in on these short corners violates Ch. 9's own doctrine ('if you're past the 50 percent point of a turn before rolling on the throttle, your entry speed was too fast'; 'get on the throttle as soon as the bike is leaned over') — a rule no listed check covers.
findings.evidence: 04 §3: "from `corner.s0 − 24 m` to `corner.s0 + 8 m`"; 04 §4.1: "roll-on bracket `+35 … +90 m` past turn-in" (marked carried/TUNING); 03 §3.1: `book90` = `lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16` (computed: arc 18.85 m, total 46.85 m); 02 §8: C30 totals ≈107 m. Book ch9 (part0015) line 48: the 50 percent rule. 04 §4.3 flags bracket re-validation only "under Tier 1R", not under the new road scale.
findings.improvement: Respecify every solver station constant corner-relative — fractions of arc length or swept angle (e.g. roll-on bracket 40–95 % of swept angle past turn-in), clamped to road extent with a typed error when the clamp empties the bracket. Add a `throttle_application_pct` doctrine check implementing Ch. 9's 50 % rule.

findings.title: Chained V2 hold-wide contradicts the wire schema's position/turn_in overlap rejection on zero-gap esses
findings.claim: The visibility mode's V2 generates `position` actions to hold wide before each blind corner, and its chained composition generates the hold 'in the inter-corner span.' But bookEsses is specified with zero inter-corner straights, and every rung 'compiles down to the same wire scenario,' where a `position` action whose window overlaps an active `turn_in` is rejected `INEFFECTUAL` at validation. On a zero-gap chain there is no legal window: the solver's own generated plan is un-wireable, and the fallback prose ('holds as wide as the budget reaches') names no plan action that realizes it.
findings.evidence: 03 §6.1: "A `position` action whose transition window overlaps an active `turn_in` commitment is **rejected at validation** (`INEFFECTUAL`, `position_overlaps_turn_in`)"; 04 §6: the hold is "generated in the inter-corner span"; 03 §3.1: bookEsses teaches "linked turns, zero inter-corner straights"; 04 §2: "Every rung compiles down to the same wire scenario."
findings.improvement: Specify V2's hold as solver-internal shaping of the turn-in target/timing (no wire `position` action) when the span is shorter than a threshold, or define a solver-generated-plan exemption with explicit window-splitting semantics. State which in 04 §6; today an implementer must invent it.

findings.title: Wall presentation height (1.2 m) is below the eye (1.4 m) while claimed to fully occlude — a wrong-but-plausible POV by spec
findings.claim: The POV extrudes occluders to per-kind presentation heights explicitly claimed 'tall enough that every kind fully occludes the 1.4 m eye,' but the listed wall height is 1.2 m — a rider's 1.4 m eye sees over a 1.2 m wall in the real world, yet the binary plan-view sight model treats it as opaque and the POV will draw road vanishing behind a wall the viewer can plainly judge see-over-able. This is precisely the 'plausible and wrong picture' class the placard policy exists to prevent, and it exposes that binary opacity is a shaky fit for the `wall` and `vehicle` kinds generally (the docs themselves refuse 'armco you can see over' as unrepresentable — then ship its twin as a preset vocabulary item).
findings.evidence: 07 §5.2: `eye_height_m = 1.4`; 07 §5.3 item 4: "`hedge 1.8 m`, `wall 1.2 m`, `bank 1.5 m`, `vehicle 1.5 m` — tall enough that every kind fully occludes the 1.4 m eye" (1.2 < 1.4); 03 §4: "Partial-height occluders (armco you can see over...) are not representable; a spec that asks for a `height` field is rejected."
findings.improvement: Raise wall (and margin-thin vehicle) presentation heights above eye height (e.g. wall 1.8 m, described as a screen wall), and add one sentence to 03 §4 stating that `wall` models a full-height visual barrier, not armco — or drop `wall` from v1's vocabulary rather than render a physically false occlusion.

findings.title: Outcome definitions and colour mapping disagree on whether 'clean with failed checks' can exist
findings.claim: 02 defines `clean` as 'all checks pass' and `violation` as 'stayed contained but failed doctrine', making the two mutually exhaustive over contained lines; yet 06's quality mapping has a branch for 'outcome = clean with failed checks' → contained/amber. Either the branch is dead code in the spec, or `clean` is actually a physics-only classification and 02's definition is wrong — an implementer must guess whether outcome is computed before or after the doctrine suite, and the answer changes the colour of edge-case lines.
findings.evidence: 02 §7: "`violation` — stayed contained but failed doctrine... `clean` — all checks pass"; 06 §5.1: `"contained" if outcome = violation, or outcome = clean with failed checks`.
findings.improvement: Redefine the outcome ladder as physics-only (contained/wide/runoff/crash decided by the engine), let the doctrine layer own pass/fail, and derive quality from the pair — or delete the impossible branch from 06 §5.1 and state that outcome already folds doctrine in. One sentence either way; pick one.

findings.title: A deterministic single-run tool about safety margins has no representation of variability, and no channel for the book's psychology of error
findings.claim: Every book mistake is a misjudgment with a psychological cause (anxiety-driven early turn-in, target fixation, panic freeze), and the reserve doctrine exists because reality varies — yet linelab is a single deterministic run over exact mu, exact reaction time, and a binary sight world. The chop compile's `freeze_s` is the sole rider-psychology fragment, and nothing in the verdict, figure, or explain output can carry 'why riders do this'. Sensitivity to variation — the actual meaning of a reserve — exists only as a manual `sweep` an author must think to run; there is no envelope/band rendering, no 'this line survives mu 0.7, that one does not' figure, despite the machinery (sweep, hazards, deterministic engine) being sufficient to build one. This is a scope-cut challenge: determinism is right for the engine, but silence about variability is wrong for the product.
findings.evidence: Book ch8 (part0014) line 17: "Many riders grow anxious... initiating it prematurely"; line 27: "fixates on the inside of the turn"; 02 §6: "Determinism: `core/` is pure — no wall-clock, no randomness"; 03 §7.1: `freeze_s = 1.0 s` is the only rider-psychology parameter; 08 §3: `sweep` emits a metrics table only; 05 §6: diagnosis vocabulary is purely mechanical (`overspeed_entry`... `stand_up`), no belief/cause channel; no doc mentions uncertainty, robustness bands, or sensitivity figures.
findings.improvement: Two cheap additions: (1) a `because` teaching field on mistake kinds (book-cited cause text) surfaced by `explain` and figure legends; (2) a `robustness` verb or figure mode built on sweep — run the line across ±entry-speed and mu bands, render the outcome-class band as a shaded envelope. Both reuse existing machinery; neither touches core determinism.

findings.title: G6/G7 coverage gap: no double-apex road preset or worked DSL example for fig 8.5
findings.claim: G6 promises 'every archetype in §5 has a worked DSL example in 03' and G7 promises shipped scenes for figs 8.1–8.6, but the preset table covers 8.1–8.3 (book90), 8.4 (bookDecreasing), 8.6 (bookEsses), hairpin, and blind — no road whose shape 'rewards' a double apex, and no worked DSL line for one anywhere in 03. The double-apex corner is also the design's self-declared riskiest solver case ('to be validated in implementation, not assumed'), making it exactly the archetype that most needs a pinned canonical road.
findings.evidence: 01 §2 G6: "every archetype in §5 has a worked DSL example in `03-...md`"; 01 §5 lists "Double apex" as an archetype and hedges its solver criterion "to be validated in implementation, not assumed"; 03 §3.1 preset table: `book90`, `bookDecreasing`, `bookEsses`, `bookHairpin`, `bookBlind` — no double-apex entry, and no other double-apex DSL example appears in 03.
findings.improvement: Add a `bookDoubleApex` preset (e.g. two arcs joined by a short straight or a taper-out/taper-in dumbbell: `lane 3.5 | S 10 | R 14 ^70 | S 6 | R 14 ^70 | S 12`), pin it as the `solveDoubleApex` golden road, and give it the fig 8.5 mapping row the other presets have.

wins: D8 (schema-valid implies effectual) with the INEFFECTUAL error code and the schema-field-times-consumer effectuality tests (09 §8) is genuinely excellent API design — it structurally abolishes the accepted-but-inert input class that produced the prior design's dead `position` actions.

The invariant-first physics specification style (02 §5.4): every TUNING constant is explicitly subordinate to a named testable behaviour, so the run-wide slice can be re-tuned without renegotiating what it must do — the right way to spec uncertain physics.

Commanded-vs-delivered recorded per sample (05 §2.1) fixes the prior 'derivable but not inspectable' defect precisely, and the HUD's clip badge turns the friction ellipse into a teaching instrument rather than an internal clamp.

The rider-eye sight cast (D4) is both physically and pedagogically correct: it is the minimal model change that makes 'hold wide to open the sight line' measurable, and the docs correctly identify why the centreline eye made the doctrine invisible.

The premature/early_apex naming trap is documented at the API surface (03 §7.1, 08 §5.1) rather than in prose an agent won't read — a rare example of designing for the first-try bar rather than asserting it.

Share-inputs-recompute (D6) elegantly generalizes the honesty property from one line to N while making failed lines first-class — the honesty invariant is preserved by construction, not by policy (the missing piece is only version skew, filed separately).

The projection invariants P1–P6 as fuzzed property tests plus the proportion gate make a formerly invisible defect class (stretched figures) mechanically detectable, with an audit mode so the renderer cannot self-certify.
Exit-code tiers treating a crash as a valid, interesting run (exit 0) and reserving 2/3/1 for input/doctrine/IO (08 §3.1) is exactly right for an agent-driven simulation tool.

The decision log format itself — ten numbered decisions with explicit supersessions, root-cause citations, and 'carried/changed/new' sections closing every document — makes the design auditable in a way few design sets are.

verdicts.title: The doctrine check suite is specified nowhere — circular ownership between 01 and 05
verdicts.note: The circularity is textually real (01 §3 sends ids+arithmetic to 05; 05 §6.2 sends content back to 01 and enumerates only the two new visibility checks), and no doc in design/ lists the carried ids or arithmetic. But 'blocker' rests on unrecoverability — 'an implementer cannot know which carried checks survived' — and that is defeated: 05 §6.2 explicitly incorporates 'the carried line-selection checks', states 'the check *ids* are stable', and names exactly which arithmetic (trail-brake taper, single-input smoothness, chop-keyed) is re-derived under Tier 1R; extract/05-doctrine-and-line-method.md §5.2 ('The checks and their exact pass/fail arithmetic') enumerates all 12 checks with exact constants in the committed repo, and 00 §5 sanctions extract/ as the default where the set is silent. Surviving nucleus: the incorporation is by reference only, and the Tier 1R re-derived arithmetic for the three touched checks is specified nowhere. A real documentation gap, not a blocker.

verdicts.title: Book-as-doctrine hard-codes a contestable baseline the book itself complicates — and there is no rubric seam
verdicts.note: Verified: the solve pipeline can only author brake-complete plans (04 §4.1/§4.2 canonical four actions with brake_gap; trail braking is authorable only via explicit plan, never solver-generated), the book quotes are accurate (ch9 'transition period where you are doing both actions simultaneously', fig 9.1 'a lot of trail braking', ch11 pointer), and no rubric-identity field exists (checks_version is an integer; config.mode='street' is an unspecified stub). But the central consequence — 'will paint a competent trail-braked line amber (late_brake fails) forever' — is refuted: late_brake is a diagnosis cause (05 §6.1), not a check; the carried check that grades trail braking, trail_brake_taper (extract 05 §5.2 #6), passes a proper monotone taper and at worst WARNs, and warn ≠ fail in 06 §5.1's colour mapping, so a competent trail-braked line can grade clean/green — 02 §5.4.1 explicitly keeps it 'representable and gradeable'. The baseline also has direct book support the claim omits: ch8 'Getting off the gas or braking while at a high lean angle will cause the bike to straighten up and run wide.'

verdicts.title: stop-within-sight uses a closed-form stopping model the design's own physics says is unrideable at lean
verdicts.note: All citations verify: alert a_ssd = 7.0 m/s² (03 §5.2), street a_noreturn ≈ 5.4 m/s² (02 §5.3), stop_within_sight 'at every station' (05 §6.2), and hard braking at lean 'widens, never tightens' (02 §5.4.2). No doc anywhere in the set (nor the carried sight_vs_stopping check) makes ssd lean- or grip-aware, so a mid-corner sample can pass the safety check via a decel the design's own run-wide slice says forces a stand-up and a wide exit. One rhetorical stretch: 02 §1's 'never by a closed-form formula' is scoped to solver line-feasibility, so 'flatly contradicts' overreads that sentence — but the 7.0-vs-5.4 inconsistency stands independently.

verdicts.title: Share-by-recompute has unaddressed version skew: same URL, different physics, no mismatch contract
verdicts.note: Verified across the set: FigureSpec = envelope minus every computed member (05 §8.1) carrying only the format id 'linelab/1'; rg finds no engine/build version, no semver, and no divergence/mismatch handling anywhere; 07 §6.2 recomputes on entry with no expected-outcome check; 09 §3.3's re-bless enumeration covers goldens/presets/oracle and explicitly decouples figures ('No exported figure is baked into a committed teaching artifact'). Authored labels/notes/captions in meta can silently contradict the recomputed outcome after any TUNING change. The claim itself already concedes the partial mitigation (colour/verdict always recompute truthfully), so the finding stands as stated.

verdicts.title: Two products in one, no phasing: the six figures need a spine; the doc set's own hedges mark the rest as risk
verdicts.note: Every factual leg checks out: no build order, milestone, or phasing appears anywhere in the ten docs; 01 §2 states G1–G9 uniformly as v1 testable requirements; the verb table has exactly 12 verbs; rg reproduces the TUNING count exactly (00:2, 02:12, 03:8, 04:6, 05:2, 06:9, 07:4, 09:3 = 46); the hedge quotes ('to be validated in implementation, not assumed' 01 §5; 're-validated empirically as an implementation gate' 04 §4.3; 'largest subsystem with no prior equivalent' 07 §1) and D1's 'export target, not the product' are verbatim. The risk-inversion framing is interpretation, but it rests on accurate evidence and a genuine absence.

verdicts.title: The diagram projection is philosophically strained and, per the design's own presets, largely redundant for v1
verdicts.note: All quotes verify, and the honesty tension is real (09 §7 concedes 'only eyes can confirm the compressed figure doesn't visually lie'). But 'largely redundant for v1' is refuted: prose-speed realistic-road figures are an explicit first-class v1 path that the presets do not cover — 03 §3.1: 'Figures teaching the book's 45–80 km/h prose speeds use realistic roads plus the diagram projection'; the canonical golden corner C30 (70 km/h, width:radius 0.23) and agent recipes (a)–(d),(f) all use realistic roads whose diagram exports must pass the gate (08 recipe b). Disclosure is also more than 'a footnote': the export manifest records mode/factors/window (06 §2.7, §7), the controls strip is never projected (06 §4), and mode=true is always reachable. And the smooth-vs-faceted 'fabrication' overstates: uniform lateral scaling plus a monotone station remap preserves hump count, crossings, and side relations (P1–P6) — faceting is amplified, not fabricated. Nucleus survives (default-distorted view vs the honesty creed); redundancy and scope are wrong.

verdicts.title: D7 absolutism blocks the highest-value coaching input, and D10 shows the invariant already quietly renegotiated
verdicts.note: The 'quietly/without the design saying so' half is refuted verbatim: 00 D10 states and defends exactly the position the claim says is silent — 'Constraints are acceptance bounds, not waypoints: D7 is untouched — the engine still decides where the line goes; constraints only say where it may not' — and 04 §4.5 repeats it; an unachievable corridor is a typed NO_SOLUTION, never a followed path, so the corridor-converges-to-waypoints reduction never yields path input. The other half survives: rg confirms no doc mentions GPS/telemetry/observed/ridden traces, and no input surface accepts an observed trajectory even as evidence — the 'grade MY line' use case is genuinely absent. Major severity is overstated once the renegotiation half falls.

verdicts.title: Read-mostly viewer is defended by a rationale D1 already invalidated
verdicts.note: The nucleus is real: 07 §2.1 ('there is no bundled viewer build of the physics that could drift', ≤100 ms recompute budget) does undercut the drift half of 07 §6.3's rationale, and 07 §6.3's own v2 sentence concedes parameter editing over the same plan/ validation is compatible. But the claim misstates the defense: the quoted rationale is co-stated with a second, still-valid leg the claim omits — 'keeping one authoring path keeps D8 enforceable in one place' — and the same section explicitly provides the future seam ('A future v2 editor may add road/plan parameter editing over the same plan/ validation'), i.e. the capability was deliberately deferred with a designed path, not refused on an incoherent ground. Deliberate documented scope cut with a stale sub-rationale, not a defect of the stated magnitude.

verdicts.title: Solver constants are absolute metres tuned for the dead R60 world and provably cannot work on the design's own presets
verdicts.note: Arithmetic verified: book90 (lane 3.5 | S 12 | R 12 ^90 | S 16) has arc 18.85 m, total 46.85 m; the 04 §3 sweep starts at station −12; the 04 §4.1 roll-on bracket lower bound (+35 past a turn-in near s≈8–12) lands at ≈43–47, at/past road end, emptying the exit bisection domain on the exact preset behind figs 8.1–8.3 and recipe (e); C30's +90 upper bound is ~13 m off its 107 m road. 04 §4.3 flags bracket re-validation only 'under Tier 1R', never under the new road scale. One aside is wrong — the carried throttle_rule (extract 05 §5.2 #5: roll-on onset ≤ apex + 12 m) does cover late throttle — but that error strengthens the core claim: a +35 m roll-on on these corners would fail the design's own self-verification.

verdicts.title: Chained V2 hold-wide contradicts the wire schema's position/turn_in overlap rejection on zero-gap esses
verdicts.note: The quotes are accurate and the mechanism is genuinely underspecified, but the flat contradiction ('the solver's own generated plan is un-wireable') is defeated by the clause 04 §6 wrote for exactly this case: 'when the gap is too short to reach vis_hold_f, the line holds as wide as the budget reaches, and the release condition is evaluated from the actual position, never the unreached target' — at zero gap the reachable hold is the emergent exit position itself, realizable through the previous corner's exit shaping with no position action generated, so nothing triggers the INEFFECTUAL rejection. Surviving nucleus: the doc names no plan action realizing the short-gap hold, so the compile-to-wire mechanics on bookEsses are underspecified rather than contradictory.

verdicts.title: Wall presentation height (1.2 m) is below the eye (1.4 m) while claimed to fully occlude — a wrong-but-plausible POV by spec
verdicts.note: The contradiction sits inside a single sentence: 07 §5.3 item 4 lists 'wall 1.2 m' among heights 'tall enough that every kind fully occludes the 1.4 m eye' (07 §5.2), and 1.2 < 1.4 — geometrically a 1.4 m eye sees ground beyond ~7× the wall's distance over a 1.2 m wall, so the plan-view binary opacity certifies blindness the drawn POV scene visibly belies. 03 §4's refusal is also quoted correctly: 'armco you can see over' is declared unrepresentable while the preset vocabulary ships its twin. No other doc corrects the height. Minor severity is apt.

verdicts.title: Outcome definitions and colour mapping disagree on whether 'clean with failed checks' can exist
verdicts.note: Both quotes are verbatim and mutually inconsistent: 02 §7 makes clean ('all checks pass') and violation ('stayed contained but failed doctrine') exhaustive over contained lines, while 06 §5.1 branches on 'outcome = clean with failed checks'. The stated dichotomy (dead branch, or clean is physics-only and 02 is wrong) is exactly right and no other doc resolves the computation order. One consequence detail is off: colour is actually invariant across both readings (contained+failed maps to amber either way), so the real divergence lands on the outcome label, the mistake-oracle pins (premature is pinned to 'violation', which requires 02's reading), and result hashes — an equally real consequence via a different channel.

verdicts.title: A deterministic single-run tool about safety margins has no representation of variability, and no channel for the book's psychology of error
verdicts.note: All citations verify: ch8's psychological causes ('Many riders grow anxious… initiating it prematurely'; 'fixates on the inside of the turn'), 02 §6 determinism, freeze_s = 1.0 s as the only rider-psychology parameter (profile skill/t_react model competence, not error psychology), a purely mechanical diagnosis vocabulary (05 §6.1), sweep as a metrics table only (08 §3), and rg confirms zero mentions of uncertainty, robustness bands, or sensitivity figures anywhere in the ten docs. The claim is fairly framed as a scope-cut challenge (it concedes engine determinism is right), and the absence it names is real; minor severity is appropriate.

verdicts.title: G6/G7 coverage gap: no double-apex road preset or worked DSL example for fig 8.5
verdicts.note: Verified: 03 §3.1's preset table is exactly book90, bookDecreasing, bookEsses, bookHairpin, bookBlind — no double-apex-rewarding road — and rg finds no double-apex DSL example anywhere in 03 (the sole 'double' mention is an expect_fail aside). G6's test ('every archetype in §5 has a worked DSL example in 03') therefore fails for the double-apex archetype, fig 8.5 (the book's Double Apex Turn) has no covering preset for G7, and 01 §5's 'to be validated in implementation, not assumed' hedge is quoted accurately — the riskiest solver case is the one without a pinned canonical road. (The gap is in fact slightly understated: the increasing-radius archetype also lacks a worked example.)

result.walkthrough: I role-played the first implementation team standing up CI exactly as 09 specifies, tests-before-code. (1) Goldens first: 09 §3.2 says 02 defines the canonical scenarios "and their worked numbers" — but 02 §8 contains no numbers, only a list of quantities to pin "once the engine exists"; the first bless is therefore the engine certifying itself, with hand-computation explicitly forbidden and independent cross-checks merely "welcome". (2) Mistake oracle: 09 §4 forward-runs "every registered preset" against "the pinned table", but no doc says which base road/scenario each of the six kinds is registered against (only chop gets C30), and the wide-vs-runoff pins hinge on a corrective-shot sub-solver specified in one sentence of 02 §7. (3) Property tests: fuzzing P-SIGHT-EYE with 03 §4's own vocabulary (occluders may sit `outside`, vehicles in the oncoming lane) falsifies "moving the eye toward the outside never shortens sight_m"; the same geometry breaks 04 §6's monotone-fixpoint argument on alternating esses, where corner n+1's outside is corner n's inside. (4) A-CHAIN-VIS demands the line "holds vis_hold_f ahead of each blind corner" on a blind-esses fixture, but bookEsses has zero inter-corner straights and 04 §6's own carve-out says the hold is budget-limited there — the acceptance test contradicts the spec on its own fixture. (5) C-RECOMPUTE-BUDGET: counting engine runs from 04 — 17 coarse-sweep candidates, then up to 4 full solves at 1 probe + 16 + 16 + 1 self-verify = 34 runs each — gives 51–153 runs per auto-solved line, ~150+ for a 3-corner chain, ×4 for the vis fixpoint ≈ 600 runs, while 07 §2.1's 100 ms budget was derived counting "3–4 × 10³ RK4 steps per line", i.e. one run per line; and 04 §3's "cheap" coarse run at ds_m = 1.0 is not cheap, because 02 §6 fixes integration at dt = 0.005 s and ds_m only coarsens resampling. (6) Proportion gate: 06 §2.3's auto width_exag solves for ≥ 0.55 — inside the gate's own 0.45–0.95 band — so width_ratio passes by construction except at the ×12 clamp (R ≳ 150 m) or degraded esses, and 09 §5.3's presets were designed in-band; the gate binds little beyond window/compression defaults, and the "measured from the book" bands have no committed measurement artifact or procedure. (7) The vision judge is the gate for static exports and re-fires on every re-bless, yet no doc specifies judge model, prompt, output contract, verdict storage, or flake policy for a nondeterministic CI leg. (8) First re-tune of A_SU_ONSET during the invariant-driven constant search that 02 §5.4 and 04 §4.3 explicitly anticipate triggers the full §3.3 migration ceremony — regenerate all goldens, enumerate movements, re-pin the oracle, re-judge figures — with no pre-bless/dev-phase carve-out. (9) Browser leg: C-ONE-CORE is "the same ESM module imported twice, so the test is cheap" — which proves nothing about browsers; the real cross-runtime story (Math.tan/atan/tanh divergence across JS engines, discrete solver selections jumping in 0.5 m/2 m quanta that ±0.01 m tolerances cannot absorb, no deadbands beyond crash classification) is unspecified. (10) The D8 conformance test 03 §6.1 promises ("schema-field × consumer enumeration... specified in 09") does not exist in 09 §8, which restates the aspiration with an undecidable quantifier and counterexample fields (meta, labels).

findings.title: Golden-numerics bootstrap: the first bless certifies nothing, and 09's cross-reference to 02's 'worked numbers' is false
findings.claim: For a fresh implementation with no prior engine, the golden regime cannot distinguish a correct first engine from a subtly wrong one. 09 forbids hand-computed goldens and makes independent analytic cross-checks optional, so the first bless is the engine grading its own homework: the suite passes by construction and thereafter only detects drift, not correctness. Worse, 09 claims 02 contains the worked numbers, but 02 §8 explicitly defers all values to the not-yet-existing engine — the only a-priori anchors are coarse doctrinal bounds (apex_pct > 50, phi_max ≤ 40.36°, outcome clean).
findings.evidence: 09 §3.2: "Golden values are produced by the engine and *blessed*, never hand-computed into the fixtures" and "Independent cross-checks... are welcome as *additional* tests but never replace the blessed fixture"; 09 §3.2 opening: "`02-physics-model.md` defines the canonical scenarios (the canonical corner and its companions) and their worked numbers" — versus 02 §8: "Once the engine exists, the golden run pins the following quantities" (no numeric values appear anywhere in 02 §8).
findings.improvement: Add a mandatory analytic-acceptance layer that must be green before the first bless is accepted: closed-form checkables derivable by hand from 02's equations (steady-state radius v²/(g·tan φ) on a constant-lean circle, straight-line braking distance v²/2a, the ssd formula, roll-rate ramp timing, upright RK4 against the exact solution). Then commit the first blessed numbers back into 02 §8 so the doc's claim becomes true and future reimplementations have a real oracle.

findings.title: C-RECOMPUTE-BUDGET: the 100 ms solve-included budget is unsubstantiated by ~two orders of magnitude in engine-run count
findings.claim: 09 §6 requires solve-included recompute of the largest committed figure within 100 ms (×3 CI margin), but the supporting arithmetic in 07 counts integration steps per line — one engine run per line. An honest count from 04: suggestTurnIn = 17 coarse runs (s0−24 to s0+8 in 2 m steps); each full solve = 1 feasibility probe + 16 decel bisections + 16 roll-on bisections + 1 self-verify = 34 runs, up to 4 candidates full-solved → 51–153 runs per auto-solved line; chainedSolve multiplies per corner plus an ascending decel scan of unspecified granularity; vis=cautious multiplies the whole chain solve by up to vis_max_iterations = 4 → order 600 runs for the blind-esses figure, each run also paying the per-sample O(targets × occluders) sightFrom scan. The claimed mitigation — 'cheap' coarse runs at ds_m = 1.0 — is illusory: 02 §6 fixes integration at dt = 0.005 s for every run; ds_m governs only the resample grid, so a coarse run costs the same integration as a full run.
findings.evidence: 09 §6 C-RECOMPUTE-BUDGET: "recomputing a loaded figure (all lines, solve included) completes within the ≤ 100 ms budget... measured on the largest committed preset figure (the linked-chain fixture)"; 07 §2.1: "roughly 3–4 × 10³ fixed RK4 steps per line; a full multi-line recompute is targeted at ≤ 100 ms"; 04 §3.1: "one cheap engine run per candidate turn-in station... in 2 m steps at coarse resolution (ds_m = 1.0)"; 04 §4.1: "16 bisection iterations per control"; 04 §4.2: probe + two bisections + "re-run the engine on the final plan"; 04 §6: "bounded by vis_max_iterations = 4"; 02 §6: "Classical fixed-step RK4, dt_s = 0.005 s... physics integrates in *time*; analysis wants uniform *arc length*".
findings.improvement: Do the run-count arithmetic in the design and reconcile: either (a) specify a genuinely coarse integrator tier (larger dt) for sweep/scan stages, with its determinism and coarse/fine-disagreement semantics spelled out; (b) cache solved plans in the FigureSpec (solve once at author time, recompute only the integration on load — requires deciding whether a shipped *plan* violates D6's recompute doctrine, which currently it does not: plans are inputs); or (c) raise the budget and re-scope which fixture the test measures. As written, the test will likely be red on day one for any vis-chained figure.

findings.title: The vis-fixpoint monotone-convergence claim and P-SIGHT-EYE are false under the design's own occluder vocabulary
findings.claim: 04 justifies the 4-iteration fixpoint bound with 'slowing and widening can only open the sight margin, never close it', and 09 pins P-SIGHT-EYE as a fuzzed property. Both hold only for a single corner with an inside occluder — an assumption no doc states. 03 permits occluders on `outside`/`left`/`right` and vehicles 'parked or oncoming-lane': moving the eye outward toward an outside occluder can shorten sight, directly falsifying P-SIGHT-EYE under fuzzing. In an alternating chain (bookEsses is L-R-L), corner n+1's outside is corner n's inside, so V2's widening for the next corner moves the eye toward the previous corner's inside occluder while its blind zone still governs — chain-wide iteration can oscillate, and the design's canonical esses scenario is precisely the case most likely to hit the non-convergence NO_SOLUTION that the docs treat as pathological. P-VIS-MARGIN-MONOTONE inherits the same unstated assumption, plus an unhandled edge where a high vis_margin governs speed below v_floor and the run terminates 'stopped'.
findings.evidence: 04 §6: "convergence is monotone because slowing and widening can only open the sight margin, never close it (bounded by vis_max_iterations = 4)"; 09 §3.4 P-SIGHT-EYE: "moving the eye laterally toward the outside of a blind corner never *shortens* sight_m", and §3.4 preamble: "Run against fuzzed schema-valid scenarios"; 03 §4: side ∈ "inside | outside | left | right" and `vehicle` = "parked or oncoming-lane vehicle"; 03 §3.1 bookEsses: "L 12 ^75 | R 12 ^75 | L 12 ^75"; 09 §3.5 P-VIS-MARGIN-MONOTONE: "raising vis_margin (all else fixed) never lowers the solved line's minimum sight margin".
findings.improvement: Restrict the quantifiers explicitly: P-SIGHT-EYE holds for scenarios whose occluders are all on the blind corner's inside (state this in 09 and in the fuzzer's scenario generator), or reformulate it as a conditional property. Reframe the fixpoint as a bounded heuristic whose correctness comes from the mandatory self-verification (which already re-checks V1/V2), not from a monotonicity theorem; document that alternating-hand blind chains may legitimately return NO_SOLUTION and give the agent-facing remediation.

findings.title: A-CHAIN-VIS contradicts 04's own budget-limited-hold carve-out on a zero-gap esses fixture
findings.claim: The acceptance test asserts the solved cautious chain 'holds vis_hold_f ahead of each blind corner until that corner's release station'. But 04 §6 explicitly says that when the inter-corner gap is too short the line 'holds as wide as the budget reaches' — not vis_hold_f — and the only named esses preset has zero inter-corner straights, so the hold target is unreachable there by construction. As literally written, the acceptance test fails on the fixture family it names, and an implementer must guess whether to weaken the assertion, pad the fixture with gaps, or read 'holds vis_hold_f' as 'holds the budget-limited actual'. There is a deeper wrinkle: the V2 hold is a generated `position` action 'in the inter-corner span', while 03 rejects position actions whose window overlaps a turn_in commitment (INEFFECTUAL) — with a zero-length span the solver's generated plan may be rejected by its own validator, and no doc resolves this.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.5 A-CHAIN-VIS: "the blind-esses fixture solved with vis=cautious... holds `vis_hold_f` ahead of each blind corner until that corner's release station"; 04 §6: "when the gap is too short to reach `vis_hold_f`, the line holds as wide as the budget reaches, and the release condition is evaluated from the **actual** position, never the unreached target"; 03 §3.1 bookEsses: "linked turns, zero inter-corner straights"; 03 §6.1: "A `position` action whose transition window overlaps an active `turn_in` commitment is **rejected at validation**... (`INEFFECTUAL`, `position_overlaps_turn_in`)".
findings.improvement: Rewrite A-CHAIN-VIS to assert the carve-out semantics: the line holds min(vis_hold_f, budget-reachable f) per inter-corner span, with the achieved hold recorded in the verdict so the assertion is checkable. Specify how solver-generated position actions interact with the overlap rejection (e.g. generated holds are exempt because the solver places them before turn-in by construction, or the zero-gap case generates no position action at all).

findings.title: The proportion gate is largely self-referential: auto width_exag solves to the gate's own band and the presets were designed inside it
findings.claim: The gate is sold as the mechanism that 'makes the stretched-paths defect class detectable', but in the default pipeline its headline metric cannot fail: 06 §2.3's auto width_exag picks the smallest factor achieving WIDTH_RATIO_TARGET = 0.55, which sits inside the gate band 0.45–0.95, so width_ratio passes by construction unless the ×12 clamp binds (needs w/R < ~0.046, i.e. R ≳ 150 m on a 7 m road) or the projection degrades on overlapping esses. Meanwhile 09 §5.3's round-trip test checks presets that 03 §3.1 says were constructed to be 'already inside the book's measured proportion band' — the presets testing the band they were designed from. What the gate actually binds is only the window-crop and compression defaults (via straight_share, road_ink, frame_aspect) and hand-set ViewSpecs. Separately, the bands' provenance ('measured from the book's figures') has no committed measurement artifact or procedure — an implementer cannot re-derive 0.55–0.9 from hand-drawn art without a stated method (what counts as the radius of a stylized figure?), so 'TUNING, measured from the book' is unreproducible.
findings.evidence: 09 §5.2: "book band ≈ 0.55–0.9 — TUNING, measured from the book's figures"; 06 §2.3: "pick the smallest factor such that... (road_width × width_exag) / R_corner ≥ WIDTH_RATIO_TARGET = 0.55" with "width_exag ≤ WIDTH_EXAG_MAX = 12"; 06 §6.1 gate band "0.45 – 0.95" and "Bands are derived from measuring the book's Chapter 8 figures... blessed in one place"; 09 §5.3: "each book preset rendered in **`true` mode** must already land near the proportion bands"; 03 §3.1: presets "render at **true scale** already inside the book's measured proportion band"; 09 §5.2 preamble: "The gate that makes the stretched-paths defect class *detectable*".
findings.improvement: Commit the measurement: a small artifact (per book figure: annotated image, measured width/radius/straight-share, the derivation of the bands) so the bands are reproducible and re-derivable. Then state honestly in 06/09 which metrics the gate actually constrains under auto defaults (crop, compression, degraded projections, hand-set specs) and add at least one adversarial fixture per failure mode — e.g. a deliberately stretched ViewSpec and a large-R road at the clamp — proving the gate can fire.

findings.title: The vision-judge CI gate is nondeterministic and entirely unspecified as machinery
findings.claim: 09 makes a vision-capable subagent's verdict the gate for every static export ('the subagent's visual verdict — not the arithmetic — is the gate') and re-triggers judging on every physics migration, but specifies none of what a CI gate needs: which judge (model identity, version pinning), what prompt/rubric operationalization (01 §3 gives two axes, not pass/fail criteria), what output contract, where verdicts are recorded or blessed, what happens on flake or disagreement (re-run? majority? human arbiter?), or how a nondeterministic judgment coexists with 08's deterministic exit-code tiers ('a failed test/gate run' exits 3). A merge gate whose outcome varies run-to-run with an LLM's sampling is a CI design decision the docs never confront, and the re-bless ceremony makes it load-bearing on every constant re-tune.
findings.evidence: 09 §7: "the editing agent never trusts its own eyeball; the subagent's visual verdict — not the arithmetic — is the gate" and "only eyes can confirm the compressed figure doesn't visually lie"; 09 §3.3(e): a re-bless commit "triggers a fresh vision judge for any figure re-exported afterwards"; 08 §3.1 exit 3: "(per **09**) a failed test/gate run"; 01 §3 defines the two axes but no scoring procedure; 09 §8 defines the runner as "the standard TS/ESM toolchain runner" with no judge integration.
findings.improvement: Specify the judge as a pinned harness: model + version recorded in the manifest, a fixed rubric checklist with per-item pass/fail (derived from 01 §3 and 06 §7's parity requirement), a JSON verdict schema, N-sample consistency policy (e.g. 2-of-3), and a blessed-verdict file so re-judging is only required when the figure's bytes change. Decide explicitly whether the judge is a merge gate or an advisory report with human sign-off, and say so in 09.

findings.title: Every TUNING re-tune is formally a physics migration; the regime has no development-phase story
findings.claim: 09 §3.3 defines any hash-moving change as a migration requiring one dedicated commit that regenerates all goldens, enumerates every moved golden and why, re-pins the mistake-oracle table, and re-triggers vision judging. But nearly every constant in 02/03/04 is marked TUNING and sits upstream of every preset's result_hash, and the design itself mandates an iterative empirical search (02 §5.4 makes constants 'servants' to invariants; 04 §4.3 requires brackets 're-validated empirically as an implementation gate'). Landing Tier 1R is presented as one migration commit, but finding K_SU/A_SU_ONSET/freeze_s values that satisfy invariants 5.4.1–5 while keeping the chop preset pinned wide/runoff and C30-trailbrake tightening is a search of dozens of iterations — during which the oracle is red and the ceremony either fires per-iteration (crushing friction) or is batched (during which the 'iron rule' — never edit the expectation — is unenforceable because expectations and constants co-evolve). The regime never distinguishes pre-first-bless development from post-release maintenance.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.3: "A physics change is a migration, not a patch" with steps (a)–(e) and "Hashes move in re-bless commits and nowhere else"; "The Tier 1R run-wide slice itself lands through exactly this procedure"; 09 §4: "The single legitimate occasion to edit the pinned outcome table is a designed physics migration"; 02 §5.4: "These are the specification; the constants above are servants to them"; 04 §4.3: "Both bisection brackets are re-tuned under Tier 1R (marked TUNING); the monotonicity assumptions behind `bisect` must be re-validated empirically".
findings.improvement: Add an explicit lifecycle tier: before the first bless (or behind a `pre-release` flag), goldens/oracle pins are provisional and constants move freely with a lightweight log; the full migration ceremony binds from the first tagged release onward. Additionally, classify constants by blast radius (physics vs solver-default vs render/gate) so a render-constant change never demands engine golden regeneration.

findings.title: The mistake oracle's base scenarios are unspecified and its wide-vs-runoff pins rest on an unspecified corrective-shot solver
findings.claim: 09 §4 runs 'every registered preset' and asserts 'the outcome class matches the pinned table', but no document says what a registered preset's base scenario is: 03 §7.1's pins are per-kind and road-independent, yet outcomes are road-dependent (early_apex by 5 m stays contained on a large-radius corner; overspeed +26 km/h may crash rather than runoff on a tight one). Only chop gets a named golden scenario (C30-chop in 02 §8); the other five kinds' registration roads, entry speeds, and profiles are guesses. Worse, several pins distinguish `wide` from `runoff` — a boundary decided by whether 'a feasible add-lean corrective exists', but the corrective shot is specified in a single sentence of 02 §7 with no algorithm (fired when? at run_wide_detect? after t_react_s? what control authority?), so the oracle's most brittle assertions depend on machinery with no design.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.3: "Every registered preset and every committed scenario file gets `spec_hash`..."; 09 §4: "asserts the declared check **actually fails** and the outcome class matches the pinned table"; 03 §7.1 table pins e.g. `early_apex` → "`runoff` (runs wide)" with no base road; 02 §8 names only "C30-chop" and "C30-trailbrake" as companions; 02 §7: "`runoff` — left the road/lane and no feasible corrective returns it (the corrective shot, integrated with the run-wide slice active, fails)" — the entirety of the corrective-shot spec; 02 §3: "`t_react_s` is the recognition delay used by run-wide correction" (a parameter with no algorithm).
findings.improvement: Pin one named base scenario per mistake kind (e.g. all six registered against C30 or book90 with stated entry speeds), listed in 03 §7.1 beside the outcome pins so the oracle is executable without guessing. Specify the corrective shot as a first-class algorithm in 02 (trigger event, delay, commanded inputs, feasibility criterion, its own deadband) — or soften the pins to the union class `wide|runoff` wherever the distinction is corrective-dependent, and pin the strict class only where the design genuinely commits to it.

findings.title: D8 effectuality testing: the promised conformance spec does not exist, and the obligation as stated is undecidable
findings.claim: 03 §6.1 promises 'the conformance test that enforces this (schema-field × consumer enumeration) is specified in 09-verification-and-testing.md', but 09 §8 contains no such specification — only the restated aspiration that 'for every schema-accepted input surface, a test asserts an observable effect... changes the trajectory of a reference scenario'. The quantifier is broken in both directions: a genuinely effectual field can be inert on the chosen reference scenario (a mu patch the line never crosses, taper_to_s on an already-clipped brake, a vis_margin delta smaller than the trend deadband), and some accepted fields provably change no physics or render output at all (FigureResult.meta is 'presentation hints only', labels, note, figure_id) — under a literal reading D8's own rule would demand these be rejected INEFFECTUAL. Nothing defines the witness-scenario set per field, the change metric (result_hash inequality? tolerance-exceeding delta?), or the field-vs-action granularity, so a first team must invent the entire mechanism the decision log advertises as enforced.
findings.evidence: 03 §6.1: "The conformance test that enforces this (schema-field × consumer enumeration) is specified in `09-verification-and-testing.md`"; 09 §8: "for every schema-accepted input surface, a test asserts an observable effect — every plan action type changes the trajectory of a reference scenario, every road DSL construct changes the road, every mistake kind changes the outcome or line, every `view:` control changes the render. An input with no effect test does not ship" (no enumeration mechanism, witness set, or metric); 05 §7: "meta: { title?, caption?, view? }  // presentation hints only, never physics"; 00 D8: "Every accepted input does something; anything unsupported is rejected at validation with a typed reason."
findings.improvement: Write the actual conformance spec in 09: a committed table of (schema field → witness scenario id → observed output channel → change metric), generated by enumerating the schema and failing CI when a field lacks a row. Explicitly carve out declared presentation-only fields (meta, labels, note) as a third category — 'presentational, exempt from physics effectuality, covered by render-diff tests' — so D8's rule is decidable rather than aspirational.

findings.title: Cross-runtime tolerance-equality has no divergence model, no deadbands for discrete solver outputs, and no browser harness
findings.claim: 09 §3.1 asserts browser results are 'tolerance-equal, with discrete-verdict flips prevented by the deadbands specified in 02' — but 02 §7's deadbands cover only crash classification. The quantities the goldens actually pin include discrete-valued solver outputs with no deadband: the turn-in station comes off a 2 m coarse grid ranked by |apex_pct − 58| ('full-solve the top 4... return the first that verifies clean'), the apex station is an argmin over a 0.5 m resample grid with a locally flat minimum, and wide-vs-runoff flips on corrective-shot feasibility. An LSB difference in a transcendental can flip a candidate ranking or an argmin, producing 0.5–2 m jumps that a ±0.01 m tolerance cannot absorb — the tolerance is category-mismatched to the quantity. Meanwhile the actual divergence channel is never named: ECMAScript pins arithmetic and sqrt to IEEE 754 but leaves Math.tan/atan/tanh implementation-approximated, differing across V8/JSC/SpiderMonkey — which also means bit-exact cross-runtime is cheaply achievable with own math kernels, an option the design never weighs. Finally C-ONE-CORE ('the same ESM module imported twice, so the test is cheap') proves nothing about browsers when run in Node, and no browser-side CI harness or per-quantity tolerance table for the cross-runtime comparison is specified anywhere.
