findings.evidence: 09 §3.1: "Across runtimes — including the browser — results are **tolerance-equal**, with discrete-verdict flips prevented by the deadbands specified in `02-physics-model.md`"; 02 §7: deadbands are "crash only when `phi > phiMax + eps_phi_deg (0.05°)` or `ellipseMag > 1 + eps_mag`"; 09 §3.2 tolerances: "positions ±0.01 m"; 04 §3.1–3.3: 2 m candidate grid, "Rank... by `|apex_pct − 58|`", "return the first that verifies clean"; 02 §6: 0.5 m resample grid; 09 §6 C-ONE-CORE: "Under D1 this is the same ESM module imported twice, so the test is cheap"; 07 §2.1 promises "a CLI-vs-viewer tolerance-equality test" without a harness.
findings.improvement: Name the divergence model: either ship deterministic tan/atan/tanh/sin/cos kernels inside core/ (making cross-runtime bit-exact and collapsing the tolerance machinery to the pinned-runtime case), or specify per-quantity comparison rules — continuous fields under the numeric tolerances; discrete/argmin/selection quantities compared as 'equal or off by exactly one grid step with matching verdict', with hysteresis or sub-grid interpolation specified for apex/exit measurement. Specify the browser CI leg concretely: headless browser matrix, which fixtures run, which tolerance table applies.

findings.title: Golden comparison ambiguity: fixtures raw vs emission-rounded, with tolerance equal to the rounding quantum
findings.claim: 09 §3.2 compares goldens 'under explicit numeric tolerances (positions ±0.01 m...)' but never says whether fixture values are raw f64 or pass through 05 §8.3's emission rounding (metres to 2 dp — a 0.01 m quantum). If fixtures are emitted values, the tolerance equals the rounding step, so a true drift of ~0.005 m can present as exactly 0.01 and flake at the boundary; if raw, the bless script must bypass the 'same loaders' emission path 09 §3.3 mandates. An implementer must guess which, and the guess changes flakiness behavior.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.2: "positions ±0.01 m, angles ±0.01°, speeds ±0.01 m/s — TUNING"; 05 §8.3: "metres / km/h / degrees to 2 dp... applied **only** at the verdict/CSV boundary"; 09 §3.3: "recomputes both for the whole set via the same loaders the bless script uses".
findings.improvement: State it: golden fixtures store raw full-precision values captured before emission rounding, and tolerances apply to raw-vs-raw comparison; hashes alone go through the canonical emitted form.

findings.title: P-RUNWIDE-UPRIGHT requires a slice-off engine that no schema, config, or API exposes
findings.claim: The property demands straight-line braking be 'byte-identical with the slice on or off', but Tier 1R is the model — 02 defines no toggle, 03 §6's config block has no field for it, and D3 says the slice is the one addition defining the tier. Running the comparison requires a test-only physics variant, which is a second engine by another name and collides with the one-core honesty stance unless its existence and confinement are specified.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.4: "P-RUNWIDE-UPRIGHT — the run-wide term contributes nothing at zero lean: straight-line braking is byte-identical with the slice on or off"; 02 §5.2 defines phi_dot_su unconditionally; 03 §6 config: "{ mu?, mode?, ds_m?, ssd_model?, checks_version }" — no slice flag; 07 §2.1: "there is no bundled 'viewer build' of the physics that could drift".
findings.improvement: Either respecify the property analytically (at phi = 0, tanh(0) = 0 forces phi_dot_su ≡ 0, so assert byte-identity against a recorded upright-braking golden instead of an alternate engine), or specify a test-only `core/` factory parameter that zeroes K_SU/K_CHOP, confined to the test package by the same import-graph lint that guards the projection.

findings.title: The proportion gate's independent audit mode has no specified re-derivation method
findings.claim: 09 §5.2 requires an audit mode that 're-derives the metrics from the SVG geometry independently of the sidecar, so the renderer cannot self-certify' — but recovering width_ratio from an exported SVG means recovering a centreline radius and road width from path data (Béziers/arcs, possibly degraded geometry), and segmenting the drawing back into corners. No doc specifies how, what fidelity is expected, or what counts as agreement between audit and sidecar, so the anti-self-certification property is asserted without a mechanism.
findings.evidence: 09 §5.2: "An audit mode re-derives the metrics from the SVG geometry independently of the sidecar, so the renderer cannot self-certify"; 06 §6 defines metrics only in terms of the DrawnScene ("computed from the `DrawnScene` (and recomputable from the SVG)") with no SVG-side algorithm.
findings.improvement: Specify the audit contract: the exporter embeds machine-readable geometry (e.g. data attributes carrying the drawn centreline polyline and per-corner drawn radius/width) that the auditor parses and re-measures with its own arithmetic — independence of computation, not of data — plus an agreement tolerance.

findings.title: Solver-intent tests (§3.5) never state their scenario quantifier
findings.claim: 09 §3.4 explicitly runs its properties 'against fuzzed schema-valid scenarios as well as the fixtures', but §3.5's solver-intent tests (P-CONSTRAINT-BINDING, P-VIS-MARGIN-MONOTONE) state no quantifier at all. Whether these run on fixtures only or under fuzzing changes both their cost (each evaluation is a full solve, 50–150 engine runs) and their truth (P-VIS-MARGIN-MONOTONE is falsifiable under fuzzed multi-occluder scenarios per the monotonicity finding). An implementer must guess the scope, and the guess determines whether the suite is green.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.4 preamble: "Run against fuzzed schema-valid scenarios as well as the fixtures"; 09 §3.5 opens directly with the test list, no scoping sentence; contrast with §5.1 which re-states its own quantifier ("These run on fuzzed roads and line sets, not only fixtures").
findings.improvement: Add one scoping sentence to §3.5 naming the scenario set (e.g. "run on the committed vis fixtures plus a bounded fuzz corpus of single-inside-occluder corners") consistent with wherever the monotonicity claims are ultimately restricted to hold.

wins: The three-layer mechanism assignment (09 §2) — pixel gates verify artifacts, contract tests verify behaviour, and neither borrows the other's mechanism — is genuinely sound and prevents the classic mistake of screenshot-testing a live viewer or contract-testing legibility.

Invariant-first specification (02 §5.4: 'These are the specification; the constants above are servants to them') is the right relationship between TUNING constants and tests — behaviors are pinned, values are free — even though the migration ceremony (see findings) undercuts it procedurally.

Decoupling result hashes from committed figures (09 §3.3.1) genuinely dissolves the prior project's 'Do NOT fix casually' coupling; a physics change no longer forces re-rendering committed teaching artifacts.

C-POV-TRUE-GEOMETRY's dual enforcement — an import-graph lint (structural) plus byte-identity across projection settings (behavioural) — is a model for verifying an honesty property rather than asserting it.

The mistake oracle's D6 extension (09 §4): the share → recompute → tolerance-equal round-trip is the mechanical form of 'never ship a trajectory the engine didn't produce', and it is cheap and decisive.

The projection invariants P1–P6 (06 §2.5, 09 §5.1) are well-chosen, provable properties precisely because the transform is defined in station space with a strictly monotone remap — the design earns its own testability here.

C-RECOMPUTE-BUDGET's framing as a doctrine tripwire ('if the engine ever grows past interactive recompute, D6's share-and-recompute story needs a redesign, and this test is where that surfaces first') plants a sentinel at the design's riskiest promise — the budget number is wrong, but the instinct to gate it is exactly right.
Reconciling the expect_fail oracle both ways (an expected failure that doesn't occur is as red as an unexpected one) closes the silent-rot direction most oracle schemes miss.

The educational-tests and no-coverage-theater rules (09 §8), with tests written from the design docs before code, match the contract-first structure of the whole document set and make the suite double as the missing usage manual.

verdicts.title: Golden-numerics bootstrap: the first bless certifies nothing, and 09's cross-reference to 02's 'worked numbers' is false
verdicts.note: 09 §3.2 states "02-physics-model.md defines the canonical scenarios... and their worked numbers", but 02 §8 says "Once the engine exists, the golden run pins the following quantities" and contains no numeric values — only bounds (apex_pct "must exceed the late bar of 50", phi_max "at/below the 40.36° reserve", outcome clean). The cross-reference is false as written. And since 09 forbids hand-computed goldens ("produced by the engine and blessed, never hand-computed") while making independent re-derivations optional ("welcome as additional tests but never replace the blessed fixture"), the first bless pins engine output against itself. Caveat that doesn't defeat the claim: property tests (P-KAPPA analytic identity, P-ELLIPSE) and the oracle's outcome pins do constrain a first engine a priori — but not the golden numeric values themselves.

verdicts.title: C-RECOMPUTE-BUDGET: the 100 ms solve-included budget is unsubstantiated by ~two orders of magnitude in engine-run count
verdicts.note: All arithmetic checks against cited text: 04 §3.1 gives 17 coarse candidates (s0−24..s0+8 in 2 m steps) with "Full-solve the top 4"; 04 §4.1–4.2 give probe + 16 + 16 bisection runs + self-verify per solve (34 runs); 04 §5–6 multiply per corner, per ascending-decel step, and ×vis_max_iterations=4. 07 §2.1's only supporting arithmetic is "roughly 3–4 × 10³ fixed RK4 steps per line" — one engine run per line. 02 §6 fixes dt_s = 0.005 s for every run and defines ds_m as the resample grid only, so the 04 §3.1 "cheap engine run... ds_m = 1.0" saves resample/sight-scan cost but not integration. 05 §7–8 confirm FigureSpec carries solveSpec, never the solved plan, so viewer recompute includes the full solve. No doc substantiates a solve-inclusive 100 ms; 09 §6's own "if the engine ever grows past interactive recompute" hedge frames it as future growth, not day-one arithmetic.

verdicts.title: The vis-fixpoint monotone-convergence claim and P-SIGHT-EYE are false under the design's own occluder vocabulary
verdicts.note: 03 §4 permits side ∈ inside|outside|left|right and an on-carriageway `vehicle` ("parked or oncoming-lane"); 01 §6 even cites the book's fig 8.1 "oncoming vehicle". Constructible falsifier: on a right-hander (outside = oncoming side), an oncoming-lane vehicle just left of centreline blocks centreline targets from a wide eye (f→1, adjacent to centreline, directly behind the vehicle) that a tight eye (f→0, 3 m right) sees around — moving toward the outside shortens sight_m, breaking P-SIGHT-EYE under its stated fuzzed quantifier (09 §3.4 preamble) and 04 §6's "slowing and widening can only open the sight margin" justification, even single-corner. No doc restricts either to inside occluders. The chain-oscillation mechanism is plausible but not demonstrated, and non-convergence is at least typed NO_SOLUTION — the property and justification as pinned are nonetheless false under the design's own vocabulary; the v_floor/stopped edge for P-VIS-MARGIN-MONOTONE is likewise unaddressed.

verdicts.title: A-CHAIN-VIS contradicts 04's own budget-limited-hold carve-out on a zero-gap esses fixture
verdicts.note: 09 §3.5 asserts the solved chain "holds vis_hold_f ahead of each blind corner until that corner's release station", while 04 §6 specifies that when the gap is too short "the line holds as wide as the budget reaches" and release is evaluated from the actual position. The only named esses preset, bookEsses, is "linked turns, zero inter-corner straights" (03 §3.1), and no doc defines the blind-esses fixture's road, so as written the acceptance assertion contradicts the solver spec on its named fixture family or forces the implementer to guess. The validator wrinkle also stands: 04 §6's V2 hold is "a generated position action... in the inter-corner span" and 03 §6.1 rejects position windows overlapping an active turn_in (INEFFECTUAL, position_overlaps_turn_in); with a zero-length span no doc resolves whether the solver's generated plan survives its own validation.

verdicts.title: The proportion gate is largely self-referential: auto width_exag solves to the gate's own band and the presets were designed inside it
verdicts.note: Surviving nucleus: default-pipeline width_ratio is closed-loop — 06 §2.3 solves exag to 0.55, inside the 0.45–0.95 band (fail via the ×12 clamp needs w/R < 0.0375, R ≳ 187 m on a 7 m road, even harder than the critic's figure), presets are built "already inside the book's measured proportion band" (03 §3.1) they are then tested against, and no committed measurement procedure/artifact backs "measured from the book's figures" (06 §6.1). Wrong scope/severity: the gate measures the *achieved* DrawnScene/SVG geometry — 09 §5.2's audit mode exists precisely so "the renderer cannot self-certify" — so it catches auto-exag, window, degradation (06 §2.6 explicitly routes degraded esses to the gate) and hand-set-view bugs; a gate confirming a controller hit its target is defense-in-depth, not tautology. And straight_share/road_ink bind against the prior defect's other root cause (~60 % straights, 06 §1). "Largely self-referential" and major overstate; the reproducibility gap is the solid part.

verdicts.title: The vision-judge CI gate is nondeterministic and entirely unspecified as machinery
verdicts.note: Confirmed: no judge identity or version pinning, no output contract, no verdict recording/blessing location, no flake/disagreement policy anywhere in the ten docs; 09 §8's runner spec has no judge integration; §3.3(e) makes judging recur on every migration. Wrong framing: the docs never constitute it as an automated CI/merge gate — 09 §7 carries the prior regime's agent-workflow discipline (extract/07 §5: a CLAUDE.md mandatory-subagent rule, "the subagent's visual verdict — not the arithmetic — is the gate for done"), the mechanical legs (render + proportion gates) own the exit codes, and 09 §7 does operationalize judging beyond 01 §3's bare axes (colour-by-verdict per D9, marker vocabulary, labels anchored on-line, mistakes reading as taught, disclosure-note presence). The machinery gap is real but "entirely unspecified" plus the CI-collision argument overstate it; severity below major.

verdicts.title: Every TUNING re-tune is formally a physics migration; the regime has no development-phase story
verdicts.note: The stated dilemma is defeated by the doc text. The ceremony is per-commit, not per-iteration: 09 §3.3 defines a migration as "one dedicated commit" whose bless script "regenerates all hashes and goldens" — batching is the designed procedure, and local iteration before that commit violates nothing because the tripwire only asserts "against the committed fixture" ("any drift outside a re-bless commit is a failure" is commit-scoped). The iron rule is not "unenforceable" during batching — 09 §4 explicitly sanctions expectation edits inside a designed migration ("The single legitimate occasion to edit the pinned outcome table is a designed physics migration landing through §3.3's re-bless procedure"), with steps (c)/(d) (enumerate every moved golden and why; re-pin the table) as the integrity mechanism. During a K_SU/A_SU_ONSET search the fixed expectations are a-priori design pins (02 §5.4 invariants, 03 §7.1 outcome classes), which is exactly the invariant-first scheme, and pre-first-bless there are no committed fixtures to drift from. What survives — heavy per-commit ceremony for hash-moving tunes — is the design's explicit intent (09 §9: "physics changes become first-class migrations"), not an overlooked defect.

verdicts.title: The mistake oracle's base scenarios are unspecified and its wide-vs-runoff pins rest on an unspecified corrective-shot solver
verdicts.note: Verified: 09 §4 requires "one per kind" mistake presets whose declared checks fail and outcome classes match the pinned table, but only chop has a named base scenario (C30-chop, 02 §8; C30-trailbrake is not a mistake kind); the other five kinds' registration roads, entry speeds, and profiles appear in no doc, while 03 §7.1's pins are road-dependent (early_apex pinned exactly `runoff`, overspeed pinned `runoff` though crash outranks it in precedence on tight geometry). The wide/runoff boundary rests on corrective-shot feasibility whose entire specification is one sentence in 02 §7 ("the corrective shot, integrated with the run-wide slice active, fails") plus scattered references (02 §3 t_react_s, 04 §4.3, 05's run_wide_detect/correction events and `corrective` field) — no trigger timing, control authority, or success criterion anywhere in the set.

verdicts.title: Cross-runtime tolerance-equality has no divergence model, no deadbands for discrete solver outputs, and no browser harness
verdicts.note: 02 §7's deadbands cover crash classification only (plus 03 §5.1's sight-trend deadband), so 09 §3.1's "discrete-verdict flips prevented by the deadbands specified in 02" overclaims: nothing deadbands the 2 m turn-in candidate ranking ("|apex_pct − 58|... return the first that verifies clean"), the 0.5 m-grid apex argmin, or corrective-shot feasibility — an LSB flip produces grid-quantum jumps that ±0.01 m tolerances cannot absorb, and no per-quantity cross-runtime tolerance table exists (09 §3.2's table is the golden table). C-ONE-CORE as specified ("the same ESM module imported twice, so the test is cheap") is vacuous against browser math divergence (Math.tan/atan/tanh are implementation-approximated in ECMAScript), and no browser-side physics harness is specified anywhere — 09 §7's headless browser only rasterizes SVGs; 07 §2.1 promises the tolerance test without machinery. The docs do name the tolerance-over-bit-exact *decision* (09 §2.1), but never the divergence channel or the own-kernel alternative.

verdicts.title: Golden comparison ambiguity: fixtures raw vs emission-rounded, with tolerance equal to the rounding quantum
verdicts.note: 09 §3.2 sets positions ±0.01 m; 05 §8.3 rounds metres to 2 dp (a 0.01 m quantum) "only at the verdict/CSV boundary" — and the golden quantities (apex station, lane fractions, v_apex) are verdict-resident (05 §6.3 corners[]), so whether fixtures pass through emission rounding is genuinely undecided by the docs. If rounded, tolerance equals the quantum and ~0.005 m drift can present as exactly 0.01 at the boundary; if raw, the bless path must bypass the emission policy while 09 §3.3 mandates "the same loaders the bless script uses". Real ambiguity, correctly rated minor.

verdicts.title: P-RUNWIDE-UPRIGHT requires a slice-off engine that no schema, config, or API exposes
verdicts.note: Verified: 02 §5.2 defines phi_dot_su unconditionally, 03 §6's config block ({ mu?, mode?, ds_m?, ssd_model?, checks_version }) has no slice field, 08's flag set exposes none, and D3 defines the tier as point-mass + the slice — so the property as written ("byte-identical with the slice on or off") implies a capability nothing specifies. Tempering the characterization: this is not really "a second engine" — zeroing the slice's own TUNING gains (K_SU = K_CHOP = 0) realizes slice-off in the same code path, and the term is analytically exactly zero at phi = 0 — but the docs specify neither that seam nor any constant-injection surface, so the minor documentation gap stands as stated.

verdicts.title: The proportion gate's independent audit mode has no specified re-derivation method
verdicts.note: 09 §5.2 mandates the audit mode ("re-derives the metrics from the SVG geometry independently of the sidecar"); 06 §6 defines the metrics only off the DrawnScene with a bare assertion "(and recomputable from the SVG)"; no doc gives an SVG-side algorithm (recovering centreline radius/road width from path data, re-segmenting corners), expected fidelity, or the audit-vs-sidecar agreement criterion, and 06 §7's export spec pins no addressable SVG structure that would make re-derivation tractable. The anti-self-certification property is asserted without a mechanism, as claimed. Minor is the right severity.

verdicts.title: Solver-intent tests (§3.5) never state their scenario quantifier
verdicts.note: Verified by contrast: 09 §3.4 opens "Run against fuzzed schema-valid scenarios as well as the fixtures", 09 §5.1 restates its own quantifier ("These run on fuzzed roads and line sets, not only fixtures"), but §3.5 opens directly with its test list and no scoping sentence anywhere in the section. The gap is load-bearing exactly as claimed: each §3.5 evaluation is a full solve (the run-count arithmetic of the budget finding), and P-VIS-MARGIN-MONOTONE's truth differs between fixtures-only and fuzzed multi-occluder scenarios (per the confirmed monotonicity finding), so the guessed scope determines whether the suite is green.

findings.title: The doctrine check catalogue does not exist anywhere in design/
findings.claim: The verdict — the object that determines every line's colour, the mistake oracle's expectations, the HUD's check-id display, and `explain`'s answers — is graded by a check suite whose membership and arithmetic no design document specifies. 01 and 05 defer to each other in a closed loop: 01 §3 says "check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in 05"; 05 §6.2 says "The check *content* is doctrine and lives in 01" and then pins the id list as "the carried line-selection checks" plus two new ids — without ever enumerating the carried checks. Only 5 check ids appear anywhere in design/, all in passing (late_apex, out_in_out, single_input in 01's mistake table; stop_within_sight, hold_wide_for_sight in 05 §6.2). The actual 12-check catalogue with arithmetic exists only in extract/05-doctrine-and-line-method.md §5.2 — the superseded prior design. Worse, the extract fallback (00 §5) is explicitly insufficient: 05 §6.2 says checks touched by the run-wide slice ("trail-brake taper, the single-steering-input smoothness bar, and anything keyed to the chop outcome class") "are re-derived under Tier 1R physics and re-pinned" — and that re-derivation is written nowhere. There is also a latent id collision: the carried catalogue already contains `sight_vs_stopping` (extract 05 §5.2 check #9), while v2 adds `stop_within_sight` doing the same job; the design does not say whether the old id is carried (redundant), renamed (contradicting 05 §6.2's "the check *ids* are stable"), or dropped. Downstream, colour law v2 (06 §5.1) defines green as "outcome = clean and no doctrine check failed" — so the green/amber boundary of every figure is undefined. And the mistake oracle (09 §4) requires each kind to fail its declared check, but under the carried arithmetic `slow_steer` fails no check (extract's `quick_steer` is WARN-only), so the oracle for at least one of six kinds cannot even be written.
findings.evidence: design/01-scope-and-doctrine.md §3: "check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in `05-result-contract-and-inspection.md`". design/05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §6.2: "The check *content* is doctrine and lives in `01-scope-and-doctrine.md`; this document pins the record shape and the id list", "check ids (v2): the carried line-selection checks + \"stop_within_sight\" ... + \"hold_wide_for_sight\"", "re-derived under Tier 1R physics and re-pinned; the check *ids* are stable". design/06-rendering-and-projection.md §5.1: "'good' if outcome = clean and no doctrine check failed". design/09-verification-and-testing.md §4: "asserts the declared check **actually fails**". extract/05-doctrine-and-line-method.md §5.2: the only enumeration (late_apex, out_in_out, single_input, quick_steer, throttle_rule, trail_brake_taper, traction_ceiling, lean_ceiling, sight_vs_stopping, exit_containment, link_continuity, rideability) — including "`quick_steer` ... **WARN** (informational, *not* FAIL)".
findings.improvement: Add a normative check-catalogue section (most naturally 01 §4.4 or a new appendix owned by 05): enumerate all v2 ids, state each check's pass/fail/warn/na arithmetic with its constants (TUNING-marked where unbookable), resolve `sight_vs_stopping` vs `stop_within_sight` explicitly (rename with a stated migration, or drop with rationale), and write the Tier-1R re-derivations for trail_brake_taper, single_input, and throttle_rule now — including which check `slow_steer`'s oracle pins (e.g. promote quick_steer WARN to FAIL above a bar, or key it to danger-zone dwell).

findings.title: Colour law v2's amber cannot be reconciled with the book's two-colour figures, and the fig 8.4 red-parity claim is unsupported
findings.claim: The book's Chapter 8 figures carry a strict binary moral: green = do this, red = this is the mistake (fig 8.1 paints the premature turn point red and running wide across the centreline toward the oncoming car). Colour law v2 introduces amber with two pedagogically opposite meanings collapsed into one colour: "contained-but-sound chained line" (a line the student should broadly accept) and "a mistake-role line that happens to stay contained" (an error the rider got away with). A student reading a teaching figure cannot distinguish 'acceptable' from 'error-you-survived' — the two things the book's palette exists to separate — while the design simultaneously insists colour is "a hard doctrinal signal". The deeper structural problem: G7 promises book-equivalent figures for figs 8.1–8.6, but under D9 colours are emergent verdicts that cannot be pinned, so book-colour parity is hoped, not designed. The design's own worked example breaks: 01 asserts fig 8.4's double-apex companion "renders red because its verdict is red" — but red requires outcome wide/runoff/crash (06 §5.1), and at the "significantly lower speed" the book itself prescribes for that path, the double-apex strategy plausibly stays contained → amber, mismatching the book's red. The book's fig 8.4 caption moreover contradicts the design's premise that the line is "legitimately failing": Parks says you can take either path. Under 00 §1 ("the book wins disputes") this is a dispute the design resolves against the book without acknowledging it.
findings.evidence: design/01-scope-and-doctrine.md §3: "a *legitimately failing* second strategy (fig 8.4's double-apex companion) renders red because its verdict is red"; §5: "under colour law v2 that red is simply the second strategy's own failing verdict on this corner". design/06-rendering-and-projection.md §5.1: "'failing' if outcome ∈ {wide, runoff, crash}"; "A `mistake`-role line that happens to stay contained shows **amber**". design/01 §2 G7: "linelab produces an equivalent figure". book_text part0014 fig 8.4 caption: "With a delayed entry, it can be safely completed with only one turning point. In the case of blind corners ... you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed." book_images/by-figure/fig-08.04__decreasing-radius-turn.jpeg (red double-apex line, green single-apex line, both staying on the road); fig-08.01__premature-initiation.jpeg (red premature line exiting across the centreline).
findings.improvement: Three changes: (1) Amend 01 §5 to state honestly that companion-line colours are emergent and per-figure parity must be *engineered* — each shipped book-figure scene pins (via the 09 oracle, per scene not per kind) the outcome class of every line at the preset's speeds, so fig 8.1's mistake line is verified red-by-outcome and fig 8.4's companion is either tuned (entry speed) to legitimately fail or the scene's caption/legend explicitly departs from the book's palette with a disclosure. (2) Resolve the fig 8.4 book dispute explicitly in 01 — either the red is 'wrong at this speed' (book prose wins over book ink) or state why the ink wins. (3) Disambiguate amber's two meanings with a non-colour channel that is normative, not incidental: e.g. the legend must print the verdict word plus role ("mistake — contained"), and a contained mistake-role line carries a warning glyph at its terminal arrowhead.

findings.title: The premature / early_apex naming inverts the book's vocabulary and is patched with prose instead of fixed
findings.claim: The book's name for the canonical turned-in-too-soon-and-ran-wide mistake is "Premature Initiation" (the fig 8.1 title); "early apex" is, in the book's own causal sentence, the *consequence* ("an early turn point creates an early apex, which forces the line wide"). linelab assigns `premature` to the contained amber variant and `early_apex` to the book's premature-initiation figure — exactly backwards from how anyone who has read the doctrine (which the tool declares supreme) will map words to kinds. The design knows this — 01 §4.3 titles it "The naming trap, resolved explicitly" and mandates that `schema` and `explain` re-explain it at every surface — which is an admission that the names fail G4's first-try bar and are being propped up by documentation. The two kinds are also evidence against their own separation: 03 §7's rule is "exactly one control perturbed", yet `early_apex` perturbs two (turn-in station AND a committed lean), i.e. the pair is really one mistake with a severity/commitment parameter, split into two kinds whose names then had to be disambiguated in prose.
findings.evidence: book_text part0014: section title "Premature Initiation"; "So an early turn point creates an early apex, which forces the line wide or requires a mid-corner steering correction." design/01-scope-and-doctrine.md §4.3: "**The naming trap, resolved explicitly.** ... An author who wants the book's canonical ... figure must use `early_apex` ... `premature` is the contained variant". design/03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §7: "exactly one control perturbed" vs §7.1 `early_apex`: "turn in `early_by_m = 5` early **and** commit an explicit lean". design/08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §5.1: the schema teaching-table exists specifically to defuse this trap.
findings.improvement: Rename so the book's word gets the book's outcome: `early_apex` → `premature` (canonical, runs wide, maps to fig 8.1), and the contained variant → `premature_contained` (the shared prefix makes the relationship discoverable and no reader picks the bare book term expecting containment). Alternatively collapse to one kind `premature` with a `commit: "full" | "eased"` parameter defaulting to the book's canonical run-wide outcome — which also honours the one-perturbation rule better than the current two-control `early_apex`. Keep the schema teaching table, but as reinforcement rather than as the only thing standing between an agent and the wrong figure.

findings.title: The stateAt phase vocabulary is defined nowhere and contradicts 06's phase bands
findings.claim: 05 §4 returns `phase: "approach"|"entry"|"steering"|"mid"|"exit"|"done" (from events)` — six values whose boundaries are never defined in any document. 06 §4 derives a *four*-band partition from events for the controls strip — approach (brake_start→turn_in), steering (turn_in→steering_complete), mid (→roll_on), exit (→exit) — with no "entry" and no "done". So the two docs disagree on the partition, "entry" as a phase exists only in 05's one line, and the words are triple-loaded across the design: `entry`/`mid`/`exit` are simultaneously station anchors (03 §6.1: `at: {ref: "entry|exit|mid:<cornerId>"}` — geometric points of a corner), event kinds (05 §5: `exit`), and phase spans (05 §4) with incompatible meanings — the `mid:<cornerId>` anchor is the corner's geometric middle, while the `mid` phase is steering_complete→roll_on, which need not contain it. Unanswered questions an implementer must guess: what phase precedes brake_start, or holds when a plan has no brake action (the approach band's left edge is brake_start)? Is "done" exit→termination, and how does it square with stateAt returning BAD_RANGE beyond termination? How does phase behave between corners of a chained sequence, where corner_id is null?
findings.evidence: design/05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §4: "phase // \"approach\"|\"entry\"|\"steering\"|\"mid\"|\"exit\"|\"done\" (from events)" — the term's only occurrence. design/06-rendering-and-projection.md §4: "**Corner-phase bands**: ... approach (`brake_start→turn_in`), steering (`turn_in→steering_complete`), mid (`→roll_on`), exit (`→exit`)". design/03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §6.1: anchors "entry|exit|mid:<cornerId>". design/00-README.md §4: "anchored corner-relative (`entry`, `exit`, `mid`, `±offset`)".
findings.improvement: Pin the phase state machine in 05 (it owns stateAt): one table mapping each phase to its entering event and its value in degenerate cases (no brake action, chained corners, post-exit, terminal). Either delete "entry" or define it (e.g. brake_end→turn_in, splitting 06's approach), and make 06 §4's bands cite 05's table verbatim instead of defining their own. Consider renaming the phase values to break collision with the anchor grammar (e.g. `approach|turning|midcorner|exiting|done`), since 00 §4 demands vocabulary be used verbatim and these words already mean stations.

findings.title: The POV's fixed-heading camera loses the limit point off-frame on the book presets and silently cuts the book's central vision doctrine
findings.claim: The POV camera yaws with bike heading only (07 §5.2: "Yaw = psi ... target fixation and head-turn modelling are out of scope") with a 60-degree FOV. On the design's own book presets this geometry pushes the limit-point marker — the POV's headline teaching device (G9: "with the limit point marked") — to or beyond the frame edge exactly when it matters: on `book90` (R 12), a limit point 12 m ahead along the arc sits ~29° off heading (half the 57° swept angle), at the edge of the ±30° frame; anything deeper is off-screen, so the mid-corner "opening" moment — the doctrinal speed-release cue (01 §6) — is invisible. No spec exists for an off-frame limit point (07 §5.3 item 7 just draws the chevron at its projected position). Beyond the geometry bug, the scope cut itself is wrong-headed for this lens: Chapter 8 attributes all three canonical mistakes to gaze behaviour ("it's important to look through the turn before you enter it"; premature initiation "often happens when the rider fixates on the inside of the turn"; fifty-pencing "is usually caused by not looking far enough through the turn"), and the POV — the one view built to show "how far they can see" — structurally cannot depict where a rider should look. Unlike every other cut, this one is not placarded: 01 §8's out-of-scope list (low-speed, body position, vertical geometry, Tier-3, HTML course) never mentions gaze/head-turn; the cut exists only as a parenthetical in 07 §5.2.
findings.evidence: design/07-viewer-animation-and-pov.md §5.2: "**Yaw** = `psi` (the bike's heading; target fixation and head-turn modelling are out of scope)", "fov_deg = 60"; §5.3 item 7: "**Limit-point marker** — the projected `(limit_x, limit_y)` drawn as a chevron" (no off-frame case). design/03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §3.1: `book90` = "R 12 ^90", `bookBlind` = book90 + hedge. design/01-scope-and-doctrine.md §2 G9 and §8 (gaze absent from the refused list). book_text part0014: "it's important to look through the turn before you enter it"; "Initiating too soon often happens when the rider fixates on the inside of the turn"; fig 8.3 caption: "usually caused by not looking far enough through the turn".
findings.improvement: Two additions to 07 §5: (1) an off-frame rule for the limit point — clamp the chevron to the frame edge with a directional arrow and keep the trend badge visible (cheap, data already per-sample); (2) a camera-yaw mode toggle, `look: "heading" | "limit_point"`, that yaws the camera toward the recorded (limit_x, limit_y) — this is a pure presentation change over existing per-sample data, it makes "look through the turn" a literal button, and it lets the fifty_pence lesson show the difference between the two gaze strategies. Add gaze modelling (as a physics/behaviour channel) to 01 §8's out-of-scope list with a placard so the cut is honest rather than silent.

findings.title: Full-phi horizon roll on a featureless flat world will read as the world tilting, and is not what a rider's eyes see
findings.claim: 07 §5.2 rolls the entire frame by phi and calls it "the POV's signature honesty: the horizon angle *is* the lean readout". At book-preset speeds phi reaches ~37° (34 km/h on R 12), so the frame rotates by more than half the 60° FOV. The rendered world is a flat two-tone ground/sky plus road ribbon with no in-frame vehicle reference — no handlebar, windscreen, or cockpit silhouette is anywhere in the draw order — so the only rotational anchor is the horizon itself; perceptually, a large rotation of a featureless scene with nothing ego-fixed in frame is ambiguous and tends to read as the environment tilting rather than the observer leaning (onboard motorcycle footage reads as lean largely because bike parts occupy the frame). It is also not a faithful "rider's-eye" experience: trained riders keep their head near level, so a full-phi tilt shows the student a view no competent rider ever sees. The unrotated HUD strip (§5.3 item 8) is the sole ego-fixed element and is not designed as an attitude reference.
findings.evidence: design/07-viewer-animation-and-pov.md §5.2: "**Roll** = `phi` — the whole image rotates with lean ... the horizon angle *is* the lean readout"; §5.3 draw order items 1–8 (no cockpit/vehicle element); §5: the view's job is to make "what lean feels like as horizon tilt" visceral. design/03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §3.1: book presets ~28–34 km/h on R 10–16 (implying 30–40° lean).
findings.improvement: Add a TUNING head-roll compensation factor `head_roll_k` (render roll = k·phi, default e.g. 0.6, with 1.0 available as the 'rigid camera' honest mode, disclosed in the frame like the diagram footnote), and/or a minimal ego-fixed frame element — a static lower-frame cockpit silhouette or a small artificial-horizon lean dial in the POV HUD strip — so the rotation has an unambiguous 'self' referent. State in 07 which mode is the default and why.

findings.title: Three of Chapter 8's load-bearing prose claims are undemonstrable, and none of the gaps is placarded
findings.claim: Simulating 'the book wins' against Tier 1R finds at least three Chapter 8 claims linelab cannot demonstrate. (1) Reserve payoff / reactive hazards — the chapter's entire street rationale: "you must have some line options in reserve ... if any hazard pops up just out of your line of sight"; "Using a slower corner entry speed will allow you to safely make a mid-corner steering correction." linelab can display the reserve (grip/lean margins) but can never show it being *spent*: plans are pre-scripted, `position` overlapping a turn_in is rejected (03 §6.1), the `vehicle` occluder blocks vision only (03 §4: blocks: ["vision"]) — nothing in the schema can pose 'a hazard appears; the line must respond', so the payoff of slow-in-fast-out is asserted by numbers, never witnessed. This matters: it is the book's stated reason the whole doctrine exists on the street. (2) Ground clearance — "you may run out of ground clearance and start scraping hard parts ... cruisers, whose lack of ground clearance is the limiting factor in cornering speed." Tier 1R's only lean ceiling is friction (phi_max = atan(mu), 05 §4 derived.phi_max_deg), implying ~45° available on any bike; the clearance-limited rider class the book repeatedly singles out cannot be represented, and the tool quietly teaches that grip is always the binding limit. This matters for a large real audience and would be a one-line profile field. (3) Perceptual causation — "your body naturally wants to go where your eyes are looking"; "looking far through the corner, your perception of speed slows way down." No physics tool can demonstrate these, and that is acceptable — but the mistake compiler presents its perturbations as *the* mistakes while the book says the mistakes are downstream of gaze; without a stated limitation, linelab's `explain` remediation ("move plan.b1.at_s earlier", 08 §5.2) teaches plan-editing where the book teaches looking. None of these three appears in 01 §8's out-of-scope list, violating the design's own placard policy ("Wherever the model cannot honestly answer, the answer is a typed refusal ... never a plausible fake").
findings.evidence: book_text part0014: "you must have some line options in reserve"; "if any hazard pops up just out of your line of sight, you may not have any ground clearance and traction left to handle it"; "Using a slower corner entry speed will allow you to safely make a mid-corner steering correction to the outside of the turn"; "This is even true of most cruisers, whose lack of ground clearance is the limiting factor in cornering speed"; "your body naturally wants to go where your eyes are looking". design/03-roads-scenarios-and-visibility.md §4 (vehicle blocks: ["vision"]), §6.1 (position_overlaps_turn_in rejected). design/05-result-contract-and-inspection.md §4 (phi_max_deg = atan(mu)). design/01-scope-and-doctrine.md §8: out-of-scope list omits all three; placard policy: "never a plausible fake".
findings.improvement: (1) Add a v1.x-flagged 'hazard event' scenario element (an obstacle with a station and a footprint that the plan must clear, paired with a solver mode that answers 'from this line and speed, does a feasible corrective exist?') — this is the minimal mechanism that turns reserve from a number into a demonstration; if it stays out of scope, add it to 01 §8 with a placard. (2) Add `phi_clearance_deg` to the rider/bike profile as a second, independent lean ceiling (min of clearance and grip governs), which is Tier-1-compatible and directly demonstrates the book's cruiser claim. (3) Add one sentence to 01 §8: gaze and perception are not modelled; mistake kinds reproduce the book's *control signatures*, not their perceptual causes — and have `explain` echo it on mistake-line results.

findings.title: The stepper/HUD is engineer-dense with no student tier, and doctrine explanation never reaches the viewer
findings.claim: The HUD presents roughly eighteen simultaneous quantities across six groups (v, psi, kappa plus equivalent radius, phi vs roll-rate cap plus a lean dial, a friction-ellipse widget with margin, cmd_a vs a_long with clip badge, cmd_lean vs phi, roll_rate, action_id, sight_m vs ssd_m with margin, deficit badge and trend, role, outcome, check ids), refreshed per cursor move, alongside three linked views, a legend, and lock toggles. No progressive disclosure, novice preset, or reading order is specified anywhere in 07 — the design specifies density, not comprehension. Worse for a teaching tool: when "the cursor crosses a check's evidence station" the HUD shows "the relevant doctrine check id" — a raw token like `out_in_out` — while the machinery that defines and narrates checks (`explain`, 08 §5.2: "given a check id ... its definition, arithmetic, and doctrine source") is CLI-only; the viewer has no explain surface, so the student who most needs the doctrine gets an identifier and the agent who least needs prose gets the narration. Relatedly, the book's danger-zone doctrine ("minimize the amount of time we spend leaned over in the danger zone, and the number of times we get into the danger zone") has vocabulary in 01 §4.1 but no instrument anywhere: no HUD readout, no check, no event marks danger-zone entry or dwell, despite phi being recorded per sample.
findings.evidence: design/07-viewer-animation-and-pov.md §3.3 (the six-group HUD table; "when the cursor crosses a check's evidence station — the relevant doctrine check id"); §6.1 (layout: three views + HUD + legend + scrubber, no modes). design/08-cli-and-agent-interface.md §5.2 (`explain` is a CLI verb; no viewer counterpart anywhere in 07). design/01-scope-and-doctrine.md §4.1: "doctrine minimizes time spent there and entries into it". book_text part0014: "we always want to minimize the amount of time we spend leaned over in the danger zone, and the number of times we get into the danger zone."
findings.improvement: Specify two HUD tiers in 07 §3.3 — a default 'ride' tier (speed, lean vs ceiling, sight vs stopping with badges, verdict) and an 'engineer' tier with the full table — and make check ids in the HUD tappable, surfacing the same JSON `explain(check_id)` already specifies for the CLI (one shared pure function; no new content). Add a danger-zone instrument: a per-corner `danger_dwell_s` and entry count in the verdict's corner measurements, a shaded high-lean band on the controls strip's phi channel, and a timeline tint while phi exceeds the reserve.

result.walkthrough: I simulated three users against the docs as written: an implementer building the verdict engine, an author reproducing the Chapter 8 figures, and a student at the viewer. (1) The implementer: starting from 01 §3's pointer (\"check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in 05\") I landed at 05 §6.2, which points straight back (\"The check *content* is doctrine and lives in 01\") and pins the id list as \"the carried line-selection checks\" plus two new ids. Grepping all of design/ finds exactly five check ids, all in passing; the twelve-check catalogue with arithmetic exists only in extract/05 §5.2, and 05 §6.2's own \"re-derived under Tier 1R and re-pinned\" language disqualifies the extract as a fallback for at least three checks. The colour of every line (06 §5.1: green requires \"no doctrine check failed\") and the mistake oracle (09 §4) both hang on this missing list; under the carried arithmetic slow_steer's oracle is unwritable because quick_steer only WARNs. (2) The author: recipe (e) in 08 reproduces fig 8.1 — but only because the design routes around its own naming: the book's \"Premature Initiation\" figure must be authored as `early_apex`, while the kind literally named `premature` yields an amber contained line the book paints red. I then authored the fig 8.4 two-strategy figure and checked the book image and caption: the book says \"you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed\", yet 01 §5 asserts the red double-apex companion \"renders red because its verdict is red\" — under 06 §5.1 red requires wide/runoff/crash, which a slowed double-apex line on that corner plausibly avoids, so the emergent colour is amber and G7 parity breaks; colours derived from emergent verdicts cannot be pinned to book ink, and the design never admits this. (3) The student: scrubbing `book90` (R 12) in the POV, the limit point sits ~29° off heading at 12 m of sight — at the edge of the ±30° frame — and beyond frame for anything deeper, while the camera (yaw = psi, head-turn \"out of scope\" in a 07 parenthetical never placarded in 01 §8) cannot look through the corner the way every page of Chapter 8 demands; the frame meanwhile rolls a full ~37° over a featureless two-tone world with no ego-fixed element in the draw order. The HUD offers ~18 readouts and raw check ids, with `explain` living only in the CLI. Finally I probed stateAt's `phase` field: its six values appear once in 05 §4 with no definitions, and 06 §4 derives a contradictory four-band partition from the same events, with `entry`/`mid`/`exit` also meaning station anchors in 03 — three vocabularies sharing words. Against the chapter text I collected prose claims linelab cannot demonstrate: reserve-spent-on-a-popup-hazard (no reactive mechanism; vehicle occluders block vision only), ground clearance as the cruiser's limit (only friction ceilings exist), and gaze causation (the book's stated root cause of all three mistakes) — none placarded in 01 §8.
wins: The rider-eye sight cast (D4, 03 §5.1) is exactly right pedagogically: it makes fig 8.1's sight-lines device ("your line of sight will offer a better angle to reveal things") measurable per line, where the prior centreline eye made hold-wide literally invisible to the model.

The blind-corner compare workflow (07 §4.3, 08 recipe c) — station-locked scrub of geometry-optimal vs visibility-governed lines with per-sample sight margins — is a genuinely better argument for the book's delayed-turn-point teaching than any static figure, and the design correctly identifies station-lock as the doctrinal comparison.

D7's emergent-line invariant structurally embodies the book's causal claim ("Creating the ideal line through a turn starts with the choice of a turning point"): no apex input anywhere, apex as measured output, enforced by property test P-EMERGENT-APEX rather than convention.

The premature/early_apex *distinction* (as opposed to its naming) is faithful to the book's own disjunction — "forces the line wide or requires a mid-corner steering correction" — and the design is honest that only a committed early lean produces the canonical run-wide.

The commanded-vs-delivered HUD row (05 §2.1 recorded controls, 07 §3.3) turns the Chapter 9 throttle-chop mechanism into one glance — command, ellipse-clipped delivery, widening line — closing the prior design's computed-and-dropped defect.

The POV sight band (07 §5.3 item 5) — tinting red "the road you would need to see to stop, and cannot" — is the most visceral single teaching device in the design, and paint-order occlusion (road painted, then hedge painted over it) is the correct minimal way to show a blind corner.

Colour law v2's core mechanics fix real prior defects: verdict-derived colour with role as an orthogonal dash channel closes the contained-linked-line-renders-red bug and the single-amber-slot cap, and the accessibility rule (colour never the sole carrier) is pinned rather than implied.

The honesty spine holds under simulation everywhere it is specified: mistake outcomes empirically pinned and never edited (09 §4's iron rule), shared figures as specs recomputed by every consumer (D6), typed refusals over plausible fakes (01 §8) — the drawing genuinely never lies to protect the lesson.

verdicts.title: The doctrine check catalogue does not exist anywhere in design/
verdicts.note: The nucleus survives: 01 §3 defers 'check ids and arithmetic' to 05; 05 §6.2 defers 'check *content*' back to 01 and pins the id list only as 'the carried line-selection checks' + 2 new ids without enumerating them; the re-derivation of the Tier-1R-touched checks ('re-derived under Tier 1R physics and re-pinned') exists in no design/ document; and the sight_vs_stopping vs stop_within_sight overlap is genuinely unaddressed. But the scope and 'blocker' severity are overstated on two grounds. (1) 00 §5 explicitly supplies a default: 'where a sibling document is silent, the prior design's choice is a reasonable default' — so catalogue membership and the arithmetic of the untouched ~9 checks are derivable from extract/05 §5.2 by the design's own rule; only the re-derived subset (trail-brake taper, single_input smoothness, chop-keyed checks) is truly unwritten, so 'the green/amber boundary of every figure is undefined' is too strong. (2) The claim that 'under the carried arithmetic slow_steer fails no check, so the oracle for at least one of six kinds cannot even be written' is false: slow_steer's pinned outcome is 'runoff' (01 §4.3, 03 §7.1), and a runoff line fails carried check #10 exit_containment ('PASS iff exit lane fraction f_exit < 1.0', extract/05 §5.2) — quick_steer being WARN-only does not leave the kind checkless, so the oracle is writable.

verdicts.title: Colour law v2's amber cannot be reconciled with the book's two-colour figures, and the fig 8.4 red-parity claim is unsupported
verdicts.note: What survives: (a) the amber conflation is real in the doc text — 06 §5.1 assigns amber both to 'a contained good line' and to 'a mistake-role line that happens to stay contained', while 04 §5 and 08 recipe (d) say the chain-aware verdict of a contained good chained line 'maps to green' — an unresolved internal inconsistency that itself proves the amber class is muddled; (b) no mechanism pins strategy-line colours: the 09 §4 oracle pins outcomes for the six mistake kinds only, so fig 8.4's companion rendering red is asserted (01 §3/§5) but never gated — for the two-strategy figures parity is indeed hoped, not designed. What is overstated: 'cannot be reconciled' — for figs 8.1–8.3/8.6 the mistake lines use kinds empirically pinned to wide/runoff (03 §7.1: 'outcome classes are empirically pinned, never asserted'), which designs red parity for most book figures. And the book-dispute framing is wrong: fig-08.04 itself paints the double-apex line red (verified in the image), so the design's red agrees with the book's art; the caption's 'you can take either path shown but at a significantly lower speed' describes a different speed regime for blind corners, not a colour dispute the design resolves against the book.

verdicts.title: The premature / early_apex naming inverts the book's vocabulary and is patched with prose instead of fixed
verdicts.note: All cited evidence checks out. The book's section title is 'Premature Initiation' and its fig 8.1 labels are 'premature turn point' (red) vs 'delayed turn point' (green); the book's causal sentence makes early apex the consequence: 'So an early turn point creates an early apex, which forces the line wide or requires a mid-corner steering correction.' linelab maps `early_apex` to that canonical figure and `premature` to a contained variant the book never names — the inverse mapping. 01 §4.3 ('The naming trap, resolved explicitly'), 03 §7.1, and 08 §5.1's teaching table all mandate re-explanation at every surface, which is documentation propping a naming choice rather than fixing it. The one-perturbation tension is also textually accurate: 03 §7 says 'exactly one control perturbed' while §7.1's early_apex row reads 'turn in early_by_m = 5 early **and** commit an explicit lean' — two changes. No doc justifies the names over alternatives; the design's schema-surface mitigation is acknowledged inside the finding itself and does not refute the inversion.

verdicts.title: The stateAt phase vocabulary is defined nowhere and contradicts 06's phase bands
verdicts.note: Verified across all ten docs: the six-value set 'approach|entry|steering|mid|exit|done' occurs exactly once (05 §4, marked only '(from events)') with no boundary definitions anywhere — not in 02's events, 06, 07, or 08. 06 §4 derives a four-band partition (approach brake_start→turn_in, steering, mid →roll_on, exit →exit) with no 'entry' and no 'done', so the two documents genuinely disagree. The triple-loading is real: entry/mid/exit are station anchors (03 §6.1, resolved to geometric points incl. the corner's s_mid), an event kind (`exit` in 05 §5's closed set), and phase spans — and the `mid` phase (steering_complete→roll_on) need not contain the `mid:<cornerId>` geometric middle. None of the listed implementer questions (phase before brake_start / brake-less plans, 'done' vs BAD_RANGE beyond termination per 05 §4, inter-corner phase when corner_id is null) is answered anywhere.

verdicts.title: The POV's fixed-heading camera loses the limit point off-frame on the book presets and silently cuts the book's central vision doctrine
verdicts.note: The geometry verifies: 07 §5.2 pins yaw = psi with fov_deg = 60 and declares 'target fixation and head-turn modelling are out of scope' only in that parenthetical; on book90 (R 12 per 03 §3.1) a limit point 12 m ahead along the arc subtends 57° of sweep, placing its chord bearing ~29° off heading — at the ±30° frame edge — with anything deeper off-screen, so the mid-corner opening cue (01 §6's doctrinal speed governor) is not depictable. 07 §5.3 item 7 specifies only 'the projected (limit_x, limit_y) drawn as a chevron' with no off-frame handling, in tension with G9's 'with the limit point marked'. The three book gaze quotes are verbatim in part0014, and 01 §8's refused-scope list (low-speed, body position, vertical geometry, Tier-3, HTML course) indeed omits gaze/head-turn — 'rider posture and body position' covers the body model, not vision behaviour. Caveat that does not overturn: fov_deg is TUNING, so a wider default could soften (not fix) the geometry; the sight band (§5.3 item 5) and HUD sight row convey sight_m but not the marked limit point G9 promises.

verdicts.title: Full-phi horizon roll on a featureless flat world will read as the world tilting, and is not what a rider's eyes see
verdicts.note: Factual substrate fully verified: 07 §5.2 rotates the completed frame by −phi and names the horizon tilt 'the POV's signature honesty'; 03 §3.1's presets (34 km/h on R 12) give phi = atan(v²/gR) ≈ 37°, over half the 60° FOV; the §5.3 draw order (sky/ground, road, markings, occluders, sight band, path, chevron, HUD strip) contains no cockpit, handlebar, or any ego-fixed vehicle element — the screen-fixed HUD strip is the only non-rotating item and is not an attitude reference. The head-level observation matches riding practice and no doc addresses head-roll stabilization (07 §5.2's out-of-scope note covers eye *position* via D5, not roll). The perceptual claim is an inference, but a well-grounded one, and the finding is correctly scoped as minor.

verdicts.title: Three of Chapter 8's load-bearing prose claims are undemonstrable, and none of the gaps is placarded
verdicts.note: What survives: (2) ground clearance is a fully confirmed gap — the only lean ceiling anywhere is phiMax = atan(mu) (02 §4, 05 §4), rider profiles carry only roll_rate/skill/t_react, no clearance field exists, and the book's cruiser claims are verbatim; (3) the gaze-causation limitation is real and explain's remediation (08 §5.2) is plan-centric; and all three are absent from 01 §8's out-of-scope list — factually verified. What is overstated: claim (1)'s 'can never show it being spent' ignores that 02 §7 defines the wide/runoff boundary as 'ran wide but a feasible add-lean corrective exists', with the corrective shot integrated under the run-wide slice — this directly operationalizes the quoted book sentence 'Using a slower corner entry speed will allow you to safely make a mid-corner steering correction'; and static gravel hazards (mu patches, 03 §4) let a reserve-rich vs reserve-spent line pair be witnessed. Also 'violating the design's own placard policy' mischaracterizes the policy: 01 §8's placard rule governs typed refusals to unmodellable *queries*, and scenarios these gaps would need (a popping hazard, a clearance field) are unexpressible and rejected typed per D8 — the policy is not violated in letter, though the pedagogy omission stands.

verdicts.title: The stepper/HUD is engineer-dense with no student tier, and doctrine explanation never reaches the viewer
verdicts.note: All components verify against the docs. 07 §3.3's six-group table enumerates ~18 simultaneous readouts; nothing in 07 (or 06/08) specifies progressive disclosure, a novice preset, or a reading order — §6.1's layout is a single workstation with three views + HUD + legend + scrubber. The HUD's Verdict row surfaces 'the relevant doctrine check id' as a raw token while `explain` — the only surface defining 'its definition, arithmetic, and doctrine source' — is a CLI verb/API function (08 §5.2) with no viewer counterpart anywhere in 07; the viewer's read-mostly stance (07 §6.3) restricts authoring, not explanation, so the omission is a gap, not a policy. The danger-zone point holds in design/: 01 §4.1 defines the vocabulary and the book's minimization rule is verbatim, but 05's pinned verdict corners block has no dwell/entries field, 05 §5's closed event set has no danger-zone kind, and no HUD row reads the danger band — the extract's dangerZone measurement cannot rescue this because 05 pins the verdict shape explicitly (not silent, so 00 §5's fallback does not apply).

result.walkthrough: I read all ten docs (00-README through 09-verification) in full, then simulated implementing each contract literally: authoring the 04 §7 example scene, running suggestTurnIn on the bookDecreasing preset, compiling each mistake kind against both pinned-outcome tables, tracing a runoff trajectory through 02's termination precedence into 06's renderer window, casting sight per 03 §5.1 and comparing units against ssd, composing the vis=cautious flags across scene/CLI/API spellings, and scripting a fig-8.4 two-strategy bake against 08's exit codes. I also greped the book text: the docs' figure mapping (8.1 premature, 8.2 slow steering, 8.3 fifty-pencing, 8.4 decreasing radius, 8.5 double apex) matches the committed chapter text, and extract/07-tooling-and-verification.md (referenced by 09) exists. Where it got hard: the scene grammar rejects its own worked example (two ride lines vs "exactly one ride line is required"); the mistake oracle has two different pinned-outcome tables to obey; the doctrine check suite is owned circularly (01 points at 05, 05 points at 01) with the id list never printed; a runoff line has no defined end; and sight_m (centreline arc metres) is compared against ssd_m (path metres) as if commensurable. Suspects 7, 10, and 12 were refuted (recorded as wins); suspect 6's "double-booked" framing was refuted but exposed a real 02-vs-05 retention contradiction.

findings.title: Scene ride-line cardinality contradicts itself
findings.claim: 04 §7 requires exactly one ride line per scene, yet the same section's worked example contains two ride lines, its role-default rule explicitly anticipates multiple ride lines, and the canonical vis-compare figure (04 §6) needs two ride lines in one figure. A literal implementation rejects the doc's own example scene and cannot author the blind-corner comparison figure the visibility mode 'exists for' as a single scene.
findings.evidence: 04 §7: mistake lines are "compiled against the figure's first `ride` line (exactly one `ride` line is required — the reference every mistake is measured against)"; the example directly above has both "good: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto" and "wide: ride entry=34 vis=cautious role=alternative"; role defaults read "first `ride` → `ideal`, subsequent `ride` → `alternative`"; 04 §9 carries "the one-`ride`-line scene rule"; 04 §6: "The canonical blind-corner figure is the comparison this mode exists for: the same corner ridden `vis=none` … against `vis=cautious`".
findings.improvement: Rewrite the parenthetical to "at least one ride line is required; the FIRST ride line is the reference every mistake is measured against", and delete "the one-ride-line scene rule" from 04 §9's carried list (or restate it as the first-ride-is-reference rule).

findings.title: Two conflicting mistake outcome-pin tables
findings.claim: The mistake oracle (09 §4) asserts the engine outcome 'matches the pinned table', but 01 §4.3 and 03 §7.1 pin different classes for three of six kinds: early_apex is wide/runoff in 01 but runoff alone in 03 (04 R2 also says runoff); slow_steer is wide/runoff in 01 but "runoff / roll-rate-limited" in 03 — and 'roll-rate-limited' is not an outcome class at all, it is diagnosis vocabulary (05 §6.1 roll_rate_limited); overspeed is "wide/runoff or crash" in 01 but bare runoff in 03. An implementer cannot write the oracle without choosing a table, and 09's iron rule forbids editing the pin later.
findings.evidence: 01 §4.3 table: early_apex → "`wide`/`runoff`", slow_steer → "`wide`/`runoff`", overspeed → "`wide`/`runoff` or `crash`". 03 §7.1 table: early_apex → "`runoff` (runs wide)", slow_steer → "`runoff` / roll-rate-limited", overspeed → "`runoff`". 09 §4: "asserts the declared check actually fails and the outcome class matches the pinned table"; "a mismatch is an engine, compiler, or doctrine bug — never fixed by editing the expectation." (premature→violation, chop and fifty_pence→wide/runoff agree across docs.)
findings.improvement: Declare 03 §7.1 the single normative pin table (it owns the compiler), make each cell a set of admissible classes ({wide, runoff} etc.), fix slow_steer's cell to legal outcome vocabulary, decide overspeed's crash admissibility once, and make 01 §4.3 cite 03 instead of duplicating.

findings.title: Doctrine check suite is circularly owned and never enumerated
findings.claim: The check ids and arithmetic — the substance of Axis B and of the verdict deliverable — are specified nowhere: 01 delegates them to 05 and 05 delegates them back to 01, pinning only the two new visibility ids. Scattered references name late_apex, out_in_out, single_input, plus a taper/trail-brake check and a smoothness bar, but no doc lists the "carried 12-check" set, and 05 admits several checks' arithmetic is "re-derived under Tier 1R" without stating the new arithmetic. The 00 §5 fallback to extract/ cannot cover checks_version 2 changes.
findings.evidence: 01 §3: "check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in `05-result-contract-and-inspection.md`". 05 §6.2: "The check content is doctrine and lives in `01-scope-and-doctrine.md`; this document pins the record shape and the id list" — then lists only "the carried line-selection checks + stop_within_sight + hold_wide_for_sight". 05 §6.2 also: "Checks whose arithmetic the run-wide slice touches … are re-derived under Tier 1R physics and re-pinned; the check *ids* are stable" — with no derivation given. Ids used but never enumerated: 01 §4.3 "fails `late_apex`, `out_in_out`", "always fails `single_input`"; 08 §5.2 "`late_brake` at s=141" (late_brake is elsewhere a diagnosis cause, 05 §6.1).
findings.improvement: Add the full checks_version-2 id list with one-line arithmetic per check to 05 §6.2 (or a dedicated section in 01), including the Tier-1R re-derived forms, and disambiguate late_brake (check id vs diagnosis cause).

findings.title: Runoff trajectories have no defined end and no termination cause
findings.claim: 02 §7's termination precedence (crash → stopped → road/corner end → runaway guards) contains no lateral off-road departure cause, so a runoff line that leaves the road sideways keeps integrating on grass — with undefined muAt(s,d) off-road, undefined station projection, and events like run_wide_detect but no off_road/road_exit event — until it happens to hit a runaway guard (120 s / 5000 m) or the longitudinal road end. Where the drawn line ends is therefore unspecified, 05's terminated:{reason,…} field has no pinned reason vocabulary, and 06 §2.4's default window (window.to = exit + WINDOW_TAIL_M) references an exit event a runoff mistake line never emits.
findings.evidence: 02 §7: "Termination precedence per step: crash → stopped (`v < v_floor_ms`) → road/corner end → runaway guards." 05 §2: "terminated: {reason, s, t}" — reason never enumerated. 05 §5 event kinds close with "crash, stop, road_end" — no off-road event. 06 §2.4: "window.to = exit + WINDOW_TAIL_M" with no rule for lines lacking an exit; 06 §2.2 applies "d′ = d × width_exag" to "every trajectory's d", so an off-road excursion is drawn 3.5× further off the exaggerated road with no clipping rule. 01 §4.3 promises runoff mistake figures (fig 8.2/8.3 mappings) whose drawn extent this leaves to the implementer.
findings.improvement: Add an off-road termination rule to 02 §7 (e.g. terminate N metres of lateral departure past the corridor, emitting an `off_road` event), pin the terminated.reason closed set in 05 §2, and define 06 §2.4's window fallback for lines without an exit event (e.g. the reference line's exit, else termination station).

findings.title: Sight distance and stopping distance are measured in different metrics
findings.claim: sight_m is arc distance along the road centreline (03 §5.1) while ssd_m is braking distance along the bike's own path (03 §5.2), yet every safety judgment compares them directly. On the book presets (R12, lane 3.5) a rider's path length per centreline station differs by up to ~15%, so the per-sample margin, the stop_within_sight check, and the V1 governor all carry a systematic units mismatch — optimistic for inside lines, conservative for outside ones. Separately, targets on the road centreline of a two-lane road (the paint line, not the rider's lane) sit farther from an inside occluder than the rider's own lane does, overstating how much of the rider's usable corridor is actually visible — in tension with the lane-constrained doctrine (01 §4.2, 03 §2).
findings.evidence: 03 §5.1: "Targets = road centreline stations … `sight_m = s_limit − s_eye` (arc distance)"; 03 §5.2: "ssd(v_ms, model) … v·t_react + v²/(2·a_ssd)" and "The per-point safety judgment is the comparison `sight_m ≥ ssd_m`"; 01 §6: "the two channels are never conflated" — but their units are. 03 §2: "the usable corridor is the rider's own lane"; 03 §5.1 keeps targets on the road centreline for cross-line comparability.
findings.improvement: Define both quantities in one metric: either scale ssd into centreline-station metres at the rider's current offset (factor 1/(1−d·kappa)), or measure sight as path distance to the blocked station; and state explicitly (with a placard-style note) that centreline targets trade lane fidelity for cross-line comparability.

findings.title: suggestTurnIn's 58% target fights the decreasing-radius 60% bar
findings.claim: suggestTurnIn ranks candidates by |apex_pct − 58| and full-solves only the top 4, returning "the first that verifies clean", while 01 §5 moves the late-apex bar past 60% on decreasing-radius corners. No doc says the target adapts per corner type, so on bookDecreasing the ranking prefers candidates that fail the very check verification applies, and the typed failure blames "solver brackets or profile" — a misleading diagnosis when the fixed target constant is the cause. The C30-DR golden pins the check-side bar but nothing pins solver-side adaptation.
findings.evidence: 04 §3: "Rank the surviving band by `|apex_pct − 58|` (`target_apex_pct = 58`, TUNING — the doctrinal late apex) … Full-solve the top 4 … return the first that verifies clean", failure mode "*non-clean band* (candidates exist but none verifies — solver brackets or profile are the problem)". 01 §5: "the late-apex bar moves later (apex past 60 % of swept angle rather than 50 %)". 02 §8: "A decreasing-radius taper twin (`C30-DR` …) pins the special-case late bar" — a golden, not a solver rule. No adaptation clause exists in 04.
findings.improvement: Make target_apex_pct corner-type-aware in 04 §3 (e.g. 58 on constant-radius, 65 on decreasing-radius tapers, na on increasing), or rank by distance-above-the-applicable-bar; extend the typed failure to name the target constant as a possible cause.

findings.title: Exit-3 semantics break intended-failure figures and scene scripting
findings.claim: 08 pins exit 3 for "a non-clean solve" with no carve-out for lines that are designed to fail, while 04 §4.2 says a non-clean self-verification "is reported as such (and still renders)". The fig 8.4 book-parity figure requires a legitimately-failing alternative strategy (01 §3/§5) produced by solveDoubleApex — so recreating a promised G7 deliverable via `solve` exits nonzero, and the `scene` verb's exit code is never specified at all, leaving an agent unable to script "bake this teaching figure containing an intended red line" and distinguish success from failure. The schema's expect_fail mechanism (03 §6) exists precisely for declared legitimate failures but is never wired to exit codes.
findings.evidence: 08 §3.1: exit 3 = "`run --gate` with a failed doctrine check, a non-clean `solve`". 04 §4.2: "A non-clean self-verification is reported as such (and still renders, so the author can see why)". 01 §3: "a *legitimately failing* second strategy (fig 8.4's double-apex companion) renders red because its verdict is red". 08 §3 `scene` row specifies no exit semantics. 03 §6: "`expect_fail` declares doctrine checks a *legitimate* non-clean line is expected to fail" — absent from 08 §3.1.
findings.improvement: State in 08 §3.1 that exit 3 applies only when the non-clean result is undeclared: a line whose failures are fully covered by expect_fail (or role=mistake/alternative lines in a scene bake) exits 0; specify `scene`'s exit tiers explicitly.

findings.title: Chained lines are promised green but the colour formula yields amber
findings.claim: 04 §5 declares a linked line "contained, not clean" and says its chain-aware verdict "maps to green", but 06 §5.1's normative quality formula gives amber for outcome=violation and green only for outcome=clean with no failed checks — there is no chain-aware carve-out. Worse, the formula's second branch ("outcome = clean with failed checks") is vacuous, since 02 §7 defines clean as "all checks pass", showing the outcome/check relationship is not agreed between docs. As written, the prior 'correct linked line renders wrong colour' defect that D9 exists to fix is reintroduced, one class softer (red→amber).
findings.evidence: 04 §5: "A linked line is **contained, not clean** … Under colour law v2 (D9) that chain-aware verdict maps to **green**". 06 §5.1: "good if outcome = clean and no doctrine check failed | contained if outcome = violation, or outcome = clean with failed checks". 02 §7: "`clean` — all checks pass." 01 §5: "a contained, flowing chained line renders by its own verdict; the prior 'lone linked line renders red' defect is structurally gone" — untrue under 06's formula.
findings.improvement: Define in 05/06 how the chain-aware check set feeds outcome: either a chained line that passes its chain-aware bar gets outcome=clean (making 06's formula work unchanged), or 06 §5.1 gains an explicit chain-verdict input; delete or justify the vacuous clean-with-failed-checks branch.

findings.title: P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN contradicts the trail-braking invariant
findings.claim: 09's property test asserts any "chop or brake applied at lean produces a line at or wider than the unperturbed line … never tighter", while 02's behavioural invariant 1 requires that gentle braking at lean (below A_SU_ONSET = 2.5 m/s²) is bit-identical to the point-mass and "still *tightens* the line" — the representability of trail braking is itself a design requirement (C30-trailbrake golden). Under tests-before-code (09 §8) the property test as written is guaranteed to fail against the physics spec as written for any sub-threshold brake.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.4: "`P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN` — a `chop` or brake applied at lean produces a line at or wider than the unperturbed line from the perturbation station on; never tighter." 02 §5.4.1: "light trail braking (taper ≤ ~2.5 m/s²) still *tightens* the line — the advanced technique remains representable". 02 §8: "`C30-trailbrake` (2.0 m/s² taper carried past turn-in → still tightens…)".
findings.improvement: Qualify P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN to sustained decel ≥ a_noreturn (or ≥ A_SU_ONSET with a widening-vs-point-mass baseline comparison rather than vs the unperturbed line), matching 02 §5.4 invariants 1–2 exactly.

findings.title: Occluder ref grammar: bare c1 vs anchor grammar vs 08's third shape
findings.claim: The placement grammar defines the station anchor as entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset or at_s, yet every occluder example in 03 and 04 — including the bookBlind preset — uses a bare corner id (`c1`) as <ref>, which the anchor grammar does not admit and whose meaning (entry? mid? s0?) is nowhere defined. 08's recipe (c) then uses a third shape, `hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30`, where a station offset appears both inside the ref and in the <offset>x<span> token, making <offset>'s meaning ambiguous (station offset? lateral margin?). The token grammar is unimplementable without guessing, on the surface (occluders) blind-corner authoring depends on.
findings.evidence: 03 §4: "a station anchor (corner-relative `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`, or absolute `at_s`) … Scene token form carried: `<kind> <side> <ref> <offset>x<span> [key=val …]`, e.g. `hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2 depth=2.5`" — the example violates its own anchor set. 03 §3.1 bookBlind: "`book90` geometry + `hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2 depth=2.5`". 04 §7: "occluders: hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2". 08 §6(c): "--occluder \"hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30\"".
findings.improvement: Pin the token grammar once in 03 §4: define bare `<cornerId>` as sugar for a stated anchor (e.g. entry:<id>), state that <offset> is the station offset from the ref and <span> the length, and correct 08's recipe (c) to a token the grammar actually parses.

findings.title: Stop-within-sight uses a braking model the tool's own physics forbids at lean
findings.claim: The V1 governor applies vis_margin·ssd(v) ≤ sight_m "at every station", with the default alert model assuming 7.0 m/s² braking — but 02 §5.3 establishes that braking beyond a_noreturn ≈ 5.4 m/s² at lean forces a stand-up and runs the bike wide, and the corrective-solver rule says such saves are "infeasible by construction". So mid-corner the tool judges safety by a stop it simultaneously models as a forced run-off; the HUD's central teaching line ("you can see 38 m but need 51 m to stop") quietly assumes an upright-only decel. No doc reconciles or placards this, despite the placard policy demanding honest refusal over plausible fakes.
findings.evidence: 04 §6: "V1 — stop-within-sight speed governor. At every station, speed must satisfy `vis_margin · ssd(v) ≤ sight_m`". 03 §5.2: "alert {a_ssd: 7.0 m/s², t_react_s: 1.0}" (default). 02 §5.3: "a_noreturn ≈ 2.5 + 0.873/0.30 ≈ 5.4 m/s². Braking harder than that while leaned *forces* the stand-up"; 02 §5.6: "a 'save' that requires braking past `a_noreturn` at lean is infeasible by construction." 01 §8: "A wrong-but-plausible picture a student could believe is strictly worse than an honest 'not modelled.'"
findings.improvement: Either make ssd lean-aware (use aLongAvail/a_noreturn at the sample's lean, which strengthens the blind-corner caution teaching), or add an explicit stated limitation in 03 §5.2 that ssd models assume an upright bike and why that is the accepted engineering yardstick.

findings.title: 02 retains both sample series; 05's contract has no home for the raw one
findings.claim: Suspect 6's 'double-booked' framing is refuted — the final exact sample and the terminal event's exact crossing are complementary, not contradictory — but the audit surfaced a real retention contradiction: 02 §6 mandates that both the raw 200 Hz series and the arc-grid series are retained, while 05 §2 collapses the record to "one flat array" (the arc grid) and offers only an optional time-uniform export series that is default-unset and is not the raw series. The Trajectory type has no field where the raw series could live, so a literal implementation cannot satisfy 02.
findings.evidence: 02 §6: "The raw 200 Hz series is resampled onto a fixed grid `ds_m = 0.5 m` … Both series are retained; the time-base and sample contract are owned by `05-…`." 05 §2: "`samples` is one flat array … there is one array, it is the channel set"; 05 §3.1: "An optional time-uniform series (`record_dt_s`, default unset — TUNING) may additionally be retained for export convenience, but no consumer may require it". 05 §2's Trajectory = {samples, events, terminated} — no raw-series member.
findings.improvement: Amend 02 §6 to "the raw series is an integrator-internal working set; only the arc-grid samples (plus exact event crossings) are retained", or add an explicit optional raw-series member to 05 §2 — one of the two docs must yield.

findings.title: sightFrom's signature cannot produce the trend it promises
