findings.claim: 03 §5.1 puts `trend` in sightFrom's return value and defines it as the change in sight_m "against the previous sample", but the function's inputs are (road, eye, occluders) — a single stateless eye with no history — and 09's P-SIGHT-EYE pins it as "a pure function of (road, eye, occluders)". Meanwhile 05 defines trend differently ("the sign of d(sight_m)/ds", derived by stateAt, not stored). The two definitions also disagree on the deadband's meaning: 2.0 m of change per 0.5 m sample implies a slope threshold of 4, which cannot be what is intended.
findings.evidence: 03 §5.1: "sightFrom(road, eye, occluders) → {sight_m, limit_point: {x, y}, s_limit, trend}" and "`trend` … from the change in `sight_m` against the previous sample with deadband `sight_trend_deadband_m = 2.0`". 09 §3.4: "`P-SIGHT-EYE` — `sightFrom` is a pure function of (road, eye, occluders)". 05 §2.1: "the limit-point *trend* (opening/closing, the sign of `d(sight_m)/ds`) are derived values, computed by `stateAt` (§4), not stored"; 05 §4 claims it uses "03 §5.1's definition … verbatim".
findings.improvement: Remove trend from sightFrom's return (it belongs to the per-sample analyzer/stateAt), and define the deadband once as a windowed Δsight over a stated station distance.

findings.title: Flag/field/scene spellings are mapped but not one-to-one as claimed
findings.claim: Suspect 9 partially confirmed: the vis surface is discoverable (04 §6 routes spellings to §7 and 08, and `schema cli` prints the mapping), but 08's claim that "Flags mirror schema fields one-to-one" is false as stated — `--visibility-governed` is a boolean renaming of the enum field `vis: none|cautious` (not a mirror), and entry speed has four spellings across surfaces (wire `rider.start.speed_kmh`, solve-spec `entry_kmh`, scene `entry=`, CLI `--entry`) with no printed equivalence table promised outside the cli section.
findings.evidence: 08 §4.1: "Flags mirror schema fields one-to-one; the mapping is itself a printed schema section (`schema cli`)" and "`--visibility-governed` with its knob flags `--vis-hold <f>` and `--vis-margin <×>`". 04 §7: "vis=none|cautious … visHold=<f> / visMargin=<×>"; 04 §6 fields "`vis_hold_f`, `vis_margin`"; 04 §8 R3 API: "solve({road, entry_kmh: 32, vis: \"cautious\"})"; 03 §6: "rider: { …, start: {speed_kmh, …} }".
findings.improvement: Either add `--vis <none|cautious>` as the mirroring flag (keeping --visibility-governed as sugar) or soften 08 §4.1's claim to "every schema field is reachable by exactly one documented flag"; add the cross-surface spelling table (schema-field ↔ scene-key ↔ flag) to the `schema cli` content spec.

findings.title: Jump-point sources: 09 adds 'plan stations' that 05/07 exclude
findings.claim: Suspect 7 is refuted at the names level — 07 §3.1's tick list maps cleanly onto 05 §5's closed Event kinds and even explicitly reconciles the run-off ambiguity — but 09's contract test asserts jump targets are "exactly the result's events and plan stations", while 05 and 07 define bookmarks as events only. Plan stations (e.g. a position action's at_s) are not events unless emitted as position_start etc., so the three docs disagree on the test's expected set.
findings.evidence: 05 §5: "The stepper's named jump targets … are exactly `events` filtered by `kind`". 07 §3.1: "These are free — the engine already emits them" (list of event ticks only). 09 §6: "`C-BOOKMARKS` — the stepper's named jump targets are exactly the result's events and plan stations".
findings.improvement: Drop "and plan stations" from C-BOOKMARKS, or add plan-station ticks to 07 §3.1 and note that action starts already surface as events (brake_start, turn_in, position_start…).

findings.title: Dangling schema fields: config.mode, required checks_version, missing hazards section
findings.claim: The scenario schema carries `mode` with default 'street' but no doc enumerates its values or effect — under the design's own D8 rule ("every field validate accepts must provably reach the controller or the analyzers") an unspecified-but-accepted field is exactly the forbidden class. `checks_version` is written without the optional `?` (hence required) yet the zero-file path promises "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag" and provides none for it. And 08's closed schema-section list has `occluders` but no `hazards`, though 03 §4 defines hazards as a distinct family.
findings.evidence: 03 §6: "config: { mu?, mode?, ds_m?, ssd_model?, checks_version }" and field note "`mode` (`street`)" — no vocabulary anywhere. 03 §6.1/D8: "every field `validate` accepts must provably reach the controller or the analyzers". 08 §4: "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag"; 08 §4.1 flag list lacks any checks-version or mode flag. 08 §5.1: "Sections (closed list…): `scenario`, `plan`, `road-dsl`, `occluders`, `mistakes`, `solve`, `scene`, `view`, `envelope`, `cli`".
findings.improvement: Enumerate config.mode's values and consumer (or delete it), mark checks_version optional-with-default (or add its flag), and either fold hazards into the occluders section by name ("placements") or add a `hazards` section to the closed list.

findings.title: Double-apex inter-touch drift: two different mechanisms claimed
findings.claim: 02 attributes the drift between the two apex touches to plain roll-on widening — listing "the double-apex inter-touch drift" as a causal consequence of the point-mass identity — and 01 §5 agrees ("the drift back to the outside between touches emerges from roll-on widening the arc"). But 04 §4.4 credits Tier 1R's stand-up slice: "the mid-corner stand-up drift between touches — previously impossible for the point-mass — becomes representable". These cannot both be the design of record: either the point-mass could always produce the drift (making 04's claim false) or it could not (making 02/01's causal story false), and solveDoubleApex's shrinking expect_fail declarations hinge on which.
findings.evidence: 02 §2: "rolling on widens … the mechanism behind late-apex exit drift, the double-apex inter-touch drift". 01 §5: "the drift back to the outside between touches emerges from roll-on widening the arc". 04 §4.4: "under Tier 1R the mid-corner stand-up drift between touches — previously impossible for the point-mass — becomes representable, and the solver's `expect_fail` declarations shrink accordingly".
findings.improvement: Reconcile in 04 §4.4: state that roll-on widening always provided the drift (per 02) and that Tier 1R adds only the roll-off/stand-up variant of the transition, then re-justify (or delete) the expect_fail-shrinkage claim.

findings.title: P-SIGHT-EYE is false under fuzzing with outside occluders
findings.claim: The property "moving the eye laterally toward the outside of a blind corner never shortens sight_m" is only a theorem for inside occluders; 09 runs properties "against fuzzed schema-valid scenarios", and the occluder vocabulary allows outside placements (side ∈ inside|outside|left|right) such as a vehicle parked on the outside edge, where moving the eye outward can tuck the road behind the obstruction and shorten sight. A test written from the spec fails on legitimate fuzzed geometry.
findings.evidence: 09 §3.4: "`P-SIGHT-EYE` — … moving the eye laterally toward the outside of a blind corner never *shortens* `sight_m`" and preamble "Run against fuzzed schema-valid scenarios as well as the fixtures." 03 §4: "`side` ∈ `inside | outside | left | right`" with `vehicle` as "discrete rectangle (parked or oncoming-lane vehicle)".
findings.improvement: Scope the property to scenarios whose occluders are all on the corner's inside (the doctrine's premise), or restate it as: with only inside occluders, sight_m is monotone non-decreasing in outward eye offset.

findings.title: 08 announces five recipes, delivers six
findings.claim: 08's preamble says the document specifies "five canonical agent recipes" while its own contents list says "Six agent recipes" and §6 contains six ((a) through (f)); 04 §8 also has six (R1–R6). A trivial count rot from adding the constraint recipe (D10) without updating the intro.
findings.evidence: 08 intro: "schema discoverability, and five canonical agent recipes". 08 §1: "5. Six agent recipes, end to end." 08 §6: "Six canonical end-to-end sequences" with items (a)–(f).
findings.improvement: Change "five" to "six" in 08's preamble.

findings.title: window:"all" is used but absent from the ViewSpec grammar
findings.claim: 06 §2.4 offers `window: "all"` as the always-reachable honest full-extent view, but the ViewSpec type in 06 §2.1 admits only `window?: {from: StationRef, to: StationRef}` — the string variant is not in the grammar, so the promised escape hatch is unexpressible as typed.
findings.evidence: 06 §2.1: "window?: {from: StationRef, to: StationRef}". 06 §2.4: "The full-extent view is one flag away (`mode: \"true\"` or `window: \"all\"`)".
findings.improvement: Extend ViewSpec to `window?: {from, to} | "all"`.

findings.title: Phase vocabulary: 'entry' and 'done' have no defining boundaries
findings.claim: stateAt's derived.phase closed set is approach|entry|steering|mid|exit|done, but the only phase-boundary definitions anywhere are 06 §4's four bands (approach, steering, mid, exit) derived from events — no doc says which events delimit 'entry' or 'done', so the two extra values are unimplementable without guessing, on a field agents will read.
findings.evidence: 05 §4: "phase — \"approach\"|\"entry\"|\"steering\"|\"mid\"|\"exit\"|\"done\" (from events)". 06 §4: "Corner-phase bands: … approach (`brake_start→turn_in`), steering (`turn_in→steering_complete`), mid (`→roll_on`), exit (`→exit`)" — four bands, no 'entry', no 'done'.
findings.improvement: Pin the event-to-phase mapping for all six values in 05 §4 (e.g. entry = brake_end→turn_in, done = after the exit event/termination), and align 06 §4's band list with it.

findings.title: 08's importable API omits functions other docs require
findings.claim: The programmatic import list in 08 §7.1 lacks suggestTurnIn, sightFrom, and chainedSolve, though 00 §4 names suggestTurnIn and sightFrom as key API names, 07 §2.4 requires the viewer to call sightFrom as a pure core function, and 04 §5 specifies chainedSolve as a distinct entry point. Relatedly, 07 §2.4's allowance for the viewer to call sightFrom sits in unacknowledged tension with 05 §1's rule that "nothing downstream ever re-derives state the engine already had" (sight is recorded per sample).
findings.evidence: 08 §7.1: "import { run, solve, compileMistake, compare, sweep, validate, renderViews, explain, stateAt } from \"linelab\"". 00 §4: "Key API names: `stateAt(…)`, `sightFrom(road, eye, occluders)`, `solve`, `suggestTurnIn`, `compileMistake`." 07 §2.4: "the return value of a pure core function (`stateAt`, `sightFrom`, …)". 05 §1: "nothing downstream ever re-derives state the engine already had."
findings.improvement: Complete 08 §7.1's export list, and state when the viewer may legitimately call sightFrom (e.g. for hypothetical eyes not on any line) versus must read the recorded per-sample sight.

findings.title: Suspect 10 adjudicated: 00's core-sample list is a declared minimum, not a mismatch
findings.claim: Refuted as a contradiction: 00 §4 frames its per-sample field list as the "canonical minimum, detailed in 05", so 05 §2.1's three extra commanded-control fields (clipped, n_long, n_lat) are an elaboration, not a conflict. Worth one line of polish: since the CSV pins those three in its column order, adding them to 00's list would prevent an agent primed on 00 from being surprised by the wire format.
findings.evidence: 00 §4: "Core per-sample fields (canonical minimum, detailed in 05): `s, t, … f` plus commanded controls (`cmd_lean`, `cmd_a`, `roll_rate`, `action_id`) plus sight (…)". 05 §2.1 adds "`clipped`, `n_long`, `n_lat`"; 05 §8.2 pins them in the Trace CSV column order.
findings.improvement: Append clipped, n_long, n_lat to 00 §4's commanded-controls parenthetical.

findings.title: Tolerance-table location: 02 points at 09, 09 points at the fixtures
findings.claim: 02 §8 says "the single tolerance table lives in `09-verification-and-testing.md` §3 and owns the ± values", but 09 §3.2 says the tolerances are TUNING and "the tolerance table lives beside the fixtures, in one place" — i.e. in the repo, not in 09. A reimplementer following 02's pointer finds only example values in 09.
findings.evidence: 02 §8: "the single tolerance table lives in `09-verification-and-testing.md` §3 and owns the ± values". 09 §3.2: "(positions ±0.01 m, angles ±0.01°, speeds ±0.01 m/s — TUNING; the tolerance table lives beside the fixtures, in one place)".
findings.improvement: Make 02 §8 point to "the blessed tolerance table beside the fixtures (per 09 §3.2)" so both docs name the same home.

wins: Suspect 7 refuted with credit: 07 §3.1's jump-point names map cleanly onto 05 §5's closed Event kinds, and 07 explicitly self-audits the one trap ("'run-off' is an *outcome* class, not an event") — cross-doc vocabulary discipline actually working.

Suspect 12 refuted: the role closed set ideal|alternative|mistake|reference is verbatim-identical across 00 §4, 01 §3, 03 §8, 04 §7 (role defaults), 05 §7, and 06 §5.2, and the scene-kind-to-role mapping (naive/plan → reference) matches 04 §4.4's solver roles.

The D10 constraint vocabulary is airtight across docs: 00 §4's closed bound set {f_min, f_max, v_max_kmh, sight_margin_min_m} maps one-to-one onto 04 §4.5's compact token grammar, with the two illegal op/field combinations (v_kmh>=, sight_margin_m<=) explicitly rejected SCHEMA — a closed set that stays closed at every surface.

Internal arithmetic checks out everywhere it is stated twice: lean_frac 0.70 × phiReserve 40.36° ≈ 28° (04 §4.1 vs 02 §4); a_noreturn ≈ 2.5 + 0.873/0.30 ≈ 5.4 m/s² (02 §5.3); C30 arc length ≈ 47 m for R30 ^90 (02 §8); book90's 7 m road on R12 gives 0.58, inside the 0.55–0.9 band with its 12 m entry under one arc length (03 §3.1 vs 06 §1); 07 §2.1's 3–4×10³ RK4 steps matches a ~250 m scenario at 200 Hz.

The Trace CSV's pinned column order (05 §8.2) reproduces the Sample contract's declaration order exactly, field for field, including the commanded-controls block — the append-only promise is checkable by eye.

The dual t_react collision is explicitly defused rather than left as a trap: 02 §3 states the rider profile's t_react_s serves run-wide correction while ssd models "carry their own `t_react_s` per model" — a place a lesser spec would have quietly conflated the two.

The D8 vis-knob story is told identically three times: 04 §6, 08 §4.1, and 09 §3.5 all specify the same rejection (INEFFECTUAL, vis_knob_without_vis_mode) for knobs without vis=cautious, and 09 adds the positive effectuality test — a genuinely closed loop from schema to CLI to test.

The book-figure mapping survives contact with the committed book text: chapter 8's actual figure numbering (8.1 premature turn point, 8.2 slow steering, 8.3 fifty-pencing, 8.4 decreasing radius, 8.5 double apex) matches every mapping cell in 01 §4.3 and 03 §7.1, and the book's own double-apex text ("will require at least one mid-turn correction") matches 01 §5's doctrine.

The super-tight refusal predicate (sweep ≥ 170° AND r ≤ 15 m) is quoted identically in 01 §8, 02 §7, and 03 §3.1 — and 03 §3.1's bookHairpin footnote checks its own preset against it (R10 ^150 clears the AND).

stateAt's no-silent-clamp rule (05 §4) and the viewer's freeze-at-terminal behaviour (07 §3.4) divide responsibility exactly as 05 declares ("clamping is a caller (viewer) policy") — the two docs meet at the seam without overlap or gap.
09 §9's citation of extract/07-tooling-and-verification.md and extract/08-design-decisions-and-rationale.md resolves — the referenced prior-design files exist in the repo.

The naming-trap resolution (premature vs early_apex) is consistently propagated to every surface that could mislead an agent: 01 §4.3's explicit resolution, 03 §7.1's compiler note, 08 §5.1's schema teaching-table requirement, and 08 recipe (e)'s inline warning all tell the same story.

verdicts.title: Scene ride-line cardinality contradicts itself
verdicts.note: 04 §7 states mistakes are "compiled against the figure's first `ride` line (exactly one `ride` line is required)" while the example block directly above contains two ride lines ("good: ride entry=34 turnIn=auto" and "wide: ride entry=34 vis=cautious role=alternative") and the role-default rule "first `ride` → `ideal`, subsequent `ride` → `alternative`" anticipates multiples; 04 §9 additionally carries "the one-`ride`-line scene rule". No other doc resolves it — 03 §8's Figure object allows N ride-specs with no cap, deepening the surface inconsistency, and 04 §6's canonical vis=none vs vis=cautious comparison needs two ride lines in one figure. The contradiction is internal to §7 itself.

verdicts.title: Two conflicting mistake outcome-pin tables
verdicts.note: The discrepancies are real: 01 §4.3 gives early_apex "`wide`/`runoff`", slow_steer "`wide`/`runoff`", overspeed "`wide`/`runoff` or `crash`", while 03 §7.1 pins "`runoff` (runs wide)", "`runoff` / roll-rate-limited", and bare "`runoff`"; and "roll-rate-limited" is indeed diagnosis vocabulary (05 §6.1 `roll_rate_limited`), not an outcome class. But the half claiming "an implementer cannot write the oracle without choosing a table" is overstated: 04 §4.3 explicitly designates "the mistake outcome pins in `03-…md` §7.1", and 03 §7.1 self-describes its column as "the outcome class each kind is **pinned to by test**" — the doc set does name the pin table. Surviving nucleus: 01's doctrine table has drifted from 03's pins (a crash overspeed outcome passes 01 but fails 03's pin) and 03's slow_steer cell is malformed as a pin.

verdicts.title: Doctrine check suite is circularly owned and never enumerated
verdicts.note: The circle is verbatim: 01 §3 "check ids and arithmetic live with the verdict contract in `05-result-contract-and-inspection.md`"; 05 §6.2 "The check content is doctrine and lives in `01-scope-and-doctrine.md`; this document pins the record shape and the id list" — and the pinned "id list" is only "the carried line-selection checks + stop_within_sight + hold_wide_for_sight", never enumerated. 05 §6.2 further admits touched checks are "re-derived under Tier 1R physics and re-pinned" with no derivation anywhere in the set, so the 00 §5 extract/ fallback cannot supply checks_version 2 arithmetic. I searched all ten docs: only scattered ids (late_apex, out_in_out, single_input in 01 §4.3/§5) exist; no doc lists the carried set. Sole weak evidence point: 08 §5.2's "`late_brake` at s=141" appears in remediation hints "phrased against the closed vocabularies", so it is plausibly the diagnosis cause, not a check id — but this does not dent the core claim.

verdicts.title: Runoff trajectories have no defined end and no termination cause
verdicts.note: 02 §7's precedence — "crash → stopped (`v < v_floor_ms`) → road/corner end → runaway guards" — contains no lateral-departure cause; 05 §2's `terminated: {reason, s, t}` never enumerates `reason`; 05 §5's closed event kinds end "crash, stop, road_end" with `run_wide_detect` but no off-road/road-exit event; muAt(s,d) off-road is nowhere defined (03 §4 defines only on-road hazard patches). 07 §3.4 even assumes runoff lines "end early" ("crash, road-end/run-off, stop") without any doc supplying the mechanism, confirming the gap rather than closing it. Minor mitigation only: 06 §2.4's window is per-figure, so a good line's exit event usually anchors it — but the doc indeed gives no rule when no line emits exit, and no clipping rule exists for the ×width_exag off-road excursion.

verdicts.title: Sight distance and stopping distance are measured in different metrics
verdicts.note: 03 §5.1: "`sight_m = s_limit − s_eye` (arc distance)" with "Targets = road centreline stations"; 03 §5.2: ssd is the physical braking distance `v·t_react + v²/(2·a_ssd)`; the judgment is the raw comparison "`sight_m ≥ ssd_m`". No doc anywhere reconciles path-metres against centreline-metres — at bookBlind's R12/lane-3.5 geometry the ratio of rider-path length to centreline arc spans roughly 0.75–1.25, so ~15% is if anything conservative, optimistic on inside lines exactly as claimed. The centreline-target choice is deliberate (03 §5.1, comparability rationale) but the ssd-metric mismatch and the paint-line-vs-own-lane occluder standoff are never acknowledged, despite 01 §8's placard policy ("A wrong-but-plausible picture … is strictly worse than an honest 'not modelled.'") and 03 §2's lane-constrained corridor.

verdicts.title: suggestTurnIn's 58% target fights the decreasing-radius 60% bar
verdicts.note: 04 §3 ranks by "|apex_pct − 58|" and full-solves only the top 4, returning "the first that verifies clean"; 01 §5 moves the decreasing-radius late-apex bar "past 60 % of swept angle rather than 50 %". I searched 04 (including §4.3/§4.4 Tier-1R adjustments and §4.5 constraints), 02 §8, and 09 for any per-corner-type adaptation of `target_apex_pct` — none exists; C30-DR (02 §8) pins only the check-side bar. The failure taxonomy's diagnosis text ("non-clean band … solver brackets or profile are the problem") would indeed misattribute the fixed-constant cause on bookDecreasing. The mechanism fails honestly (typed result, no wrong line ships), but the design tension and misleading diagnosis are exactly as stated.

verdicts.title: Exit-3 semantics break intended-failure figures and scene scripting
verdicts.note: 08 §3.1 pins exit 3 for "a non-clean `solve`" with no carve-out; 03 §6's `expect_fail` ("declares doctrine checks a *legitimate* non-clean line is expected to fail") appears nowhere in 08 — no wiring to exit codes exists in any doc. The `scene` verb row and §3.1 never state scene's exit when a line's internal solve is legitimately non-clean (fig 8.4's red companion, promised by 01 §3/§5 and G7). Small caveat that does not defeat the claim: stdout always carries the JSON envelope, so an agent can disambiguate by parsing — but the exit-code tier is the stated scripting/gating surface ("gate-friendly JSON output and the exit-code tiers", 09 §8), and at that surface success and failure of an intended-red bake are indistinguishable or unspecified.

verdicts.title: Chained lines are promised green but the colour formula yields amber
verdicts.note: A real inconsistency survives, but not the one as stated. 04 §5 says linked lines are "graded by a chain-aware check set … rather than the single-corner clean bar" — under that clause a chain line passing its applicable checks is outcome `clean` (02 §7: "`clean` — all checks pass") and 06 §5.1's unmodified formula yields green, so "the formula yields amber" is not compelled and no carve-out is strictly needed. And "the prior defect is reintroduced one class softer" mischaracterizes: the prior defect was red, and 01 §3 explicitly blesses "a contained-but-sound chained line renders amber or green per its verdict" — amber is sanctioned behaviour, not the defect. Surviving nucleus: 04's own label "contained, not clean" contradicts the outcome=clean reading (02 §7 reserves "stayed contained" for `violation`), 01 §3's "amber or green" conflicts with 04 §5/08 §6(d)'s flat "green", and 06 §5.1's "outcome = clean with failed checks" branch is vacuous under 02 §7's definition — the outcome/check relationship is genuinely unagreed.

verdicts.title: P-RUNWIDE-WIDEN contradicts the trail-braking invariant
verdicts.note: 09 §3.4's preamble, immediately above the property list, defeats the claim: "Each is one sentence here; thresholds and constants belong to `02-physics-model.md`." The scoping the critic says is missing is exactly what that sentence delegates — 02 §5.4.2 scopes the widening invariant to "sustained `−a_clip ≥ a_noreturn` at `|phi| ≥ 15°`", and 02 §5.4.1 owns the sub-threshold tightening case. A test written from the spec (which mandates reading 02 for thresholds) is scoped above A_SU_ONSET/a_noreturn and coexists with C30-trailbrake; the "guaranteed to fail" conclusion only follows from reading 09's one-sentence summary in isolation, which the doc explicitly forbids. What remains is loose summary wording, not a spec-level contradiction.

verdicts.title: Occluder ref grammar: bare c1 vs anchor grammar vs 08's third shape
verdicts.note: 03 §4 defines the station anchor as "corner-relative `entry|exit|mid:<cornerId> ± offset_m`, or absolute `at_s`", then immediately exemplifies the token form with a bare corner id: "`hedge inside c1 -6x26 margin=1.2 depth=2.5`" — bare `c1` is not in the anchor set and its resolution (entry? mid? s0?) is defined nowhere (checked 03 §3.1 bookBlind, 04 §7, 06, 08). 08 §6(c)'s "`hedge inside entry:c1-25 -1.0x30`" then puts a station offset inside the ref while also carrying the `<offset>x<span>` token, leaving `-1.0`'s meaning (station vs lateral) genuinely ambiguous — 03 never glosses the `<offset>` field at all. Three mutually incompatible example shapes on the surface bookBlind, R3, and recipes (c)/(e) depend on; unimplementable without guessing, as claimed.

verdicts.title: Stop-within-sight uses a braking model the tool's own physics forbids at lean
verdicts.note: The numbers and quotes check out: 04 §6's V1 applies "at every station"; 03 §5.2's default is "alert {a_ssd: 7.0 m/s², t_react_s: 1.0}"; 02 §5.3 puts the street-profile point of no return at ≈5.4 m/s² ("Braking harder than that while leaned *forces* the stand-up") and 02 §5.6 declares saves past it "infeasible by construction". The 7.0 m/s² stop assumed at leaned stations is thus one the model itself says cannot be executed while holding the line — and no doc (checked 01 §6/§8, 03 §5, 04 §6, 05 §6.2, 07 §3.3's HUD sight row) acknowledges the upright-decel assumption or placards it, against 01 §8's own "wrong-but-plausible … strictly worse than an honest 'not modelled'" policy. A defender could argue ssd is a deliberate highway-engineering yardstick (aashto framing), but the design never says so for the leaned case, which is precisely the finding.

verdicts.title: 02 retains both sample series; 05's contract has no home for the raw one
verdicts.note: 02 §6: "Both series are retained; the time-base and sample contract are owned by `05-…`" — but 05 §2's Trajectory is exactly `{samples, events, terminated}` with `samples` as "one flat array" on the arc grid, and 05 §3.1's only other series is the optional export-convenience time-uniform series, "default unset", which "no consumer may require" and which has no field in the Trajectory shape either. A literal implementation of 05 cannot satisfy 02's retention mandate; even reading 02's ownership clause as ceding authority to 05 leaves 02's sentence contradicting the contract it defers to. Minor severity is right — the fix is one stale sentence — but the contradiction is real as stated.

verdicts.title: sightFrom's signature cannot produce the trend it promises
verdicts.note: 03 §5.1 puts `trend` in `sightFrom(road, eye, occluders)`'s return and defines it "from the change in `sight_m` against the previous sample" — but the signature carries no history, and 09 §3.4's P-SIGHT-EYE pins it as "a pure function of (road, eye, occluders)". Meanwhile 05 §2.1 says trend is "the sign of `d(sight_m)/ds` … computed by `stateAt` (§4), not stored" — a location and definition that both differ from 03's, even as 05 §4 claims to use "03 §5.1's definition … verbatim". The deadband arithmetic point also holds: 2.0 m of change against a 0.5 m-spaced previous sample is a slope-4 threshold under which trend would read "steady" almost everywhere — evidently not the intent. No doc reconciles the two definitions or the signature; confirmed at minor severity.

verdicts.title: Flag/field/scene spellings are mapped but not one-to-one as claimed
verdicts.note: All evidence verifies: 08 §4.1 claims "Flags mirror schema fields one-to-one", yet `--visibility-governed` is a boolean over the enum field `vis: none|cautious` (04 §6/§7) — and under 08 §4.2's precedence ("a flag always overrides the corresponding loaded field") a boolean flag cannot express the override to `vis=none` at all, so it is functionally not a mirror. Entry speed genuinely has four spellings (`rider.start.speed_kmh` 03 §6, `entry_kmh` 04 §8 R1/R3, `entry=` 04 §7, `--entry` 08 §4.1) with the printed mapping promised only for the CLI↔schema pair (`schema cli`), not across scene/solve-spec surfaces. The finding's own concession (surface is discoverable) keeps this fairly scoped at minor.

verdicts.title: Jump-point sources: 09 adds 'plan stations' that 05/07 exclude
verdicts.note: 05 §5 is exclusive: named jump targets "are exactly `events` filtered by `kind`"; 07 §3.1 lists only event ticks ("These are free — the engine already emits them"); 09 §6's C-BOOKMARKS asserts "exactly the result's events and plan stations". A charitable reading (plan actions surface as brake_start/turn_in/crack/roll_on/position_start events) makes the sets coincide in the common case, but it fails at the edges — a plan action never activated before termination has a station but no event, and 05 §5 guarantees only events are stateAt-resolvable — so the three docs do state different expected sets for the same contract test. Correctly scoped as minor.

verdicts.title: Dangling schema fields: config.mode, required checks_version, missing hazards section
verdicts.note: All three sub-points verify. (1) 03 §6 carries `mode?` with field note "`mode` (`street`)" and no doc in the set enumerates its values or effect — the exact class 03 §6.1's D8 rule ("every field `validate` accepts must provably reach the controller or the analyzers") forbids. (2) `checks_version` has no `?` (required), no listed default (unlike mu/mode/ds_m/ssd_model), and 08 §4.1's flag list contains no flag for it — contradicting 08 §4's "every field an authoring input can carry has a flag". (3) 08 §5.1's closed section list has `occluders` but no `hazards`, while 03 §4 defines hazards as "Two distinct families" — no doc assigns hazards a schema section, against 08 §2's schema-complete rule.

verdicts.title: Double-apex inter-touch drift: two different mechanisms claimed
verdicts.note: The quotes are accurate, but the dichotomy ("cannot both be the design of record") fails: 04 §4.4 names specifically "the mid-corner *stand-up* drift between touches — previously impossible for the point-mass", which is trivially true (the point-mass has no stand-up term) and can coexist with 01 §5/02 §2's roll-on-widening drift as a second, distinct mechanism (e.g. a decelerating inter-touch phase). What survives is a real underspecification: 01 §5 attributes THE drift of the canonical two-touch plan to roll-on widening, no doc says when the stand-up variant is the operative mechanism instead, and 04's "the solver's `expect_fail` declarations shrink accordingly" is underivable without knowing which — so the nucleus (muddled mechanism attribution affecting solveDoubleApex's expect_fail story) stands at minor, but the flat contradiction claim does not.

verdicts.title: P-SIGHT-EYE is false under fuzzing with outside occluders
verdicts.note: 09 §3.4 states the property universally ("moving the eye laterally toward the outside of a blind corner never *shortens* `sight_m`") and its preamble mandates "fuzzed schema-valid scenarios"; 03 §4 admits `side` ∈ "inside | outside | left | right" with `vehicle` as a "parked or oncoming-lane vehicle" rectangle. A vehicle on the outside edge ahead of the eye is legal fuzz geometry under which moving outward tucks the road behind the obstruction and shortens sight — the property is a theorem only for inside occluders (the D4 hold-wide premise it cites). 09 §3.4's threshold delegation to 02 cannot save it: occluder-side scoping is not a threshold or constant. Genuine spec overreach; minor is the right severity since the fix is a one-clause scoping.

verdicts.title: 08 announces five recipes, delivers six
verdicts.note: Verified verbatim: 08's intro says "schema discoverability, and five canonical agent recipes"; 08 §1 item 5 says "Six agent recipes, end to end"; §6 is headed "Six canonical end-to-end sequences" with (a)–(f), and 04 §8 has R1–R6. Simple count rot from adding the D10 constraint recipe (f)/R6 without updating the intro.

verdicts.title: window:"all" is used but absent from the ViewSpec grammar
verdicts.note: 06 §2.1's type admits only `window?: {from: StationRef, to: StationRef}`; 06 §2.4 promises "The full-extent view is one flag away (`mode: \"true\"` or `window: \"all\"`)". The string variant is untypeable as specified (and 04 §7's `window=auto` spelling is likewise outside the grammar, reinforcing rather than resolving the gap). No other doc extends ViewSpec.

verdicts.title: Phase vocabulary: 'entry' and 'done' have no defining boundaries
verdicts.note: 05 §4 pins `phase` as the six-value closed set "approach|entry|steering|mid|exit|done … (from events)"; the only phase-boundary definitions in the set are 06 §4's four event-delimited bands (approach `brake_start→turn_in`, steering `turn_in→steering_complete`, mid `→roll_on`, exit `→exit`). I checked 01 §4.1's vocabulary, 05 §5's event kinds, and 07 — no doc says which events delimit `entry` or `done` (`done` is guessable as post-exit/termination but never stated). Two of six values on an agent-facing field are implementable only by guessing, as claimed.

verdicts.title: 08's importable API omits functions other docs require
verdicts.note: 08 §7.1's import statement — `{ run, solve, compileMistake, compare, sweep, validate, renderViews, explain, stateAt }` — omits `suggestTurnIn` and `sightFrom` (both named "Key API names" in 00 §4), and `chainedSolve` (a distinct entry point per 04 §5, required by R4). The section is the design of record for "the programmatic API", so the omission is real even if the list is arguably illustrative. The noted tension also verifies: 07 §2.4 licenses the viewer to call `sightFrom` while 05 §1 rules "nothing downstream ever re-derives state the engine already had" with sight recorded per sample — unacknowledged in either doc. Correctly filed as polish.

verdicts.title: Suspect 10 adjudicated: 00's core-sample list is a declared minimum, not a mismatch
verdicts.note: The adjudication is accurate: 00 §4 frames its list as "Core per-sample fields (canonical minimum, detailed in 05)", so 05 §2.1's `clipped`, `n_long`, `n_lat` are a sanctioned elaboration, not a conflict — and 05 §8.2 does pin all three in the Trace CSV column order, making the suggested one-line addition to 00 reasonable polish. Nothing in the doc set contradicts this reading.

verdicts.title: Tolerance-table location: 02 points at 09, 09 points at the fixtures
verdicts.note: Verbatim conflict: 02 §8 says "the single tolerance table lives in `09-verification-and-testing.md` §3 and owns the ± values"; 09 §3.2 gives only example TUNING values and says "the tolerance table lives beside the fixtures, in one place" — i.e. in the repo, not in 09. Both claim single-source ownership at different locations; a reimplementer following 02's pointer finds no owning table. Correctly filed as polish.
